Thin ivory lines on near-black: classic **line illusions** drawn as thin straps along straight segments, in 6 variants: two **Zöllner illusions** (6 long upright parallel lines, each with a short tick every 1/12 at 60° or 35° to it, the tilt turned over from line to line, so that the parallel lines look slanted), the **Ehrenstein illusion** (a 4×4 lattice of points, each with 20 rays round an empty centre of radius 0.03, where a disc seems to be), the **Müller-Lyer illusion** (6 horizontal shafts of one length, with inward arrowheads on the even rows and outward tails on the odd ones, which make them look unequal), the **Hering illusion** (24 rays from the middle with two straight horizontal lines across them, which look bowed) and the **Ponzo illusion** (two lines converging downward with two bars of one length, of which the one in the narrow part looks longer). Each line is a strap with the half width 0.004 (solid) to 0.009 (faded out) in tile lengths, and the straps are merged as 1 − Π(1 − strap), so there are no corners where they cross. The tone is 0.04 + 0.1·smooth(clamp(ink/0.35)) + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5); the height is 0.8·ink (the grain is not in the height); the AO is lowest, 0.6, where there is no line; roughness is 0.5 and metallic 0. The pattern wraps with `fract(u)` and `fract(v)` and is **exactly periodic** (the long lines of the Zöllner variants run through the tile and the other figures are inside it). The illusions are perceptual effects; only the geometry is guaranteed here (the parallel lines really parallel, the bars really of one length, the horizontal lines really straight), and nothing about perception is measured.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the usual forms of the illusions (for instance that the bar in the narrow part of the Ponzo figure looks longer) are described from memory, not looked up in the literature, and the parameters at which each illusion is strongest were not checked; the numbers of lines, the angles, the numbers of rays, the sizes, the strap widths 0.004 and 0.009, the ivory-on-near-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile of the 6 variants are authored choices. I left out the Poggendorff illusion, the Fraser spiral, the Kanizsa figure and other illusions, which is my choice and was not asked for. Unlike `opticalillusions` (the café wall and the Hermann grid, whole areas of light and dark), this kind draws thin figures along segments. The tests check only the geometry, not the illusion. Mistakes of mine while testing: (1) the ring-arc routine of the probe did not handle an arc spanning the angle 0 and counted it twice (21 arcs for the Ehrenstein variant and 25 for the Hering one), so it now starts at the first place without ink; (2) the mutation check again showed that the occlusion formula was not caught, and a pointwise comparison was added; (3) the mutation that cut the Zöllner long lines from [−0.1, 1.1] to [0, 1] was not caught either, which I reason to be an equivalent mutant (the sampled points are always inside [0, 1), so the foot of the perpendicular on the line is always on the segment), without any check beyond the mutation run. The seed-to-variant table was found by a probe that compared 40 seeds with the independent model and is not an independent oracle. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 11 (covering all 6 variants). The standard C1 sweep gives 0 violations on seeds 3, 0, 2, 7, 4 and 11.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 105, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant; the segments of the variant are generated (Zöllner: 6 long lines and 72 ticks, 78 in all; Ehrenstein: 16 points × 20 rays, 320; Müller-Lyer: 6 shafts and 24 fins, 30; Hering: 24 rays and 2 horizontal lines, 26; Ponzo: 2 oblique lines and 2 bars, 4), and each is put into the buckets of a 32×32 grid that its strap (outer half width 0.009) reaches; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): only the segments in the pixel's bucket are looked at, the squared distance to each gives a strap = smoothstep((outer² − d²)/(outer² − inner²)), ink = 1 − Π(1 − strap), tone = dark 0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·smooth(clamp(ink/0.35)) + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5); height = 0.8·ink (times relief 0.0008). I measured single-threaded sampling of 512×512 in Bun: lineillusions took 92 and 90 ms in two runs and talbotcarpet 177 and 172 ms in the same environment (a full test run was going on in the background, so the numbers are noisy); the time in a browser Worker was not measured.

`opticalillusions` adds optical illusions, bringing the current catalog from 1125 to 1126 kinds (1127 gallery choices including plain). Ivory on near-black: geometric **optical illusions** drawn exactly, in 6 variants: three **café walls** (8 rows of alternating black and white squares, every row shifted against the one above by 1/2, 1/4 or 3/4 of a square and parted by grey mortar lines; the mortar lines are in fact straight and level but look sloped), two **Hermann grids** (black squares parted by light lanes 0.2 or 0.12 of a cell wide, with grey ghosts seen at the crossings) and a **scintillating grid** (black squares, grey lanes and a white disc of radius 0.12 of a cell on every crossing). The edges are smoothed over 0.02 of a pitch (C1): for the café wall the squares come from the signed distance along the row, and for the grids the mask of a square is the product of two one-dimensional masks (so the corners are round). The tone is 0.06 + 0.84·value (0 black, 1 light, mortar and grey lanes 0.5) + 0.03·(grain − 0.5); the height is 0.8·value (the grain is not in the height); the AO is lowest, 0.6, in the dark; roughness is 0.55 and metallic 0. The pattern wraps with `fract(u)` and `fract(v)` and is **exactly periodic**. The illusion itself is a perceptual effect; only the geometry is guaranteed here (the mortar lines straight, the shift of the rows and the width of the lanes as set), and nothing about perception is measured.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the usual forms of the café wall, the Hermann grid and the scintillating grid are described from memory (not looked up in the literature, and the parameters at which each illusion is strongest were not checked); the number of rows or cells, the shifts, the widths of the mortar and the lanes, the disc radius 0.12, the smoothing 0.02, the ivory-on-near-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile of the 6 variants are authored choices, and I did not compare it one by one with the existing checkerboard or grid kinds. The tests check only the geometry, not the illusion. Three mistakes of mine happened while testing: (1) the first area mean compared the sampler on a 256² grid with the independent model on a 1024² grid, and variant 4 differed by 0.0066 (0.0087 at 1024²); the cause was that the model sampled on a grid aligned with the cells (a lane 15.36 pixels wide caught 16 pixels), not the sampler, so both now use a 1021² grid (a prime, not aligned with the cells) and differ by at most 0.00125, the Hermann grids having the closed form 1 − (1 − width)² of 0.36000 and 0.22560; (2) the mean of the tone contains the mean offset of the grain (0.0066 at seed 0), so the height (without grain) is used; (3) the scan of the lane widths first counted the lanes that the border of the tile cuts in two (their width is half), and now leaves them out. The mutation check also showed that the occlusion formula was not caught, and a pointwise comparison was added. The seed-to-variant table was found by a probe that compared 40 seeds with the ideal pattern of plain predicates and is not an independent oracle. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 11 (covering all 6 variants). The standard C1 sweep gives 0 violations on seeds 4, 1, 7, 2, 0 and 6.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 104, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): for the café wall, the row is floor(fv·n), and the distance from the edge of the row (in row pitches) gives the mortar weight smooth(clamp((distance − width/2)/0.02)); the position along the row fu·n − row·shift (in square widths) is turned into a phase of period 2, giving the signed distance to the nearest edge of the squares, whose value is smooth(clamp(0.5 + distance/(2·0.02))); value = mortar value + (square value − mortar value)·weight; for the grids, each direction gives 0.5 − |position in the cell − 0.5| − width/2 and smooth(clamp(0.5 + ·/(2·0.02))), the product is the mask of the square, and value = lane value·(1 − mask); the scintillating grid adds the mask of the disc of the points less than 0.12 from the nearest crossing (smoothed the same way). There is no loop per pixel, only a few multiplications and one hypot. I measured single-threaded sampling of 512×512 in Bun: opticalillusions took 64 and 65 ms in two runs and talbotcarpet 131 and 133 ms in the same environment; the time in a browser Worker was not measured.

`gerstnerocean` adds the Gerstner ocean, bringing the current catalog from 1124 to 1125 kinds (1126 gallery choices including plain). Pale cyan-white on a deep sea blue: one instant of **Gerstner (trochoidal) ocean waves** — plane waves in several directions added together, where every water particle moves horizontally along the wave as well as up and down, so the crests are sharp and the troughs wide. Each wave is [m, n, s, phase]: the wave vector 2π(m, n) (integers m and n, so the tile is exactly periodic), the steepness s = A·|k| (A the amplitude); the water particle with the rest position x₀ is moved to x₀ − Σ A·k̂·sin(k·x₀ − phase) and is at the height Σ A·cos(k·x₀ − phase). Where the **Jacobian of the displacement** (the area of the surface per area at rest, 1 where nothing is stretched) is small the crests are squeezed together, and there is foam (fully white at a Jacobian of 0.38 or less, none at 0.7 or more, a smoothstep in between). The seed picks one of 6 variants: a single swell (one wave of steepness 0.62 with a line of foam on the crests), a wind sea (9 waves, total steepness 0.55), a cross sea (10 waves in two directions, 0.65), a choppy sea (12 waves, 0.8), a storm (14 waves, 0.92) and a swell with chop (11 waves, 0.35); the wave table of each variant is data written into the preset. The steepnesses add up to less than 1, so the surface never folds over itself. The tone is 0.08 + 0.42·level + 0.45·foam + 0.03·(grain − 0.5); the height is the level (0 to 1, no grain); the AO is lowest in the troughs, 0.65 (1 − 0.35·(1 − level)); roughness is 0.08 and metallic 0. The pattern wraps with `fract(u)` and `fract(v)` and is **exactly periodic**; it is a snapshot of one instant, with no time parameter.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the Gerstner waves and the use of the Jacobian for foam are described from memory (not looked up in the literature); the wave tables of the 6 variants (generated once by a small script with a fixed random seed and then written into the preset, the script is not in the repository), the total steepnesses, the foam thresholds 0.7 and 0.38, the deep-sea-blue and pale-cyan colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices, and there is neither the deep-water dispersion relation nor any time evolution. That the Jacobian stays positive when the steepnesses add up to less than 1 is my inference (the operator norm of the matrix Σ s·cosθ·k̂k̂ᵀ is at most Σ s) and was not proved separately; what I measured is the minimum Jacobian of the variants on a 300×300 grid: 0.3800, 0.6497, 0.5854, 0.4829, 0.4925 and 0.6560 (the 0.38 of variant 0 is 1 − 0.62). My first probe compared the height without dividing by relief (the height of createSurfaceSampler is already multiplied by relief), so every seed was taken for variant 5 and the differences were close to 1; after the correction the differences from the forward map are 1.2e-15 to 4.0e-15 (400 points). The first version had too narrow a tone range and the preview was grey, so waterSpan went from 0.3 to 0.42; the foam thresholds were first 0.5 and 0.12, but the minimum Jacobian of most variants is above 0.48, so there was almost no foam, and they became 0.65 and 0.25 and then 0.7 and 0.38, so most variants still have a little foam only where crests add up, and variants 1 and 5, whose minimum Jacobian is about 0.65, have almost none. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 11 (covering all 6 variants); the seed-to-variant table was found by a probe that compared 40 seeds with the forward map and is not an independent oracle. The standard C1 sweep gives 0 violations on seeds 2, 3, 5, 0, 7 and 1.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 103, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant; the waves of the variant are expanded into Float64Arrays (wave vector, unit direction, amplitude A = s/(2π·|(m, n)|) and phase); there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): Newton's method finds the rest position of the water that is at (fu, fv): the residual is rest position + displacement − (fu, fv) and the Jacobian matrix is [[1 − Σ s·cosθ·ux², −Σ s·cosθ·ux·uy], [the same, 1 − Σ s·cosθ·uy²]], with at most 24 steps and a stop when the sum of the absolute step is under 1e-15; at the converged position the height and the determinant of the Jacobian are computed again; level = 0.5 + 0.5·Σ A·cosθ / Σ A; foam = smooth(clamp((0.7 − J)/(0.7 − 0.38))). Every Newton step costs one sin and one cos per wave per pixel. I measured single-threaded sampling of 512×512 in Bun: gerstnerocean took 304 and 324 ms in two runs and talbotcarpet 147 and 152 ms in the same environment; the time in a browser Worker was not measured.

`islamicstars` adds Islamic star patterns, bringing the current catalog from 1123 to 1124 kinds (1125 gallery choices including plain). Dark gold straps on a deep teal-blue: star patterns drawn on tilings of regular polygons by **Hankin's polygons-in-contact method** — in every polygon (side 1) two rays leave the midpoint of each edge towards the two neighbouring vertices at a fixed angle to the edge (the contact angle), the rays of neighbouring edges meet on the bisector of the vertex, and so a star is drawn in each polygon, joined into one strapwork over the whole tile. The seed picks one of 6 variants: the tiling of octagons and squares 4.8.8 at the contact angles 45°, 60° and 75°, the tiling of squares 4.4.4.4 at 60° and 30°, and the snub square tiling 3.3.4.3.4 at 70°; one tile holds 2×2, 2×2, 2×2, 3×3, 3×3 and 2×2 periods of the tiling. The star point is on the bisector at a·cosθ / cos(θ − π/n) from the centre (a the apothem, n the number of sides), and the half width of a strap is 0.05 (solid) to 0.09 (faded out); the straps are merged as 1 − Π(1 − strap), so there are no corners where they cross. The height is cellHeight times the strap, the grain goes only into the colour, the dark gaps have an AO of 0.6, metallic is 0 and roughness 0.38. The pattern wraps with `fract(u)` and `fract(v)` and is **exactly periodic** over a whole number of periods of the tiling; there is no over-and-under weaving.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; Hankin's polygons-in-contact method is described from memory and was not looked up in the literature; the tilings and contact angles of the 6 variants, the number of periods per tile, the strap half widths 0.05 and 0.09, the deep-teal-and-dark-gold colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices, and only tilings on a square lattice are used, with none on a hexagonal lattice (the tile is square, so a hexagonal lattice does not fit into a whole number of periods). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype in Bun (not in the repository): the polygons of the three tilings cover 20,000 random points with no hole, and no point is covered twice for 4.8.8 and 3.3.4.3.4 while 1 point is covered twice for 4.4.4.4 (probably exactly on a boundary; I did not check it) (the polygon areas of 4.8.8, 4.4.4.4 and 3.3.4.3.4 add up to 5.828427, 1.000000 and 3.732051, the area of the lattice cell), and I looked at the images from the prototype. The prototype's snub square at the contact angle 50° came out as very large arcs and did not look good, so 70° is used. The independent model of the test first found each star point by intersecting the rays from two neighbouring midpoints, but for the squares of 4.8.8 at 45° the two rays lie on one line (the determinant is 0) and the probe showed a difference of 1.0 for variant 0; after intersecting the first ray with the bisector of the vertex the difference was 9.2e-15 (the sampler uses the closed form a·cosθ / cos(θ − π/n)). The test of the ray angles at the midpoint of an octagon edge first used a ring of radius 0.25 and a threshold of 0.5, and at θ = 75° the four arcs ran into two, so it became radius 0.4 and threshold 0.99. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 11 (covering all 6 variants); the seed-to-variant table was found by a probe that compared 40 seeds with the independent model and is not an independent oracle. The standard C1 sweep gives 0 violations on seeds 0, 10, 2, 5, 1 and 9.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 102, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant; the polygons of one period of the tiling are built (octagons and squares for 4.8.8, squares for 4.4.4.4, and for the snub square tiling 2 squares turned by ±15° and 4 triangles taken across the edges of the squares, with the duplicates removed); for the periods −1 to cells every polygon gets its star points, giving 2n segments per polygon (24 per period for 4.8.8, 8 for 4.4.4.4 and 40 for the snub square tiling), and each segment is put into the buckets of a 32×32 grid that it reaches with the outer half width; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): only the segments in the pixel's bucket are looked at, the squared distance to each gives a strap = smoothstep((outer² − d²)/(outer² − inner²)), ink = 1 − Π(1 − strap), tone = gap 0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·smooth(clamp(ink/0.35)) + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5); height = 0.8·ink (times relief 0.0008). I measured single-threaded sampling of 512×512 in Bun: islamicstars took 119 and 122 ms in two runs and talbotcarpet 205 and 195 ms in the same environment (a full test run was going on in the background, so the numbers are noisy); the time in a browser Worker was not measured.

`fresneldiffraction` adds Fresnel diffraction, bringing the current catalog from 1122 to 1123 kinds (1124 gallery choices including plain). Pale violet on a dark blue-violet: the **near-field (Fresnel) diffraction** of a monochromatic plane wave of wavelength 1 behind an opening in a screen — the intensity on the (x, z) plane (x across from −4 to 4, z down the page as the distance from the screen from 0.05 to 8). The tone is 1 − exp(−I/0.6), I being the intensity with the free field as 1. The seed picks one of 6 variants: a straight edge (the half-plane x > 0), single slits of width 1.6 and 3.2, opaque strips of width 1.6 and 0.6 (the field being the free field minus that of the opening of the same width), and a double slit (two slits of width 0.8 centred at ±1.1). At the shadow boundary of the edge (x = 0) I is 1/4 for every z, the first maximum on the lit side is 1.3704 (at v = x·√(2/z) = 1.217) and the dark side falls off monotonically; slits and strips show dense Fresnel fringes at the top (small z) that widen and merge going down. Every pixel is evaluated from the Fresnel integrals C and S (a power series and a continued fraction) at the ends of each opening: the amplitude is e^(−iπ/4)/√2·Σ[(C + iS)(v₂) − (C + iS)(v₁)] with v = (x′ − x)·√(2/z); the height is cellHeight times the tone (the grain is not in the height) and the grain goes only into the colour; the dark gaps have an AO of 0.6, metallic is 0 and roughness 0.34. The pattern wraps with `fract(u)` and `fract(v)` and is not periodic (the whole tile is one picture with a dark border of 0.04).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 6 variants' openings (the straight edge, slits of half width 0.8 and 1.6, strips of half width 0.8 and 0.3, and a double slit of half width 0.4 centred at ±1.1), the window x ±4 and z 0.05–8, the reference intensity 0.6, the pale-violet-on-dark-blue-violet colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Before the implementation I wrote a prototype in Bun (not in the repository): the power series of C(v) and S(v) (for |v| ≤ 3.5) and the asymptotic series agreed with Simpson's integral to within 9.4e-10, and the first maximum of the straight edge was 1.37044 at v = 1.2170. Three problems in the implementation were found by probes and fixed: (1) the first version let z become zero or negative in the margin, so the square root gave NaN (2304 non-finite pixels for every seed), now z is at least 0.05; (2) the edge was first an opening [0, 60], which put I at the shadow boundary x = 0 off 1/4 by 6.9e-3 and the maximum at 1.3766–1.3862, now it is [0, 1e7] and C and S take their limit 1/2 for |v| > 1e5; (3) the standard C1 sweep found 1382 to 13305 violation records on the 6 variants (w up to about 9.5), which I infer came from a jump of about 1e-9 where the power series and the four-term asymptotic series meet at |v| = 3.5 (amplified by the second difference over h), so the asymptotic series became a continued fraction (the modified Lentz method for |v| > 1.5, the coefficients written from memory and checked numerically) and the records are 0; the continued fraction and Simpson differ by at most 1.7e-13 for v from 1.6 to 50 (prototype measurement, limited by Simpson's own accuracy). The reference intensity was first 1.2, the preview was too low in contrast, and it became 0.6 (I looked at the preview). I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 11 and seed 14 (covering all 6 variants); the seed-to-variant table was found by a probe that compared 40 seeds with the analytic formula and is not an independent oracle. After the fix the standard C1 sweep (the points of the vortexstreet test, second difference over h) gives 0 violations on seeds 1, 14, 6, 7, 0 and 2 of the 6 variants.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 101, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x = half width 4·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin), z = max(0.05, 0.05 + 7.95·(fv − margin)/(1 − 2·margin)) and v = (end − x)·√(2/z); for each interval of an opening there are two ends with (C, S): for |v| ≤ 1.5 the power series (41 terms), for |v| > 1.5 the continued fraction (modified Lentz, convergence at 1e-16, at most 200 iterations, measured 44 at v = 1.6 and 13 or fewer for v ≥ 3.5), and for |v| > 1e5 (the far end 1e7 of the straight edge) simply 1/2; the amplitude is multiplied by e^(−iπ/4)·√½, and for a strip it is 1 minus that; ink = edge fade·(1 − exp(−|amplitude|²/0.6)), tone = gap 0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·smooth(clamp(ink/0.35)) + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5); height = 0.8·ink (times relief 0.0008). I measured single-threaded sampling of 512×512 in Bun: fresneldiffraction took 140, 145 and 143 ms in three runs and talbotcarpet 120, 128 and 126 ms in the same environment; the time in a browser Worker was not measured.

`zetalandscape` adds the Riemann zeta landscape, bringing the current catalog from 1121 to 1122 kinds (1123 gallery choices including plain). Pale blue on a dark navy: bands of the phase and modulus of the **Riemann zeta function** ζ(s) on the complex plane s = σ + i t (σ to the right, t upward) — the bright bands are 0.5 + 0.5·cos(4·arg ζ) (the phase) and 0.5 + 0.5·cos(2π·ln|ζ|/ln 2) (one band for every doubling of the modulus), mixed 0.55 : 0.45 and going dark where |ζ| is below 0.003, so every **zero** is a dark core with pinwheel-like fringes round it, the **pole** at s = 1 is a set of ever denser concentric rings, the right side σ > 1 is flat (ζ tends to 1), and along the critical line σ = 1/2 there is a row of non-trivial zeros, with dense fringes on the left where the modulus grows. Each pixel is evaluated by the Euler–Maclaurin formula (the sum of n^(−s) for n < 24, plus N^(1−s)/(s − 1), N^(−s)/2 and the Bernoulli corrections up to B₁₄). The seed picks one of 6 square windows: one centred on s = −0.5 (with the pole and the trivial zeros at the negative even integers), one centred on 0.5 + 14.1347 i (the first non-trivial zero), and others centred on 23 i, 1 + 12 i, 31 i and −1 + 9 i (with some of the first six zeros of the critical line). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04) and is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only bands of the phase and the modulus, with no real colour function, and the error of Euler–Maclaurin at the far left of the windows (σ down to −11) was not measured directly (the tone differs from the functional equation by 0.0092 at the worst); unlike the existing `phasevortices` (the phase picture of one specific periodic complex field cos(2π(2x + a)) + i·cos(2π(2y + b)), 16 vortices per tile), it draws the Riemann zeta function itself, whose zeros, pole and functional-equation symmetry have mathematical meaning. (The zeta function, the Euler–Maclaurin formula and the ordinates of the non-trivial zeros are from my memory, checked in a prototype; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 6 windows (centres and half widths), the 24 terms and 7 Bernoulli terms, the 4 phase bands, the modulus ratio 2, the mixing 0.55, the zero radius 0.003, the pale-blue-on-dark-navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Before the implementation I wrote a prototype in Bun (not in the repository) to check Euler–Maclaurin: ζ(2) = 1.6449340668, ζ(3) = 1.2020569032, ζ(4) = 1.0823232337, ζ(0) = −0.5, ζ(−1) = −0.0833333333 and ζ(1/2) = −1.4603545088 agree with the known values, |ζ| at ζ(−2) and ζ(−4) is 1.8e-12 and 9.8e-10, and |ζ| at the first six non-trivial zeros is between 2e-16 and 9e-11 (which also confirms the ordinates I remembered). The first image the prototype drew had a zero fade radius of 0.05, which made a big dark region round the whole negative real axis (where |ζ| is small), so it is now 0.003, and I moved the window centres to the left (to shrink the flat region at σ > 2 on the right). I looked at the previews of 12 seeds (0 to 11, covering variants 0, 3, 4 and 5) and then of seeds 12 and 14 (variants 1 and 2). The tests **read only the sampler output back** (the tone is recovered from the height), the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written — the sampler uses Euler–Maclaurin, and the test finds ζ by entirely different methods and computes the expected tone with the preset formula: (1) **the Euler product (σ ≥ 2)**: the test multiplies the factors 1/(1 − p^(−s)) of the primes below 1000 (the tail is under 2e-4), and on 400 points of each variant (σ from 2 to the edge of the plot) the tones agree to within 0.01 (0.0002 at the worst in the probe on 1500 points), with at most 2 exceptions allowed; (2) **the alternating series in the critical strip**: for σ between 0.15 and 0.85 and t up to 16, ζ(s) = η(s)/(1 − 2^(1−s)) with η summed by the Euler transform (60 terms), and on 300 points of each of the five variants whose windows contain such points the tones agree to within 0.01 (0.0000 in the probe); (3) **the functional equation (σ ≤ −1.5)**: ζ(s) = 2^s·π^(s−1)·sin(πs/2)·Γ(1−s)·ζ(1−s), with Γ by the Lanczos approximation (g = 7 and 9 coefficients, written in the test; I checked it in the prototype with Γ(1/2)² = π and Γ(5) = 24, and with ζ(−3), which came out as 0.0083333) and ζ(1−s) by the Euler product; on 300 points of each variant the tones agree to within 0.02 (0.0092 at the worst, in the window of −1 + 9 i, and under 0.0015 in the others in the probe), with at most 2 exceptions allowed; the sampler's values at the left of the windows are up to about 1e8; (4) **exact values and zeros**: on the real axis ζ(2) = π²/6, ζ(4) = π⁴/90, ζ(3) = 1.2020569031595942, ζ(0) = −1/2, ζ(−1) = −1/12 and ζ(1/2) = −1.4603545088095868 (the last three decimals from my memory, which the sampler reproduces to the 7 digits that the probe printed): the tones agree with those of the exact values to 1e-4, the tone at the trivial zeros −2 and −4 is below 1e-6, and at the first six non-trivial zeros 1/2 + i t (t = 14.134725141734693, 21.022039638771555, 25.010857580145688, 30.424876125859513, 32.935061587739189 and 37.586178158825671, from my memory) the tone is below 1e-6 (1e-15 at the most in the probe) in the windows that contain them (11 pairs of window and zero); (5) **the conjugate symmetry**: ζ(s̄) = conj ζ(s), so in the window centred on −0.5, which is symmetric about the real axis, the tones at σ + i t and σ − i t are the same (4.5e-5 at the most on 300 points in the probe, rounding in the sums). Mutation checks (done seven times): changing the B₄ coefficient −1/720 of the tail to −1/700 makes 4 of the 9 tests of that describe fail (the functional equation, the exact values, the seed difference and the maps); changing N^(−s)/2 to /3 makes 6 fail (but the Euler product test passes, since the term is small for σ ≥ 2); reversing the sign of the imaginary part of the pole term makes 7 fail; reversing the sign of the angle of n^(−s) makes 7 fail; changing the phase band 0.5 + 0.5cos to 0.5 − 0.5cos makes 7 fail; multiplying the zero fade radius by 4 makes 3 fail (the tone ranges, the functional equation and the seed difference; the zeros are still dark, so the zero test passes); changing the B₁₀ coefficient 1/47900160 to 1/47900000 (a relative change of 3e-6) makes **all 9 pass, not caught**; all were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the window for each seed was found with a probe (which window's values of ζ, computed by Euler–Maclaurin with N = 40, match the tones of the seed at 12 points) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) in the critical strip for t above 16 there is no independent check (most of the window of 31 i is there): only the zero positions and the regions covered by the Euler product and the functional equation; (c) the tone formula (the phase and modulus bands and the fade) is copied from the preset and not independently checked; (d) **the standard C1 sweep fails**: the six variants have 31093, 501, 24106, 14717, 24947 and 31255 records over the threshold, not because the function is not smooth but because of rounding noise — the terms of the sum at the left of the windows are as large as 1e15 to 1e16 and the relative error is about 1e-8 by my estimate, which I did not measure, above the roughly 3e-12 that a second difference at the step 1e-10 can tolerate; the window of 501 records (centred on 0.5 + 14.1347 i, with the smallest values) comes closest to passing; so **I did not change the sampler to satisfy C1** (that would need the functional equation to evaluate for σ < 0) and the test only checks that the values at the points that are exact in binary are identical at (u − 7, v + 11); (e) I did not check the literature or compare any reference picture. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the zero fade radius 0.05 → 0.003 and the window centres (see above); (2) the test first came out with a syntax error: I wrote `-(j + 1) ** -sigma`, and JavaScript does not allow a unary minus on the left of an exponentiation, so it is now `-((j + 1) ** -sigma)`; (3) I first wrote the number of pairs of window and zero as 12 in the zero check, while it is 11 (1, 3, 1, 5 and 1), so the first run failed; after correcting the count all 10 tests (including the kinds entry) passed, with no numerical threshold adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 100, seed ^ salt)` picks the window; ln n is precomputed for n < 24; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): σ = window centre σ + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin) and t = window centre t + half width·(0.5 − fv)/(0.5 − margin); the sum over n = 1 to 23 of exp(−σ ln n)·(cos(t ln n), −sin(t ln n)); plus N^(−s)/2 and N^(1−s)/(s − 1) (N = 24, with a floor of 1e-18 under the denominator); plus 7 terms B₂ₖ/(2k)!·s(s + 1)…(s + 2k − 2)·N^(−s−2k+1) (k = 1 to 7, with the coefficients 1/12, −1/720, 1/30240, −1/1209600, 1/47900160, −691/1307674368000 and 1/74724249600); ink = edge fade·smooth(clamp(|ζ|/0.003))·(0.55·(0.5 + 0.5·cos(4·arg ζ)) + 0.45·(0.5 + 0.5·cos(2π·ln|ζ|/ln 2))); color is `0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5)` (mask = smooth(clamp(ink/0.35))), height is `0.8·ink` (without grain, so the tone can be recovered), roughness is fixed at 0.34, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: about 23 exp, cos and sin calls per pixel plus the Euler–Maclaurin tail; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('zetalandscape', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 204, 213 and 205 ms in three runs (only three measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one window (the 6 chosen 10, 6, 3, 8, 9 and 4 times; seeds 1, 12, 14, 5, 0 and 7 for variants 0 to 5); the comparisons with the independent methods are above (the Euler product on 1500 points of each variant: worst 0.0002, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000 and 0.0001; the critical strip on 400 points of each of the five variants: worst 0.0000; the functional equation on 1500 points of each: worst 0.0001, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0000, 0.0014 and 0.0092); the tones on the real axis agree with those of the exact values to 5 decimals; the tones at the zeros are between 1.2e-26 and 1.5e-15; the conjugate symmetry is 4.5e-5 at the most; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 58.952%/53.732%/54.665%, color is 0.025691/0.025602/0.026061 to 0.874011/0.871722/0.873524 with a mean of 0.536735/0.486663/0.499368 and height is at most 0.800 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 58.977%/53.804%/54.695%/54.711%, color is 0.025197/0.025176/0.025422/0.025259 to 0.874644/0.873977/0.874001/0.874107 with a mean of 0.536770/0.486687/0.499393/0.499521 and AO is at least 0.6; between seeds 0 and 1 27.504% of the cells of the 256² grid differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (97.91, 124.39, 141.39), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0253 and the minimum z component is 253.

`lyapunovfractal` adds the Markus–Lyapunov fractal, bringing the current catalog from 1120 to 1121 kinds (1122 gallery choices including plain). Amber gold on a dark brown-black: the distribution on the (a, b) parameter plane of the Lyapunov exponent of the **logistic map driven by a repeating sequence of letters** — the map is x → r·x·(1 − x) with r taken in turn from the sequence (a for the letter A and b for the letter B), and every pixel (a to the right, b upward) starts at x = 1/2, skips 60 steps of warm-up and averages ln|r(1 − 2x)| over the next 120 steps; the tone is −exponent (bright where the motion is regular, dark in the chaos, over the range 0 to 1), so the bright areas are regions of stable cycles and the dark ones are chaos, with thin curling and "jellyfish" structures along the boundaries. The seed picks one of 6 variants: the sequences AB, AAB, ABB, AABAB and AABB in a window of 2 to 4 for (a, b) (2.6 to 4 for AABAB), and the sequence BBBBBBAAAAAA in a window of 3.4 to 4 for a and 2.5 to 3.4 for b (I remember it as the picture usually called "Zircon City", from memory, which I did not check). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04) and is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only a 120-step finite average, not the true Lyapunov exponent, with no statistical meaning; unlike the existing `logisticbifurcation` (the one-dimensional bifurcation diagram of the same map, with r along the axis and the points of the orbit drawn), it draws the exponent on the two-dimensional plane of two parameters. (The names Markus–Lyapunov fractal and Zircon City, and the multipliers of the fixed point and the 2-cycle on the diagonal, are from my memory and hand calculation; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 6 sequences and windows, the 60 steps of warm-up and 120 steps of averaging, the tone −exponent (over a range of 1), the amber-gold-on-dark-brown-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Before the implementation I wrote a prototype in Bun (not in the repository) that drew grey images of the 6 sequences (220², some 40 to 60 ms each) to pick the windows. I looked at the previews of 12 seeds (0 to 11, covering variants 0, 1, 3 and 5) and then of seeds 15, 16 and 6 (variants 2, 4 and 3). The tests **read only the sampler output back** (the tone is recovered from the height), the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written: (1) **agreement with another way of writing the iteration where the motion is regular**: the test iterates x′ = r(x − x·x), writes the derivative as |r − 2rx| and multiplies eight factors together before taking the logarithm, which rounds differently from the sampler; where the motion is regular the two agree, and where it is chaotic the rounding errors grow, so the pixels cannot be compared one by one: of 2000 points of each variant the points whose exponent in the test is below −0.05 (938 to 1445 of them) agree in tone to within 0.005, with at most 3 exceptions allowed (0, 1, 2, 1, 0 and 1 in the probe for the six variants, the worst difference 0.215 at a point near the edge of a regular region), and on the other points the mean tone agrees to within 0.002 (the mean is about 0.006 to 0.008 and the two differ by 1e-4 at the most in the probe); (2) **the exponents of the stable fixed point and 2-cycle on the diagonal a = b**: on the diagonal the sequence plays no part and the map is the logistic map with r = a = b, whose stable fixed point 1 − 1/r has the multiplier 2 − r (r between 1 and 3) and whose stable 2-cycle has the multiplier 4 + 2r − r² (just above 3), so the exponent is ln|2 − r| or ½·ln|4 + 2r − r²|; at r = 2.7, 2.8, 2.9, 3.1, 3.2, 3.3 and 3.4 the tones of the five variants whose window contains the diagonal agree with them to 1e-4 (3.4e-6 at the most in the probe), and in the chaos at r = 3.6, 3.7 and 3.9 the tone is 0 (the exponent is positive); the multipliers are my hand calculation. Mutation checks (done six times): writing the derivative as r(1 − x) makes 5 of the 6 tests of that describe fail; changing the map to r·x·(1.01 − x) makes 5 fail; swapping a and b for the letters A and B makes only 2 fail (the point-by-point one and the seed difference; the diagonal one is unaffected because the sequence plays no part on the diagonal); removing the warm-up makes 5 fail; shifting the a range of the window makes 5 fail; changing the floor 1e-12 that guards ln 0 to 1e-6 makes **all 6 pass, not caught** (it affects only the superstable orbits that pass exactly through x = 1/2); all were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (which variant's exponent matches the tones of the seed best at 30 points) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) chaotic points cannot be compared one by one, only their mean; (c) only the fixed point and the 2-cycle on the diagonal are checked against closed forms, and the other periodic orbits with different sequences only against the other way of writing the iteration; (d) **this material is not C1**: the exponent jumps where the period changes or the motion becomes chaotic, and the standard second-difference sweep found 1088, 1387, 1144, 2589, 1910 and 1731 records over the threshold for the six variants, so the test makes no C1 check and checks instead that the values at the points that are exact in binary are identical at (u − 7, v + 11); (e) I did not check the literature or compare any reference picture. **Record of adjustments**: (1) I first wrote a symmetry test ("the exponent is the same when the letters A and B and a and b are swapped", using the pixel (1 − v, 1 − u)), and in the probe 55 to 124 of 1000 or so points differed by more than 0.02 (the largest difference 1.0) — the logarithmic average of superstable orbits is very sensitive to the starting phase (A first or B first), so it is not a bug, and I **dropped that test**; (2) when I regenerated the test with my generator script I looked for the markers by string index and found the line where the script itself calls `indexOf` instead of the template content, which produced a script with a syntax error (nothing was written to the test file); to start again I also ran `git checkout -- tests/procedural-material.test.ts`, which removed the new entry that the generator had added to the kinds list earlier (the test file had no other uncommitted content at the time), and I then put it back by hand and rewrote the generator; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (7 tests including the kinds entry) with no threshold adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 99, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant (sequence and window); there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): a = a minimum + a range·(fu − margin)/(1 − 2·margin) and b = b maximum − b range·(fv − margin)/(1 − 2·margin); x = 0.5; 60 + 120 steps, each with r = a if the letter at that position is A and b otherwise, accumulating ln(max(|r(1 − 2x)|, 1e-12)) over the last 120 steps and then x ← r·x·(1 − x); λ = sum/120; ink = edge fade·clamp(−λ); color is `0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5)` (mask = smooth(clamp(ink/0.35))), height is `0.8·ink` (without grain, so the tone can be recovered), roughness is fixed at 0.36, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: 180 iterations per pixel, 120 of them with a logarithm; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('lyapunovfractal', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 298, 287 and 295 ms in three runs (only three measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one variant (the 6 chosen 5, 9, 3, 6, 11 and 6 times; seeds 8, 0, 15, 6, 16 and 1 for variants 0 to 5); against the other way of writing the iteration, of 2000 points of each variant the points with an exponent in the test below −0.05 number 1445, 1435, 1442, 938, 977 and 1266, of which 0, 1, 2, 1, 0 and 1 differ by more than 0.005, and the mean tone of the other points (sampler against test) is 0.0076 against 0.0075, 0.0084 against 0.0085, 0.0080 against 0.0080, 0.0059 against 0.0058, 0.0062 against 0.0062 and 0.0075 against 0.0075; on the diagonal the tones at r = 2.7 to 3.4 differ from the closed forms by 3.4e-6 at the most and at r = 3.6 to 3.95 the tone is 0; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 27.618%/8.505%/26.840%, color is 0.025840/0.025871/0.025969 to 0.874688/0.873268/0.874703 with a mean of 0.310401/0.193124/0.305872 and height is at most 0.8 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 27.630%/8.434%/26.859%/27.622%, color is 0.025256/0.025290/0.025234/0.025134 to 0.874888/0.874048/0.874847/0.874638 with a mean of 0.310442/0.193237/0.305772/0.310335 and AO is at least 0.6; between seeds 0 and 8 21.452% of the cells of the 256² grid differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (91.55, 71.93, 38.62), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0517 and the minimum z component is 252.

`standardmap` adds the standard map, bringing the current catalog from 1119 to 1120 kinds (1121 gallery choices including plain). Jade green on a dark green-black: the **finite-time Lyapunov exponent of the Chirikov standard map** p′ = p + K·sin x, x′ = x + p′ (on the torus of side 2π) — every pixel is an initial condition (x to the right, p upward, the middle of the tile being p = 0) followed for 40 steps with the product of the Jacobians of the steps, and the tone is the logarithm of the largest singular value of the product over the number of steps (dark in the islands of regular motion and bright in the chaotic sea, with a range that follows K), so one sees the island round the elliptic fixed point (π, 0) with its invariant curves, surrounded by winding bands of the chaotic sea, and the hyperbolic fixed point (0, 0) in a bright area. The picture fills the whole tile (x and p both repeat every 2π), so it is a **seamless periodic pattern**. The seed picks one of 6 kicks K: 0.6 (mostly regular motion), 0.9716 (from memory near the value at which the golden-mean invariant circle breaks up), 1.2, 1.6, 2.4 and 3.6 (mostly chaotic). It is a schematic picture: only a 40-step finite-time quantity, not the true Lyapunov exponent (so the regular regions also have a floor of about ln N/N), with no statistical meaning or convergence; unlike the existing `mapattractors` (orbit density of dissipative maps), `lorenzattractor` (one trajectory of a continuous flow), `logisticbifurcation` (the bifurcation diagram of a one-dimensional map) and `arnoldtongues` (mode locking of the circle map), it shows the distribution of chaotic and regular motion of a conservative (area-preserving) two-dimensional map over the plane of initial conditions. (The form of the standard map, the critical value K ≈ 0.9716 and the idea of the finite-time Lyapunov exponent are from my memory; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 40 steps, the 6 kicks, the tone range of each variant (lower limits 0.03, 0.03, 0.03, 0.05, 0.1 and 0.2, upper limits 0.2, 0.4, 0.45, 0.6, 0.8 and 1.1, set from the 99th percentile of the chaotic sea of each variant that the probe measured: 0.18, 0.38, 0.45, 0.58, 0.84 and 1.11), the jade-green-on-dark-green-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews: the first version (one range 0.08 to 0.6 for all variants, which saturated the whole picture for K = 3.6) at 12 seeds, then 12 seeds again after each variant got its own range (seeds 0 to 11, covering variants 0, 1, 2, 4 and 5), and finally seed 13 (variant 3, K = 1.6). The tests **read only the sampler output back** (the tone is recovered from the height), the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written: the sampler multiplies the two rows of the Jacobian, and the test follows the same steps with forward-mode automatic differentiation (dual numbers carrying the two partial derivatives) and finds the singular value from the eigenvalues of JᵀJ: (1) **agreement with the exponent from automatic differentiation**: for the first five variants (K up to 2.4) 800 points of each are compared one by one (all 3000 points were within 0.01 in the probe; at most 5 are allowed over here), and since the chaos of K = 3.6 amplifies a rounding error by e^(40λ) (a factor of about 1e17), only the mean tone over 2000 points is compared for it (0.5873 against 0.5875 in the probe, a difference of up to 1e-3 allowed) and at least 85% of the points to within 0.01 (about 91% in the probe); (2) **the hyperbolic and elliptic fixed points**: the origin (x = 0, p = 0) is a fixed point with the Jacobian [[1 + K, 1], [K, 1]] of trace above 2, so the exponent of 40 steps is about the logarithm of the larger eigenvalue (0.757 to 1.692, above the top of the range of every variant) and the tone is 1; the point x = π, p = 0 has the Jacobian [[1 − K, 1], [−K, 1]] with the trace 2 − K between −2 and 2, so the exponent is only 0.005 to 0.037, below the lower limit, and the tone is 0; the exponents come from matrix products written in the test and the pixels are exactly at (u, v) = (0, 1/2) and (1/2, 1/2), and all six variants agree; (3) **the reversal symmetry (x, p) → (−x, −p)**: the standard map is reversible under it, so the exponent is the same at a point and its image (the pixel (1 − u, 1 − v)); on 1000 points of each of the five variants of K up to 2.4 at least 99% agree to within 0.01 (all of them for the first four in the probe and all but one of 1500 for K = 2.4; K = 3.6 is left out, where 26% of the points differ because of rounding errors that the chaos amplifies). Mutation checks (done six times): changing the cos of the Jacobian to sin makes 6 of the 7 tests of that describe fail; multiplying the kick of the orbit by 0.9 (leaving the Jacobian) makes 4 fail; using the wrong element in the update of the second row of the Jacobian makes 5 fail; dropping the −4 of the singular value formula makes all 7 pass — **not caught**; removing the wrap of q onto the torus makes all 7 pass — **not caught** (it affects only rounding); removing the offset −π of the start of q makes 5 fail; the ones that failed were restored, and so were the three that were not caught (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (which variant's automatic-differentiation exponent matches the tones of the seed best at 10 points) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) K = 3.6 cannot be compared point by point because the chaos amplifies rounding errors, so only the mean and the fraction are compared; (c) the fixed-point check reads only the tones clipped to 0 and 1, not the exponents themselves; (d) **this material is not C1**: the exponent of 40 steps changes with the initial condition about e^(40λ) times faster, and the standard second-difference sweep found 499, 9469, 29784, 55449, 69818 and 76924 records over the threshold for the six variants, so the test makes no C1 check and checks instead that the values at the points (k/1024, j/1024), which are exact in binary, are identical at (u − 7, v + 11) (the rounding of u − 7 would be amplified by the chaos); (e) I did not check the literature or compare any reference picture. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the tone range changed from one shared range to one for each variant (see above); (2) when I wrote the generator I made the anchor in the kinds list too wide, so it failed after partly applying; I reset the working tree (`git checkout`, which held only this generator's changes at that time) and reran it with a corrected anchor; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry) with no threshold adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 98, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant (the kick K and the tone range of that variant); there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x = 2π·fract(u) and q = 2π·fract(v) − π, with the Jacobian (a, b; c, d) starting as the identity; for 40 steps, slope = K·cos x, the first row ← (1 + slope)·first row + second row and the second row ← slope·old first row + second row, then q += K·sin x and x += q, with x and q wrapped into [0, 2π) and [−π, π); the determinant is 1, so the squared largest singular value s satisfies s + 1/s = a² + b² + c² + d², s = (F + √(F² − 4))/2 and λ = ln s/(2·40); ink = clamp((λ − lower)/(upper − lower)); color is `0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5)` (mask = smooth(clamp(ink/0.35))), height is `0.8·ink` (without grain, so the tone can be recovered), roughness is fixed at 0.36, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: 40 steps per pixel, each with one sin, one cos and about 12 multiply-adds; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('standardmap', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 416, 416 and 418 ms in three runs (only three measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one variant (the 6 chosen 3, 6, 5, 10, 7 and 9 times; seeds 10, 4, 6, 13, 11 and 0 for variants 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 74.918%/74.994%/23.155%, color is 0.025556/0.025278/0.025917 to 0.873164/0.873889/0.871897 with a mean of 0.546854/0.546915/0.304260 and height is at most 0.8 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 75.039%/75.039%/23.248%/75.036%, color is 0.025318/0.025093/0.025337/0.025397 to 0.874349/0.874394/0.874471/0.874573 with a mean of 0.546819/0.546879/0.304635/0.546878 and AO is at least 0.6; between seeds 0 and 4 69.682% of the cells of the 256² grid differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (83.84, 146.70, 115.72), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0340 and the minimum z component is 253; against automatic differentiation the first five variants agree at all 3000 points to within 0.01 (differences of the mean tone 2.8e-16, 2.3e-15, 2.0e-14, 2.1e-10 and 3.2e-7) and K = 3.6 has 269 points (9.0%) over 0.01 and a mean difference of −1.7e-4; the exponents of the 40 steps at the hyperbolic fixed point are 0.75714, 0.94962, 1.04705, 1.19340, 1.42692 and 1.69200 (the logarithm of the larger eigenvalue is 0.75643, 0.94961, 1.04697, 1.19291, 1.42542 and 1.68924, the difference being the 1/N correction) and at the elliptic one 0.00488, 0.00532, 0.01099, 0.01937, 0.02830 and 0.03731.

`diffractioncatastrophes` adds the diffraction catastrophes, bringing the current catalog from 1118 to 1119 kinds (1120 gallery choices including plain). Pale ice blue on a dark navy: the intensity |P(x, y)|² on the (x, y) parameter plane of the **diffraction integral of a catastrophe**, P = ∫ exp(i (t^(2d) + a·t⁴ + x·t² + y·t)) dt — d = 2 is the **Pearcey integral of the cusp catastrophe** (a plays no part): two fold caustics y = ±(4|x|/3)·√(|x|/6) meet in the cusp at x = 0, with a lattice of interference spots inside them and a quick decay outside; d = 3 is a slice of the **butterfly catastrophe** for a fixed a (a more complicated lattice of spots). Each pixel integrates along the ray t = s·e^{iπ/(8d)} in the complex plane (on which the integrand falls off; some 70 to 85 nodes) by the trapezoid rule, and the tone of the intensity is 1 − exp(−intensity/3). The seed picks one of 6 variants: three windows of the Pearcey integral (centres x = −3, −2 and −4.5, half widths 6, 3.2 and 4.5) and three of the butterfly (a = −2, −1 and −3). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04) and is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: the scalar interference integral on one two-dimensional slice of the parameters, with no physical optical scale or source; unlike the existing materials that draw caustics as envelopes of rays (the envelope of `ellipsebilliard`, `stringart` and so on), the visual approximation `poolcaustics`, `lensarray`, `diffractionpatterns` (far-field Fraunhofer diffraction) and `talbotcarpet` (self-imaging of a grating), it draws the **wave interference fringes** near a caustic. (The Pearcey integral, the formula of the fold lines and the value 2Γ(5/4)·e^{iπ/8} at the origin are from my memory and hand calculation, the last also compared with a numerical integral in a prototype; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 6 windows and the values of a of the butterfly (−2, −1 and −3, chosen by eye), the angle and the number of nodes of the integration ray, the tone 1 − exp(−intensity/3) (the first version used 1, which left the bright lobes a flat plateau; with 3 there are gradations), the ice-blue-on-dark-navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews in three rounds: 12 seeds (0 to 11, with the tone reference 1 and the old ray angle, covering variants 0, 1, 3, 4 and 5), then 6 seeds (0, 1, 2, 6, 8 and 9) after the reference was changed to 3, and finally seed 21 (variant 2, which I had not seen before); after the ray angle was halved I did not look again (the values differ only at the 1e-3 level). The tests **read only the sampler output back** (the intensity is recovered from the height), the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written: the sampler integrates along a ray in the complex plane and the test integrates along the real axis from −T to T by Simpson's rule (T = 5 for the Pearcey integral and 4 for the butterfly, with 20,000 to 80,000 nodes): (1) **agreement with the real-axis integral**: on 80 points of each variant (inside the plot, on a golden-ratio sequence) the intensities differ by at most 0.04 for the Pearcey variants (0.0209, 0.0206 and 0.0199 at the most in the probe on 150 points, mainly the error of cutting the real axis at T = 5, some 0.006 at the larger intensities) and by at most 0.005 for the butterfly variants (0.0016, 0.0015 and 0.0014 in the probe); (2) **mirror symmetry in y and the value at the origin**: |P(x, −y)| = |P(x, y)| (1.1e-14 at the most on 100 points in the probe), and at the origin the Pearcey integral is ∫exp(it⁴)dt = 2Γ(5/4)·e^{iπ/8}, so the intensity is (2Γ(5/4))² = 3.28626 (the same to the 5 digits printed by the probe), for the two variants whose plot contains the origin; (3) **the outermost fringe is near the fold caustic**: going down along y from the edge of the plot, the outermost local maximum of the intensity (over 0.15) lies within −0.2 and 0.55 of y = (4|x|/3)·√(|x|/6) (−0.05 for x = −3 and +0.40 for x = −4 in the probe; at x = −4 it is a little beyond the caustic, which I did not explain with theory, I only measured it and made the bound loose). Mutation checks (done five times): changing the phase cos(2θ) of the t² term to cos(θ) makes 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the real-axis one, the seed difference and the maps) **but the caustic test still passes**; multiplying the y term by 0.9 makes 5 fail (including the caustic one); changing the weight of the k = 0 node of the trapezoid rule to 2 makes 5 fail (including the mirror and origin one); multiplying the quartic coefficient of the butterfly by 0.5 makes 4 fail (it affects only the butterfly variants, so the mirror/origin and caustic tests pass); replacing the tone curve by I/(1 + I) makes 5 fail; all five were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (which variant's real-axis integral matches the intensities of the seed best at 6 points) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the real-axis integral is cut off at T, so it has an error of about 0.006 itself; (c) the butterfly variants have no independent closed-form check except the real-axis integral, and the caustic check is for the Pearcey integral only; (d) the 6 variants look alike (windows and butterfly parameters of one kind of lattice of spots); (e) I did not check the literature or compare any reference picture; (f) it is not a periodic pattern. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version integrated along the ray with the full angle π/(4d), and the trapezoid step 0.1 gave 53.9 at (−9, 6) where the real-axis integral is 1.383, so the step is now 0.05 (Pearcey) and 0.04 (butterfly); (2) the standard C1 sweep failed for 3 of the 6 variants (3686, 3343 and 1044 violation records, all in the AO channel): the cause is not a discontinuity but rounding noise — at the full angle the terms grow to about 1e4 to 1e6 and cancel in the sum, so the second difference at the step 1e-10 has noise of about 5 (Pearcey); I compared ray angles, and half the angle lowers the noise to about 1e-3 (about 1e-4 for the butterfly) at the same accuracy, so it is now π/(8d) (about 12% more nodes, a little more time), after which the 6 variants have 0 violation records; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry) with no threshold adjusted; (4) I first meant to test that the global maximum of the intensity is near the caustic, and the probe showed that the spots further inside are larger, so the test was changed to the outermost local maximum.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 97, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant; for every node s = k·step it precomputes the phase of t² (s²cos2θ and s²sin2θ) and of the fixed terms (s^(2d), and a·s⁴ for the butterfly, at t = s·e^{iθ} with θ = π/(8d)); there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin) and y = half width·(0.5 − fv)/(0.5 − margin); for every node it adds exp(−Im(fixed + x·t²))·e^{i·Re(fixed + x·t²)} times cos(y·t) (t = s·e^{iθ}, the cosine taken of a complex argument, the even parts of the nodes ±s combined, with weight 1 for k = 0 and 2 for the others), and finally multiplies by e^{iθ}·step; the intensity is |P|², ink = edge fade·(1 − exp(−intensity/3)); color is `0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5)` (mask = smooth(clamp(ink/0.35))), height is `0.8·ink` (without grain, so the intensity can be recovered), roughness is fixed at 0.34, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: about 76 nodes (Pearcey) or 85 nodes (butterfly) per pixel, each with about 6 trigonometric/exponential calls; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('diffractioncatastrophes', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 556, 579 and 542 ms in three runs (before the ray angle was changed I measured about 0.38 s twice, and the first run after the change gave 543 ms; only a few measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one variant (the 6 chosen 7, 5, 4, 7, 7 and 10 times; seeds 6, 1, 21, 3, 2 and 0 for variants 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 9.541%/34.094%/8.845%, color is 0.026332/0.025458/0.026118 to 0.825278/0.798560/0.796306 with a mean of 0.251398/0.368729/0.245626 and height is at most 0.749043/0.720931/0.720060 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 9.553%/34.129%/8.844%/13.089%, color is 0.025417/0.025339/0.025376/0.025281 to 0.827210/0.800425/0.797116/0.763747 with a mean of 0.251416/0.368765/0.245647/0.277295, height is at most 0.749086/0.720950/0.720136/0.680234 relief and AO is at least 0.6; between seeds 0 and 2 18.698% of the cells of the 256² grid differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (43.16, 75.28, 92.39), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.00188 and the minimum z component is 255; the C1 sweep has 0 violation records for the 6 variants; the largest mirror disagreement is 1.1e-14 and the intensity at the origin is 3.28626.

`talbotcarpet` adds the Talbot carpet, bringing the current catalog from 1117 to 1118 kinds (1119 gallery choices including plain). Amber gold on a dark brown-black: the intensity behind a grating of period 1 in the near (Fresnel) field — the field behind the grating is the sum over the harmonics n of c_n·exp(2πi·n·x)·exp(−2πi·n²·z) (x in periods of the grating, z in Talbot lengths 2d²/λ going down), the picture shows the intensity |field|² (the tone 1 − exp(−intensity), the intensity being 1 in an open slit); because the phase 2πn²z of every harmonic is a multiple of 2π at z = 1, the pattern **repeats exactly every Talbot length** (the whole tile is exactly one Talbot length high and 3 periods of the grating wide, so it is a seamless periodic pattern along both x and z, and at z = 1/2 it is the picture at z = 0 shifted by half a period). The seed picks one of 6 gratings: **amplitude gratings** of the open fractions 0.5, 0.25, 0.15 and 0.35 (1 transmitted in the slits, 0 between them) and **π-phase gratings** of the open fractions 0.5 and 0.25 (+1 in the slits, −1 between them, with a uniform intensity at z = 0). It is a schematic picture: paraxial scalar theory and an ideal infinitely thin grating, with only 24 harmonics (so there is a Gibbs ripple at the edges near z = 0 and the total power is short by 0.0040 to 0.0042 for amplitude gratings or 0.0169 for phase gratings), no dispersion and no finite grating size; unlike the existing `diffractionpatterns` (far-field Fraunhofer diffraction), `fourierseries` (partial-sum curves of Fourier series), `moire` and `zoneplate`, it draws the self-imaging "carpet" of the near-field intensity behind a grating against the distance. (The Talbot length 2d²/λ and the paraxial propagation formula are from my memory and hand calculation; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 3 periods across, the 24 harmonics, the 6 open fractions, the tone 1 − exp(−intensity), the amber-gold-on-dark-brown-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; there is no grain. I looked at the previews of 12 seeds (0 to 11, with the salt of that time, covering all 6 gratings). The tests **read only the sampler output back** (the intensity is recovered from the height): (1) **conservation of the total power**: the intensity averaged over one period equals the power that the grating transmits (the open fraction for an amplitude grating and 1 for a phase grating), whatever the depth z; what is missing is the power of the harmonics above 24 (probe: 0.4958, 0.2458, 0.1460 and 0.3459 for the amplitude gratings of the open fractions 0.5, 0.25, 0.15 and 0.35 and 0.9831 for the phase gratings, the same to 4 digits at the four depths z = 0.07, 0.31, 0.5 and 0.77; 128 samples per period are exact for these harmonics); (2) **half and a quarter of a Talbot length**: the intensity at z = 1/2 is that at z = 0 shifted by half a period (the factor (−1)ⁿ), and at z = 1/4 the even harmonics are unchanged and the odd ones are multiplied by −i, so the intensity is the same at x and x + 1/2; both agree to 1e-9 in intensity and in colour for all 6 gratings on 200 values of x (7.3e-14 at the most in the probe); (3) **z = 0 is the grating itself**: for an amplitude grating about 1 in the middle of a slit (0.937 to 1.010 in the probe, the Gibbs ripple of 24 harmonics) and under 0.001 in the middle of the gap between slits, for a phase grating about 1 everywhere (0.877 to 0.978); (4) **agreement with the Fresnel integral of the slits (space domain)**, for the amplitude gratings only: the sampler sums 24 harmonics (the frequency domain) and the test adds up the Fresnel integrals of 121 slits (the space domain, Simpson's rule); they differ by the harmonics above 24 and by the slits beyond 60 periods, by at most 0.082, 0.113, 0.132 and 0.079 in the probe (open fractions 0.5, 0.25, 0.15 and 0.35, on z = 0.1, 0.3, 0.5, 0.7, 0.9 and eight values of x), and the bound 0.16 is loose, but a wrong Talbot length or a wrong sign of the phase gives differences of order 1. The phase gratings are not compared with the Fresnel integral: I measured the difference between 24 and 200 harmonics on a phase grating at up to about 0.59 (near z = 0.5, open fraction 0.25) and between 60 slits and 200 harmonics at up to about 0.26, both too large. Mutation checks (done five times): changing the phase from 2πn²z to 2πnz makes 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the Fresnel one, the seed difference and the maps) **but the half and quarter Talbot test still passes** (it needs only the parity structure, not n²); dropping the factor 2 of c_n makes 6 fail; multiplying the sin(πnf) of c_n by 1.1 makes 5 fail; replacing the tone curve 1 − exp(−I) by I/(1 + I) makes 6 fail; shifting x by 0.01 makes only 2 fail (the Fresnel one and the seed difference; the total power and the half/quarter tests are unchanged by it, and did not catch it); all five were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the grating for each seed was found with a probe (which of the six series models matches the intensities best; the model is the same series formula as the sampler, so this is **not an independent oracle**, and I did not print the residual); (b) only 24 harmonics, so there is a Gibbs ripple where z is small, which is an approximation and not a bug; (c) the Fresnel comparison is loose and does not include the phase gratings; (d) the n² of the phase is not pinned by the total power and the half/quarter tests alone; (e) there is no grain and only 6 different pictures, so two seeds that pick the same grating give exactly the same tile (the generic "adjacent seeds differ" test uses seeds 123 and 124, and with the first salt 0x5a3d both picked the same grating and the test failed, so the salt is now 0x5a3e, which makes them pick different gratings); (f) I did not check the literature or compare any reference picture. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the salt adjustment above (changing the salt only swaps neighbouring seeds, and the distribution of the counts is unchanged); (2) I first measured the difference between the space-domain Fresnel integral and the 24-harmonic series and found that it came mainly from the truncation to 24 harmonics and to the number of slits (at most 0.28 to 1.06 with M = 10 and 0.08 to 0.29 with M = 25), which is why the check is made only for amplitude gratings and with a loose bound; (3) after the salt change the new tests all passed (9 tests including the kinds entry) the first full run, with no threshold adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 96, seed ^ salt)` picks the grating (fraction, amplitude or phase); the coefficients are c₀ = a·f + b and cₙ = a·sin(πnf)/(πn) (a = 1, b = 0 for amplitude gratings and a = 2, b = −1 for phase gratings). There is no grain cache. At sampling time (per pixel): x = 3·fract(u) and z = fract(v); for n = 1…24 it accumulates amplitude = 2cₙ·cos(2πn·x), adds amplitude·cos(2πn²z) to the real part of the field and subtracts amplitude·sin(2πn²z) from its imaginary part; the intensity is real² + imaginary²; ink = 1 − exp(−intensity); color is `0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·mask + 0.72·ink` (mask = smooth(clamp(ink/0.35))), height is `0.8·ink`, roughness is fixed at 0.36, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0007 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: about 72 trigonometric calls per pixel; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('talbotcarpet', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 182, 203 and 198 ms in three runs (only three measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one grating (the 6 chosen 9, 10, 2, 9, 6 and 4 times; seeds 4, 6, 0, 1, 3 and 5 for gratings 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 0.696%/12.195%/27.759%, color is 0.040000 to 0.707042/0.760419/0.776275 with a mean of 0.165663/0.291535/0.362026 and height is at most 0.630046/0.689355/0.706973 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 0.638%/12.378%/27.426%/27.426%, color is at most 0.734293/0.760439/0.790928/0.790928 with a mean of 0.165680/0.291569/0.361886/0.361886, height is at most 0.660326/0.689377/0.723254/0.723254 relief and AO is at least 0.6; between seeds 0 and 2 11.938% of the cells of the 256² grid differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (105.04, 77.48, 41.08), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.00335 and the minimum z component is 255; the C1 sweep has 0 violation records for the 6 gratings (it is an analytic sum of harmonics, with no discontinuity); the largest disagreement of the half and quarter Talbot shifts is 7.3e-14 (in intensity). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`newtonfractal` adds the Newton fractal, bringing the current catalog from 1116 to 1117 kinds (1118 gallery choices including plain). Rose pink on a dark indigo-black: the **basins of attraction of the roots of a polynomial under Newton's (or Halley's) iteration** — every pixel is a point z₀ of the complex plane that is iterated until |f(z)| is below a tolerance, the root that it reaches decides the tone (the roots are ordered by argument, one tone from dark to light each), and the number of iterations (made continuous by the doubling of the digits of the residual) decides the shading, so it is bright near the roots and dark on the boundaries between basins, which are fractal petals; the height depends only on the number of iterations (high cores, low boundaries); a point that has reached no root in 64 steps (for instance near the attracting cycle 0, 1 of z³ − 2z + 2) is dark and low. The seed picks one of 6 variants: z³ − 1, z⁴ − 1, z⁵ − 1 (all by Newton's method), z³ − 2z + 2 (Newton, with the attracting cycle 0 → 1 → 0, in a larger window), Halley's method on z³ − 1 (cubic convergence, smoother boundaries), and Newton's method zoomed in on a small piece of the boundary of z⁵ − 1 (centre 0.6 + 0.5i, half width 0.4). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04) and is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture and not a theoretically complete fractal (the cut-off at 64 steps makes slowly converging boundary points dark); unlike the existing escape-time fractals (`mandelbrottiles`, `juliatiles` and the escape fractals family with the Burning Ship, tricorn and multibrot, which are mosaics of escape times of z ↦ z² + c type maps), it draws the basins of the roots and not an escape set. (The iteration formulas of Newton's and Halley's methods and the 0 ↔ 1 cycle of z³ − 2z + 2 are from my memory and hand calculation; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 variants, the half widths of the windows (1.5, 1.5, 1.5, 2.4, 1.5, 0.4) and the centre of the zoomed one, the 64 steps, the tolerances (1e-6 for Newton and 1e-4 for Halley), the shading decay 7 and floor 0.06, the tone range 0.22 to 1, the rose-pink-on-dark-indigo-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; the position of the zoomed window was picked by drawing a few candidate windows with a discarded throwaway script (not in the repository) and has no theoretical basis. I looked at the previews in three rounds: the first (tolerance 1e-9, decay 12, floor 0.18, tones 0.3 to 0.95, and the sixth variant being Halley's method on z⁴ − 1) was grey overall and had clear concentric rings inside the basins; the cause of the rings was that with the tolerance 1e-9 the next residual falls below the rounding noise of double precision, which spoils the estimate of the digits of the residual that makes the iteration count continuous (a small script of mine printed it along one line: ν differs by about 0.2 at a step of the count, and 0.014 to 0.042 at the first four steps on the same line with the tolerance 1e-6, the later steps falling where ν itself changes quickly within the 0.002 sampling step of that line, so they say nothing); so the tolerance is now 1e-6 for Newton and 1e-4 for Halley (whose residual is cubed), the contrast was raised (decay 12→7, floor 0.18→0.06, tones 0.3 to 0.95→0.22 to 1) and the sixth variant was changed from Halley on z⁴ − 1 to the zoomed z⁵ − 1; the second round (after the tolerance and contrast adjustments) looked at 12 seeds (0 to 11) and the third, after the sixth variant was changed to the zoomed z⁵ − 1, at 16 seeds (0 to 15, covering all 6 variants) of the final version, where the tones are clearer and the rings are gone. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written: the sampler iterates general polynomials by Horner's rule (with f′ and f″) and finds the roots by the Durand–Kerner method, and the test uses rational maps in closed form (powers in polar form; for Halley, z((n−1)zⁿ+(n+1))/((n+1)zⁿ+(n−1)), which I simplified by hand from the general formula) and roots in closed form (the roots of unity, and Cardano's formula for z³ − 2z + 2): (1) **point by point**: on 1000 points of each variant (a golden-ratio sequence inside the plot) the test iterates to get the root, the count and the residual and predicts the height (0.8 × the shade) and the colour (from the preset formula, using the predicted tone × shade): at least 995 points have the height within 0.03 and the colour within 0.02 (in the probe all 2000 points of every variant matched, with the largest differences 0.020 and 0.015, the grain; the z⁵ − 1, z³ − 2z + 2 and zoomed variants have 6, 18 and 7 points that reach no root in 64 steps, and the prediction and the readback agree on them; the tone formula is copied from the preset, so what is independent is the iteration, the basin and the count); (2) **the tones of the basins follow the arguments of the roots**: the colour at 1.01 times each root rises (probe: 0.228/0.488/0.722; 0.207/0.411/0.563/0.708; 0.219/0.376/0.485/0.601/0.698; 0.216/0.484/0.703; 0.244/0.548/0.795), which also tests that the root at −1 of z⁴ − 1 is counted as argument π; (3) **the discs round the cycle have no root**: Newton's map sends 0 to 1 and 1 to 0 for z³ − 2z + 2 and its derivative vanishes at 0 (by hand), so on circles of radius 0.08 round 0 and 0.005 round 1 the height is only the grain (<0.025; the probe's largest was 0.0177, and the discs reach about 0.1 round 0 and 0.01 round 1); (4) **rotation and mirror symmetry**: z ↦ z·e^{2πi/n} and z ↦ z̄ do not change the number of iterations, so for the rotations of z³ − 1, z⁴ − 1, z⁵ − 1 and the Halley variant and the mirror image of all five full-window variants the heights at 1500 points differ by less than 0.025 (0.0166 to 0.0184 in the probe).
