Mutation checks (done four times): dropping the factor 2 from the real part of the Halley numerator makes 2 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the point-by-point one and the symmetry one); reversing the comparator of the sort makes 3 fail (point by point, the tone order and the seed difference); reversing the sign of the imaginary update of Newton's step makes 6 fail; changing the singularity guard `squared < 1e-30` to `< 0` makes all 8 pass — **not caught** (where f′ = 0 at the origin the division gives NaN, which the later `!(|z| < 1e6)` turns into "did not converge", so the guard only saves a step with the same result); the first three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the variant for each seed was found with a probe (which closed-form model matches the height; every one of 40 seeds matched at all of 150 points) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the tone and shading formulas are copied from the preset and not independently checked; (c) **this material is not C1**: the boundaries between basins are discontinuities at every scale, and the standard second-difference sweep found 26,546 to 65,302 records over the threshold for each of the six variants, so the test makes no C1 check and checks instead that the values at the origin and at every root are finite and in [0, 1] and that signed UV shifts agree to 1e-6 — iteration amplifies the rounding in u − 7, and the probe found up to 4.23e-8 on these 4096 points (2.64e-14 to 6.41e-9 for the other five variants), not the 5e-10 of the smooth presets; (d) the 64-step cut-off, AO, roughness and the edge fade are not tested; (e) I did not check the literature or compare any reference picture. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the adjustments of tolerance and contrast above; (2) the test first reused the UV tolerance 5e-10 and failed (4.2e-8), and I had left a meaningless sentence in a test comment ("(the drift was 0 in the probe at this tolerance? see ACCEPTANCE)"), which was corrected to the real numbers before the commit; (3) my first probe compared the height with the prediction without dividing by the relief, so nothing matched, and the match above came only after that was fixed.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 95, seed ^ salt)` picks the variant; the roots are found by Durand–Kerner (200 rounds, monic polynomials) and sorted by argument (the root at −1 counted as π), the tone of each root being 0.22 + 0.78·rank/(n − 1); there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): z₀ = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5, 0.5 − fv)/(0.5 − margin); at most 64 steps: f, f′ and f″ by Horner's rule, stopping when |f|² < tolerance²; Newton's step is z ← z − f/f′ and Halley's z ← z − 2ff′/(2f′² − ff″); if f′ is too small 1e-6 is added to the real part and the iteration goes on; it gives up if |z| passes 1e6. When a root is reached the nearest root decides the tone, the continuous count is ν = count + log(ln tolerance / ln|f|)/ln(order of convergence), the shade is 0.06 + 0.94·exp(−ν/7) and ink = edge fade·tone·shade; color is `0.04 + (0.14 − 0.04)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(grain − 0.5)` (mask = smooth(clamp(ink/0.35))), height is `0.8·edge fade·shade + 0.02·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.42, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0009 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: up to 64 iterations per pixel, each with one Horner pass; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('newtonfractal', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 271 ms and 260 ms in two runs (`vortexstreet` measured at the same time took 170 and 163 ms, slower than the 131 ms measured earlier, so the machine's timing is noisy; only two measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one variant (the 6 chosen 6, 10, 11, 5, 4 and 4 times; seeds 1, 2, 0, 13, 3 and 6 for variants 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 6.064%/14.804%/5.995%, color is 0.025510–0.025877 to 0.718464–0.730576 with a mean of 0.225561/0.267354/0.225603 and height is at most 0.668106/0.667618/0.660129 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 6.069%/14.850%/6.020%/6.186%, color is 0.025158–0.025371 to 0.718026–0.746608 with a mean of 0.225522/0.267340/0.225565/0.225649, height is at most 0.697595/0.687822/0.687155/0.690209 relief and AO is at least 0.6; between seeds 0 and 2 12.099% of the cells of the 256² grid differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (68.38, 44.55, 69.49), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0100 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews: 12 seeds (0 to 11) in the first round, 12 seeds again after the tolerance and contrast adjustments, and 16 seeds (0 to 15) of the final version after the sixth variant was changed. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`vortexstreet` adds the vortex street, bringing the current catalog from 1115 to 1116 kinds (1117 gallery choices including plain). Pale green on a dark green-black: the streamlines of **two staggered rows of point vortices** (the von Kármán vortex street) — the upper row has circulation +1 at (n, h/2) and the lower row −1 at (n + ½, −h/2) (period a = 1, the rows h = ratio·a apart); the stream function of an infinite row of vortices has the closed form −(Γ/4π)·ln((cosh 2π(y − y₀) − cos 2π(x − x₀))/2); the street itself moves at the speed U = tanh(πh)/2 (a = 1, Γ = 1), and the picture shows the streamlines ψ − U y in the **frame that moves with the street** (ψ at the multiples of 0.03 with |ψ − U y| ≤ 1, fading out near the vortex cores): round every vortex there are cat's-eye rings, far away straight lines, and the vortices are marked with bright dots; the seed picks one of 6 ratios h/a of the rows: 0.281 (the stable von Kármán street), 0.15, 0.2, 0.4, 0.55 and 0.7. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern (although the street is periodic along x, the plot is about 2.4 periods wide). It is a schematic picture: point vortices in an ideal fluid, with no viscosity, no creation and shedding of vortices, no stability analysis of the street and no real flow; unlike the other flow materials (for example the flow round a cylinder with circulation of cylinderflow) it draws the streamlines of two staggered rows of point vortices. (The closed form of the stream function, the speed U of the street and the stable ratio 0.281 are from my memory, and were compared in a prototype with a direct sum and with a numerically found velocity; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 ratios, the half width 1.2 of the plot (centred at x = 0.25), the streamline step 0.03 and limit 1 (fading over 0.2), the line half width 0.003 (of the tile), the tones (0.7 for the streamlines and 1 for the vortex dots), the dot radius 0.04, the pale-green-on-dark-green-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I viewed the previews of seeds 0 to 5 first (which turned out to cover only the ratios 0.15, 0.2, 0.281 and 0.55, rendered before the floor under the denominators was added, which affects only a pixel exactly on a vortex centre) and then those of seeds 13 and 6 (0.4 and 0.7). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype (Bun, not in the repository): the closed form and the direct sum of 801 vortices differ by at most 2.3e-4, 1.5e-4, 3.3e-4 and 5.9e-4 (h = 0.281, 0.15, 0.4 and 0.7; caused by the truncation of the sum), and the speed U of the street, found numerically as the velocity that the other vortices induce on one vortex, differs from tanh(πh)/2 by under 1.1e-4 (for h = 0.281, 0.35386 against 0.35391). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler uses the closed form in cosh and cos, and the test sums the vortices directly and finds U numerically): (1) **the streamlines where a direct sum puts them**: the test sums 801 vortices and finds ψ − U y, scans eleven horizontal lines (x from −0.95 to 1.45) for where it crosses a multiple of 0.03 (up to 0.7; by linear interpolation and one secant step), and at those points in the plot where the gradient is over 0.15 (the truncation of the sum causes an error of up to 6e-4) the colour is above 0.4 (0.529 at the lowest in the probe; 137 to 205 points per variant); (2) **periodic along x and the glide symmetry of the street**: the street repeats every a = 1, and the second row is the first one shifted by a/2 along x, mirrored in y and with the circulation reversed, so the streamlines (the same step, positive and negative) map onto each other under (x, y) → (x + ½, −y): on a 70 by 70 grid the colours at the points and their images differ by under 0.05 (0.029 at the most in the probe, the grain; 3850 points per variant); (3) **the vortices marked at h/2 above and below the axis**: the colour at the four vortices (n from −1 to 1) is above 0.8 (0.850 at the lowest in the probe). Mutation checks (done three times): multiplying the speed U of the street by 1.1 makes 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the streamlines, the seed difference and the maps); changing the x offset of the lower row from a/2 to 0.4 makes 4 fail (including the streamlines and the periodic and glide test); multiplying only the lower position of the dots by 1.1 (leaving the stream function) makes 2 fail (the glide symmetry and the vortex positions); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the ratio for each seed was found with a probe (the distance between the bright dots of the two rows, within 0.001 of the preset ratio) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the direct sum has a truncation error of up to 6e-4, so points where the gradient is under 0.15 are not checked; (c) the streamlines with |ψ − U y| above 0.7 (near the vortex cores) are not checked; (d) the stable ratio 0.281 itself is not tested (it is only one of the 6 ratios); (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) when the probe happened to sample the centre of a vortex exactly for one ratio it got NaN (a denominator of exactly 0), so the sampler now puts a floor of 1e-300 under the two denominators (only a pixel that falls exactly on a vortex centre is affected); (2) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry) and no threshold was adjusted; (3) the standard C1 sweep passed the first time (0 violation records).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 93, seed ^ salt)` picks a ratio h; U = tanh(πh)/2; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x = 0.25 + 1.2·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin), y = 1.2·(0.5 − fv)/(0.5 − margin); the denominators of the two rows are D₁ = cosh(2π(y − h/2)) − cos(2πx) and D₂ = cosh(2π(y + h/2)) − cos(2π(x − ½)) (with a floor of 1e-300); ψ′ = (−ln D₁ + ln D₂)/(4π) − U y; the gradient ∇ψ′ is ((−2π sin(2πx)/D₁ + 2π sin(2π(x − ½))/D₂)/(4π), (−2π sinh(2π(y − h/2))/D₁ + 2π sinh(2π(y + h/2))/D₂)/(4π) − U) (x and y components); the distance to the nearest multiple of 0.03 is about the difference divided by |∇ψ′| (in tile units), the kernel is clamp(1 − (distance/0.003)²)², times the fade smooth((1 − |ψ′|)/0.2) and the tone 0.7; the maximum with the vortex dots (5 columns × two rows, radius 0.04) clamp(1 − (distance/radius)²)² is taken; the edge fade is applied and color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: about two cosh/cos, two log and two sinh calls and the distances to 10 dots per pixel; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('vortexstreet', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 131 ms in both of the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one ratio (the 6 chosen 7, 9, 7, 7, 5 and 5 times; seeds 2, 0, 1, 13, 3 and 6 for the ratios 0.281, 0.15, 0.2, 0.4, 0.55 and 0.7; the distance between the two rows of bright dots is within 0.0010 of the ratio); the speed U of the street is 0.3539, 0.2196, 0.2784, 0.4250, 0.4693 and 0.4877; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 6.888%/7.834%/7.838%, color is 0.025481–0.025558 to 0.851655–0.866401 with a mean of 0.098984/0.103886/0.103817, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.832092–0.861000 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 7.012%/7.334%/7.336%/8.360%, color is 0.025108–0.025206 to 0.861465–0.865451 with a mean of 0.099015/0.103630/0.103561/0.112320, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.847428–0.857713 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 12.943% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (24.42, 44.62, 31.99), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0260 and the minimum z component is 253; the C1 sweep has 0 violation records for the 6 variants; the largest difference for the period and glide is 0.029 and the lowest colour at a vortex dot is 0.850. I viewed the previews of seeds 0 to 5 first (which turned out to cover only the ratios 0.15, 0.2, 0.281 and 0.55, rendered before the floor under the denominators was added, which affects only a pixel exactly on a vortex centre) and then those of seeds 13 and 6 (0.4 and 0.7). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hydrogenorbitals` adds hydrogen orbitals, bringing the current catalog from 1114 to 1115 kinds (1116 gallery choices including plain). Ember orange on a dark brown-black: the probability density |ψ|² of the electron of a hydrogen atom in a **plane through the nucleus** (y = 0, z up) — the cut at φ = 0 of the real orbital ψ = R(n, l; r)·P_l^m(cos θ)·cos(mφ), with R(n, l; r) ∝ ρ^l e^{−ρ/2} L^{2l+1}_{n−l−1}(ρ) (ρ = 2r/n in Bohr radii, L being the generalised Laguerre polynomial); the density over its greatest value in the plot is drawn to the power 0.4, so the **nodes are dark lines**: n − l − 1 **radial nodes** (spheres round the nucleus, circles in this plane) and l − m **angular nodes** (cones about the z axis, straight lines through the nucleus in the plane), the z axis itself being a node as well when m > 0; the seed picks one of 6 orbitals: 2s, 3p, 3d, 4p, 4d (m = 1) and 4f. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only |ψ|² in one plane, with no phase (sign), spin or relativistic correction, and no measurement of any kind; unlike the other pattern materials (for example sphericalharmonics, which has only the angular part on a sphere, and zernikemodes) it draws the radial and angular nodes of the orbitals of the hydrogen atom. (The forms of the radial function and the associated Legendre function are from my memory and the nodes were checked in a prototype: 2s at 2.001, 3s at 1.902 and 7.099, 3p at 6.000, 4p at 5.528 and 14.473 and 4d at 12.001 Bohr radii; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 orbitals and the half widths of the plot (13, 26, 26, 45, 45 and 45 Bohr radii), the power 0.4 of the density, the ember-orange-on-dark-brown-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 orbitals once (of the final version). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype (Bun, not in the repository) to check: the recurrence of the associated Legendre function and the m-th derivative of the explicit sum of the Legendre polynomial differ by at most 1.8e-15; the radial function changes sign n − l − 1 times, at 2.001 for 2s, 1.902 and 7.099 for 3s, 6.000 for 3p, 5.528 and 14.473 for 4p and 12.001 Bohr radii for 4d (matching the 2, 1.9 and 7.1, 6 and 12 that I remember). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler sums the explicit series of the Laguerre polynomial and uses the recurrence in l for the Legendre function; the test uses the three-term recurrence for the Laguerre polynomial and the derivative of the Legendre polynomial): (1) **dark rings on the radial nodes**: along the ray at the polar angle where the angular function is the largest (found by a scan; near the z axis for m = 0) the radial function changes sign n − l − 1 times, and at each node (within 0.9 of the half width) the colour is under 0.08 (0.05 at the highest in the probe, the grain) and 4 pixels to either side it is at least 0.04 higher (0.068 at the lowest in the probe); 3d and 4f have no radial node; (2) **dark cones and axis on the angular nodes**: on the circle (3600 steps) at the radius where the radial function is largest, the number of local minima of the colour under 0.3 equals the zeros of P_l^m(cos θ) (one on each side of the plane) plus, for m > 0, the two points on the z axis (0, 2, 4, 2, 4 and 6 for the six orbitals), and they are within 0.01 rad of the predicted angles (0.0011 at the worst in the probe); (3) **symmetry under x → −x and z → −z**: the density depends on cos²(mφ) (1 in the plane) and on P_l^m(cos θ)², which is even in cos θ, so it is unchanged, and the colours differ by under 0.05 (0.0292 at the most in the probe, the grain; 3600 points per variant). Mutation checks (done three times): removing the sign (−1)ⁱ from the Laguerre coefficients makes 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the radial nodes, the seed difference and the maps); changing the (l + m − 1) of the Legendre recurrence to (l + m) makes only the angular-node test fail; changing the n of ρ = 2r/n to n + 0.2 makes 4 fail (including the radial nodes); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the orbital for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the colour with the density that the probe computes with the explicit series and the Legendre derivative, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.146) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) only one plane (φ = 0) is cut; (c) the relative size of the radial and angular density is not tested (only the nodes); (d) the normalisation by the greatest value in the plot and the power 0.4 are not tested; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry) and no threshold was adjusted; (2) while generating the test I added a meaningless assertion (`l − m ≥ 0`) only to use a variable that was otherwise unused, which I noticed and removed (together with the variable) before running the mutation checks; (3) the explanatory comment of the radial-node test was first unclear ("3s-like zeros") and was rewritten; (4) the standard C1 sweep passed the first time (0 violation records).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 92, seed ^ salt)` picks an orbital (n, l, m, half width); the coefficients (−1)ⁱ·C(k + α, k − i)/i! of the generalised Laguerre polynomial L^{2l+1}_{n−l−1} (k = n − l − 1, α = 2l + 1) are precomputed; the greatest density in the plot is found by a scan on a 96×96 grid; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (x, z) = half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin) and half width·(0.5 − fv)/(0.5 − margin) (Bohr radii); r = √(x² + z²), ρ = 2r/n, cos θ = z/r (0 when r is almost 0); the radial part is ρ^l·e^{−ρ/2}·L(ρ); the associated Legendre function P_l^m(cos θ) comes from P_m^m = (2m − 1)!!·sin^m θ, P_{m+1}^m = (2m + 1)·cos θ·P_m^m and (l − m)P_l^m = (2l − 1)·cos θ·P_{l−1}^m − (l + m − 1)·P_{l−2}^m; the density is (radial·P)²; ink is the edge fade times clamp(density / greatest)^0.4, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: about ten multiply-adds and one exp per pixel; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('hydrogenorbitals', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 137 ms in the one run I made (a single measurement, not a benchmark, taken while another full test run was using the machine; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one orbital (the 6 chosen 6, 6, 4, 8, 5 and 11 times; seeds 2, 6, 4, 1, 0 and 3 for the orbitals 0 to 5); the dark rings of the radial nodes are at most 0.013 Bohr radii from the predicted positions (a pixel being 0.055 to 0.191); the numbers of dark points on the circle are 0, 2, 4, 2, 4 and 6 as predicted with a largest angle difference of 0.0011 rad; the largest symmetry difference is 0.0292; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.490%/0.328%/2.434%, color is 0.025632–0.025819 to 0.869025–0.872427 with a mean of 0.151598/0.112953/0.151549, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.864873–0.873138 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.454%/0.323%/2.416%/1.054%, color is 0.025157–0.025381 to 0.869133–0.873581 with a mean of 0.151572/0.112943/0.151523/0.137913, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.864354–0.876217 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 2.565% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (50.69, 25.86, 17.58), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0019 (very smooth) and the minimum z component is 255; the C1 sweep has 0 violation records for the 6 orbitals. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 orbitals, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`machcone` adds the Mach cone, bringing the current catalog from 1113 to 1114 kinds (1115 gallery choices including plain). Yellow-green on a dark olive: the **wavefronts of a moving source** — the source moves to the right at the speed M (in units of the wave speed, the Mach number) and emits a pulse at fixed intervals, and the picture is the circular crests that all the pulses make now: the radius of each circle is the time s since the pulse was emitted (the wave speed being 1), and its centre is where the source was then, that is M·s behind it now; the s of a point (x, y) is solved from (x + M s)² + y² = s², s = (x² + y²) / (−M x ∓ √(x² − (M² − 1) y²)), and the crests are where s is a whole number of periods; **below the speed of the waves** (M < 1) the crests ahead are crowded ((1 − M) periods apart) and those behind are spread out ((1 + M) periods) — the Doppler effect; at **M = 1** all the circles touch at the source and there are no waves ahead; **above** it (M > 1) there are waves only inside the cone behind the source (two families of crests), the half angle θ of the cone having sin θ = 1/M (tan θ = 1/√(M² − 1)) — the Mach cone; the seed picks one of 6 Mach numbers: 0, 0.5, 0.8, 1, 1.5 and 2.5. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: pure geometry of non-dispersive wavefronts in two dimensions, with no shock strength, pressure or interference detail; the amplitude decaying as exp(−s/4), the small taper at the edge of the cone and the fade of crests closer than 0.02 apart (which avoids moiré) are authored looks; unlike the other wave materials (for example the two-source interference of twosourcewaves and the dispersive wake of kelvinwake) it draws the Doppler effect and the Mach cone of non-dispersive waves. (The Doppler spacing and sin θ = 1/M are from my memory, with the quadratic for s derived by hand; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 Mach numbers, the pulse spacing 0.3 (in units of the width of the plot over 4, the source at 0.68 of the width), the crest exponent 12, the decay length 4, the cone taper 0.03, the fade of crowded crests between 0.04 and 0.02, the source dot radius 0.05, the yellow-green-on-dark-olive colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 Mach numbers once (of the final version; earlier versions were also viewed, see the record of adjustments). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being closed forms that do not depend on how the sampler is written: the sampler solves the quadratic for s, and the test uses the geometry of circles and the Doppler spacing: (1) **the crests are on the circles of the pulses emitted k periods ago**: on the circles of radius k·period centred M·k·period behind the source, every 0.05 rad and for k from 1 to 14, the points in the plot are lit (colour above 0.3; 0.378 at the lowest in the probe, for 298 to 929 points per variant), except where the crests crowd (where the distance period·(1 − M cos ψ) between the circles k and k + 1 is under 0.06, as beside the source at M = 1) and, for M above 1, near where the circles touch the Mach cone (the discriminant under 0.15 of x² + y²); (2) **the Doppler spacing of the crests on the track below the speed of the waves**: on the track the crests ahead of the source are (1 − M) periods apart and those behind it (1 + M) periods apart; for M = 0, 0.5 and 0.8 the mean distance between the crests (maxima of the colour above 0.3 along the axis, leaving out those within 0.05 of the source) differs from that by under 0.01 (0.0018, 0.0040 and 0.0055 at the worst behind [9, 6 and 5 crests] and 0.0003 at the worst ahead [4, 8 and 18 crests] in the probe); (3) **it stops at the Mach cone and leaves the region ahead empty**: for M > 1 (1.5 and 2.5), along the rays with 0.9 and 0.95 times the slope tan θ = 1/√(M² − 1) the greatest colour is above 0.6 (0.801 at the lowest in the probe), along those with 1.03, 1.06 and 1.1 times it is under 0.1 (0.055 at the highest, the grain), and for M of 1 and more the points ahead of the source (x from 0.1 to 1.2, 2090 points per variant) are under 0.1 too (0.055); (4) **mirror symmetry about the track**: the colours at (x, y) and (x, −y) differ by under 0.05 (0.0282 at the most in the probe, the grain; 3822 pairs per variant). Mutation checks (done three times): changing the coefficient M² − 1 of the quadratic to M² − 0.8 makes 5 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the circles, the cone, the seed difference and the maps); multiplying −M x by 0.9 makes 6 fail (including the circles, the Doppler spacing and the cone); multiplying the period of the phase by 1.05 makes 5 fail (including the circles and the Doppler spacing); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the Mach number for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the lit pixels with the crests predicted in the probe from the roots of the quadratic; the smallest margin to the second best was 0.797 before the fade of crowded crests was added and 0.755 after) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the Doppler spacing is tested only for M < 1; (c) the angle of the cone is only bracketed between 0.95 and 1.03 times the slope (about ±5%); (d) the amplitude decay and the fade of crowded crests are not tested; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) I first wrote a draft file of the sampler with unfinished placeholder code that was never run or applied, and then wrote the final version directly; (2) **the standard C1 sweep failed for the M = 1 configuration**: beside the source (x slightly below 0) s = (x² + y²)/(2|x|) grows without bound and the density of the crests diverges, and the unfiltered sweep had 219 violation records (one per point, axis and channel, with w up to about 5.8×10⁵); I first changed the amplitude decay from 1/√(1 + s/1.5) to exp(−s/4), which still left 17 violation records (w up to about 5), so I added the fade "crests closer than 0.04 apart fade in between 0.04 and 0.02 and are 0 below 0.02" (the spacing being period/|∇s|, |∇s| = hypot(M s + x, y)/√discriminant), after which the standard C1 sweep (grid lines at 13, 129 and 509 divisions and 16384 random points per variant) has 0 violation records and the smoothness test did not need to be relaxed; the moiré beside the source at M = 1 in the preview is reduced as a result; (3) the first probe of the points on the circles had a lowest colour of 0.026 at M = 1, because the circles crowd beside the source and are faded out; leaving out the points within 0.12 and then 0.45 of the source was not enough, and in the end the closed-form distance period·(1 − M cos ψ) between the circles under 0.06 is used to leave them out; (4) the first cone probe used the rays at 0.97 and 0.99 times the slope, and the greatest colour for M = 1.5 was only 0.318 (the taper fades the edge), so the test uses 0.9 and 0.95; (5) the first Doppler check used each gap between crests and was off by 0.022 at the worst (the amplitude envelope pushes the maxima), so it became the mean spacing (0.0055 at the worst); (6) the comment in the test that holds the seed table first gave the same number for the smallest margin before and after the fade of crowded crests, which I noticed and corrected to 0.797 and 0.755 before running the mutation checks; (7) the new tests all passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 91, seed ^ salt)` picks a Mach number M and a pulse spacing; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x = 4·(tu − 0.68), y = 4·(0.5 − tv) (tu and tv being the fractions inside the margin); the discriminant is x² − (M² − 1) y²; if it is not negative, for each of the two denominators −M x ∓ √discriminant that is above 0, s = (x² + y²)/denominator; the crest of each root is ((1 + cos(2πs/period))/2)¹², its weight is exp(−s/4) times the fade of crowded crests (the spacing being period·√discriminant/hypot(M s + x, y), faded in with smooth between 0.02 and 0.04), and for M > 1 the whole is multiplied by the cone taper smooth(discriminant/(x² + y²)/0.03); the two roots are combined as 1 − Π(1 − weight·crest); the maximum with the source dot (radius 0.05) is taken and the edge fade applied; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: one square root and two cosines per pixel; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('machcone', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 99 ms and 106 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one Mach number (the 6 chosen 5, 8, 5, 8, 8 and 6 times; seeds 3, 2, 0, 5, 1 and 8 for the Mach numbers 0, 0.5, 0.8, 1, 1.5 and 2.5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 6.628%/4.971%/5.508%, color is 0.025596–0.025601 to 0.817363–0.842270 with a mean of 0.116239/0.096373/0.094072, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.804959–0.817146 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 6.540%/4.989%/5.434%/4.991%, color is 0.025165–0.025280 to 0.845210–0.852346 with a mean of 0.116260/0.096382/0.094088/0.096475, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.820143–0.841250 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 13.199% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.84, 39.06, 17.12), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0444 and the minimum z component is 252; the C1 sweep has 0 violation records for the 6 variants. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 Mach numbers, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`raindropoptics` adds raindrop optics, bringing the current catalog from 1112 to 1113 kinds (1114 gallery choices including plain). Pale amber on a dark teal-blue-black: the **ray diagram** of parallel sunlight (entering from the left) through a droplet of unit radius — 36 rays evenly spaced in the impact parameter b = sin i, refracted at the surface by the law of refraction (Snell), reflected k times inside by the law of reflection (k = 1 for the primary rainbow, 2 for the secondary and 3 for the tertiary) and refracted out again, with the outline of the droplet; the **rainbow ray** (the one of least deviation D = kπ + 2i − 2(k + 1)r, sin r = sin i / n) is drawn on both sides, at b and −b, brightest: the least deviation makes the rays that leave bunch up into the rainbow, the primary rainbow of water (n = 1.333, k = 1) having the rainbow angle D = 137.92°, that is about 42° (180° − 137.92°); the seed picks one of 6 droplets: (n, k) = (1.333, 1), (1.333, 2), (1.5, 1), (1.2, 1), (1.333, 3) and (1.5, 2). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only the geometry of the rays is drawn, each ray only along the one path with exactly k internal reflections (not the other paths that exist at the same time), with no Fresnel intensities, no dispersion (so no colours) and none of the supernumerary bows from diffraction; unlike the other optics materials (for example the caustics on a pool floor of poolcaustics) it draws the rays inside a droplet and the rainbow angle. (The laws of refraction and reflection, Descartes's condition of least deviation cos²i = (n² − 1) / ((k + 1)² − 1) and the 42° are from my memory, and were compared in a prototype with vector ray tracing and the angle formulas; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width of 2.2 droplet radii for the plot, the 36 rays, the 6 pairs (n, k), the line half width 0.003 (of the tile), the tones (0.5 for the incoming and outgoing rays, 0.35 inside the droplet, 1 for the rainbow ray and 0.7 for the outline), the pale-amber-on-dark-teal-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 droplets once (of the final version). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype (Bun, not in the repository) that compares vector ray tracing (refraction by the vector form, internal reflection by mirroring) with the angle formulas: the exit direction −D differs by at most 3.3e-13 and the polar angle of the exit point by at most 1.9e-12 (n = 1.333 and 1.5, k = 1, 2 and 3), and the closed form of Descartes agrees with a scan for the least deviation (for n = 1.333 and k = 1 an incidence angle of 59.41° against 59.40° from the scan, D = 137.92°). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being formulas that do not depend on how the sampler is written: the sampler traces with vectors and the test uses the angle formulas and the closed form of Descartes, while the sampler finds the rainbow ray by a scan: (1) **every ray along the path that the law of refraction and the law of reflection give**: the ray of impact parameter b = −1 + (2j + 1)/36 enters at the polar angle π − i, every chord turns the point clockwise by π − 2r, and after k reflections it leaves along the direction −D, D = 2(i − r) + k(π − 2r); the colour is above 0.35 on the incoming part (before the entry point, from x = −2.05) and on the points 0.4 to 1.6 along the exit ray from the exit point (inside the window), and above 0.25 on the chords inside the droplet (from 0.1 to 0.9 of each) (0.485, 0.485 and 0.377 at the lowest in the probe; 1764 incoming points, 1812 to 1908 exit points and 1152 to 2304 chord points per variant); (2) **the rainbow ray, the ray of least deviation, is brightest and goes in the direction of the rainbow angle**: from the closed form cos²i = (n² − 1)/((k + 1)² − 1) for the incidence angle, on the incoming part and along the exit direction ∓D_min of the two rays at ±i (D_min being 137.92°, 230.89°, 157.16°, 113.62°, 318.26° and 266.87° in the order of the preset) the colour is above 0.8 (0.845 at the lowest in the probe, tone 1 against 0.5 for an ordinary ray; 210 to 218 points), while at the directions 0.05 rad to either side (t from 1.0 to 1.4) the colour is under 0.7 (0.5 at the highest, an ordinary ray); (3) **mirror symmetry about the axis of the sun**: the colours at (x, y) and (x, −y) differ by under 0.05 (0.0287 at the most in the probe, the grain; 3200 pairs per variant); (4) **nothing on the side away from the sun when there is one reflection**: for the three droplets with k = 1 (n = 1.333, 1.5 and 1.2) every ray is thrown back with a deviation of at least the rainbow angle, so at the radii 1.3, 1.6 and 2.0 and the polar angles every 2° up to 80° (for n = 1.2, whose rainbow angle is 113.62°, up to the rainbow angle less 50°, that is 63.6°) the colour is under 0.1 (0.054 at the highest in the probe; 243, 243 and 192 points). Mutation checks (done three times): changing the ratio of refractive indices 1/n to 1/(1.03n) makes 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the path of the rays, the rainbow ray and the seed difference); changing the comparison of the scan for the least deviation to look for the greatest makes 4 fail (including the rainbow ray); removing the rainbow ray on the −b side makes 4 fail (including the symmetry and the rainbow ray); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the droplet for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the lit pixels with the segments of the rays traced by vectors in the probe, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.148) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the tones (incoming, inside the droplet, outline) and the evenness of the rays are not tested; (c) that the far side is empty is tested only for k = 1; (d) ray intensities, total internal reflection and the other paths that exist at the same time are neither simulated nor tested; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) in the prototype I first wrote the turn of every chord as counterclockwise, and the polar angle of the exit point was off by about 2.0; as clockwise the error is 1.9e-12; (2) eslint caught an assignment that was not used (`ink` set to 0 and then set again at once), which now starts from the outline directly; (3) the test generator wrote the apostrophe of "Snell's" into a single-quoted string, so that the test file did not parse (no test had run yet), and the title was changed before the tests were run; (4) the first probe of "the far side is empty" used 80° for all three droplets with k = 1, and the droplet with n = 1.2 (rainbow angle 113.62°) has rays there (up to 0.674), so the limit became min(80°, rainbow angle − 50°); (5) the standard C1 sweep passed the first time (0 violation records); (6) the other tests passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry) and no threshold was adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 90, seed ^ salt)` picks a droplet (n, k); for the 36 rays (b = −1 + (2j + 1)/36) and the rainbow rays ±sin(i_c) the path is traced with vectors: the entry point (−√(1 − b²), b); refraction in (vector form, ratio 1/n); k + 1 chords (chord length −2 p·d) with k mirror reflections between them (d − 2(d·p)p); a last refraction out (ratio n); every ray is stored as segments (the incoming part starting outside the window, the chords and an exit part of length 6) with its tone; the incidence angle i_c of the rainbow ray is found by scanning (0, π/2) in 4000 steps for the least D(i) = kπ + 2i − 2(k + 1)·asin(sin i / n); there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x, y (in droplet radii, the half width being 2.2); the outline kernel clamp(1 − (||(x, y)| − 1|/0.003)²)² (in tile units) times 0.7; the distance to every segment (about 36·(k + 3) + 2·(k + 3) segments, up to about 230) is computed and, where it is under 0.003 of the tile, the maximum of tone·clamp(1 − (d/0.003)²)² is taken; the edge fade is applied and color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: the distance to up to about 230 segments per pixel; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('raindropoptics', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 672 ms and 645 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, taken while another full test run was using the machine; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one droplet (the 6 chosen 8, 5, 7, 8, 5 and 7 times; the first seeds in the order of the preset (1.333, 1), (1.333, 2), (1.5, 1), (1.2, 1), (1.333, 3) and (1.5, 2) are 1, 3, 8, 5, 0 and 2); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.066%/1.372%/1.479%, color is 0.025443–0.025677 to 0.870023–0.873381 with a mean of 0.113038/0.100388/0.100489, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.867945–0.875685 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.119%/1.751%/1.802%/1.789%, color is 0.025168–0.025234 to 0.870333–0.873791 with a mean of 0.113221/0.100526/0.100628/0.100558, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.871639–0.876864 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 3.093% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (30.14, 35.32, 41.48), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0518 and the minimum z component is 252; the C1 sweep has 0 violation records for the 6 variants. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 droplets, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hofstadterbutterfly` adds the Hofstadter butterfly, bringing the current catalog from 1111 to 1112 kinds (1113 gallery choices including plain). Pale blue on a dark blue-black: the **energy spectrum** of an electron on a two-dimensional square lattice in a magnetic field (Harper's equation ψ(n+1) + ψ(n−1) + 2cos(2παn + k)·ψ(n) = E·ψ(n)) — the horizontal axis is the magnetic flux α per unit cell (0 to 1) and the vertical axis upward is the energy E (−4 to 4); at a rational α = p/q (in lowest terms) the spectrum is q bands (for even q the two middle bands touch at E = 0), the bands being the E with |P(E)| ≤ 4, where P(E) is the trace of the product of the q transfer matrices [[E − 2cos(2πpn/q + k), −1], [1, 0]] (taken at the phase where cos(qk) = 0); every pixel draws the bands of all the rationals p/q with a denominator up to the limit that lie within 0.003 of the tile (about 1.5 pixels at 512²) of it, with a brightness falling with q (limits of q = 12 to 48), which grows the fractal butterfly; the seed picks one of 6 windows: the full α (q up to 24), α from 0 to 0.5 (q up to 48), the full α (q up to 12), only the upper half of E (q up to 36), α from 0 to 0.5 (q up to 24), and the full α (q up to 48). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only the bands of a finite number of rationals are drawn (the spectrum for an irrational α is a Cantor set, which is not drawn here), and there is no band topology (Chern numbers) or density of states; unlike the other fractal or lattice materials it draws the spectrum of a lattice electron in a magnetic field. (Harper's equation and the band condition are from my memory and were compared with the eigenvalues of the q×q Hamiltonian in a prototype; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 windows and denominator limits, the width 0.003 (of the tile) round a rational, the softening 0.004 (of the tile) of the band edges, the tones (1 for q = 1, 0.02 less for each denominator, 0.5 at the lowest), the pale-blue-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 windows once (of the final version; an earlier version was also viewed, see the record of adjustments). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype (Bun, not in the repository) to compare the band condition: for α = 1/3, 1/4, 1/5, 2/5 and 1/2 the band edges from |P(E)| ≤ 4 agree with the ranges of the eigenvalues of the q×q Hamiltonian over 16×16 Bloch phases to about 1e-3 (for example the three bands at α = 1/3 are [−2.732, −2.000], [−0.732, 0.732] and [2.000, 2.732]). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being an independent calculation that does not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler uses the trace of the transfer matrices, and the test finds the eigenvalues itself by real symmetric Jacobi rotations): (1) **lit on the bands found from the eigenvalues and dark in the gaps**: for every fraction p/q in lowest terms with q from 2 to 7 that lies in the plot (0.07 to 0.93 of the tile; 17 values for the full windows and 8 for the half ones) the test builds the q×q Harper Hamiltonian (the Hermitian matrix being solved as a real symmetric 2q×2q one), finds its eigenvalues for 16×16 Bloch phases, and takes the range of each level as a band (touching ones merged); along the column of that flux, every 0.004 in energy over 90% of the plot, the colour is above 0.5 where the energy is at least 0.02 inside a band and below 0.5 where it is at least 0.02 outside every band (the drawn edges were within 0.006 of the eigenvalue edges in the probe; the bands narrower than 0.04 are only checked for the dark outside them); (2) **mirror symmetry in E → −E (the windows centred on E = 0) and in α → 1 − α (the windows over the full α)**: the colours at the two points differ by under 0.05 (0.0294 at the most in the probe, the grain; 14898 and 11136 pairs); (3) **nothing above E = 4**: the energy stays within [−4, 4] (the hopping adds at most 2 and the potential at most 2), so every pixel from E = 4.06 up to the top of the window at 4.4 has a colour under 0.1 (0.0549 at the most in the probe, the grain; 2583 or 4018 pixels). Mutation checks (done three times): changing the band condition 4 − |P| to 3.7 − |P| makes 5 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the bands, the seed difference, the smoothness and the maps); changing the phase π/(2q) in the transfer matrix to 0 makes 4 fail; changing the flux numerator p to p + 1 makes 5 fail; all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the window for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the lit pixels with the bands that the probe finds from the trace of the transfer matrices, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.101) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) only the fractions up to q = 7 are checked, the bands of larger q being too narrow to check one by one; (c) the bands narrower than 0.04 are not checked to be drawn; (d) within 0.02 of E = 0 for even q, where the two middle bands touch, nothing is checked (see the record of adjustments); (e) the fall of the brightness with q is not tested; (f) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version looked dim and sparse (tone floor 0.35, width 0.0024, a darker pale blue) and the zoomed windows showed only scattered vertical bars, so I raised the denominator limit of the zoomed windows (30, 16 and 36 became 48, 24, 36 and 48), made the width 0.003, made the tone fall by 0.02 per denominator with 0.5 as the lowest, and made the pale blue brighter; (2) the first probe that told the window of each seed correlated the mean colour of each column with an indicator that the column holds a rational; it chose only 2 of the windows (smallest margin 0.009), and after correlating with the lit pixels predicted from the trace of the transfer matrices all 6 windows occur (smallest margin 0.101); (3) when the probe compared the number of drawn band intervals with that of the eigenvalue bands, the counts did not agree (for example 5 drawn against 3 expected for 1/6), because for even q the drawing has two separate pieces at the touching point E = 0 and the outer bands narrower than 0.03 are drawn as well; that was the way my probe filtered, not a drawing error, so the test checks point by point (lit inside bands, dark outside) and does not use the number of intervals; (4) **the test failed the first time**: for even q the bands touch at E = 0, and when the test sampled exactly E = 0.000 the sampler's edge test in the branch where the slope is 0 used inside > 0 (here inside = 0) and gave dark; after changing it to inside > −1e-9 that point is lit (only pixels exactly on the touching point are affected, no other number changed, confirmed by rerunning the probes); (5) **the C1 sweep does not hold**: the band edges are softened over only 0.004 of the tile, and the unfiltered sweep had 4, 6, 2, 0, 0 and 9 violation records in the 6 windows (one per point, axis and channel, with w up to about 1.69), so as for arnoldtongues it now checks only the values whose central slope is under 100 (98.0% to 99.6% of the 259392 values per window were kept, the worst w being 0.0148 and the difference after shifting the UV by whole periods at most 1.3e-13); the steep places (about 0.4% to 2.0% of the values) are not checked for smoothness; (6) the other tests passed the first time and no threshold was adjusted afterwards.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 89, seed ^ salt)` picks a window [centre and half width of α, centre and half width of E, denominator limit]; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): α = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin) and E likewise (upward); for q = 1 up to the denominator limit: p = round(α·q), and if 0 ≤ p ≤ q, gcd(p, q) = 1 and |α − p/q| is below the width (0.003 of the tile converted to α), the product of the q transfer matrices and its derivative in E are computed (q steps of a few multiply-adds), giving the trace P and |P′|; the distance to a band edge is about (4 − |P|)/|P′| (in E), softened over 0.004 of the tile (smooth); when the slope is almost 0 (< 1e-9) the test is 4 − |P| > −1e-9; the brightness of that rational is max(0.5, 1 − 0.02(q − 1))·(the kernel round p/q)²·the softening; the maximum over the rationals is taken and the edge fade applied; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: a loop over up to 48 denominators per pixel, with the q-step product only where a rational is within reach; in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('hofstadterbutterfly', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 1997 ms and 2025 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark; the time in a browser Worker was not measured; in the same runs jacobielliptic took 144 and 158 ms), which makes it one of the slower materials I have measured. Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one window (the 6 chosen 7, 6, 8, 5, 8 and 6 times; seeds 0, 2, 8, 7, 1 and 5 for the variants 0 to 5); the largest difference between the drawn band edges and the eigenvalue edges is 0.0048 to 0.0059; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.486%/1.160%/1.164%, color is 0.025371–0.025656 to 0.807162–0.810103 with a mean of 0.069838/0.054701/0.054780, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.790387–0.798229 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.665%/1.224%/1.229%/2.852%, color is 0.025116–0.025193 to 0.840778–0.844978 with a mean of 0.069675/0.054604/0.054684/0.073509, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.829892–0.841092 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 2.748% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (21.00, 26.17, 44.69), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0259 and the minimum z component is 253; in the symmetry probe the largest difference is 0.0294 and the highest colour above E = 4.06 is 0.0549. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 windows, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`jacobielliptic` adds the Jacobi elliptic functions, bringing the current catalog from 1110 to 1111 kinds (1112 gallery choices including plain). Gold on a dark purple: the **phase lines and modulus lines** of the Jacobi elliptic functions sn(u | m), cn(u | m) and dn(u | m) in the complex plane u = x + iy — 24 bright lines (where the argument arg f is a multiple of π/12) radiate from every zero and pole, and the fainter ring lines are where ln|f| is a multiple of 0.6 (drawn only for |ln|f|| ≤ 2.5); the line width is corrected by |f′/f|, so it is constant on the picture; the functions are doubly periodic (up to a sign of f, so the pattern repeats every 2K along the real axis and every 2K′ along the imaginary axis): sn has its zeros at 2aK + 2b·iK′, cn at (2a + 1)K + 2b·iK′ and dn at (2a + 1)K + (2b + 1)·iK′, and all three have their poles at 2aK + (2b + 1)·iK′ (K = K(m) and K′ = K(1 − m) being the complete elliptic integrals); the seed picks one of 6: sn (m = 0.5), cn (0.5), dn (0.5), sn (0.8), cn (0.2) and dn (0.8). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern (although the functions are periodic, the plot covers only about 1.5 to 3 periods). It is a schematic picture: the functions are computed from the theta series in the nome q = exp(−πK′/K) (8 terms) after u is reduced by the periods; it is not an arbitrary-precision elliptic function library and it does not draw the Riemann surface. Unlike the other complex-variable or periodic materials it draws the zeros, poles and lines of equal phase of the Jacobi elliptic functions. (The theta-function representation and the places of the zeros and poles are from my memory, with the identities checked by a prototype; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1.6·max(K, K′) of the plot, the 8 terms of the theta series, the phase step π/12, the ring step 0.6 and limit 2.5, the line half width 0.004 (of the tile), the tones (0.9 for the phase lines and 0.45 for the rings), the gold-on-dark-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 functions once (of the final version). Before the implementation I wrote a prototype (Bun, not in the repository) to check the theta-function formulas: for m = 0.2, 0.5 and 0.8 sn² + cn² − 1 is at most 5.4e-15, dn² + m·sn² − 1 at most 1.8e-15, sn′ − cn·dn (central difference, step 1e-6) at most 1.7e-10, the difference after the periods 4K and 2iK′ at most 4.9e-15, sn(K) = 1.000000000, and near a pole |sn| agrees with 1/(√m·ε); K(0.5) = 1.854075 (matching the 1.8540747 I remember). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being closed forms that do not depend on how the sampler is written: (1) **the periods**: on a 60×60 grid, for every pair of points u and u + 2K, and u and u + 2iK′, that both lie in the plot (0.06 to 0.94 of the tile), the colours differ by under 0.05 (0.0276 at the most in the probe, the grain; 2320 or 2900 pairs per variant; K and K′ found in the test by the arithmetic-geometric mean separately); (2) **24 phase lines at every zero and pole**: on a circle of radius 0.2 round each zero and pole in the plot (their places from the closed forms of the periods, 3 to 6 per variant) there are exactly 24 bright arcs (colour above 0.65, which only the bright phase lines reach, the ring lines being fainter), and at the centre (moved by 0.01 and 0.004) the colour is above 0.65 (0.773 at the lowest in the probe), while at the zeros of the other two functions that are not singular for this one (3 to 6 points per variant, at least 0.5 from a singular one) there are fewer than 24 arcs (4 in the probe); (3) **mirror symmetry about the real axis**: sn, cn and dn take conjugate values at conjugate points, so the colours at x + iy and x − iy differ by under 0.05 (0.0278 at the most in the probe, the grain; 1624 pairs per variant). Mutation checks (done four times): computing K with sqrt(1 − 1.1·m) makes 5 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the periods, the 24 lines, the seed difference and the maps); changing the centre K of the plot for cn and dn to K/2 makes 4 fail (the periods test was not caught); changing the phase step π/12 to π/13 makes 4 fail; removing the sign (−1)ⁿ from θ₄(0) (which only changes the scale factors of cn and dn, that is, the places of the ring lines, and not the phase) makes only the tone-range test fail; all four were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the function for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the colour with the phase lines computed with the theta series without the reduction by the periods, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.122) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) **the modulus ring lines (positions, spacing and scale factors) and the derivatives of cn and dn (the line-width correction) are not covered by a dedicated test** (the fourth mutation above was caught only by the tone-range test); (c) K is computed with the arithmetic-geometric mean both in the test and in the sampler, so it is not an independent algorithm (K(0.5) matches the value I remember); (d) the radius 0.2 and the threshold 0.65 of (2) were chosen after the probe; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first probe that told the function of each seed used the colour at the singular points; it chose only 3 of the functions with smallest margins of 0.004 and 0.001, and sampling exactly at a pole gave NaN; after switching to the correlation with the phase lines predicted by the theta series without the reduction by the periods all 6 functions occur (smallest margin 0.122); to avoid the NaN the sampler now puts a floor of 1e-300 under the squared modulus of θ₄ (a pixel that falls exactly on a pole now gives a finite value, and no other pixel is affected); (2) I had written 12 phase lines, but the probe showed 24 rays at every singular point (the multiples of π/12 are 24 in a full turn), so the test and the documents say 24; (3) **the C1 sweep with a step of 1e-10 had a few violations** (5 violation records in total for the 6 variants, one per point, axis and channel, with w of 0.034 and 0.047 against the usual limit of 0.03); I checked two of the points: the second difference divided by the step fell with the step (0.0229, 0.0023, 0.0004 for the steps 1e-10, 1e-9 and 1e-8), which is the rounding error of the theta series and not a kink, so the step of the sweep in the test is now 1e-8 (the jump of the slope of a kink does not depend on the step and would still be found); at 1e-8 there are 0 violation records, the largest w is 0.0228 to 0.0240 (true curvature, where the slope is about 520) and the difference after shifting the UV by whole periods is at most 2.6e-13; (4) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 88, seed ^ salt)` picks a function and m; K = π / (2·AGM(1, √(1−m))) and K′ = π / (2·AGM(1, √m)) are found by the arithmetic-geometric mean (24 steps); the nome is q = exp(−πK′/K); q^((n+½)²) and q^(n²) (8 terms) and θ₂(0), θ₃(0), θ₄(0) are precomputed; there is the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): u = x + iy (x = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin), the centre being 0 for sn and K for cn and dn; y = half width·(0.5 − fv)/(0.5 − margin)); u is reduced by the periods to [−K, K] × [−K′, K′]; z = πu/(2K); θ₁, θ₂, θ₃ and θ₄ (8 terms, each with a few sin/cos/sinh/cosh calls); sn = (θ₃/θ₂)·θ₁/θ₄, cn = (θ₄/θ₂)·θ₂(z)/θ₄, dn = (θ₄/θ₃)·θ₃(z)/θ₄; the derivatives sn′ = cn·dn, cn′ = −sn·dn, dn′ = −m·sn·cn; ln|f|, arg f and |f′/f|; the distance is the change to the nearest line divided by |f′/f| (in tile units); the phase kernel and the ring kernel are each clamp(1 − (distance/0.004)²)², with the tones 0.9 and 0.45 (the ring lines fade out over a width of 0.5 once |ln|f|| exceeds 2.5); ink is the larger of the two times the edge fade, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: in Bun on this machine `generateProceduralMaps('jacobielliptic', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 171 ms and 175 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, taken while another full test run was using the machine; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one function (the 6 chosen 7, 5, 7, 7, 4 and 10 times; seeds 3, 2, 7, 1, 4 and 0 for the variants 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 12.033%/8.133%/11.237%, color is 0.025468–0.025672 to 0.799554–0.801046 with a mean of 0.151094/0.114319/0.142187, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.784348–0.786162 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 11.494%/7.597%/10.596%/10.600%, color is 0.025093–0.025239 to 0.801435–0.802581 with a mean of 0.150441/0.114036/0.142694/0.142815, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.788152–0.790313 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 16.246% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (48.42, 37.42, 45.71), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0340 and the minimum z component is 253; in the period, singularity and symmetry probes the largest difference over the period pairs is 0.0276, the lowest colour at the centre of a singular point is 0.773 and the largest mirror difference is 0.0278. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 functions, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`kelvinwake` adds the Kelvin wake, bringing the current catalog from 1109 to 1110 kinds (1111 gallery choices including plain). Pale cyan on a dark sea blue-black: the **far-field crest lines** of the waves behind a ship moving over water — the ship is at the middle of the left edge (a small bright dot) and the wake opens to the right as a wedge: the **transverse waves** (arc-shaped crests roughly across the track, one wavelength 2πV²/g apart) and the **divergent waves** (crests curving inward from the two edges of the wedge), the two edges of the wedge (where the two families merge) making the Kelvin angle arcsin(1/3) ≈ 19.47° (tan = 1/(2√2)) and no waves outside; the positions come from the stationary-phase analysis of deep-water gravity waves (the dispersion relation k ∝ sec²θ): for a wave vector at the angle θ to the track the crest is at x = φ·cosθ·(1 + sin²θ), y = φ·sinθ·cos²θ (φ being the phase, a whole number of wavelengths), and for a point (x, y) the two angles θ of the transverse and divergent waves are found from y/x = sinθ·cosθ / (1 + sin²θ); the seed picks one of 6 wavelengths (3, 4, 5, 6, 8 or 10 transverse wavelengths along the track). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture, not a fluid simulation: only the crest lines of the far-field approximation are drawn, with no near field and no influence of the hull shape, no Airy-function smoothing along the Kelvin lines (only a very small taper outside the angle), and the decay of the amplitude with distance (1/√(1 + r/0.6)) and the weight of the divergent waves (cos²θ, faded out near the track) are authored looks; unlike the other wave materials (for example the two-source interference of twosourcewaves) it draws the wake shape of dispersive waves. (The stationary-phase derivation, the dispersion relation and the Kelvin angle are from my memory and hand calculation and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 6 wavelengths (3, 4, 5, 6, 8 and 10 transverse wavelengths), the crest sharpness (exponent 20), the amplitude decay length 0.6, the taper 0.004, the axis fade 0.1, the ship dot radius 0.012, the pale-cyan-on-dark-sea-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 wavelengths once (of the final version; earlier versions were also viewed, see the record of adjustments). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being closed forms that do not depend on how the sampler is written: the sampler finds θ from y/x by bisection for every pixel, and the test generates the points on the crests directly with the **forward** parametrisation x = φ·cosθ·(1 + sin²θ), y = φ·sinθ·cos²θ: (1) **the transverse and divergent crests are on the parametrised curves**: the points with θ from −0.8 to 0.8 every 0.0125 rad, φ being m wavelengths (m from 1 up to the number of wavelengths), inside the plot (x 0.05 to 0.95, |y| up to 0.46) have a colour above 0.3 (0.358 at the lowest for the transverse family and 0.349 for the divergent one in the probe; 198 to 853 transverse and 58 to 233 divergent points), and the point half a wavelength further out along the same ray of θ (variants 0 to 4) has a colour lower by at least 0.1 (0.227 at the lowest difference in the probe; the variant with 10 wavelengths had 2 of 1160 pairs not lower by 0.1, because the neighbouring crest of the other family lies there, so it is left out); (2) **it stops at the Kelvin angle**: along the rays with y/x equal to 0.97 and 0.99 times the Kelvin slope 1/(2√2) the greatest colour is above 0.6 (0.69 at the lowest in the probe), along those with 1.02, 1.04, 1.06 and 1.1 times it is under 0.1 (0.055 at the highest, the grain), and every point of the whole range outside (x from 0.1, y/x from 1.04 times the slope up to 2.5) is under 0.1 too; (3) **the transverse crests on the track are one wavelength apart**: on the track (y = 0) the phase is x itself, so the crests are at the whole numbers of the wavelength and the maxima of the colour along the axis are within 0.001 of those places (0.00067 at the worst in the probe), N − 1 of them (x = 1 lies in the fade at the edge of the plot); (4) **mirror symmetry about the track**: the colours at (x, y) and (x, −y) differ by under 0.05 (0.0287 at the most in the probe, the grain; 2970 pairs per variant). Mutation checks (done three times): changing (1 + sin²θ) in the phase to (1 + 2 sin²θ) makes 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the crests on the parametrised curves, the seed difference and the maps; the axis test was not caught, because θ = 0 on the axis); changing the Kelvin slope √2/4 to 0.3 makes 5 fail (including the stop at the Kelvin angle); multiplying the phase by 1.02 makes 5 fail (including the spacing of the crests on the track); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the wavelength for each seed was found with a probe (the reciprocal of the spacing of the crests along the axis, rounded) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the divergent crests are checked only up to θ = 0.8 rad (the divergent waves nearer the track have a very small weight); (c) the amplitude decay and the weight of the divergent waves are not tested; (d) the Kelvin angle is tested only to about ±2% (the width of the taper); (e) the variant with 10 wavelengths has no "brighter than half a wavelength further out" check; (f) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version had a crest exponent of 6, which made the transverse arcs thick and blurred, so it became 20; (2) **the standard C1 sweep failed in large numbers at first**: the bisection had only 36 steps, and the quantisation of θ (about 1e-11) amplified by the phase gave 6004, 7128, 7605, 7806, 8159 and 8577 violation records (one per point, axis and channel) for the 6 variants (w up to about 12.7); with 50 steps there were still 2, 21, 10, 17, 25 and 28 violation records (one per point, axis and channel), all near y ≈ 0, where the phase x²/(4yλ) of the divergent wave tends to infinity and the density of its crests diverges (true steepness, not rounding); I first changed the weight of the divergent waves to cos⁴θ, which gave 0 violations but left the divergent waves and the Kelvin lines almost invisible in the preview, so it became cos²θ times smooth(y/(x·0.1))² (fading out only near the track), with 0 violations in the standard C1 sweep (grid lines at 13, 129 and 509 divisions and 16384 random points per variant) and clear divergent waves in the preview; the smoothness test therefore did not need to be relaxed as it was for arnoldtongues; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted (before that first run the test generator had one replacement string wrong, which was fixed before anything was written to the test file).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 87, seed ^ salt)` picks the number N of wavelengths; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): x = (fu − margin)/(1 − 2·margin), y = (0.5 − fv)/(1 − 2·margin) (the unit being the width of the plot, the ship at x = 0); if x > 1e-4, the slope s = |y|/x; 50 bisection steps on [0, θc] and on [θc, π/2] (θc = arcsin(1/√3)) solve sinθ·cosθ/(1 + sin²θ) = min(s, 1/(2√2)) (the θ of the transverse and of the divergent waves); the phase of each family is 2π·x / (cosθ·(1 + sin²θ)·wavelength) and the crest is ((1 + cos phase)/2)²⁰; the weight is 1 for the transverse family and cos²θ·smooth(clamp(s/0.1))² for the divergent one; ink = the taper inside the wedge (smooth, the Kelvin slope ± 0.004)·1/√(1 + r/0.6)·the two families combined as 1 − Π(1 − weight·crest); the maximum with the ship dot (radius 0.012) is taken and the edge fade is applied; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: about 100 sin/cos calls per pixel; in Bun on this machine, `generateProceduralMaps('kelvinwake', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 412 ms and 354 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, taken while another full test run was using the machine; the time in a browser Worker was not measured). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one wavelength (the 6 chosen 4, 8, 6, 9, 6 and 7 times; seeds 0, 2, 15, 1, 12 and 10 for the variants 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 1.865%/2.213%/2.289%, color is 0.025583–0.025645 to 0.727620–0.797703 with a mean of 0.062259/0.064802/0.065635, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.697095–0.773925 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 1.862%/2.212%/2.294%/2.040%, color is 0.025159–0.025247 to 0.728639–0.803326 with a mean of 0.062254/0.064800/0.065640/0.063410, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.699270–0.782507 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 3.880% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (13.59, 28.33, 38.64), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0315 and the minimum z component is 253; in the crest and angle probes the largest position error of the crests on the axis is 0.00067, the highest colour outside the wedge is 0.055 and the largest mirror difference is 0.0287. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 wavelengths, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`arnoldtongues` adds Arnold tongues, bringing the current catalog from 1108 to 1109 kinds (1110 gallery choices including plain). Coral orange on a dark indigo: the **mode locking** of the circle map θ → θ + Ω − K·sin(2πθ)/(2π) — the horizontal axis is the frequency Ω, the vertical axis upward is the coupling K (0 to 1, with K = 0 at the bottom); every pixel iterates 240 steps from θ = 0 and takes the rotation number ρ = θ / 240; where ρ is within 0.006 of a fraction p/q with the denominator q up to 7 it is drawn as a locked "tongue" with the tone max(0.3, 1 − 0.12(q − 1)) (brightest for q = 1), and elsewhere as a dark background that depends on ρ (symmetrically in ρ and 1 − ρ); the tongues widen upward from the rational values of Ω at K = 0 (the tongues 0/1 and 1/1 being the widest); the seed picks one of 6 windows: the full plot (Ω 0 to 1, K 0 to 1), the left half (Ω 0 to 0.5), the middle half (Ω 0.25 to 0.75), the right half (Ω 0.5 to 1), K up to 0.6 only, and K from 0.5. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture: only the tongues with a denominator up to 7 are marked, the other locked regions (the tongues of higher order) are merged into the dark background, and the rotation number after a finite number of steps changes very fast near the edges of the tongues, so the colour is steep there; unlike the other iterated-map materials (Mandelbrot, Julia) it draws the parameter plane of the circle map. (The description of mode locking and the tongues is from my memory and I did not check the literature; the edge |Ω| = K/(2π) of the 0/1 tongue and the locking to 1/2 at Ω = 1/2 can be derived directly and the tests use them.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 240 steps, the lock half width 0.006, the largest denominator 7, the tones (1 for q = 1, 0.12 less for each denominator, 0.3 at the lowest), the background tone 0.22, the 6 windows, the coral-on-dark-indigo colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I first looked at the previews of the seeds 0 to 5 (windows 1, 0, 0, 1, 2 and 0) and then at each of the 6 windows once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being closed forms or independent calculation that do not depend on how the sampler is written: (1) **the tongue 0/1 between the closed-form edges Ω = ±K/(2π)**: for the windows that start at Ω = 0 (the variants 0, 1, 4 and 5), K from 0.2 (or the lowest K of the window plus 0.01) to 0.95 in steps of 0.01, the pixels from Ω = 0.03 to 0.01 inside the edge have a colour above 0.8 (0.822 at the lowest in the probe; 994, 994, 252 and 854 pixels) and those from 0.03 to 0.06 outside it a colour under 0.45 (0.401 at the highest; 592, 592, 312 and 352 pixels); (2) **locked to 1/2 along Ω = 1/2 for every K**: the orbit 0, 1/2, 1 (mod 1) satisfies the map for Ω = 1/2 at every K (sin π = 0), so the rotation number is 1/2 and the colour is between 0.75 and 0.83 (0.778 to 0.807 in the probe, leaving out the pixels within 0.04 of the lowest and highest K; 87, 87, 47 and 42 pixels for the variants 0, 2, 4 and 5); (3) **the symmetry Ω → 1 − Ω**: on the windows spanning Ω from 0 to 1 (the variants 0, 4 and 5) the colour at the two points differs by under 0.05 (0.0286 at the most in the probe, the grain; 988, 570 and 494 pairs); (4) **agreement with an independent rotation number**: on a 96×96 grid (0.06 to 0.94 of the tile) the test finds the rotation number with 2000 steps; where it is within 0.003 of a fraction with the denominator up to 3 the colour is above 0.45 (0.516 at the lowest in the probe; 964 to 2542 pixels per variant), and where it is more than 0.012 from every fraction with the denominator up to 7 the colour is under 0.36 (0.276 at the highest, the background; 3552 to 4968 pixels). **The smoothness check was changed**: the C1 sweep of the other materials (a step of 1e-10, second difference / step < 0.03) does not hold here: near the edges of the tongues the rotation number after a finite number of steps changes very fast (at one random point in the probe the slope was −1.68×10⁵ per UV unit, and the second difference / step at that point was 11.67, 116.9 and 1169 for the steps 1e-10, 1e-9 and 1e-8, proportional to the step, so it is true curvature and not rounding error), and the unfiltered sweep had 6, 7, 8, 17, 0 and 16 violation records (one per point, axis and channel) in the 6 windows (w up to about 12.2); I first changed the iteration to keep the angle in [0, 1) and count the whole turns apart (less rounding error), which only reduced the violations to 6, 6, 2, 2, 0 and 14, so that form was kept but the test was changed as well: the second difference / step < 0.03 is required only for the values whose central slope (step 1e-10) is under 100 in absolute value (99.3% to 99.8% of the 259392 values per window were kept, the largest slope kept being 99.98 and the worst second difference 0.016), so a kink of the margin, the fade or the grain (a jump of slope over 0.03) would still be found; and the output is unchanged by shifting the UV by whole periods (7.5e-14 at the worst).
