Limits: the steep places (about 0.2% to 0.7% of the values) are not checked for smoothness, and the filter looks at the slope of the same function. Mutation checks (done three times): changing the coupling K/(2π) to K/6 makes 5 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the independent rotation number, the seed difference, the smoothness and the maps; the 0/1 tongue test was not caught, the shift being within its tolerance); mirroring the direction of Ω makes 3 fail (the 0/1 tongue, the independent rotation number and the seed difference; the symmetry test was not caught because the full window is symmetric anyway); changing the round of the lock test to floor makes 5 fail; all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the window for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the colour with the lock colours predicted from an independent rotation number, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.503) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the positions and widths of the individual tongues are not tested (only the 0/1 edge and the 1/2 line are closed forms); (c) the decrease of the tone with the denominator is not tested; (d) the independent rotation number uses the same recurrence (2000 steps, the angle not split into turns), only the number of steps and the rounding differ; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) I had expected the tongues to be wider, and it was only on looking at the rotation numbers that I saw the 1/2 tongue at K = 0.9 is about 0.05 wide, so the thin lines in the preview are right; (2) the C1 sweep failure and its handling are above; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 86, seed ^ salt)` picks a window [centre of Ω, half width of Ω, lowest K, highest K]; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): Ω = centre + half width·(fu − 0.5)/(0.5 − margin), K = lowest K + (highest K − lowest K)·(0.5 − (fv − 0.5)/(2·(0.5 − margin))); θ += Ω − (K/2π)·sin(2πθ) is iterated 240 times (the angle kept in [0, 1) and the whole turns counted apart); ρ = (whole turns + θ) / 240; for q = 1 to 7 with the distance d to round(ρq)/q, the lock kernel clamp(1 − (d/0.006)²)² times the tone max(0.3, 1 − 0.12(q − 1)) is taken, and the maximum over q; the background is 0.22·(1 − |2ρ − 1|); ink = edge fade·(1 − (1 − background)(1 − lock)), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **Time**: every pixel iterates 240 steps with 240 `Math.sin` calls; in Bun on this machine, `generateProceduralMaps('arnoldtongues', 512, 7, { heightMap: true })` took 1393 ms and 1441 ms in the two runs I made (only two measurements, not a benchmark, and the time in a browser Worker was not measured; in the same runs powderdiffraction took 64 and 65 ms and brillouinzones 158 and 157 ms). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one window (the 6 chosen 6, 11, 9, 4, 6 and 4 times; seeds 1, 0, 4, 8, 7 and 14 for the windows 0 to 5); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 18.800%/18.828%/28.200%, color is 0.025909–0.026188 to 0.872723–0.873615 with a mean of 0.273264/0.272122/0.334469, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.874781–0.877594 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 18.826%/18.958%/28.444%/11.126%, color is 0.025252–0.025438 to 0.873053–0.874138 with a mean of 0.273253/0.272694/0.335467/0.221508, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.876709–0.878429 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 20.186% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (65.83, 41.67, 49.94), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0469 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 windows, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`powderdiffraction` adds powder diffraction, bringing the current catalog from 1107 to 1108 kinds (1109 gallery choices including plain). Mint green on a dark green-black: the **Debye–Scherrer rings** (X-ray powder diffraction) of a cubic crystal — each allowed reflection (h, k, l) makes a ring at the Bragg angle θ, sin θ = √(h²+k²+l²) / (2a/λ), with the ring at the radius L·tan 2θ (L being the distance from the sample to the flat detector, the half width of the window being equal to L); the brightness of a ring is proportional to the multiplicity × the Lorentz-polarisation factor × the Debye–Waller factor exp(−12 sin²θ) (compressed by a square root so that weak rings stay visible); the **selection rules** of the lattice decide which rings are missing: the simple cubic lattice allows everything, the body-centred one only h+k+l even and the face-centred one only h, k, l all odd or all even (the simple one also lacks N = 7, 15, 23… because N = h²+k²+l² cannot be a sum of three squares); there is a small beam stop in the middle; the seed picks one of 6 configurations: simple cubic (2a/λ = 10, 13), body-centred cubic (11, 14) and face-centred cubic (10, 13). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic picture, not a simulation: there are no atomic scattering factors in a structure factor, no particle-size broadening, no angular dependence of the intensity beyond the LP and DW factors above, and the ring width is a fixed visual width; unlike the other concentric-ring materials (zone plates, Airy rings) it draws the ring positions and missing rings fixed by the selection rules of a lattice. (Bragg's law, the selection rules and the form of the LP and DW factors are from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1 of the window (= L), the 6 pairs (lattice, 2a/λ), the ring half width 0.004 (in tile units), the tone floor 0.25 and span 0.7, the Debye–Waller coefficient 12, the background tone 0.05, the beam stop radius 0.05, the mint-on-dark-green-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler accumulates the N value of the reflections into rings and then computes the radii; the test enumerates the (h, k, l) from −9 to 9 with its own selection-rule function to find the allowed and forbidden N and calculates the radius with L·tan(2·asin(√N / ratio))): (1) **a ring at the Bragg angle of every allowed reflection**: on a ray at 0.64 rad sampled every 0.0005, the maxima of the colour above 0.2 between the radii 0.1 and 0.95 are exactly as many as the allowed rings (12, 20, 8, 13, 5 and 8 for the 6 configurations) and each is within 0.001 of the predicted radius (0.0003 at the worst in the probe; the lowest colour on a ring was 0.370); (2) **no ring for a forbidden reflection**: at the radii of the forbidden reflections (the odd N for the body-centred lattice, the mixed-parity N for the face-centred lattice and, for the simple lattice, the N that are not a sum of three squares) that are more than 0.03 from every allowed ring (1, 3, 8, 4, 8 and 15 radii for the 6 configurations), the colour is under 0.12 at every angle in steps of 0.1 rad (0.092 at the most in the probe, grain and background); (3) **the rings are circles**: on each allowed ring, at the angles (0.02 rad apart) whose point lies within 0.96 of the centre along both axes, the colour varies by under 0.05 (0.0289 at the most in the probe, the grain) and stays above 0.3. Mutation checks (done three times): changing tan(2θ) in the ring radius to tan(1.9θ) makes 6 of the 7 tests of that describe fail; changing the body-centred rule h+k+l even to h+k even makes 5 fail (including (1) and (2)); making the condition that k and l have the same parity in the face-centred rule always true makes 4 fail (including (1) and (2)); all three were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (rings found at the allowed radii and none at those of the other configurations, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.583) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) **the brightness of the rings (multiplicity, LP, DW) is not tested**, only the positions and presence; (c) the forbidden radii within 0.03 of an allowed ring (for example the odd N from 9 to 25 for the body-centred lattice with 2a/λ = 14) are not tested because they overlap allowed rings; (d) the ring positions are checked only on the ray at 0.64 rad, and at other angles only the variation of the brightness on a ring; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version had a ring half width of 0.003, which looked thin in the preview, so it became 0.004; (2) the first probe that told the configuration of each seed did not exclude the negative radii for 2θ above 90° (tan is negative); its table had only 3 configurations and a smallest margin of 0.073 and was not trustworthy, and after adding the condition that the radius be above 0 all 6 configurations occur (smallest margin 0.583); (3) the threshold of the diff test was first taken from the wrong probe (the "maskdiff 0.038036" printed by another probe, not the comparison of seeds 0 and 2), and the test failed; I then measured that seeds 0 and 2 differ in 3.7628% of the cells of the 256² grid and changed the bounds to 0.0376 and 0.0377; (4) the other tests passed the first time.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 85, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (lattice, ratio); the (h, k, l) from −12 to 12 (about 15,600) are enumerated and the multiplicity of each N = h²+k²+l² is accumulated by the lattice rule; for each N, sin θ = √N / ratio and, when it is below 1, the radius is L·tan 2θ, skipped beyond 1.6 times the half width of the window; the weight is multiplicity·(1 + cos²2θ) / (sin²θ·cos θ)·exp(−12 sin²θ); there is also the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): the radius r = √(x²+y²) (world units, the half width of the window being 1); for each ring the kernel is clamp(1 − ((r − R)·tile conversion / 0.004)²)², times 0.25 + 0.7·√(weight / largest weight), and the maximum over the rings is taken; it is combined with the background 0.05 / (1 + 4r²), the beam stop (fading in within the radius 0.05) and the edge fade, and then color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (a loop over the rings for every pixel, at most a few dozen rings). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 9, 5, 6, 7, 10 and 3 times; seeds 18, 8, 0, 9, 1 and 2 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 1.823%/1.968%/3.581%, color is 0.025602–0.025782 to 0.828816–0.835848 with a mean of 0.086983/0.076583/0.136357, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.813566–0.829941 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 1.769%/2.035%/3.482%/1.768%, color is 0.025178–0.025439 to 0.835181–0.838347 with a mean of 0.086992/0.076577/0.136247/0.087063, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.823521–0.832727 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 3.7628% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (20.19, 34.98, 30.98), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0340 and the minimum z component is 253; in the ring probe the largest position error for the 6 configurations is 0.00022 to 0.00030 (sampling step 0.0005), the highest colour at forbidden radii is 0.070 to 0.092 and the largest variation of colour on a ring is 0.0282 to 0.0289. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`brillouinzones` adds Brillouin zones, bringing the current catalog from 1106 to 1107 kinds (1108 gallery choices including plain). Rose pink on a dark purple-black: the **Bragg planes** of a two-dimensional reciprocal lattice (straight lines, the perpendicular bisector k·G = |G|²/2 of every reciprocal lattice vector G) and the **Brillouin zones** they cut out (shaded by the zone number, the first zone brightest and then darker, the zones from the 7th on sharing the darkest tone); the zone number of a point k is 1 plus the number of lattice points closer to k than the origin (that is, how many Bragg planes lie between the origin and k); the half width of the window is 2 (in units of the shortest reciprocal lattice vector), so zones from the 1st to about the 22nd can be seen; the seed picks one of 6 reciprocal lattices: square, hexagonal (b₂ = (0.5, √3/2)), rectangular (1 : 1.4), oblique (b₂ = (0.3, 0.9)), rhombic (centred rectangular, b₁ = (0.6, 0.8), b₂ = (−0.6, 0.8)) and a stretched hexagonal one (b₂ = (0.2, 1.15)). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not a solid-state calculation (there are no bands); unlike the other lattice or tiling materials it draws the Bragg planes and Brillouin zones of a reciprocal lattice. (The definition of the Brillouin zones is from my memory and I did not check the literature; the theorem that every Brillouin zone has the same area as the first is also from my memory, but it is **not** tested and neither the documentation nor the tests rely on it.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 2 of the window, the bases of the 6 reciprocal lattices, the tones of the zones (0.85 for the first, 0.14 less for each next one, 0.1 at the darkest), the Bragg plane half width 0.002 and tone 0.8, the rose-on-dark-purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the sampler counts the zone number with the inner-product inequality k·G > |G|²/2, the test counts with the distance comparison |k − G| < |k|): (1) **shading by zone number**: on a 384×384 grid, for the pixels in the plot that are more than 0.03 from every Bragg plane, grouped by the zone number calculated in the test, the mean colour falls from zone to zone (by at least 0.04 at each step among the zones 1 to 6 and the group of the zones 7 and up; the means were 0.752, 0.652, 0.550, 0.450, 0.341, 0.187 and 0.132 in the probe) and every pixel is within 0.025 of the mean of its zone (0.015 at the worst in the probe, from the grain), with at least 5000 pixels in the first zone (6016 at the lowest in the probe); (2) **a line on every Bragg plane**: for the 24 shortest reciprocal lattice vectors G, the points G/2 + t·G⊥/|G| of the perpendicular bisector (t from −2.5 to 2.5 in steps of 0.005, inside the plot) have a colour above 0.6 (0.715 at the lowest in the probe, for 16520 to 18532 points per variant); (3) **the point-group symmetry of the lattice**: the lattice is unchanged by a half turn, so the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs after a half turn is under 0.005 (0.0025 at the most in the probe), a mirror (x → −x, y → −y; decided in the test by solving for the integer coordinates) that maps the lattice to itself gives under 0.005 too (0.00244 at the most), and a mirror that does not (the oblique and the stretched hexagonal lattices) changes over 0.05 of the cells (0.159 at the lowest). Mutation checks (done twice): with the position |G|²/2 of the Bragg planes changed to 0.45·|G|², 5 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the shading by zone, the lines on the planes, the seed difference and the maps); with the counting condition k·G > |G|²/2 changed to k·G > 0.6·|G|²/2, 4 fail (the tone ranges, the shading by zone, the seed difference and the maps); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation of the pixels away from the planes with the independent zone tones, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.100) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the pixels of zones above 6 share one tone, so zones 7 and up are not checked one by one; (c) **the theorem that all zones have the same area is not tested**; (d) the pixels within 0.03 of a plane (including the line width near each plane) are not checked for the zone number; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version had a half width of 3 for the window, zone tones starting at 0.8 and falling by 0.1 per zone (darkest 0.16), and plane half width 0.003 with tone 0.95; the picture was a dense web of lines in which the zone tones could hardly be seen, and telling the 6 lattices apart by the correlation of the colour with the zone tones gave only 0.24 to 0.46 with a smallest margin of 0.006, so it was changed to a half width of 2, tones 0.85 falling by 0.14 (darkest 0.1) and plane half width 0.002 with tone 0.8, and the probe excluded the pixels near the planes, which gave 0.996 and 0.997 for the configuration of the seed and 0.889 at most for the others in the two seeds printed (smallest margin over the 40 seeds 0.100); (2) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 84, seed ^ salt)` picks a reciprocal lattice; the 168 vectors i·b₁ + j·b₂ (|i|, |j| ≤ 6, without the zero vector) and their lengths are listed; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into k = (kx, ky) (y up, half width 2); for every vector G, a = k·G, the zone number is increased by 1 if a > |G|²/2, and the minimum of |a − |G|²/2| / |G| is the distance to the nearest Bragg plane (an exact distance); the zone tone is max(0.1, 0.85 − 0.14·(zone number − 1)); the plane kernel is clamp(1 − (the distance in tile units / 0.002)²)²; ink = edge fade·(1 − (1 − zone tone)(1 − 0.8·plane kernel)), color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (168 inner products per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one lattice (the 6 chosen 8, 7, 6, 6, 7 and 6 times; seeds 2, 4, 1, 3, 0 and 5 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 23.045%/27.594%/27.600%, color is 0.025494–0.025724 to 0.826074–0.837035 with a mean of 0.274171–0.307197, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.815799–0.827381 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 23.45%/27.31%/27.31%/22.69%, color is 0.025194–0.025338 to 0.830497–0.848483 with a mean of 0.271314–0.305112, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.822152–0.842361 relief; between seeds 2 and 4 16.06% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (83.76, 50.40, 65.82), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0296 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`mapprojections` adds map projections, bringing the current catalog from 1105 to 1106 kinds (1107 gallery choices including plain). Thin teal lines on a dark blue-black: the **graticule** and the **Tissot indicatrices** of the unit sphere in six map projections; the parallels and meridians are every 15°, the equator and the central meridian (longitude 0) being brighter and thicker; a Tissot circle is a small circle of angular radius 6° on the sphere, centred at latitudes 0°, ±30° and ±60° and at every 30° of longitude, which appears as a circle or an ellipse after projection and shows the distortion there (still a circle on a conformal projection, with the area unchanged on an equal-area one); the map has a very faint fill; the seed picks one of 6 projections: Mercator (x = λ, y = ln tan(π/4 + φ/2)), the equirectangular (x = λ, y = φ), the sinusoidal (x = λ·cos φ, y = φ), Mollweide (x = (2√2/π)·λ·cos θ, y = √2·sin θ with 2θ + sin 2θ = π·sin φ), the stereographic projection (centred at 30°N, longitude 0) and the orthographic projection (centred at 20°N, longitude 0, drawing only the hemisphere facing us). The sampler has only the **inverses** of the projections (the latitude and longitude from the plane position), and the positions of the lines and circles use the first-order distance from the numerical gradient of the inverse. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not a cartography program; unlike `sphericaltiling` and `sphericaltriangles` (stereographic views of spherical polyhedra; I read only the beginnings of their entries) it draws a graticule and distortion circles. (The formulas of the projections are from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the graticule spacing 15°, the Tissot spacing 30° and radius 6°, the half width of the plot for each projection (π for Mercator, equirectangular, sinusoidal and Mollweide, 2.4 for the stereographic and 1.15 for the orthographic), the centres (30°N and 20°N), the line tones 0.4 / 0.62 / 1, the fill 0.07, the teal-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The distance to a line or a circle is a first-order approximation: the angle difference divided by the gradient of the angle with respect to the plane position, the gradient being the central difference of the inverse (step 1×10⁻², in units of the sphere radius); **this leaves a band about 0.01 wide (about 2.4 pixels) at the boundary of the map and at the edge of the orthographic globe with no lines**, because the neighbouring points of the difference fall outside the map. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written: the test has the **forward** formulas of the projections written separately (the sampler has only the inverses): (1) the positions of the parallels and meridians: the parallels every 15° from −75° to 75° (longitude −170° to 170° in steps of 1°) and the meridians every 15° from −165° to 165° (latitude −80° to 80° in steps of 0.5°) are projected to the plane with the forward formulas of the test and at every point inside the plot (and, for the orthographic one, inside 0.97 of the radius) the colour is above 0.38 (0.443 at the lowest in the probe, for 4197 to 11134 points per variant); (2) **a Tissot circle through the four points given by spherical geometry**: the circle of angular radius ρ (6°) about a point on the central meridian passes through the points ρ north and ρ south of it on that meridian and through the two points on the same parallel at the longitude difference arccos((cos ρ − sin²φ) / cos²φ); for the centres at latitudes 0°, 30°, −30°, 60° and −60° (30 rings, 5 for each of the 6 projections) the colour at the forward-projected positions of those four points is above 0.8 (0.85 at the lowest in the probe, the ring being brighter than the graticule) while at 0.7 and 1.3 of the way from the centre to each of them it is below 0.8 (0.72 at the highest), so the ring is where the geometry puts it and not 30% in or out; points of the orthographic globe beyond 0.97 of the radius are not tested (the band with no lines above); (3) **the outline of the map**: at the outline of the equirectangular, sinusoidal, Mollweide and orthographic maps (the meridians ±180°, the sides of the rectangle and the circle of radius 1) the colour 4% inside is above 0.07 (0.087 at the lowest in the probe) and 4% outside below 0.07 (0.053 at the highest); (4) **mirror symmetry**: the projections are about longitude 0, so the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs under x → −x is under 0.01 (0.0047 at most in the probe, which I suppose comes from the grain without having tested it), under y → −y too for the four projections centred on the equator (0.0049 at most), while the stereographic and orthographic views centred at 30°N and 20°N change over 0.05 of the cells (0.0927 at the lowest in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with sin 2θ changed to sin θ in the Mollweide inverse, 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the positions of the lines, the Tissot circles, the outline and the C1 sweep); with the stereographic 2·atan(ρ/2) changed to atan ρ, 4 fail (the positions of the lines, the Tissot circles, the C1 sweep and the maps); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (whether a point is inside the map plus the brightness along the equator at the forward positions; the smallest margin to the second best is only 0.028) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; this margin is small, but each of the 6 seeds passes the tests of the lines and the outline, so the correspondence is right; (b) the tests check only positions (the graticule passes through predicted points, the Tissot circles through four predicted points) and not the amount of distortion (conformal or equal-area) itself; (c) the Tissot circles are tested only for centres on the central meridian; (d) the formulas of the projections were written from my memory in both the sampler and the test, once as inverses and once as forward maps (a formula remembered wrongly would make the two disagree, which is an advantage of this design, though not a proof); (e) there is a band about 2.4 pixels wide with no lines at the boundary of the map and the edge of the globe; (f) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version used a step of 1×10⁻⁴ for the central difference of the gradient, and the C1 sweep found 651 to 2121 violations for each of the 6 configurations (second differences up to 0.6): the neighbouring points of the difference are 1e-4 apart, the rounding of 1e-16 becomes a relative error of about 1e-12, and the 1e-10 step of the C1 sweep amplifies it, which I believe is the cause (not checked separately); with a step of 1×10⁻² there are 0 violations, at the price of the band with no lines above; (2) the first run of the new tests had 1 failure: the south end of the Tissot circle at latitude −60° on the orthographic globe is less than 0.01 from the edge, inside the band with no lines (colour 0.033), and I excluded points beyond 0.97 of the radius from the Tissot test (the line test already excluded them) without changing the sampler; (3) I first wrote 0.0049 in the test comment for the mirror in x, the real maximum is 0.0047, corrected before committing.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 83, seed ^ salt)` picks a projection; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into the plane position (x, y) (y up, the half width depending on the projection); the latitude and longitude on the sphere come from the inverse of the projection (at the position and at four neighbours 1×10⁻² away) and nothing is drawn if any of them is outside the map; the gradients of the latitude and the longitude with respect to the plane position come from the central difference, the longitude difference being wrapped to (−π, π]; for the graticule the angle difference to the nearest multiple of 15° is divided by the gradient (the first-order distance, in tile units) with the kernel clamp(1 − (d / half width)²)², half width 0.0022 for a normal line and 0.0035 for the equator and the central meridian; for the Tissot circles the spherical distance (acos(sin φ sin φc + cos φ cos φc cos Δλ)) to each of the 3×3 nearby centres minus 6° is divided by the gradient of that distance, with a ring half width of 0.002; ink is the union `1 − Π(1 − tone·kernel)` (fill 0.07, graticule 0.4, equator and central meridian 0.62, Tissot rings 1) times the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (5 inverses and up to 9 circle centres with distances and gradients per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one projection (the 6 chosen 4, 4, 6, 4, 9 and 13 times; seeds 8, 4, 5, 17, 0 and 1 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations (gradient step 1×10⁻²); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.150%/1.508%/1.665%, color is 0.025575–0.026096 to 0.869334–0.871393 with a mean of 0.096053–0.126247, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.869253–0.872036 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.36%/1.79%/2.14%/2.37%, color is 0.025216–0.025385 to 0.872845–0.874153 with a mean of 0.095805–0.126045, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.874429–0.878033 relief; between seeds 8 and 4 2.79% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (20.66, 40.11, 46.33), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0469 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`diffractionpatterns` adds diffraction patterns, bringing the current catalog from 1104 to 1105 kinds (1106 gallery choices including plain). Cream-coloured light and dark patterns on a dark blue-black: the intensity of far-field (Fraunhofer) diffraction, the pattern of a single aperture times the array factor of N equal apertures in a row: a circular aperture gives the Airy pattern (2·J₁(ρ) / ρ)² with ρ = a·r, whose first dark ring is at ρ = 3.8317, then 7.0156, 10.1735, … (the zeros of J₁); a rectangular aperture gives sinc²(a·x)·sinc²(b·y), which is zero on the whole lines x = nπ / a and y = nπ / b, making a cross-shaped grid; the array factor of N apertures is [sin(Nφ) / (N·sin φ)]² with φ = (spacing / diameter)·a·x' (x' being the coordinate along the row), the principal maxima being at φ = mπ with N − 1 dark lines and N − 2 secondary maxima between neighbouring ones, so N = 2 is Young's double hole (fringes inside the Airy envelope); the brightness is compressed as (1 + 0.02)·I / (I + 0.02) so that the secondary maxima can be seen; the seed picks one of 6 configurations: a circular aperture with a = 22, a circular aperture with a = 36, a rectangular aperture (20 and 32), 2 circular holes (a = 26, the spacing 3 diameters, horizontal), 5 circular holes (a = 22, the spacing 4, at 35°) and 3 circular holes (a = 30, the spacing 2.5, vertical). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic scalar far-field approximation, not a full wave-optics simulation. Unlike `twosourcewaves` (the hyperbolic interference of two point sources) and `zoneplate` (a plate of concentric rings; I read only the beginning of its entry) it is the Fraunhofer diffraction of finite apertures. (The formulas of the Airy pattern, of sinc and of the array factor are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the zeros of J₁ are computed in the test by the power series and Newton's method.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1, the parameters of the 6 configurations, the brightness compression constant 0.02, the cream-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The sampler integrates J₁(x) = (1 / 2π)∫cos(t − x·sin t)dt with a 64-point trapezoid rule; **I did not measure the accuracy of that integral on its own** and it is only checked indirectly by the tests below (the positions of the zeros, the correlation with the intensity from the power series). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the test sums the power series for J₁, finds the zeros by Newton's method and writes the array factor as the direct ratio of sines): (1) the intensity correlation: on a 96×96 grid (within 0.45 of the middle) the correlation of the colour with the tone of the intensity written in the test (with the same compression) is above 0.99 for the configuration of the seed (0.995 to 0.996 in the probe) and below 0.85 for each other configuration (0.734 at most in the probe); (2) **dark rings at the zeros of J₁**: perpendicular to the row (where the array factor is 1) the darkest point near the first and second zeros (3.83171 and 7.01559, divided by the scale) is within 0.002 and 0.006 of the zero (0.0007 and 0.0047 at the worst in the probe for the five circular configurations); the later rings are not tested: their contrast is too low against the grain (the offset of the third zero was up to 0.0100 in the probe, the edge of the search window); (3) **N − 1 dark lines between apertures**: along the row the zeros of the array factor are at φ = (m + k/N)π (k = 1 to N − 1) and inside the main lobe (before 0.95 of the first Airy zero, 3, 19 and 6 of them for the rows of 2, 5 and 3 apertures, 28 together) the darkest point near each is within 0.001 of it (0.0003 at the worst in the probe) and the colour there is below 0.07 (0.051 at the highest in the probe); (4) **the zero lines of a rectangular aperture**: along the whole lines x = π/a, x = 2π/a and y = π/b (from −0.6 to 0.6 in steps of 0.002) the colour stays below 0.06 (0.0535 at the highest in the probe), the middle is above 0.8 (0.856) and the middle of the first side lobe is above 0.5 (0.636); (5) **symmetry**: it is unchanged by a half turn, the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs being under 0.002 (0.0007 at the most in the probe), and for the configurations whose row lies along an axis (or that are a single aperture) the mirrors are under 0.002 too (0.00052 at the most), while for the row of 5 at 35° a mirror changes over 0.005 of the cells (0.0142). Mutation checks (done twice): with the sine term of the J₁ integral removed, 7 of the 9 tests of that describe fail; with the starting value 2cos φ of the array-factor recurrence changed to cos φ, 5 fail; both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the correlation with the independent intensity, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.266) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the compression formula of the brightness is repeated in the test; (c) only the first two Airy rings and the array zeros inside the main lobe are tested, not the heights of the secondary maxima; (d) it is a scalar Fraunhofer approximation, with no Fresnel region or obliquity effects; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version of the array factor used the direct ratio sin(Nφ) / (N·sin φ) and returned 1 where the denominator is below 1×10⁻⁹, and the C1 sweep found 6 violations for the row of 5 at 35° (second differences of about 0.15, near the principal-maximum lines φ ≈ mπ, which I believe is rounding when numerator and denominator both approach 0, not checked separately); using the recurrence of the Chebyshev polynomial U(N − 1)(cos φ) (sin(Nφ) / sin φ = U(N − 1)(cos φ), no division) gave 0 violations for the 6 configurations; (2) the new tests all passed the first time (10 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 82, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; a table of 64 values of cos(2πk/64) and sin(2πk/64) and the `Float64Array(128²)` of grain are prepared. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into (x, y) (y up, half width 1); for a circular aperture ρ = a·√(x² + y²) and the single-aperture intensity is (2·J₁(ρ) / ρ)² (J₁ by the 64-point trapezoid rule, two trigonometric functions per point); for a rectangular one (sinc(a·x)·sinc(b·y))²; the array factor of N apertures is the square of U(N − 1)(cos φ) / N by the Chebyshev recurrence (φ = the spacing ratio·a·(x·cos θ + y·sin θ)); I = the single-aperture intensity times the array factor and tone = 1.02·I / (I + 0.02); ink = edge fade·tone, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (about 128 trigonometric calls per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 5, 10, 8, 10, 4 and 3 times; seeds 7, 12, 1, 0, 10 and 2 for the configurations 0 to 5); the first four zeros of J₁ (in the test, by the power series and Newton's method) are 3.83171, 7.01559, 10.17347 and 13.32369; the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 0.768%/1.474%/0.774%, color is 0.025413–0.025752 to 0.860830–0.871120 with a mean of 0.056670–0.062489, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.850796–0.872328 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 0.797%/1.472%/0.794%/1.481%, color is 0.025122–0.025232 to 0.861966–0.873948 with a mean of 0.056686–0.078087, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.854847–0.877750 relief; between seeds 7 and 12 0.911% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (25.44, 26.11, 37.74), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0020 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`errordiffusion` adds error-diffusion dithering, bringing the current catalog from 1103 to 1104 kinds (1105 gallery choices including plain). Pale round dots on a dark blue-black: a black-and-white dithered image of 96×96 cells, each cell being lit (a pale dot) or dark (a very faint small dot); a grey-level source image is turned into black and white by error diffusion: the cells are processed in raster order (left to right, top to bottom), the value of a cell is the grey level of the source plus the error diffused to it from the cells already processed, a value ≥ 0.5 is lit, and the error = value − output (0 or 1) is shared with the cells not yet processed according to the kernel (what falls outside the grid is dropped); the seed picks one of 6 configurations (kernel × source image): Floyd–Steinberg (7, 3, 5, 1 over 16) on a horizontal ramp, Atkinson (six cells of 1 over 8, sending on only 3/4 of the error) on a horizontal ramp, Jarvis–Judice–Ninke (over 48) on 8 steps, Stucki (over 42) on a radial ramp, Burkes (over 32) on a diagonal ramp and Sierra Lite (2, 1, 1 over 4) on 8 steps. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.03), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern; unlike ordered dithering such as `bayerdither` (I read only the beginning of its entry), the pattern comes from the error being passed on cell by cell. (The weights of the kernels and Atkinson's 3/4 are from my memory; I checked the sums of the weights with a small program: 16/16, 6/8, 48/48, 42/42, 32/32 and 4/4; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 96 cells, the margin 0.03, the 8 steps, the 6 configurations (the pairing of kernel and image), the lit tone 0.92 with a dot radius of 0.47 cell, the dark tone 0.1 with a radius of 0.12 cell, the pale-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being: (1) **cell by cell agreement**: the lit/dark state read back at the centres of the 96×96 cells equals the error diffusion written in the test as a **pull** (the error arriving in a cell is the sum of the shares of the errors of the cells already processed, where the sampler pushes the error to the cells to come) in every cell (0 cells differ in the probe, the test allows 0.001 for ties in the floating-point sums), while the dither of each of the other 5 configurations differs from the read-back for over 0.2 of the cells (0.2998 at the lowest in the probe); (2) **the mean grey level is kept**: the kernels whose weights add up to 1 send the whole error on, so the number of lit cells equals the sum of the grey levels of the source image (the error can only fall off the edges): the difference is under 0.01 of the cells (0.0053 at the most in the probe, for all six), and on strips of 12 columns the lit fraction differs from the mean grey level by under 0.03 for the five kernels that keep the error (0.026 at the most in the probe), while Atkinson (which sends on only 3/4 of the error) goes over 0.05 (0.0853), with a negative sign in the darkest strip and a positive one in the lightest (−0.058 and 0.058 in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with one weight of Floyd–Steinberg changed from 5 to 4, 2 of the 6 tests of that describe fail (the cell-by-cell agreement and the seed difference) and the mean-grey-level test does **not** notice (the weights then add up to 15/16 and the difference stays under 0.01); with the lit/dark threshold changed from 0.5 to 0.6, 3 of the 6 fail (the tone ranges, the cell-by-cell agreement and the mean grey level); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the agreement with the dither, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.300) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the weights of the kernels were written from my memory in both the sampler and the test, so (1) cannot find a weight that I remembered wrongly in the same way twice; I checked the sums with a small program but did not compare with the literature; (c) the pull and the push are two ways of writing the same algorithm, not two algorithms, with a different order of the floating-point sums; (d) the local density of 8×8 blocks deviates more (0.04 to 0.12 at the most in the probe), so the tests use only the whole picture and the strips of 12 columns; (e) only the raster order is used, no serpentine scan. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version mapped the cells to the plot area treating the half width as the full width, so the picture took only about a quarter of the middle of the tile, which I noticed in the preview; it was changed to (fu − 0.5) / (2·half width) + 0.5 and measured again; (2) the new tests all passed the first time (7 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 81, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; the 96×96 lit/dark cells are computed by error diffusion in raster order (the grey level of the source image: the horizontal ramp column / 95, the 8 steps (⌊8·column / 96⌋ + 0.5) / 8, the radial one 1 − the distance to the centre / (√2·the distance of the centre), the diagonal ramp (column + row) / 190), using a `Uint8Array(9216)` and a `Float64Array(9216)` (about 82 KB together) and the 128² grain cache; at sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into cell coordinates, the lit or dark state of the cell is taken, with the dot kernel clamp(1 − r² / R²) (R = 0.47 cell for a lit cell, 0.12 cell for a dark one); ink = edge fade·tone (lit 0.92, dark 0.1)·kernel², color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time** (the construction is 96×96 cells with at most 12 diffusion targets each). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 6, 5, 8, 4, 3 and 14 times; seeds 5, 8, 0, 9, 4 and 1 for the configurations 0 to 5) and the read-back of every seed equals the push-form dither exactly; the colour at the centre of a lit cell is at least 0.447 and that of a dark cell at most 0.147; the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 8.086%/8.018%/8.047%, color is 0.025608–0.025695 to 0.812210–0.814435 with a mean of 0.124061–0.124657, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.795836–0.802129 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 7.65%/7.64%/7.69%/7.67%, color is 0.025224–0.025290 to 0.813773–0.815387 with a mean of 0.124593–0.125205, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.79985–0.804088 relief; between seeds 5 and 8 4.99% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.62, 42.87, 51.12), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0241 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`keplerorbits` adds Kepler orbits, bringing the current catalog from 1102 to 1103 kinds (1104 gallery choices including plain). Light violet on a dark purple-black: a star in the middle (the focus shared by all the orbits) and four elliptical orbits (thin lines) around it, with a bright dot at every **equal time step** along each orbit and a faint spoke from the star to each dot, so that the sectors between the spokes have equal areas (Kepler's second law: the dots are far apart near the perihelion and crowded near the aphelion); the positions of the dots come from Kepler's equation M = E − e·sin E (solved by Newton's method), E being the eccentric anomaly; the semi-major axis of each orbit follows from the third law, a^(3/2) proportional to the period (that is, to the number N of equal time steps in a period, so a ∝ N^(2/3)), scaled so that the largest aphelion is 0.85 (the half width of the picture being 1); the seed picks one of 6 configurations of 4 orbits, each with [dots per period, eccentricity, direction of the perihelion in degrees, the phase of the first dot], for example configuration 0 is [8, 0.55, 20°, 0], [14, 0.3, 140°, 0.4], [22, 0.5, 250°, 0.7] and [32, 0.2, 80°, 0.2] (the other 5 are in the preset). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not an ephemeris: only two-body Kepler motion without perturbations. Unlike `ellipsebilliard` (the path of a ball in an elliptical table) and `confocalconics` (a grid of confocal conics) (I read only the beginnings of their README entries), it draws Kepler's laws. (The form of Kepler's equation and of the second and third laws is from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the largest aphelion 0.85, the 4 orbits, the dots per period, eccentricity, direction and phase of each orbit, the orbit half width 0.0035, the spoke half width 0.0016, the dot radius 0.016, the star radius 0.024 (tile units), the violet-on-dark-purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version, seeds 7, 13, 1, 2, 9 and 0); in the composition the orbits all lie to one side of the star (which is in the middle of the tile) and I did not change that. The curve distance is a first-order approximation: the implicit function of the ellipse divided by its gradient. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the test solves Kepler's equation by its own Newton iteration and uses the implicit function of the ellipse and the area integral of a conic): (1) the orbits, time steps and star: of the pixels with a colour above 0.45 inside the plot (7605 to 9872 per configuration), the fraction lying within 0.8 of the half width of an ellipse of the configuration (the semi-major axes being calculated in the test from the third law a ∝ N^(2/3)), or within 1.1 dot radii of any equal-time-step dot solved in the test, or within 1.1 star radii of the star, is above 0.99 for the configuration of the seed (1.0000 in the probe) and below 0.4 for each other configuration (0.2659 at most in the probe); (2) **a bright dot at every equal time step**: at the 72 to 92 dot positions calculated in the test (for all 6 configurations) the colour is above 0.8 (0.846 at the lowest in the probe), and so it is at the star; this checks Kepler's equation (sampling the eccentric anomaly uniformly would misplace the dots on the orbits of high eccentricity) and the third law together (a wrong orbit size makes (1) and (2) fail); (3) **the second law**: for the dots at least 0.05 from the star and 0.045 from every other time step (tile units), the centre of the bright disc is read back (the weighted centroid of the colour above 0.8 within 0.025, in steps of 0.001), and for consecutive dots on one orbit that can both be read, the area swept between them, the integral of r²/2 over the angle along the conic r = a(1 − e²) / (1 + e·cos(θ − ω)), is within 4% of the area of the ellipse divided by the number of steps (5 to 41 pairs per configuration and 0.0156 at the worst in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with the number of Newton iterations changed to 0, 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the fit of the orbits and dots, the dot positions and the second law); with the exponent 2/3 of the semi-major axis changed to 0.5, 6 of the 7 fail; both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the brightness at the independent dot positions, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.848) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) **the third law was not measured independently from the picture**: the geometry of the test is calculated with a ∝ N^(2/3), so (1) and (2) only show that the picture matches that geometry; I tried to estimate a from the perihelion and aphelion distances measured along a ray in the direction of the perihelion, the error was up to 3.5% (from crossings with the lines of other orbits), the deviation from the third law came to 3.7%, which was not stable enough and I abandoned that check; (c) the second law is checked only for isolated pairs of dots (5 to 41 pairs per configuration); dots of different orbits that are too close merge into one bright spot on the picture: the number of connected pieces with a colour above 0.8 is smaller than the number of dots plus the star for configurations 1, 3, 4 and 5 (83 against 85, 92 against 93, 72 against 73 and 88 against 89), so there is no test of the number of connected dot pieces; (d) the positions of the orbit lines and the spokes are only checked through the first-order half width in (1), the spokes are not checked on their own; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first version of the isolation rule for the second-law test used 0.06 and left 0 to 13 pairs, so it was relaxed to 0.05 and 0.045, leaving 5 to 41 pairs; (2) the new tests all passed the first time (8 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 80, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; for each orbit a = scale·N^(2/3) (the scale making the largest a(1 + e) 0.85) and b = a·√(1 − e²); for every equal time step j, M = 2π(j + phase) / N, Kepler's equation E − e·sin E = M is solved by Newton's method (12 steps) and the position (a(cos E − e), b·sin E) is rotated by the direction of the perihelion, giving about 72 to 92 points; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain and these points. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into (x, y) (y up, half width 1); for every orbit the first-order distance (the implicit function ((x' + a·e) / a)² + (y' / b)² − 1 divided by its gradient) with the kernel clamp(1 − d² / 0.0035²); for every dot the distance to the point (kernel radius 0.016) and to the segment from the star to it (kernel half width 0.0016); the star is a disc of radius 0.024; ink is the union `1 − Π(1 − tone·kernel²)` (orbits 0.6, spokes 0.2, dots and star 1) times the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (two distances per dot per pixel, at most 92 dots). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 8, 7, 8, 5, 5 and 7 times; seeds 7, 13, 1, 2, 9 and 0 for the configurations 0 to 5); the total numbers of dots for the configurations 0 to 5 are 76, 84, 78, 92, 72 and 88; the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 3.055%/2.692%/2.904%, color is 0.025513–0.025618 to 0.869168–0.871102 with a mean of 0.069059–0.072856, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.866479–0.869988 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 3.02%/2.68%/2.89%/2.90%, color is 0.025125–0.025184 to 0.870660–0.872834 with a mean of 0.069079–0.072836, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.869252–0.875079 relief; between seeds 7 and 13 5.35% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (27.11, 19.36, 42.63), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0177 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`zerovelocitycurves` adds zero-velocity curves, bringing the current catalog from 1101 to 1102 kinds (1103 gallery choices including plain). Thin golden lines on a dark teal-black: the contours of the effective potential Ω = (x² + y²)/2 + (1 − μ)/r₁ + μ/r₂ of the circular restricted three-body problem (two primaries of masses 1 − μ and μ moving in circles about their centre of mass, and a third body of negligible mass) in the rotating frame, which are the boundaries of the zero-velocity curves (the Hill regions); the primaries are at (−μ, 0) and (1 − μ, 0), the half width of the picture is 1.8 (in units of the distance between the primaries), each primary being a small disc; the thin lines are about 16 contours above the minimum Ω = 3/2 − μ(1 − μ)/2 at L4 and L5, starting at 0.04 above it with a ratio of 1.45; the brighter and thicker lines are the critical contours: the three through the saddle points L1, L2 and L3 (which decide the topology of the Hill region: the dumbbell, horseshoe and tadpole regions) and the contour of L4 and L5 that shrinks to two points; L1, L2 and L3 are on the x axis at the zeros of the force along the axis (found by bisection when the sampler is built) and L4 and L5 are at (1/2 − μ, ±√3/2); the seed picks one of 6 mass ratios μ: 0.5 (equal masses), 0.3, 0.12, 0.01215 (Earth and Moon), 0.0009537 (Sun and Jupiter) and 0.04. The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern, not an orbit simulation. Unlike `cylinderflow` and `fieldlines` (contours of a potential flow and of an electric field) it is the potential of a rotating frame with a centrifugal term. (The potential of the circular restricted three-body problem, the positions of the Lagrange points and the formula for the minimum at L4 and L5 are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests use a potential, a bisection and closed forms written separately in the test.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the half width 1.8, the start 0.04 and the ratio 1.45 of the levels, the line half widths 0.0035 (regular) and 0.006 (critical) (tile units), the primary disc radius 0.06 + 0.08·mass, the 6 mass ratios, the gold-on-dark-teal-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version). The line distance is a first-order approximation: the potential difference divided by the strength of the force; 1×10⁻³ (it was 1×10⁻⁴) is added to the squared force to avoid dividing by zero at a saddle point. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written: (1) the fit: of the pixels with a colour above 0.45 (16298 to 19392 per configuration) more than 0.3 from both primaries, the fraction lying within 0.8 of the critical half width of a drawn level (regular and critical) of the potential calculated in the test is above 0.97 for the mass ratio of the seed (0.985 to 1.000 in the probe) and below 0.9 for each other mass ratio (0.836 at most in the probe, for the neighbouring ratios 0.01215 and 0.0009537); (2) **a bright critical contour through each Lagrange point**: L1, L2 and L3 are the zeros of the force along the axis found by bisection in the test, and L4 and L5 are at (1/2 − μ, ±√3/2), where the test also checks that the potential equals the minimum 3/2 − μ(1 − μ)/2 to within 1×10⁻¹²; the colour at all five points is above 0.75 (0.814 at the lowest in the probe); (3) **the number of contours across the axis**: on the axis between the primaries (starting 0.15 plus a mass-dependent part from each primary) the number of runs with a colour above 0.45 is exactly the number of roots, found in the test by sign changes and bisection, of the potential at each drawn level, plus 1 (the critical level of L1 only touches the axis there, with no sign change): 7, 7, 7, 10 and 8 for the mass ratios 0.5, 0.3, 0.12, 0.01215 and 0.04; the ratio 0.0009537 is not tested: its two closest lines are only 0.0364 apart (0.0093 in tile units, less than the sum of their half widths) and merge into one run, 11 runs against 12 roots in the probe; (4) **mirror symmetry**: the potential does not depend on the sign of y, so the fraction of cells of a 256² grid whose lit state differs is under 0.006 (0.0038 at most in the probe), and for the equal masses (μ = 0.5) the mirror about x = 0 is as well (0.0027), while for the other mass ratios it changes over 0.02 of the cells (0.0286 at the lowest in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with the critical level of L2 removed, 4 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the Lagrange points, the seed difference and the maps) but the fit and the number of contours across the axis do **not** notice (L2 lies outside the primaries and one line fewer does not change the fit fraction of the others); with the potential term of the second primary multiplied by 1.1, 7 of the 8 fail; both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the fit of the bright pixels to the independent contours, the smallest margin to the second best being 0.183; the table was measured with the squared force regularised by 1×10⁻⁴, the choice of the mass ratio for a seed does not depend on the regularisation, and the fit fractions of each mass ratio were measured again with 1×10⁻³) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) the levels of the regular contours (start, ratio, upper limit) are repeated in the test from the preset, so (1) and (3) do not check the choice of the levels; (c) the distance is a first-order approximation and is not exact near the saddle points; (d) the mass ratio 0.0009537 has no check of the contours across the axis; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments**: (1) the first probe used a fit threshold that was too loose (the largest margin was only 0.013), and using the colour at the centres of the primaries to tell the mass ratios apart tied for 0.01215 and 0.0009537 (their second primaries are less than 0.0012 apart); the tight fit fraction with the critical levels included separates them; (2) the probe found one more run on the axis than there are sign-change roots, because the critical contour of L1 is tangent to the axis, and adding that one makes them agree; (3) with 1×10⁻⁴ the C1 sweep had 1 violation each for the mass ratios 0.01215 and 0.0009537 (second differences of the occlusion of 0.0348 and 0.0307, just over 0.03, near u ≈ 0.25 and 0.49), which I believe is rounding noise amplified by large derivatives near a saddle point (not checked separately), so the regularisation was changed to 1×10⁻³ and with that the 6 configurations have 0 violations; this makes the lines a little wider near the saddle points; (4) the new tests all passed the first time (9 tests including the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 79, seed ^ salt)` picks a mass ratio μ; L1, L2 and L3 (the zeros of the force along the axis) and their potentials are found by bisection, and with the minimum 3/2 − μ(1 − μ)/2 these give 4 critical levels; the regular levels are minimum + 0.04·1.45^k while Ω < 14 (about 16); there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into (x, y) (y up, half width 1.8); Ω = (x² + y²)/2 + (1 − μ)/r₁ + μ/r₂ and the gradient is (x − (1 − μ)(x + μ)/r₁³ − μ(x − 1 + μ)/r₂³, y − (1 − μ)y/r₁³ − μy/r₂³), the strength being √(|∇Ω|² + 10⁻³) in tile units; the minimum of |Ω − level| over the regular levels and over the 4 critical levels is taken, with the kernel clamp(1 − (difference / strength)² / half width²); the primary discs have the kernel clamp(1 − r² / R²) with R = 0.06 + 0.08·mass; ink is the union `1 − Π(1 − tone·kernel²)` (regular 0.6, critical 0.95, primaries 1) times the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (about 20 level comparisons per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one mass ratio (the 6 chosen 9, 6, 5, 5, 8 and 7 times; seeds 4, 1, 2, 11, 7 and 0 for the configurations 0 to 5); the C1 sweep covers all 6 with 0 violations (regularisation 1×10⁻³); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 12.111%/11.732%/12.276%, color is 0.025414–0.025835 to 0.857597–0.864972 with a mean of 0.141510–0.150688, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.841255–0.854378 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 12.11%/11.86%/12.27%/11.73%, color is 0.025176–0.025246 to 0.857812–0.868178 with a mean of 0.141622–0.150589 (0.149346 for seed 7), AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.840009–0.862430 relief; between seeds 4 and 1 19.41% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (39.78, 45.51, 36.02), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0300 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`escapefractals` adds escape-time fractals, bringing the current catalog from 1100 to 1101 kinds (1102 gallery choices including plain). Glowing light-blue fractals on a dark blue-black: for each parameter c in the plane the escape-time iteration z → F(z) + c (z₀ = 0) is run for at most 150 steps and counts as escaped when |z|² exceeds 4096; a parameter that never escapes is inside the set (dark), and an escaped one gets a tone 0.2 + 0.7·(0.5 + 0.5·cos(2πν / 6)) from the smooth iteration count ν = n + 1 − ln(ln|z| / ln 64) / ln d, which gives a glowing gradient and contour bands around the set; the seed picks one of 6 configurations: the Burning Ship (F(z) = (|Re z| + i|Im z|)², centre (−0.45, −0.5), half width 1.8, the imaginary part growing downward), a zoom near the antenna of the Burning Ship (centre (−1.762, −0.028), half width 0.06), the tricorn (F(z) = z̄², centre (−0.3, 0), half width 1.8) and the multibrot sets of power 3, 4 and 5 (F(z) = z^d, centre (0, 0), half widths 1.5, 1.5 and 1.4). The picture is in the middle of the tile (a margin of 0.04), so it is not a periodic pattern. Unlike `mandelbrottiles` and `juliatiles` (a 64×64 table of rounded tiles of escape counts) it is a continuously sampled high-resolution picture and shows different sets. It is a schematic pattern, not a numerically exact boundary of the sets. (The definitions of the Burning Ship, the tricorn and the multibrot sets and their symmetries are from my memory and I did not check the literature; before writing the tests I measured the symmetries with a separate small program, see below.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin 0.04, the 150 iterations at most, the escape radius 64, the tone band period 6, the inside tone 0.05 and the outside tones 0.2 to 0.9, the centre and half width of each of the 6 configurations, the light-blue-on-dark-blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version, seeds 7, 0, 6, 18, 2 and 1). **It is not C1**: the boundary of the set is a fractal, the tone jumps across it and the contour lines of the escape count have kinks everywhere near it, so the C1 sweep of the other materials does not apply here (I measured it first with the usual sweep: the 6 configurations had 2408, 11072, 363, 663, 564 and 627 violations); the test instead checks that the colour is smooth far from the set (at most 6 iterations to escape, 8 for the zoom of variant 1). The tests **read only the sampler output back**, the core being checks that do not depend on how the sampler is written (the test rewrites the iteration with complex numbers as objects and with the power by repeated multiplication): (1) the independent escape-time iteration: on a 128×128 grid whether a pixel is dark (inside the set) agrees completely with the test's own iteration (0 pixels disagree in the probe, the test allows under 0.002), the inside takes 0.0773 to 0.3579 of the grid (the test requires above 0.05), and for the escaped pixels the correlation of the colour with the tone calculated in the test from the smooth iteration count is above 0.99 (0.9972 to 0.9983 in the probe; the tone formula is repeated in the test, so this checks the iteration and the smooth count and not the choice of the tone); (2) **the extent of the set on the real axis**: the orbit of a real parameter stays real, so on the real axis the Burning Ship and the tricorn are inside from −2 to 1/4 (as for z² + c), and the multibrot z^d + c from −2^(1/(d−1)) (even power) or −(d − 1)·d^(−d/(d−1)) (odd power) to (d − 1)·d^(−d/(d−1)); scanning in steps of 0.0005, the first and last inside points are within 0.001 of these closed forms (the probe found 0.25, −1.99999 and 0.25, ±0.385, −1.2595 and 0.4725, and ±0.535); the left end of the Burning Ship is not tested, because the rounding of the imaginary part, about 1e-16, is amplified by the orbit near −2 and the probe found −1.9855, which I believe is the cause but did not check separately; (3) **symmetry**: the tricorn and the multibrots are symmetric under conjugation, the tricorn has 3-fold and the multibrot of power d (d − 1)-fold rotational symmetry, and on 4000 points the inside/outside state of the mirrored or rotated parameter differs for under 0.002 of them (none in the probe); I also measured with a separate program that does not use the sampler that the Burning Ship is not symmetric under conjugation (about 33.6% of the points differ), so its symmetry is not tested; (4) **smooth far from the set and periodic**: at points that escape in at most 6 iterations (8 for variant 1) the second difference over a step of 1e-10 divided by the step is under 0.03 (7.05×10⁻⁴ at the worst in the probe, 20000 points per configuration), and shifting the UV by whole periods gives the same output (1.6×10⁻¹⁴ at the worst in the probe). Mutation checks (done twice): with the absolute value of the imaginary part removed from the Burning Ship, 4 of the 7 tests of that describe fail (the tone ranges, the independent iteration, the seed difference and the maps) while the real-axis test does not notice (the imaginary part is 0 on the real axis, so the change does not affect it); with the conjugation sign of the tricorn changed (making it the Mandelbrot set), 3 of the 7 fail (the independent iteration, the symmetry and the smoothness); both were restored (confirmed with `cmp`). **Limitations**: (a) the configuration for each seed was found with a probe (the agreement of the inside/outside classification with the independent iteration on a 40×40 grid, taking the best one, without printing the agreement fraction of each seed) and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle**; (b) being inside is decided by a colour below 0.12, so an outside pixel with a very dark tone (if any) would count as inside — the probe and the test verify against the independent iteration, with 0 disagreeing; (c) nothing checks the tone close to the boundary of the set; (d) membership uses only addition, subtraction, multiplication and absolute values, which should be identical in Node and Bun, but I measured it only in those two environments and did not verify it in a browser GPU or another engine; (e) I did not check the literature. **Record of adjustments and discarded attempts**: (1) before this I had implemented 'the points of an elliptic curve over a finite field' (`ellipticcurvedots`) and rendered previews: the dots were sparse, the tone differences (the rank of the group order) were hardly visible and most of the picture was empty, so I abandoned and reverted it without committing; (2) I measured the symmetries and the real-axis extents with a separate small program before writing the tests: the Burning Ship is not symmetric under conjugation (I had expected it to be, and only the measurement showed it is not), so I made no such claim; (3) the new tests all passed the first time (7 tests of the describe plus the kinds entry), without any threshold being adjusted.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 78, seed ^ salt)` picks a configuration; there is only the `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B for grain. At sampling time (per pixel): (u, v) is turned into the parameter c = centre + ((u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46)·half width; starting from z = 0, at most 150 times: the Burning Ship z ← (|Re z| + i|Im z|)² + c, the tricorn z ← z̄² + c, the multibrot z ← z^d + c (by repeated multiplication, not Math.pow); it escapes when |z|² > 4096; the inside has ink 0.05 and an escaped parameter has ink = 0.2 + 0.7·(0.5 + 0.5·cos(2πν / 6)), multiplied by the fade by the signed distance to the plot rectangle; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (gapTone 0.04, toneFloor 0.14, mask = smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.38, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time**; in the worst case each pixel takes 150 iterations (d − 1 complex multiplications each for the multibrot) and every pixel inside the set runs all of them; I did not time the probes. Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches one configuration (the 6 chosen 4, 5, 7, 6, 7 and 11 times; seeds 7, 0, 6, 18, 2 and 1 for the configurations 0 to 5); the inside takes 0.1828, 0.0803, 0.0773, 0.2642, 0.2932 and 0.3579 of the probe grid for the configurations 0 to 5; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 30.714%/6.033%/31.032%, color is 0.025664–0.026413 to 0.80142–0.80190 with a mean of 0.222210–0.379806, roughness is always 0.38, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.787233–0.788659 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 30.60%/6.09%/31.09%/29.09%, color is 0.025097–0.025494 to 0.80180–0.80253 with a mean of 0.222685–0.379820, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.78817–0.79019 relief; between seeds 7 and 0 27.52% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (45.51, 90.51, 106.65), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the previews (one for each of the 6 configurations, of the final version). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`fourierseries` adds Fourier-series partial sums, bringing the current catalog from 1099 to 1100 kinds (1101 gallery choices including plain). Orange curves on a dark brown-black: the tile is divided into 4 rows, each drawing one period of the Fourier **partial sum** of a waveform, with the number of terms growing from the top row to the bottom — a square wave (4/π)·Σ sin((2j + 1)x) / (2j + 1), a sawtooth (2/π)·Σ (−1)^(k+1) sin(kx) / k, or a triangle wave (8/π²)·Σ cos((2j + 1)x) / (2j + 1)²; each row has dim thin horizontal lines at 0 and ±1 (the amplitude is 0.085); the seed picks one of 6 configurations (the waveform and the number of terms of the 4 rows): a square wave with 1, 2, 4 and 10 terms; a square wave with 2, 3, 6 and 16; a sawtooth with 1, 2, 4 and 10; a triangle wave with 1, 2, 3 and 6; a sawtooth with 2, 4, 8 and 20; and a square wave with 3, 5, 8 and 20. The square wave and the sawtooth show the Gibbs phenomenon at their jumps: however many terms are summed, the first peak overshoots by about 9% of the jump and only gets narrower; the triangle wave has no jump and so no overshoot. The tile has exactly one period horizontally and the 4 rows repeat vertically, so it is a periodic pattern. It is a schematic pattern; the curve is a first-order distance approximation, so its steep parts at the jumps are drawn as a straight stroke. Unlike the other materials this one draws the graphs of functions, not a two-dimensional pattern. (The coefficients of the series and the Gibbs constant (2/π)·Si(π) ≈ 1.179 are from my memory; the test computes that constant by numerical integration; I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 4 rows, the amplitude 0.085, the curve half width 0.005 and the half width 0.0022 of the horizontal lines (tile units), the tones 0.92 / 0.16 / 0.1 of the curve and the lines, the 6 configurations, the orange-on-dark-brown-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of each of the 6 configurations once (of the final version; seeds 0 to 5 happen to cover all 6). The distance to the curve is a first-order approximation: the height difference divided by √(1 + slope²).
