The bifurcation diagram of the logistic map x → r·x·(1 − x): the horizontal axis is the parameter r, and for each column the orbit of x = 0.5 is iterated 300 times to settle and then the next 120 values are drawn, the vertical axis being x (larger x is up); so for small r there is one curve, the stable fixed point x = 1 − 1 / r, at r = 3 it splits into the 2-cycle (x = ((r + 1) ± √((r − 3)(r + 1))) / 2r), then successive period-doublings (4, 8, 16, …) lead into the chaotic bands, interrupted by stable windows of periodic orbits (the most visible being the period-3 window at r about 3.83); the whole orbit lies between f(f(1/2)) = r²(4 − r) / 16 and f(1/2) = r / 4, which are the upper and lower edges of the chaotic bands; fine cream dots on dark brown-black with a rectangular frame around; the seed picks one of 6 ranges (r start, r end, x low, x high): (2.4, 4, 0, 1) (the whole diagram), (3.4, 4, 0, 1), (3.7, 3.9, 0.05, 1), (3.5, 3.6, 0.3, 0.92), (2.9, 3.6, 0.3, 0.95) and (3.82, 3.87, 0.3, 0.96) (the period-3 window enlarged). The plot is in the middle of the tile with 0.07 left all round; it is not a periodic pattern (the edges of the tile do not join). Unlike the other kinds that draw trajectories of dynamical systems (the path of `lorenzattractor`, the damped pendulums of `harmonograph`), this is a bifurcation diagram of a parameter sweep. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The fixed point, the 2-cycle, the bounds on the orbit and the order of the bifurcations of the logistic map are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check with an independent iteration and with closed forms.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the margin of the plot 0.07, the transient of 300 iterations, 120 plotted points, the dot half width 0.0025 (in tile units), the frame half width 0.004, the fade 0.01, the 2048 column steps, the 6 ranges, the cream-on-dark-brown colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of the final version for seeds 1, 8, 7, 13, 2 and 0 (sets 0 to 5 by the probe's table), so all 6 ranges have been seen. The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) with an **independent iteration** (written as r·x − r·x² and not as the sampler's r·x·(1 − x), with the preset's 300 steps of transient, requiring the point set after them to equal that after 20000 steps, the Lyapunov exponent to be below −0.05 and at most 40 points, so that only columns whose orbit has really settled are taken) the points of the stable cycles of each range are found, and those of the range of each seed (487, 438, 216, 1136, 743 and 196 for the ranges, at least 0.015 inside the edge of the plot) all have a colour above 0.5 (1.000 in the probe), while for each other range fewer than 30% of its points do (at most 0.131 in the probe, 0.226 with the columns the test lists); (2) in such columns (with all the points at least 8 rows from the edge of the counting window and the points either within 1.5 rows of each other or more than 6 apart) the number of runs of bright pixels equals the number of groups of points (5 to 49 columns per range in the probe, 0 mismatches), that is, there are no extra bright dots; (3) the **bounds** (closed forms): no pixel inside the plot (0.02 off the edge) with a colour above 0.6 has an x above r / 4 or below r²(4 − r) / 16 by more than 1% of the range of x (0.0023 at worst in the probe, with 1.9 to 35 thousand bright pixels per range); (4) the **closed forms of the fixed point and the 2-cycle**: for r from 2.45 to 2.95 the only stable point is x = 1 − 1 / r and for r from 3.12 to 3.38 they are ((r + 1) ± √((r − 3)(r + 1))) / (2r) (covered by ranges 0 and 4), and such a column has exactly one bright run (two for the 2-cycle) whose middle is within 1.5 rows of the closed form. Mutation check (done once): with the map multiplied by 0.99, 6 of the 8 tests of that describe fail (ranges and tones, stable cycle points, run counts, bounds, closed forms and the difference between ranges) while the C1 and maps ones still pass; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) only **stable** columns and the bounds are checked, **the chaotic bands are checked only by the bounds (the upper and lower edges), not by the density distribution in them or the positions of the bifurcation points** (a chaotic orbit is sensitive to the last bit, so there is no point-by-point comparison); (b) the number of column steps 2048 and the transient of the preset are shared by both sides; (c) the range for each seed (seeds 1, 8, 7, 13, 2, 0 for the ranges 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered). **On continuity (important)**: in the chaotic bands the orbit is extremely sensitive to r (when I first took r for the column of each pixel directly, the C1 sweep had thousands of violations with second differences as large as about 1.5×10¹⁰, because a change of 1e-10 in r makes all the points of the column different), so **r is taken at the middle of one of 2048 column steps, the picture is constant along u within a column step and jumps at the boundaries of the steps (2047 of them), the jumps being large in the chaotic bands**; the C1 sweep therefore avoids the boundaries of the steps (including u = 0.5, which is exactly the boundary of steps 1023 and 1024), and after the repeated points of a cycle are removed the jump of the second derivative at the edge of the kernel is not amplified by identical points; **continuity along u is not claimed**. The maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0444, unlike the 0.0543 and others of earlier kinds, which I did not look into further. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid; as the chaotic bands vary a lot with how the grid meets them, the ranges of the lit area and the mean are wide.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 66, seed ^ salt)` picks a range (r start, r end, x low, x high); the plot is in the middle of the tile with 0.07 left all round, its width being span = 0.86. At sampling time (per pixel): the signed distance to the rectangle of the plot gives the frame (half width 0.004, tone 0.45) and the fade `smooth(clamp(−distance / 0.01))`; inside the plot u is turned into the position c ∈ [0, 1] along the columns, the column step is k = floor(c·2048) and r = r start + ((k + 0.5) / 2048)·(r end − r start); for that step (computed when first needed and remembered) the orbit of x = 0.5 under x → r·x·(1 − x) is iterated 300 times and the next 120 values are taken, those within 1e-9 of an earlier one being kept once (a point on a cycle is drawn once); v is turned into the value of x = x high − (row position)·(x high − x low); for each point the vertical (x direction) distance to it (in tile units) gives `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.0025)²)` and the coverage of the dots is `1 − Π(1 − t²)`; ink is `clamp(0.9·fade·coverage + 0.45·frame²)`; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the points of each column step (at most 2048 steps, each with at most 120 doubles, about 2 MB, built only for the steps that are used) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (one iteration per column step, and up to 120 kernels per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one range (the 6 ranges chosen 9, 7, 7, 6, 6 and 5 times); the C1 sweep covers all 6 ranges (seeds 1, 8, 7, 13, 2, 0) with 0 violations (avoiding the boundaries of the column steps; see above); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 4.80%–16.37%, color is 0.02565–0.02570 to 0.80107–0.80178 with a mean of 0.08480–0.17591, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.7866–0.7881 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 4.70%–16.25%, color is 0.02515–0.02525 to 0.80179–0.80274 with a mean of 0.08348–0.17474, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.7881–0.7907 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 10.1% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (9.95% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (56.1, 49.3, 33.0), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0444 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`zordercurve` adds the Z-order (Morton) curve, bringing the current catalog from 1088 to 1089 kinds (1090 gallery choices including plain). The 2^b × 2^b cells of a grid (4×4, 8×8, 16×16) are put in a row in the Z order (Morton order): the index of the cell (column, row) is the number made by interleaving the bits of the row and the column (at each level the bit of the row and then that of the column; the other way round for the transposed N order); cells with consecutive indices are joined by a straight segment between their centres, so the curve repeats a "Z" at every scale and has big jumps (it is not a continuous space-filling curve, unlike the Hilbert curve); the nodes (the cell centres) are small dots whose tone rises along the curve from dark (0.3) to bright (0.95), the lines having a fixed tone 0.7; magenta on dark purple; the seed picks one of 6 pairs (b, transposed): (2, Z), (3, Z), (4, Z), (2, N), (3, N) and (4, N); the whole curve fills the tile and no line crosses the seam (half a cell is left at each end). Unlike `hilbertcurve`, `peanocurve` and `moorecurve` (continuous space-filling curves, the Hilbert one closing across the tile seam and the Peano one shifted around the torus by the seed), the Z-order curve has big jumps between neighbouring cells and keeps the structure of the interleaved bits. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on the Morton order and the interleaving of bits are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below build the order independently from binary strings.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the line half width 0.08 cell, the node radius 0.2 cell, the line tone 0.7, the node tones 0.3 to 0.95, the 6 pairs (b, transposed), the magenta-on-dark-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5 (the lines are a little blurred after the scaling of the preview), which by the probe's table cover sets 1, 4, 0 and 5; **set 2 (16×16 Z order) and set 3 (4×4 N order) have not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) the **Morton order is built from binary strings** (not with the shifts of the sampler): the index of a cell is read from the string that puts, from the most significant bit down, the bit of the row and then that of the column at each level (or the other way round for the transposed order), the cells are sorted by index to give the nodes, and on the segment between each pair of consecutive nodes the check points at 0.3, 0.5 and 0.7 (off the node discs and on the lines; 45, 189 and 765 for the sets) are taken; at most 2 of the check points of the variant of each seed may read lower than 0.5, and each of the other 5 sets has at least 10 check points reading lower (at least 18 in the probe); (2) at the points of a low-discrepancy sequence that are more than 0.3 cell from every segment and more than 0.35 cell from every node (brute-force distances; about 4 to 6 thousand per seed in the probe, and the test takes 8,000 points and requires more than 1,500 of them to qualify) the colour is below 0.1 (0.055 at most in the probe); (3) the colour at the centre of node number i of n equals 0.14 + 0.72 × (nodeLow + (nodeHigh − nodeLow)·i / (n − 1)) to within 0.03 (0.0172 at most in the probe, the grain being ±0.015), so it rises from dark to light along the curve. Mutation check (done once): with the interleaving of the bits replaced by a row-major order, all the dedicated tests except the C1 one fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: nodeLow, nodeHigh and the line width of the preset are shared by both sides; (1) checks only the middles of the segments, not the ends near the nodes or the shape of the node discs, and (2) checks only the dark places, **not the line width**; the variant for each seed (seeds 5, 0, 9, 7, 2, 4 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered); seeds 0 and 1 give the same variant, so the seed-difference test uses seeds 0 and 2. **On C1**: the distance of the lines is the minimum over the segments, so where two segments meet at a node, outside the node disc and near the bisector of the angle between them, the minimum has a crease that may lie inside the line band (the line half width is 0.08 and the node disc radius 0.2; for an angle of 45 degrees the point on the bisector at 0.08 from both segments is about 0.21 cell from the node, just outside the node disc); the C1 sweep (random samples) did not meet a violation, but **I did not look at those places, so C1 near the nodes is not claimed**. The maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0020, far below other kinds (thin lines and little difference in tone; I did not look into it). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid; the extreme brightness and the highest height vary with how the grid meets the lines, so the ranges are wider.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 65, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (b, transposed), the side being s = 2^b and the number of nodes n = s²; the index of each cell (column, row) is found: over the b bit levels the k-th bit of the column (of the row when transposed) is put at bit 2k of the index and the k-th bit of the row (of the column when transposed) at bit 2k + 1; the centre of the cell with that index is stored as the node. At sampling time (per pixel) the tile coordinates are multiplied by s, the distance of the point to each of the n − 1 segments between consecutive nodes is found (the projection parameter clamped to 0 to 1) and the least is taken, and the node disc of the cell the point is in is found; the coverage of the lines is `t = clamp(1 − distance² / 0.08²)`, that of the node is `clamp(1 − (distance to the cell centre)² / 0.2²)`, and ink is `0.7·t²·(1 − node²) + node tone·node²` (node tone = 0.3 + 0.65·index / (n − 1)); color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the table of nodes (at most 256 × 2 doubles) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (every pixel scans all the segments, 255 for 16×16, with no spatial index, and I did not measure the cost of this on a large map). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one variant (the 6 sets chosen 7, 9, 4, 7, 7 and 6 times); the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 5, 0, 9, 7, 2, 4) with 0 violations (at the first try); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 9.935%–9.967%, color is 0.02540–0.02592 to 0.8152–0.8300 with a mean of 0.13039–0.13055, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.7976–0.8191 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 8.30%–9.38%, color is 0.02509–0.02526 to 0.8194–0.8363 with a mean of 0.11993–0.13031, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8062–0.8299 relief; between seeds 0 and 2 (8×8 Z order and 16×16 N order) 12.7% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (seeds 0 and 1 are the same variant and differ by only 0.10%, from the grain); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (57.0, 26.2, 52.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0020 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`polygonoffsets` adds the offset curves of a polygon, bringing the current catalog from 1087 to 1088 kinds (1089 gallery choices including plain). A polygon stands in the middle of the disc (6 of them: a five-pointed star, a six-pointed star, an L, a triangle, a cross and an arrow), and a line is drawn at every fixed step (0.045 disc radii) of the signed distance to the polygon (negative inside, positive outside), that is the offset curves of the polygon: outside, the corners of the curves are circular arcs (the equidistant lines from the corners), and inside they are sharp corners (the folds on the medial axis); the bands between the lines are coloured with four tones by inside or outside and the parity of the band number (0.08 and 0.2 outside, 0.32 and 0.48 inside), as thin green lines on dark green; the disc radius is 0.46 of the tile (diameter 0.92), the outside fades out between 0.94 and 0.96 with a ring added, and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam; the seed picks one of the 6 polygons. Unlike `topographicmap` (contours of a sinusoidal terrain, every fifth line heavy) and `kaleidoscope` (iso-bands of an averaged noise), the distance field here is the geometric distance to a polygon and the lines are exact offset curves. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on offset curves, signed distance and the medial axis are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below compute the distance by brute force and check independently.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the step 0.045, the line half width 0.009, the ring half width 0.004, the fade range 0.94 to 0.96, the vertices of the 6 polygons (the five-pointed star with the outer radius 0.55 and the inner radius 0.23, the six-pointed star with 0.55 and 0.30, the L, the triangle, the cross and the arrow), the four band tones, the green-on-dark-green colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, which by the table cover all 6 polygons. The tests **read only the sampler output back** and compute the distance **by brute force and not with the formula of the sampler**: the least distance to 401 points taken along each side of the polygon, and the inside by the winding number (the sum of the angles the sides subtend at the point, 2π inside and 0 outside); (1) a **forward construction**: from the middle of each side, along its normal, the signed distances ±(k + f) steps (k = 1 to 30, f = 0 on a line and f = 0.5 in the middle of a band) are walked, keeping only the points whose brute-force distance equals the distance walked to within 0.001 (that is, where that side is the nearest part) and that are within 0.85 of the middle; all the check points on the lines of the polygon of each seed (70, 72, 61, 54, 88 and 72 for the shapes) read bright with at most 2 lower than 0.7, each of the other 5 shapes has at least 20 check points reading lower (at least 43 in the probe), and the check points in the middle of a band all read below 0.6 (at most 0.5 in the probe); (2) the **offset property**: for every pixel of the 256 by 256 reading within 0.85 of the middle with a colour above 0.78, the brute-force signed distance is within 0.006 of a whole multiple of the step (0.0032 at worst in the probe, with 3,064 to 3,479 pixels per seed); (3) the colours in the middle of a band: outside even below 0.18 (0.098 to 0.125 in the probe), outside odd from 0.19 to 0.30 (0.231 to 0.259), inside even from 0.30 to 0.42 (0.356 to 0.380; the star shapes have none, their inside bands being too narrow to have a band midpoint where a side is the nearest part) and inside odd from 0.43 to 0.56 (0.472 to 0.498). Mutation check (done once): with the position of the lines multiplied by a factor 1.02, these two tests and the range test fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: the vertex data of the polygons come from the preset, shared by both sides; the band midpoints cover only the places where a side is the nearest part, so the arc regions near the corners and the bands near the medial axis are covered only by the property (2) of the bright line pixels; the polygon for each seed (seeds 0, 1, 5, 2, 4, 3 for the shapes 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 are covered). **Important limitation on C1**: the offset curves have **folds on the medial axis inside and on the cut locus outside (for the concave shapes), which are not C1**; in the first C1 sweep, with random and grid samples, some grid points fell exactly on the axes of symmetry (u = 0.5 and so on), giving 348 and 622 violations with second differences up to about 563, which I judge to be real folds on the medial axis (they lie on the axes of symmetry) — **I did not check the other violation records (one per point, axis and channel) one by one**; the later sweep, with the grid made of odd divisions (13, 129, 509) and y values off the axes of symmetry, has 0 violations for all 6 polygons, so the test covers only points that avoid the medial axis and the cut locus and **does not claim that the whole picture is C1**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning; the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0543, the same as for several earlier kinds. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 64, seed ^ salt)` picks a polygon (its vertices being preset data). At sampling time (per pixel) the disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46` are taken and for each side the distance of the point to the segment (the projection parameter clamped to 0 to 1) is found; the least is the distance, the parity of the number of ray crossings gives inside or outside, and that gives the signed distance s (negative inside); the distance to the nearest line is |s − step·round(s / step)|, `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.009)²)` and the coverage of the lines is t²; the band number is floor(|s| / step), and the fill by inside or outside and the parity of the band number is 0.08 or 0.2 outside and 0.32 or 0.48 inside; the content of the disc is multiplied by the fade outside `smooth(clamp((0.94 − r) / 0.02))` and a thin ring (radius 1) is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`, ink = `fill·(1 − line) + line`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (one projection for each of at most 12 sides per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matches exactly one polygon (the 6 polygons chosen 7, 7, 9, 7, 7 and 3 times); the C1 sweep (with the grid avoiding the axes of symmetry) covers all 6 polygons with 0 violations (the first sweep, which included grid points on the axes of symmetry, had violations, see above); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 14.83%–15.01%, color is 0.02563–0.02586 to 0.87257–0.87422 with a mean of 0.22502–0.22988, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8735–0.8779 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 14.72%–14.98%, color is 0.02519–0.02535 to 0.87394–0.87450 with a mean of 0.22486–0.22971, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8773–0.8788 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 20.8% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (20.9% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (53.3, 78.2, 41.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`powerdiagram` adds the power diagram (Laguerre–Voronoi diagram), bringing the current catalog from 1086 to 1087 kinds (1088 gallery choices including plain). The tile is divided into c × c cells (c = 5, 6, 7) with one disc in each (its centre jittered inside the cell and its radius 0.19 ± 0.09·spread cell widths, the discs not touching each other), and the whole tile is divided into polygonal cells by the power: the power of a point p about a circle (c, r) is |p − c|² − r², each point belongs to the circle of least power, the edges between cells lie on the radical axes (the lines of equal power) of two circles and so are straight; with equal radii it is the ordinary Voronoi diagram and with different radii the edges move towards the smaller circle; thin coral lines (the cell edges and the outlines of the discs) on dark wine, the inside of a disc in two tones (0.5 and 0.65, chosen at random by the hash) and the rest of the cell dark (0.12); the seed picks one of 6 pairs (c, spread): (5, 0), (6, 0.5), (7, 1), (5, 1), (6, 1) and (7, 0.5); the figure is periodic with the tile, the discs are all inside their own cells, and the edges of the cells may cross the seam. Unlike `voronoicells` (one jittered site per cell, split into colour plates by the nearest site, with soft weights to keep C1), the cells here are decided by the power of discs with radii, the edges are radical axes and the discs themselves are drawn. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on the power, radical axes and the power diagram are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below read the picture back only, find the discs in it and then check the edges independently.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the line half width 0.035 cell, the disc radii 0.19 ± 0.09·spread cells, the range of the centres (0.35 to 0.65 of the cell width), the 6 pairs (c, spread), the three fills (0.12, 0.5, 0.65), the coral-on-wine colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. **The first preview looked too much like an ordinary Voronoi diagram** (radii 0.2 ± 0.06·spread, centres from 0.3 to 0.7, a variant with c = 8) and the edges moved too little from the midlines; after seeing it I changed to the present radii and range of centres and replaced the variants with c = 8 by c = 5 and 7; I looked at the final preview for seeds 0 to 5, which by the table found from the picture cover sets 0, 3, 1, 4 and 5; **set 2 ((7, 1)) has not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back**, find the discs in the picture and then check the edges independently: (1) the 4-connected regions of at least 60 pixels in the 512 by 512 reading with a colour from 0.42 to 0.70 and a roundness (2πI / area²) within 0.03 of 1 are taken as discs (the bands of the lines are not round and are excluded), the radius of the outline of a disc being the colour-weighted mean distance from the centroid of the bright pixels (colour above 0.7) within 7 pixels outside its region; the number of discs is c², each has a roundness within 0.01 of 1 (0.002 at worst in the probe), the centres are at 0.35 to 0.65 of the width of the cell (within 1.5 pixels), and the difference between the largest and the smallest radius over 2 × 0.09 × the cell width equals the spread of the variant to within 0.1 (0.03, 0.49 and 0.94 for the spreads 0, 0.5 and 1 in the probe); (2) the **radical axis property**: for every bright line pixel (colour above 0.78, more than 5 pixels from every outline), using the centres and outline radii found in the picture (plus copies in the eight neighbouring tiles), the two circles of least power are found and the distance of the point from the line of equal power of the two, (power_b − power_a) / (2|c_a − c_b|), has a median below 0.6 pixel, a 99th percentile below 1.1 pixels and a maximum below 1.8 pixels (0.30 to 0.46, 0.69 to 0.95 and 0.81 to 1.40 in the probe; a pixel is 1), and in the variants whose radii differ (all but the first) the same distance with the radii ignored (the ordinary Voronoi bisector) has a 99th percentile above 1.3 (1.5 to 3.8 in the probe), so the edges are those of the power diagram and not of the Voronoi diagram. Mutation check (done once): changing the power to the plain squared distance makes both tests, the range test, the seed-difference test and the maps test fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: (a) the positions and outline radii of the discs are estimated from the picture, so the residuals include pixel quantisation (the tolerances are in pixels); (b) only the bright line pixels are checked, not the line width or the tones (the distribution of the two tones of the discs is not checked); (c) the discs not touching is guaranteed by the design, so the tests do not cover a power diagram of intersecting discs; (d) the cell width and the range of the jitter come from the preset data, shared by both sides; (e) near the vertices of the cells the lines take the minimum of the distances to the nearest radical axes, so **there is a short stretch (within the line half width) inside a cell near each vertex where the distance function has a crease and is not C1**; the C1 sweep (random samples) did not meet it, so C1 near the vertices cannot be claimed. The variant for each seed (seeds 0, 2, 15, 1, 3, 5 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, but each variant is also checked against the number of discs and the range of the radii read from the picture. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning; the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0260, unlike the 0.0543, 0.0378, 0.0197 and 0.0075 of earlier kinds, which I did not look into further. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid; as every pixel belongs to some cell there is no ground colour, and color is at least about 0.139 and AO at least about 0.709 (unlike 0.0255 and 0.6 for other kinds).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 63, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (c, spread); for the (c + 4) × (c + 4) cells covering the tile and two cells beyond on each side the centre of a cell is (column + 0.35 + 0.3·h₁, row + 0.35 + 0.3·h₂) (h being hashes of the wrapped cell numbers), the radius is 0.19 + spread·0.09·(2h₃ − 1) and the tone choice is h₄ < 0.5; they are stored in a `Float64Array`. At sampling time (per pixel) the tile coordinates are multiplied by c and made periodic, and among the 5 × 5 sites about the cell the power |p − c|² − r² of each is found, the one of least power giving the circle the point belongs to; the distance to a cell edge is the least over the other sites of (power_j − power_i) / (2|c_j − c_i|) (for a convex cell this is the distance to its boundary); the distance to the outline of the disc is `| |p − c| − r |`; each gives `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.035)²)` and the coverage of the lines is `1 − (1 − t₁²)(1 − t₂²)`; the fill is 0.5 or 0.65 inside a disc (power below 0) and 0.12 elsewhere; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`, ink = `fill·(1 − line) + line`), height is `0.8·line·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark (0.709 at the least in this kind, whose whole tile is filled) and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the table of sites ((c + 4)² × 4 doubles, about 3.9 KB for c = 7) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (25 sites scanned twice per pixel). Measured (tool-run): the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 0, 2, 15, 1, 3, 5) with 0 violations (at the first try, but see the limitation about the creases at the vertices above); in the analysis of seeds 0 to 39 from the picture every seed finds exactly one matching (c, spread), the 6 sets being chosen 5, 10, 6, 5, 8 and 6 times (none unmatched); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 19.70%–20.53%, color is 0.13894–0.13929 to 0.87277–0.87311 with a mean of 0.27557–0.28191, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.709 and height is at most 0.8740–0.8755 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 19.52%–20.53%, color is 0.13873–0.13879 to 0.87416–0.87429 with a mean of 0.27456–0.28192, AO is at least 0.709 and height is at most 0.8778–0.8784 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 27.5% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (27.6% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (91.8, 48.4, 47.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0260 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`reuleauxfield` adds the Reuleaux polygon field, bringing the current catalog from 1085 to 1086 kinds (1087 gallery choices including plain). The tile is divided into c × c square cells (c = 3, 4 or 5), and in the middle of each cell stands a Reuleaux polygon — a curve of constant width: for an odd number n of corners (3, 5, 7) a regular n-gon, a circle drawn about each corner with the distance between opposite corners as the radius, and the intersection of those n discs; its width is the same in every direction (Barbier's theorem; the Reuleaux triangle is the best known example), and the larger n is the closer it is to a circle; the width of every polygon is 0.8 of the cell, each is turned by a random angle in [0, 2π / n), so every shape is inside its own cell and does not cross the seam; thin teal lines on dark teal-black, the inside of a polygon filled with two alternating tones (0.3 and 0.5) by the parity of the sum of the cell's column and row; the seed picks one of 6 pairs (n, c): (3, 4), (3, 5), (5, 4), (5, 3), (7, 3) and (7, 4). Unlike the other materials that arrange shapes in cells, what is drawn here is a curve of constant width, the positions of the corners and arcs being fixed by n. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on Reuleaux polygons and Barbier's theorem and the area formula are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below read the picture back only and check it with geometric properties that do not use the construction.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the line half width 0.035 cell, the shape width 0.8 cell, the 6 pairs (n, c), the two fills (0.3 and 0.5), the teal-on-dark-teal colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5 (each preview crops only the top-left 512 pixels of one tile), which by the table cover sets 3, 2, 4 and 0; **set 1 ((3, 5)) and set 5 ((7, 4)) have not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back** and do not use the construction at all: the 4-connected regions of at least 2500 pixels with a colour from 0.32 to 0.62 in the 512 by 512 reading are taken as the shapes; (1) the number of shapes is c²; every shape has widths (the extent of the pixel centres along a direction plus one pixel) that differ by less than 3.5 pixels over 180 directions (at most 2.38 in the probe, with a width of about 97 to 130) and the mean widths of the shapes of one picture differ by less than 2.5 pixels (at most 1.58 in the probe); the area over the squared mean width is within 2% of the textbook Reuleaux polygon (the area of the regular n-gon plus n circular segments: (n / 2)R²sin(2π / n) + (n / 2)w²(π / n − sin(π / n)), R = w / (2cos(π / 2n)), giving 0.705, 0.759 and 0.772; 0.3% to 1.4% less in the probe because the lines eat the rim); the ratio of the largest to the smallest distance from the centroid to the boundary is within 0.06 of R / (w − R) (1.37, 1.11 and 1.05; the worst shapes in the probe are 0.040 off for 3 corners, 0.016 for 5 and 0.016 for 7, the lines eating the rim making the ratio larger) and above 1.04 (so none is a circle); reading the number of corners from the ratio and c from the count gives back the variant of the preset; (2) the centroid of every shape is within 1.5 pixels of the middle of its cell, the shape is narrower than its cell (mean width below 0.82 of the cell), and the mean colour is below 0.43 for an even sum of column and row and above 0.43 for an odd one (about 0.35 and 0.5). Mutation check (done once): with the radius of the discs of the fill temporarily shrunk to 0.96 of its value the constant-width check, the range test, the seed-difference test and the maps test fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: the shapes are found by a colour threshold and what is compared is the shape **after** the lines have eaten its rim, so the area ratio and the distance ratio are checked with loose tolerances and not exact values; the shape and width of the lines themselves are not checked (only the filled areas); the cell width, the positions and the rule for the parity of the fill are given by the design and shared by both sides; the variant for each seed (seeds 3, 16, 1, 0, 2, 7 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, but each variant is also checked against the number of shapes and the corner ratio read from the picture, so the table is not simply trusted. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning; the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0197, between the 0.0543, 0.0378 and 0.0075 of other recent kinds, which I did not look into further. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 62, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (n, c); the width of a shape is w = 0.8 (a cell having the side 1) and its circumradius is R = w / (2cos(π / 2n)). At sampling time (per pixel) the tile coordinates are multiplied by c to get the cell (column, row) and the position (x, y) in the cell relative to its middle; the turn of the shape in that cell is hash(column, row, …)·2π / n; the n corners are at the radius R and the angles turn plus 2πk / n; for each corner k the distance d to it is found and the point is outside the shape if any d > w (the shape is the intersection of all d ≤ w); the arc belonging to a corner k is the arc of the circle of radius w about it, between the two opposite corners (k + (n − 1)/2 and k + (n + 1)/2), subtending the angle π / n; if the direction of the point about the centre is within ±π / 2n of the direction to the middle of the polygon, the distance to the arc is `|d − w|`, otherwise it is the smaller of the distances to the two end points (the opposite corners); each arc gives `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.035)²)` and the coverage of the lines is `1 − Π(1 − t²)`; the fill is 0.3 (even sum of column and row) or 0.5 (odd) inside a shape and 0 outside; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`, ink = `fill·(1 − line) + line`), height is `0.8·line·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (one atan2 for each of at most 7 arcs per pixel). **On C1**: the distance to a single arc is C1 near the arc and the lines of the arcs are combined as `1 − Π(1 − t²)`, the sweep found no violation; I did not prove anything away from the lines (near the centre of an arc's circle or opposite the end points), where the coverage of the lines is 0 anyway. Measured (tool-run): the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 3, 16, 1, 0, 2, 7) with 0 violations (at the first try); in the analysis table for seeds 0 to 39 the 6 sets are chosen 8, 3, 9, 5, 8 and 7 times (every seed finds its variant from the number of shapes and the corner ratio of the picture, none unmatched); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 20.76%–21.95%, color is 0.02544–0.02576 to 0.87322–0.87365 with a mean of 0.27469–0.28952, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8752–0.8765 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 20.75%–22.26%, color is 0.02512–0.02525 to 0.87362–0.87449 with a mean of 0.27470–0.29314, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8763–0.8788 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 34.1% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (34.1% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (39.4, 90.1, 87.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0197 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`eisensteinprimes` adds the Eisenstein primes, bringing the current catalog from 1084 to 1085 kinds (1086 gallery choices including plain). The Eisenstein integers a + bω (ω a primitive cube root of unity, ω² = −1 − ω) form a triangular lattice, the point a + bω sitting at (a − b/2, b√3/2) lattice spacings, with the norm N = a² − ab + b²; the lattice points of norm up to the square of the radius are drawn: the Eisenstein primes (a prime norm, or a unit times a rational prime q with q = 2 (mod 3), the norm being q²) as bright dots (dimmer farther from the origin, down to 0.7 of the brightest), the composites, the units and the other points as very small dim dots, and the origin not drawn; lilac on dark purple, a star-like dot pattern with six-fold rotational symmetry; the seed picks one of 6 radii R = 8, 10, 12, 14, 16 and 18 (240, 366, 516, 720, 930 and 1164 lattice points, of which 102, 150, 204, 264, 324 and 390 are primes — counted by the brute-force search in the tests, not taken from the literature); the disc radius is 0.46 of the tile (diameter 0.92), the spacing is 1 / (R + 0.6) disc radii, and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike `gaussianprimes` (a 64×64 square grid with the Gaussian primes glowing), this is a triangular lattice with the Eisenstein primes, six-fold and not four-fold symmetric, with the number of points changing with the radius. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on Eisenstein integers, the norm and the criterion for primes are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check independently by a brute-force search for factors.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the prime dot radius 0.44 spacings, the composite dot radius 0.1 spacings, the fall-off 0.3, the 6 radii, the lilac-on-dark-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. **The first preview was too dim** (prime dot radius 0.36 spacings and fall-off 0.45), and after seeing it I changed to the present 0.44 and 0.3; I looked at the final preview for seeds 0 to 5, which by the probe's table cover sets 3, 0, 1, 4 and 5 (R = 14, 8, 10, 16, 18); **set 2 (R = 12) has not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) a **brute-force search for primes**: a + bω is divisible by c + dω exactly when both a(c − d) + bd and bc − ad are divisible by c² − cd + d² (from multiplying by the conjugate (c − d) − dω); a prime has a norm above 1 and no divisor of a norm between 1 and its own; this criterion differs from the rule the sampler uses (a prime norm, or a unit times a rational prime = 2 mod 3); at every lattice point of the variant of each seed the colour is above 0.5 (0.64 to 0.87 in the probe) exactly when it is a prime and below 0.4 (0.32 to 0.35) for the rest (composites and units), and each of the other 5 sets disagrees with the brute-force result at at least 30 points; (2) **six-fold rotational symmetry**: multiplying by 1 + ω turns the plane by 60 degrees and takes (a, b) to (a − b, a), a lattice point of the same norm, so the colours at the two points differ only by the grain (by less than 0.04); the middle of the segment joining two neighbouring lattice points ((a, b) and (a + 1, b)) is farther from both than the radius of the biggest dot and so reads as the ground (below 0.1; 0.025 to 0.055 in the probe, with the largest difference under a 60-degree turn 0.027). Mutation check (done once): changing "= 2 mod 3" to "= 1 mod 3" makes the prime test and the range test fail; it has been restored. **Limitations**: the formula for the position of the lattice points (the spacing 1 / (R + 0.6), (a − b/2, b√3/2)) and the preset data are shared by both sides; the colours are only checked for the division between primes and non-primes and for the invariance under rotation, not for the exact fall-off; places other than the lattice points and the middles of neighbouring pairs are not checked. The radius for each seed (seeds 1, 2, 11, 0, 3, 4 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning; the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0075, far below the 0.0543 and 0.0378 of other kinds, probably related to whether the features are wide or form connected areas, which I did not check. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid (the extreme brightness and the highest height vary with how the grid meets the lattice points, so the ranges are wider).

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 61, seed ^ salt)` picks a radius R; for all integer pairs (a, b) (|a| and |b| at most ⌈1.2R⌉ + 1) the norm N = a² − ab + b² is found and those with N from 1 to R² become lattice points; if N is a prime, or N = q² with q a prime = 2 (mod 3) and (a, b) is q times a unit ((±q, 0), (0, ±q), (±q, ±q) with equal signs), the point is marked as a prime (2), otherwise 1, and N / R² is stored. At sampling time (per pixel) the disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46` are turned into lattice coordinates b₀ = 2y / (s√3) and a₀ = x / s + b₀ / 2 (s = 1 / (R + 0.6)), and the nearest lattice point (only marked ones) is found among the rounded point and its 6 neighbours; with d the distance to it, the kernel radius is 0.44 s for a prime and 0.1 s otherwise, `t = clamp(1 − (d / radius)²)` and ink is `tone·t²` (tone 1 − 0.3·N / R² for a prime, 0.28 otherwise); the kernel radius is under half the spacing, so the kernel is zero midway between points and the field is C1; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·ink·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the retained cache is the table of lattice points (about (2·⌈1.2R⌉ + 3)² bytes and double-precision norms, about 47² entries for R = 18) and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (at most 7 lattice points checked per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed has exactly one radius for which the brute-force primes agree with all the lattice points (the 6 radii chosen 8, 3, 5, 10, 11 and 3 times); the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 1, 2, 11, 0, 3, 4) with 0 violations (at the first try); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 3.81%–4.27%, color is 0.02545–0.02566 to 0.8206–0.8603 with a mean of 0.08308–0.08840, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8069–0.8553 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 3.61%–4.29%, color is 0.02515–0.02529 to 0.8596–0.8676 with a mean of 0.08141–0.08840, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8502–0.8699 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 7.55% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (7.51% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (35.5, 27.5, 57.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0075 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`confocalconics` adds the confocal conic grid, bringing the current catalog from 1083 to 1084 kinds (1085 gallery choices including plain). Elliptic coordinates about the two foci (±f, 0): the ellipses d1 + d2 = 2f·cosh μ and the hyperbolas d1 − d2 = 2f·cos ν (d1 and d2 the distances to the foci) cut each other at right angles; the grid lines are at equal steps 2π / m of μ and ν (m even), so the cells are curved squares (the map z = f·cosh(μ + iν) is conformal), coloured dark (0.1) and bright (0.3) by the parity of the sum of their two indices; the segment between the foci (μ = 0) and the axis outside the foci (ν = 0) are grid lines too, so the cells across them have opposite colours, and the two foci are bright points where lines gather; thin rose-pink lines on dark purple-red, the line width on the picture measured by the distance to the curve (half width 0.03, the distance being the coordinate difference times the scale factor f·√(cosh²μ − cos²ν)), the seed picking one of 6 sets (f, m, angle): (0.35, 16, 0.3), (0.5, 12, 1.1), (0.5, 20, 2), (0.65, 16, 0), (0.8, 24, 0.7) and (0.4, 24, 2.6); the disc radius is 0.46 of the tile (diameter 0.92), the outside fades out between 0.94 and 0.96 with a ring added, and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike `conformalspiral` (squares in the complex logarithm, with no foci) and `ellipsebilliard` (chords in an ellipse), this is a square grid made by two families of confocal conics. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The formulas of elliptic coordinates and confocal conics are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below build the grid forwards from the standard parametrisation and then check it independently by the focal property.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the line half width 0.03, the ring half width 0.004, the fade range 0.94 to 0.96, the 6 sets (f, m, angle), the two tones (0.1 even, 0.3 odd, plus up to 0.08 brightening with the radius), the rose-on-dark-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews of seeds 1, 0, 3, 4, 9 and 2 (sets 0 to 5 by the probe's table), **rendered again with the final fixed angles**, so all 6 sets have been seen (the first preview used a random angle, and after I made the angle preset data I rendered and looked again). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: (1) a **forward construction**: the points of each set come from the standard parametrisation x = f·cosh μ·cos ν, y = f·sinh μ·sin ν (turned by the angle of the set), the points on the grid lines taken at (μ, ν) = (i·step, (j + 0.37)·step) and ((i + 0.37)·step, j·step) with step = 2π / m; all the check points on the lines of the set of each seed (radius 0.12 to 0.85; 130, 62, 162, 84, 138 and 270 for the sets) read bright with at most 3 lower than 0.7, and each of the other 5 sets has at least 30 check points reading lower (at least 46 in the probe); (2) the **focal property** (independent): an ellipse has a constant d1 + d2 and a hyperbola a constant d1 − d2, so for every pixel of the 512 by 512 reading with a radius from 0.12 to 0.85 and a colour above 0.75 (16 thousand to 33 thousand per seed) either (d1 + d2) / 2 is within 0.03 of f·cosh(i·step) for some i or (d1 − d2) / 2 is within 0.03 of f·cos(j·step) for some j (the worst pixel is 0.012 off in the probe; the half sum and half difference change by at most 1 per unit of distance, so a point near a curve has a value near it), the foci being taken from the preset data (±f and the angle) and not from the sampler; (3) the colour at the middle of the cells (μ and ν at the middle of the cell, keeping only the cells whose scale factor times half a step exceeds 0.04, i.e. not covered by the line bands; 56, 24, 68, 36, 60 and 100 for the sets) is below 0.25 (0.14 to 0.22 in the probe) when i + j is even and above 0.3 (0.35 to 0.42) when it is odd, the same way for all the seeds — cells across the segment between the foci or the axis are opposite too. **Limitations**: the focal-property check is only a necessary condition and its **tolerance is wide**: in a mutation check (the scale of the ellipses temporarily multiplied by 2 / 2.04) this check did **not** fail (the shift is only about 0.01 to 0.02, less than 0.03), it was the line check, the range test, the parity test and the maps test that caught it; so this item catches only large errors, and I did not tighten it because the probe's worst value 0.012 is already about 40% of the threshold; the tests share the definition of the grid (step = 2π / m, the representation of the middle points) and the preset angle data, so they do not show that this definition is the most suitable one; the radii below 0.12 and above 0.85 and the fade zone are not covered. The set for each seed (seeds 1, 0, 3, 4, 9, 2 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, the same as for the six earlier kinds such as poincaretiling; steinerchain has 0.0378, so my earlier guess of a shared slope limit does not hold, and I think it more likely depends on the line width, which I did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 60, seed ^ salt)` picks a set (f, m, angle), step = 2π / m. At sampling time (per pixel) the disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46` are turned back so that the foci are on the x axis, the distances d1 and d2 to the foci are found, cosh μ = (d1 + d2) / 2f and cos ν = (d1 − d2) / 2f (each clamped to its valid range), μ = acosh and ν = acos, replaced by 2π − acos when y < 0; the cell indices are i = floor(μ / step) and j = floor(ν / step), the distance to a line of either family is the scale factor f·√(cosh²μ − cos²ν) times step times min(frac, 1 − frac), each giving `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.03)²)`, and the coverage of the lines is `1 − (1 − t₁²)(1 − t₂²)`; m is even, so the period 2π of ν is compatible with the cells, and across the segment between the foci ν becomes 2π − ν and the cell index j becomes m − 1 − j, reversing the parity, exactly what is wanted on the two sides of that line; the fill is 0.1 (even) or 0.3 (odd) by the parity of i + j plus up to 0.08 rising with the radius, the content of the disc is multiplied by the fade outside `smooth(clamp((0.94 − r) / 0.02))`, and a thin ring (radius 1) is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (two hypots, one log and one acos per pixel, no loop). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed has exactly one set for which all the check points on the lines are bright, the 6 sets being chosen 8, 7, 7, 4, 8 and 6 times; the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 1, 0, 3, 4, 9, 2) with 0 violations (at the first try; the angle is preset data and not random, so the sweep does not meet the singular points on the axis); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 13.46%–20.03%, color is 0.02552–0.02583 to 0.87250–0.87330 with a mean of 0.25114–0.28339, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8735–0.8761 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 13.53%–25.44%, color is 0.02513–0.02539 to 0.87403–0.87461 with a mean of 0.25098–0.31049, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8775–0.8790 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 24.0% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (24.1% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (104.0, 52.1, 78.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`steinerchain` adds the Steiner chain, bringing the current catalog from 1082 to 1083 kinds (1084 gallery choices including plain). Between two circles, one inside the other and not concentric, a ring of n circles, each touching its two neighbours, the inner circle and the outer circle, and closing up exactly (the Steiner porism: if one circle can go round and close up like this, a ring started from any position does); thin pale-blue lines on dark blue, the inside of the beads (the circles) filled in order with two alternating tones (0.3 and 0.5), the space between the inner circle and the beads with a darker fill (0.1) and nothing outside the outer circle; the seed picks one of 6 pairs (number of beads n, shift q): (6, 0) (concentric), (8, 0.35), (10, 0.5), (12, 0.45), (6, 0.55) and (8, 0.2), and the hash chooses the turn of the whole picture and the starting angle of the beads; the outer radius is 0.46 of the tile (diameter 0.92) and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Construction: in the concentric case the inner circle has the radius s = (1 − sin(π / n)) / (1 + sin(π / n)), the n beads have the radius (1 − s) / 2 and their centres at (1 + s) / 2 from the middle (neighbours touch); the Mobius map w → (w + q) / (1 + q w) (which keeps the unit circle, sends circles to circles and touching to touching) then gives the eccentric chain. Unlike `apollonianmosaic` (nineteen unequal tangent circles from two rounds of Descartes reflection, a glazed-disk mosaic on rough grout), this is a ring of n circles between two eccentric circles, n changing with the variant, with the tangency coming from the Mobius map; the sizes of the beads change continuously from small to large with the eccentricity. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on Steiner chains, the porism, the Mobius map and the formula of the inner radius are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below read the picture back only and check it independently of the construction.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the line half width 0.012 (in outer radii), the 6 pairs (n, q), the three fills (0.1, 0.3, 0.5), the pale-blue-on-dark-blue colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, which by the probe's table cover sets 3, 4, 5 and 2 ((12, 0.45), (6, 0.55), (8, 0.2), (10, 0.5)); **set 0 ((6, 0), concentric) and set 1 ((8, 0.35)) have not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back** and **do not use the construction at all**: the 4-connected regions of at least 200 pixels with a colour from 0.32 to 0.62 in the 512 by 512 reading are taken as the beads, and the only region of colour 0.095 to 0.17 with a roundness near 1 as the inner disc; the roundness is 2πI / area² (I the polar moment of the pixels about the centroid, which is 1 for a disc). They check (1) that for each seed the number of bead regions equals the n of the variant, that each bead has a roundness within 0.005 of 1 (1.0000 to 1.0002 in the probe) and that exactly one dim region is a disc (the other pockets have a roundness of at least 1.37); (2) that the lines are bands of equal width, so the inset e between a circle and its region is the same everywhere: from the radii and centroids of the beads, the outer circle (the centre of the tile and 0.46 of the tile as the radius, which is given by the design) and the inner disc, the e found from the tangency with the outer circle, with the inner disc and between neighbours round the ring differs by less than 1.2 pixels over all the 3n contacts (0.73 to 0.76 in the probe) and its mean is between 1 and 3 pixels (1.5 to 2.25 in the probe); (3) that, corrected by that e, the radius of the inner circle and the distance of its centre from the middle, in outer radii, are those of the concentric circle after the Mobius map — the radius s(1 − q²) / (1 − q²s²) and the centre q(1 − s²) / (1 − q²s²) (from the formula for the image of a circle, taking the images of ±s), to within 0.004; and (4) that the mean colours of the beads in order round the ring (about 0.36 and 0.5, told apart at 0.43) alternate, n being even in every variant so that it closes up. This shows that the beads drawn are really circles, touch each other and the two circles and close up, in agreement with a completely different method; it does **not** show the line width or the values of the tones (only the alternation) and does not check which bead gets which tone. The variant for each seed (seeds 6, 19, 4, 0, 1, 3 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). **Mutation check (done once)**: with the radius of the beads temporarily shrunk to 0.97 of its value the tangency check, the range test and the maps test fail; it has been restored. The maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is 0.0378, unlike the 0.0543 of the previous six (poincaretiling, sphericaltiling, poincaretriangles, sphericaltriangles, fareydisc, conformalspiral) — I had guessed that 0.0543 was a shared upper limit of the slope of the height profile, and **this kind's result does not fit that guess** (the line width is different; I did not look further). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 59, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (n, q), and `hash(1, 59, …)` and `hash(2, 59, …)` choose the turn of the picture and the starting angle of the beads; the radius s of the inner circle, the radius (1 − s) / 2 of the beads and the distance (1 + s) / 2 of their centres in the concentric case are as above; with the Mobius map w → (w + q) / (1 + q w) the images of 3 points of the inner circle and of each bead (the centre plus and minus the radius, and the centre plus i times the radius) are taken and the circle through them is found, giving the centres and radii on the picture of the inner circle and the n beads; the outer circle is the unit circle. At sampling time (per pixel) the disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46` are turned and, for each of the n + 2 circles, the distance to the circle `|d − radius|` gives `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.012)²)`, and the coverage of the lines is `1 − Π(1 − t²)`; the fill is 0.1 inside the disc, 0.3 or 0.5 (in order) inside a bead and 0 outside the disc; color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`, ink = `fill·(1 − line) + line`), height is `0.8·line·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) and at most 14 circles (3 numbers each), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (the distances to up to 14 circles per pixel, no loop beyond that). Measured (tool-run): for each of seeds 0 to 39 the number of beads and the offset and radius of the inner circle match exactly one variant (the 6 sets chosen 3, 7, 5, 5, 11 and 9 times); the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 6, 19, 4, 0, 1, 3) with 0 violations (at the first try); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 12.83%–18.06%, color is 0.02567–0.02580 to 0.87238–0.87346 with a mean of 0.24897–0.26481, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8740–0.8761 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 12.81%–18.10%, color is 0.02516–0.02544 to 0.87355–0.87423 with a mean of 0.24897–0.26597, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8769–0.8785 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 21.3% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (21.2% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (57.9, 77.2, 94.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0378 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`conformalspiral` adds the conformal spiral checkerboard, bringing the current catalog from 1081 to 1082 kinds (1083 gallery choices including plain). A lattice of equal squares in the complex logarithm L = ln z (the logarithm of the radius and the angle) with the side vectors A = (a, b) and B = (−b, a) (a = 2πq / (p² + q²), b = 2πp / (p² + q²), so that a turn of the angle by 2π is exactly p times A plus q times B); since the exponential map is conformal, on the disc the cells are curved squares (all the angles right angles) that shrink without end towards the middle, coloured dark (0.1) and bright (0.3) by the parity of the sum i + j of the two cell numbers (neighbours always differ), and the picture is self-similar (unchanged by scaling by exp(a) together with a turn by b); with q = 0 it is a log-polar grid of concentric rings and radial arms, with q ≠ 0 the two families of lines are mutually orthogonal logarithmic spirals; thin amber lines on dark purple with the line width fixed in the logarithm plane (half width 0.03, so thinner towards the middle), the seed picking one of 6 pairs (p, q): (15, 1), (17, 3), (19, 5), (11, 11), (17, −7), (21, −1) (the side of a cell 2π / √(p² + q²) is about 0.42, 0.36, 0.32, 0.40, 0.34 and 0.30; p + q is even in all); the disc radius is 0.46 of the tile (diameter 0.92), in the middle between the radii 0.07 and 0.11 the cells are smaller than a pixel or two and fade out to empty, the outside fades out between 0.94 and 0.96 with a ring added, and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. This is **not** the full Droste effect (there is no picture-within-picture recursion and no picture placed in the cells as in Escher's Print Gallery) but only the conformal spiral lattice behind it, so the name Droste is not used. Unlike the existing `sacksspiral`, `vogelspiral` and `ulamspiral` (dot patterns and disks of integers or phyllotaxis points along a spiral), this is a spiral checkerboard of the whole plane, not points. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on the complex logarithm, conformal maps and the Droste effect are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check self-consistency with a forward construction from the cells to the picture.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the line half width 0.03, the ring half width 0.004, the fade ranges (0.07 to 0.11 in the middle, 0.94 to 0.96 outside), the 6 pairs (p, q), the two tones (0.1 even, 0.3 odd, plus up to 0.08 brightening with the radius), the amber-on-dark-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. I looked at the final preview for seeds 0 to 5, which by the probe's table cover sets 4, 0, 1 and 5 ((17, −7), (15, 1), (17, 3), (21, −1)); **set 2 ((19, 5)) and set 3 ((11, 11)) have not been seen**. The tests **read only the sampler output back** and check with a **forward construction**: the points of the cell (i, j) are exp(L)·(cos Im L, sin Im L) for L = (i + x)·A + (j + y)·B with x and y in (0, 1), Im L taken in (−π, π) so that each cell is listed once; the middle of a cell is x = y = 0.5, the middle of a side of the first family is (0, 0.5) and of the second family (0.5, 0); the sampler goes the other way, taking the logarithm of the point, solving the linear map and taking floors. They check (1) that all the check points on the cell sides of the set of each seed (radius 0.13 to 0.85; 134, 178, 230, 132, 202 and 266 for the sets) read bright with at most 3 lower than 0.7, and that each of the other 5 sets has at least 20 check points reading lower (at least 113 in the probe for seeds 0 to 5); and (2) that the colour at the middle of every cell (radius 0.13 to 0.85; 68, 89, 116, 80, 101 and 132 for the sets) is below 0.25 (0.130 to 0.211 in the probe) when i + j is even and above 0.3 (0.349 to 0.417) when it is odd, the same way for all the seeds — neighbouring cells always differ by one in i + j, so this is the checkerboard. **Limitation**: this is a self-consistency check: the forward map of the test and the backward map of the sampler share the definition of the lattice (the formulas of A and B, the parity of i + j), so it can find errors of the inversion, of the atan2 branch at 180 degrees and of the parity, but it **cannot** show that this lattice definition is right; the edge of the view and the fade zones (below radius 0.13 and above 0.85) are not covered. The set for each seed (seeds 1, 2, 14, 9, 0, 3 for the sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, the same as for poincaretiling, sphericaltiling, poincaretriangles, sphericaltriangles and fareydisc; I guess it is the same upper limit of the slope of the height profile and did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 58, seed ^ salt)` picks a pair (p, q), the side of the cells being side = 2π / √(p² + q²). At sampling time (per pixel) the disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46` are put through the complex logarithm L = (ln r, atan2(y, x)) and L = m·A + n·B is solved, giving m = (q·Lx + p·Ly) / 2π and n = (−p·Lx + q·Ly) / 2π, i = floor(m) and j = floor(n); p + q is even, so the cut of the angle at 180 degrees (m and n jumping by p and q) does not change the parity of i + j. The distances to the two families of grid lines are each `side·min(frac, 1 − frac)`, each giving `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.03)²)`, and the coverage of the lines is `1 − (1 − t₁²)(1 − t₂²)`; the fill is 0.1 (even) or 0.3 (odd) by the parity of i + j plus up to 0.08 rising with the radius, the content of the disc is multiplied by the fade in the middle `smooth(clamp((r − 0.07) / 0.04))` and the fade outside `smooth(clamp((0.94 − r) / 0.02))`, and a thin ring (radius 1) is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (one log and one atan2 per pixel, no loop). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed has exactly one set for which all the check points on the cell sides are bright, the 6 sets being chosen 14, 6, 4, 3, 7 and 6 times (set 0 most often, which includes seeds 7 and 0xffffffff); the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 1, 2, 14, 9, 0, 3) with 0 violations (at the first try); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 10.86%–13.05%, color is 0.02519–0.02561 to 0.87278–0.87383 with a mean of 0.23650–0.24705, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8741–0.8771 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 10.85%–12.98%, color is 0.02509–0.02525 to 0.87372–0.87457 with a mean of 0.23627–0.24680, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8766–0.8789 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 18.2% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (18.2% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (75.5, 51.0, 58.9), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`fareydisc` adds the Farey disc, the tessellation of the Poincare disc by ideal triangles, bringing the current catalog from 1080 to 1081 kinds (1082 gallery choices including plain). The Poincare disc is tiled by ideal triangles (all three corners on the circle, the sides being arcs that cut the circle at a right angle), which is the Farey tessellation (the tessellation {3, ∞}): every edge is a geodesic, and towards the circle the triangles get ever more numerous and smaller and never reach the edge; green thin lines on a dark teal ground, neighbouring triangles coloured alternately dark (0.1) and bright (0.3) by whether the number of mirrors between them and the central triangle is even or odd (neighbours always differ), and a ring drawn at the circle; the line width is fixed in hyperbolic terms (half width 0.03); the seed picks one of 5 viewpoints: the centre of the central triangle, the middle of one edge, and 3 shifted positions (Euclidean radii 0.5, 0.7 and 0.72, authored choices); the disc radius is 0.46 of the tile (diameter 0.92) and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike `fareygraph` (the Farey graph in the upper half-plane: order 7 to 12, the edges semicircular arcs mirrored in the baseline, only lines) and `poincaretiling` and `poincaretriangles` (the {p, q} tilings with finite corners and the (2, p, q) triangle groups), here the set of edges is that of the Farey graph (the corners are rational numbers and edges join fractions with p s − q r = 1; I take it so from memory and did not check the literature) but drawn in the disc model, with all corners at infinity, the parity two-colouring and 5 viewpoints. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on hyperbolic geometry and the Farey tessellation are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below verify the result independently in a completely different way.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the line half width 0.03, the ring half width 0.004, the start of the fade of the content 0.925 (fade width 0.02, the ring at radius 1), the 5 viewpoints, the two tones (0.1 even, 0.3 odd, plus up to 0.08 brightening with the squared distance to the middle after folding), the green-on-dark-teal colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 1, 0, 8, 4 and 2, which by the probe's table **cover all 5 viewpoints**, with the final parameters). The tests **read only the sampler output back** and build the tessellation **in a completely different way**: the corners are the rationals p / q and 1 / 0 put on the unit circle by x → (x − i) / (x + i); the triangles are taken from the Stern–Brocot tree (from the root 0, 1, 1 / 0, the mediant of an interval (a, b) adding numerators and denominators separately, the triangle being a, the mediant and b, depth 7; the negative side from −1 / 0 and 0 / 1) and the edges are their sides; the root triangle is taken to the central regular triangle (corners at 90, 210 and 330 degrees) by the Mobius map found from three pairs of points with the cross ratio, then moved by the isometry of the viewpoint; no point is folded and nothing is derived from the circles of the sampler. They check (1) that all the check points on the edges of the viewpoint of each seed (24 per edge, only those within 0.9 of the middle: 1488, 1488, 1380, 1363 and 1107 for the viewpoints) read bright with at most 3 lower than 0.7, and that each of the other 4 viewpoints has at least 100 check points reading lower (in the probe the viewpoint of the seed has none, the others at least 1041 for seeds 0 to 7); and (2) that the colour at the centre of every listed triangle within 0.8 of the middle (found by taking that triangle to the central one with the map and taking the origin back; 10, 6, 9, 7 and 8 of them per viewpoint, so 6 to 10) is low (below 0.2, 0.122 to 0.145 in the probe) for an even depth and between 0.3 and 0.4 (0.340 to 0.365 in the probe) for an odd depth, the same way for all the seeds — the dual graph being a tree, the parity of the depth is the two-colouring. This shows that the edges and parity tones the sampler draws by mirror folding agree with the independently built Farey tessellation; it does **not** show anything about the edge of the view (beyond 0.9, where the edges are extremely thin and the positions sensitive to rounding), and there is no negative check that places far from the edges are not lines (the depth stops at 7 so the list of edges is incomplete there, hence no such item). The viewpoint for each seed (seeds 1, 0, 8, 4, 2 for the viewpoints 0 to 4) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 5 are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, the same as for poincaretiling, sphericaltiling, poincaretriangles and sphericaltriangles; I guess it is the same upper limit of the slope of the height profile and did not check). **The C1 threshold was passed by tuning parameters** (see ACCEPTANCE): with the shifts of the viewpoints and the start of the fade first at 0.8, 0.93 and 0.955, the second difference at h = 1e-10 had 248 points above 0.03 near the circle, and the final values are the shifts 0.7 and 0.72 and the fade start 0.925. The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.
