At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 57, seed ^ salt)` picks a viewpoint; the three mirror circles have their centres at the distance 2 in the directions 150, 270 and 30 degrees (two corners of a side being 120 degrees apart: the centre at 1 / cos 60 = 2 and the radius tan 60 = √3), the central triangle is the region outside these three circles with its corners on the unit circle at 90, 210 and 330 degrees; the offset a of the viewpoint (a Euclidean radius and an angle) defines the isometry z → (z + a) / (1 + conj(a) z) that takes the middle of the picture to a, viewpoint 0 being the centre of the central triangle (a = 0) and viewpoint 1 the middle of the bottom side (a = (2 − √3) towards 270 degrees, when the bottom side is the horizontal diameter through the middle). At sampling time (per pixel) the disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46` are moved by that isometry and then folded at most 120 times: the three circles are checked in turn and the point is inverted in a circle it is inside, every inversion being counted, until it is outside all three; the distances of the folded point to the three circles times the conformal factor `2 / (1 − |z|²)` (an approximation of the hyperbolic distance that is exact to zeroth order on the edge) each give `t = clamp(1 − (distance / 0.03)²)` and the coverage of the lines is the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` of the three (the set of all mirrors is invariant under the group, so the union of the three sides is symmetric about every mirror and the field stays C1 without an extra mirror term); the fill is 0.1 (even) or 0.3 (odd) by the parity of the number of reflections plus up to 0.08 rising with the squared distance of the folded point to the middle, the content of the disc fades out between the radii 0.925 and 0.945 and a thin ring is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (up to 120 folds per pixel; with the earlier shifts 0.8 and 0.93 and the fade start 0.955, on a 400 by 400 grid at most 16 passes (each checking three circles) were needed per pixel, so far fewer than 120 in practice). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed has exactly one viewpoint for which all the check points on the edges are bright, the 5 viewpoints being chosen 5, 6, 11, 9 and 9 times; the C1 sweep covers all 5 viewpoints (seeds 1, 0, 8, 4, 2) with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 5.04%–5.25%, color is 0.02549–0.02585 to 0.87139–0.87331 with a mean of 0.18748–0.18833, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8714–0.8756 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 5.10%–7.06%, color is 0.02508–0.02522 to 0.87348–0.87416 with a mean of 0.18744–0.19876, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8760–0.8782 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 8.5% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (8.4% on the 512² grid); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.6, 69.9, 63.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sphericaltriangles` adds the stereographic view of the mirror triangles of a polyhedral group, bringing the current catalog from 1079 to 1080 kinds (1081 gallery choices including plain). All the mirror planes (great circles) of a polyhedral symmetry group as seen by stereographic projection: the spherical triangles they cut out are coloured alternately in a dark and a bright tone by whether the number of mirrors between them and the basic triangle is even or odd (neighbouring triangles always differ), as thin amber lines on dark brown with the line width a fixed angle on the sphere (half width 0.03 radian); the seed picks one of 6 sets: the icosahedral group (15 mirrors) seen along a 5-fold axis (towards a corner), a 3-fold axis (towards a face centre) and a 2-fold axis (towards an edge middle), the cube group (9 mirrors) seen along a 4-fold axis (a face centre) and a 3-fold axis (a corner), and the tetrahedral group (6 mirrors) seen along a 3-fold axis; the disc radius corresponds to `|z| ≤ 1.5`, the disc has a diameter of 0.92 of the tile and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike the just-added `sphericaltiling` (the edges of regular polyhedra and the icosahedral mirrors, only lines and no two-colouring), this draws all the mirrors of the three groups with the parity colouring and with other viewing axes; the lines of its set 0 are the same as those of the 'icosahedron mirrors' set of sphericaltiling (the icosahedral group seen along a 5-fold axis), the difference being the two-colouring and the colours. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on polyhedral groups, mirrors and stereographic projection are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below verify the result independently in a completely different way.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the view radius 1.5, the line half width 0.03 radian, the rim half width 0.006 (in disc radii), the 6 sets, the two tones (0.1 even, 0.3 odd, plus up to 0.08 brightening with the square of the angle to the face centre), the amber-on-brown colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, which cover set 0 (seeds 0 and 4, the icosahedral group along a 5-fold axis), set 5 (seed 1, the tetrahedral group), set 2 (seeds 2 and 5, the icosahedral group along a 2-fold axis) and set 4 (seed 3, the cube group along a 3-fold axis); **set 1 (the icosahedral group along a 3-fold axis) and set 3 (the cube group along a 4-fold axis) have not been seen**). The tests **read only the sampler output back** and build the mirrors **in a completely different way**: the normals of the mirror planes are written directly as closed forms — the 6 normals (1, ±1, 0), (1, 0, ±1) and (0, 1, ±1) of the tetrahedral group, the 9 of the cube group (those 6 and the 3 coordinate planes) and the 15 of the icosahedral group, taken as the directions of the middles of the edges (the pairs of corners at the shortest distance) of the icosahedron with its corners at the cyclic permutations of (0, ±1, ±φ) — not by folding points and not derived from corners and faces; the viewing axes and picture axes are the convention of the preset, and the same stereographic formula puts the circles in the tile. They check (1) that for each seed all the check points on the mirror circles of its set (96 per circle, only those within 0.9 of the view centre; at most 3 may read lower than 0.7) read bright (> 0.7, the least value > 0.8) and that every other set has at least 4 check points reading lower (they differ by the group or the viewing axis; the only exception is that the 6 mirrors of the tetrahedral group are among the 9 of the cube group seen along the same axis, so the tetrahedral set is not checked for a seed with the cube group along a 3-fold axis), and that lattice points within 0.8 of the disc radius and more than 0.03 from every dense point of the circles (240 per circle) all read as not a bright line (< 0.5) — 71, 62, 62, 242, 304 and 522 of them (seeds 0, 11, 2, 6, 3, 1; the sets with many mirrors have lines so dense that fewer points are left); and (2) that for every lattice point within 0.8 of the disc radius and more than 0.08 (the sine of the angle) from every mirror plane, the tone class (the colour below or not below 0.32) equals the product of the signs of `n·P` over all the mirror planes for the point P of the sphere at that position, up to one fixed choice of which sign is light — the two-colouring of the triangles of a reflection group, found here directly from the planes and not by counting reflections — with 271, 279, 258, 653, 723 and 983 points and 0 wrong. This shows that the lines and the parity tones the sampler draws by mirror folding agree with the independently built mirrors; it does **not** show anything about the edge of the view (> 0.9). The projection formula and the viewing-axis convention are settings both sides share (not an independent oracle), and the set for each seed (seeds 0, 11, 2, 6, 3, 1) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, the same to nine digits as for poincaretiling, sphericaltiling and poincaretriangles; I guess it is the same upper limit of the slope of the height profile and did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 56, seed ^ salt)` picks one set; the corners of the polyhedron of that group (the tetrahedron, the cube or the icosahedron) are taken in the usual coordinates (the tetrahedron at alternate corners of the cube, the cube at (±1, ±1, ±1) and the icosahedron at the cyclic permutations of (0, ±1, ±φ)); from the first corner V, one of its nearest neighbours and the neighbour that makes the smallest angle with it, a face F (as a normal vector) and the edge middle M are found; the sides of the basic triangle (corner V, edge middle M, face centre F) lie in three mirror planes: through the origin, V and M, through F and M, and through F and V, the normals taken so that the inside of the triangle is positive. The viewing axis comes from the second word of the set (icosahedral group: corner `(0, 1, φ)`, face `(1, 1, 1)`, edge `(0, 0, 1)`; cube group: face `(0, 0, 1)`, corner `(1, 1, 1)`; tetrahedral group: `(1, 1, 1)`). At sampling time (per pixel) the point (disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46 × 1.5`) is put on the sphere by the inverse stereographic map (`(2z, 1 − |z|²) / (1 + |z|²)`) and turned to the viewing axis; then at most 40 folds: the three planes are checked in turn and the point is mirrored in each plane it is on the negative side of, every reflection being counted, until it is on the inner side of all; the angles to the three planes, `asin(point · normal)`, each give `t = clamp(1 − (angle / 0.03)²)` and the coverage of the lines is the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` of the three (the set of all mirrors is invariant under the group, so the union of the three sides is symmetric about every mirror and the field stays C1 without an extra mirror term; the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets and found 0 violations the first time); the fill is 0.1 (even) or 0.3 (odd) by the parity of the number of reflections plus up to 0.08 rising with the square of the angle to F, the disc fades out between 0.98 and 1 and a thin ring is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) plus a few vertices and normal vectors, with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (up to 40 folds per pixel). Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matched exactly one set, the 6 sets being chosen 8, 4, 5, 9, 3 and 11 times; the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 0, 11, 2, 6, 3, 1) with 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 7.95%–18.07%, color is 0.02573–0.02596 to 0.87215–0.87332 with a mean of 0.23246–0.28015, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8740–0.8757 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 7.85%–18.03%, color is 0.02520–0.02528 to 0.87392–0.87417 with a mean of 0.23235–0.28001, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8771–0.8780 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 (the icosahedral group along a 5-fold axis and the tetrahedral group) 19.8% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (78.5, 57.3, 34.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`poincaretriangles` adds the triangle group of the Poincaré disc, bringing the current catalog from 1078 to 1079 kinds (1080 gallery choices including plain). The triangle group (2, p, q) of the hyperbolic plane drawn in the Poincaré disc: all the mirror lines of the regular tiling {p, q} (the sides of its polygons and their lines of symmetry) cut the plane into triangles with the angles π/2, π/p and π/q, all the mirror lines are drawn as thin rose-pink lines, and the triangles are coloured alternately in a dark and a bright tone by whether the number of mirrors between them and the first triangle is even or odd (the reflections of the group make neighbouring triangles always differ), with the line width fixed in the hyperbolic metric so it gets thinner towards the circle, and with a fade and a thin ring at the rim; the seed picks one of 6 sets (p, q): (3,7), (3,8), (4,5), (4,6), (5,5), (3,9); the disc has a diameter of 0.92 of the tile and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike the just-added `poincaretiling` (the edges and polygons of the regular tiling {p, q}, without the two-coloured triangles and the lines of symmetry), this draws all the mirror lines and two-coloured triangles. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The triangle group and its formulas are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check the result independently.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the line half width 0.03 in the hyperbolic metric, the rim half width 0.004, the fade start 0.955, at most 80 folds, the 6 sets (p, q), the two tones (0.1 even, 0.3 odd, plus up to 0.08 brightening from the centre outwards), the rose-pink-on-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, which cover (3,8) (seed 0), (3,7) (seed 1), (4,5) (seed 2) and so on — I did not match the sets of seeds 3 to 5 one by one and the other sets have not been seen; I later changed the line width and the fade start (see below) and only looked again at seeds 0 and 1). The tests **read only the sampler output back** and build the triangles **in a completely different way**: instead of folding points, they start from the first triangle (the centre O of the disc, the corner B in the disc and the point A where the circle through B and its mirror image crosses the real axis) and keep mirroring triangles in their own sides (the circle through two corners that cuts the unit circle at a right angle, with the centre found from two linear equations, or the line through the centre when the two corners and the centre are collinear — **my first version missed the case where one end of a side is the centre itself, whose direction is the zero vector, which gave NaN and a runaway number of triangles**), take a triangle as new when the mean of its corners is not yet known (to 1e-4), mark odd and even by the parity of the number of mirrorings from the first triangle, and then take points on the geodesics with the Möbius map. They check (1) that in this independently built triangulation exactly 2p, 2q and 4 triangles meet at the centre O, the corner B and the edge middle A (a check of the corner-radius formula that both share; I did not run a negative control with the formula deliberately wrong); (2) that for each seed exactly one of the 6 sets (p, q) has all points at 30%, 50% and 70% of all the sides with corners within 0.9 of the centre (570 to 2,664 points) reading bright (> 0.7, the least value > 0.8), and that lattice points within 0.85 of the centre and more than 0.02 from every side (24 points per side; 402 to 1,106 of them) all read as not a bright line (< 0.5); and (3) that at the mean of the corners of every triangle (corners within 0.9, mean within 0.7 and more than 0.02 from every side; 462 in all) the colour is below 0.32 for even triangles and 0.32 or above for odd ones (0.133–0.171 and 0.348–0.385 in the probe), with 0 wrong, so neighbouring triangles always differ in colour. This shows that the lines and the parity tones the sampler draws by mirror folding agree with the independently built triangles; it does **not** show anything about the rim of the disc (radius > 0.9). The set (p, q) for each seed (seeds 1, 0, 2, 16, 7, 4 give the sets in the order above) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, the same to nine digits as for poincaretiling and sphericaltiling; I guess it is the same upper limit of the slope of the height profile and did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 55, seed ^ salt)` picks one set (p, q); `R = acosh(cot(π/p)·cot(π/q))` and the corner radius is `r = tanh(R / 2)`; the side opposite the centre of the basic triangle (centre, edge middle, corner) lies on the circle about (`(1 + r²) / (2 r cos(π/p))`, 0) of radius `√(centre² − 1)` (so it meets the unit circle at a right angle). At sampling time (per pixel) the point (disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46`) is folded into the basic triangle: at most 80 times, if y < 0 then y ← −y; if it is on the other side of the line through the centre at the angle π/p it is mirrored in that line; if it is inside the circle it is inverted in that circle — every reflection is counted — until nothing moves; the reflections form a group, so the distance of the folded point to the three sides is the distance to all the mirror lines (a mirror line outside the triangle cannot be nearer than the side that has to be crossed to reach it) and the parity of the number of reflections is the same for all ways of folding; the coverage of the lines is the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` of the three sides with t = `clamp(1 − (hyperbolic distance / 0.03)²)` each (the hyperbolic distance is `2·distance / (1 − |z|²)`; the union of the three sides is symmetric about every mirror so the field is C1, with no need for the extra mirror term of poincaretiling); the fill is 0.1 or 0.3 by the parity of the number of reflections plus up to 0.08 brightening from the centre outwards, the disc fades out between 0.935 and 0.955 and a thin ring of half width 0.004 is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (up to 80 folds per pixel). Measured (tool-run): the independently built triangulations (at most 8,000 triangles, those whose mean is within 0.93 are expanded) have 1,302, 786, 656, 424, 370 and 636 triangles and 2,091, 1,278, 1,092, 732, 630 and 1,056 sides for the 6 sets, with (2p, 2q, 4) triangles meeting at O, B and A in every one; in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matched exactly one set, the 6 sets being chosen 6, 9, 7, 5, 8 and 5 times; the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 1, 0, 2, 16, 7, 4) with 0 violations (**the tuning is described in ACCEPTANCE: with my first line half width 0.022 and fade start 0.985 four sample points near the rim of the disc for seed 1 slightly exceeded the threshold (0.0305 to 0.0476 against 0.03) in the second difference; I widened the lines to 0.03 and moved the fade start in to 0.955 and then all passed; those excesses are far smaller than the values of real creases (hundreds and more), but I changed parameters to pass the threshold**); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 10.80%–20.67%, color is 0.02565–0.02606 to 0.87319–0.87454 with a mean of 0.23286–0.27932, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8753–0.8788 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 10.82%–20.66%, color is 0.02523–0.02542 to 0.87375–0.87453 with a mean of 0.23295–0.27911, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8768–0.8788 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 ((3,8) and (3,7)) 24.1% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (77.8, 41.1, 67.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sphericaltiling` adds the stereographic view of a regular polyhedron, bringing the current catalog from 1077 to 1078 kinds (1079 gallery choices including plain). The edges of a regular polyhedron as seen by stereographic projection: a point of the disc is put on the unit sphere by the inverse stereographic map (`(2z, 1 − |z|²) / (1 + |z|²)`, the disc radius corresponding to `|z| ≤ 1.5`, so a little more than a hemisphere is seen), then folded into the basic triangle by the mirror group of the polyhedron, and the angle to the mirror plane that holds the edges is the distance to an edge; thin cyan lines on dark blue-black, every face brightening from its centre to its edge, with a thin ring at the rim of the disc; the line width is a fixed angle on the sphere (half width 0.035 radian), so in the projection it is wider towards the outside; the seed picks one of 6 sets: the edges of the icosahedron, the dodecahedron, the cube, the octahedron and the tetrahedron, and all 15 mirror planes of the icosahedral group (including lines that are not edges); the viewing axis (the pole of the projection) is a corner for the icosahedron, the dodecahedron and the tetrahedron, and (0, 0, 1) for the cube (a face centre) and the octahedron (a corner), so that the centre of the picture has 5, 3, 0 (a face centre), 4 and 3 lines meeting in that order; all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The statements on stereographic projection, the coordinates of regular polyhedra and the mirror groups are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below verify the result independently in a completely different way.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the view radius 1.5, the line half width 0.035 radian, the rim half width 0.006 (in disc radii), the 6 sets, the tone range 0.1 to 0.42 inside faces, the cyan-on-navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, which cover the icosahedron (seed 0), the dodecahedron (seeds 1 to 3), the tetrahedron (seed 4) and the octahedron (seed 5); seeds 6 to 11 were rendered to files but I did not look at each, so **the cube and the icosahedron-mirrors sets have not been seen**; when I first looked at the dodecahedron preview I wrongly took the centre for a pentagon and checked it by counting the lines that cross a small circle round the centre of the picture with a probe: 3 lines meet there, which agrees with a corner as the viewing axis). The tests **read only the sampler output back** and build the lines **in a completely different way**: instead of folding points, they take the corners of the regular polyhedron in the usual coordinates, take the pairs of corners at the smallest distance as the edges, take points on the great circle arcs by spherical interpolation (3 points at 30%, 50% and 70% of every edge, where in range), and for the mirrors set the 15 great circles perpendicular to the middles of the edges of the icosahedron (48 points each), and then put them in the tile with the same stereographic formula (the viewing axis and the picture axes by the convention of the preset), keeping only those within 0.9 of the view radius from the middle. They check (1) that for each seed all check points of the lines of its set (at most 3 may read lower than 0.7) read bright (> 0.7, the least value > 0.8) and the other sets have at least 4 check points reading lower (the tetrahedron has only 9 check points in all), the only exception being that the edges of the icosahedron are among its mirrors, so the edge set is not checked for a mirrors seed; and (2) that lattice points within 0.8 of the disc radius that are more than 0.03 from every dense point of the lines of the set (25 per edge, 120 per great circle) all read as not a bright line (< 0.5, the fill being at most 0.44) — 657, 861, 984, 726, 1,096 and 73 of them (seeds 0, 1, 8, 5, 4, 12; the lines of the mirrors set are so dense that the fewest points are left). This shows that the lines the sampler draws by mirror folding agree with the independently built lines; it does **not** show anything about the edge of the view (> 0.9). The projection formula and the viewing-axis convention are settings both sides share (not an independent oracle), and the set for each seed (seeds 0, 1, 8, 5, 4, 12) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 54, seed ^ salt)` picks one set; the corners of that regular polyhedron are taken in the usual coordinates (the tetrahedron at alternate corners of the cube, the octahedron on the axes, the cube at (±1, ±1, ±1), the icosahedron at the cyclic permutations of (0, ±1, ±φ) and the dodecahedron at the cube corners and the cyclic permutations of (0, ±1/φ, ±φ)); from the first corner V, one of its nearest neighbours and the neighbour that makes the smallest angle with it, a face F (as a normal vector) and the edge middle M are found; the sides of the basic triangle (corner V, edge middle M, face centre F) lie in three mirror planes: through the origin, V and M (it holds the edges of the polyhedron), through F and M, and through F and V, the normals taken so that the inside of the triangle is positive. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (up to 40 folds per pixel). `poincaretiling` adds the Poincaré-disc hyperbolic tiling, bringing the current catalog from 1076 to 1077 kinds (1078 gallery choices including plain). The regular tiling {p, q} of the hyperbolic plane (regular p-gons, q at every corner) drawn in the Poincaré disc: the edges are circular arcs that meet the unit circle at a right angle, and the polygons get smaller and crowd towards the circle the further they are from the centre; thin gold lines on dark blue, each polygon gradually brighter from its centre towards its edge, with a thin ring at the rim; the line width is fixed in the hyperbolic metric, so it gets thinner towards the circle; the seed picks one of 6 sets {p, q}: {7,3}, {5,4}, {4,5}, {6,4}, {8,3}, {3,7}; the disc has a diameter of 0.92 of the tile and all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The names 'Poincaré disc' and '{p, q}' and the formulas behind them — the corner radius `tanh(R / 2)`, `cosh R = cot(π/p)·cot(π/q)`, and folding by the mirrors of the triangle group — are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests below check the result independently.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the disc radius 0.46, the line half width 0.03 in the hyperbolic metric, the rim half width 0.004, the fade start 0.985, at most 80 folds, the 6 sets {p, q}, the tone range 0.1 to 0.42 inside the polygons, the gold-on-blue colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, but they cover only 3 sets: {7,3} (seeds 0, 2, 5), {5,4} (seed 1) and {4,5} (seeds 3, 4); seeds 6 to 9 were rendered to files but I did not look at each, so {6,4}, {8,3} and {3,7} have **not been seen**; and the previews were looked at **before** the C1 fix described below, which only changes the line shape near the corners, and I did not look again afterwards). The tests **read only the sampler output back** and build the tiling **in a completely different way**: instead of folding points, they start from the central polygon and keep mirroring polygons in their own sides (the circle through two corners that cuts the unit circle at a right angle, with the centre found from two linear equations, or the line through the centre when the two corners and the centre are collinear), take a polygon as new when the mean of its corners is not yet known (to 1e-4), which gives all the edges, and then find points on the geodesics with the Möbius map `z → (z − a)/(1 − conj(a)·z)`. They check (1) that in this independently built tiling exactly q polygons meet at the first corner of the first polygon (a check of the corner-radius formula that both share; I did not run a negative control with the formula deliberately wrong); (2) that for each seed exactly one of the 6 sets {p, q} has all its edges with corners within 0.9 of the centre (36 to 140 edges, 108 to 420 points at 30%, 50% and 70% of each edge) reading bright (> 0.7, the least value > 0.8); and (3) that lattice points within 0.85 of the centre and more than 0.02 from every edge (24 points per edge) all read as not a bright line (< 0.5, the fill being at most 0.44). This shows that the lines the sampler draws by mirror folding agree with the independently built tiling; it does **not** show anything about the lines near the rim of the disc (radius > 0.9), where they are denser than a pixel. The set {p, q} for each seed (seeds 0, 1, 3, 6, 7, 26 give the sets in the order above) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0543, higher than for the neighbouring kinds; I guess because the lines get narrower and steeper towards the circle in the hyperbolic metric and did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 53, seed ^ salt)` picks one set {p, q}; `R = acosh(cot(π/p)·cot(π/q))`, the corner radius is `r = tanh(R / 2)` and the corners of the central polygon are at the angles π/p, 3π/p and so on; the circle of one side of the polygon (through the two corners at π/p and −π/p) has its centre at (`(1 + r²) / (2 r cos(π/p))`, 0) and radius `√(centre² − 1)` (so it meets the unit circle at a right angle). At sampling time (per pixel) the point (disc coordinates `(u − 0.5, v − 0.5) / 0.46`) is folded into the basic triangle with the centre, the middle of a side and a corner as its vertices (angles π/p, π/q and π/2): at most 80 times, if y < 0 then y ← −y; if it is on the other side of the line through the centre at the angle π/p it is mirrored in that line; if it is inside the circle of the side it is inverted in that circle; until nothing moves; these mirrors form the symmetry group of the tiling, so the distance of the folded point to that circle is the distance to the edges of the tiling, and the hyperbolic distance is `2·distance / (1 − |z|²)`; the coverage of the lines is the union of that circle and its mirror image in the line through the centre, `1 − (1 − t₁²)(1 − t₂²)` (t = `clamp(1 − (hyperbolic distance / 0.03)²)`, exactly zero at the rim; the mirror image is there to make the field symmetric about that line at the corners, which keeps it C1, **and at first I used only one circle: the C1 sweep then found 30 to 40 creases near corners, which this change fixed**); the fill of a polygon rises from 0.1 to 0.42 with the folded `|z|²`, the disc fades out between 0.965 and 0.985 and a thin ring of half width 0.004 is added: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·mask + 0.72·ink + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(ink / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·(lines + ring)·(0.88 + 0.12·ink) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the dark and metallic is 0; the only retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain), with no geometry data. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (up to 80 folds per pixel). Measured (tool-run): the independently built tilings (at most 6,000 polygons; the probe used the same construction) have 232, 146, 149, 103, 161 and 286 polygons and 1,078, 515, 416, 486, 928 and 519 edges for the 6 sets; in a probe of seeds 0 to 79 every seed matched exactly one set, the 6 sets being chosen 12, 12, 12, 10, 17 and 17 times; the C1 sweep covers all 6 sets (seeds 0, 1, 3, 6, 7, 26) with 0 violations after the fix; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 4.93%–5.64%, color is 0.02538–0.02572 to 0.87262–0.87311 with a mean of 0.20309–0.21657, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8738–0.8750 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 3.91%–5.64%, color is 0.02505–0.02525 to 0.87335–0.87369 with a mean of 0.20303–0.21644, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8756–0.8765 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 ({7,3} and {5,4}) 8.9% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (61.2, 55.3, 56.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0543 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews (before the C1 fix). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`pursuitpolygons` adds the pursuit-polygon swirl, bringing the current catalog from 1075 to 1076 kinds (1077 gallery choices including plain). n bugs sit on the n corners of a regular n-gon and each runs at the next one: after each interval every corner is moved the fraction f of the way to the next corner, which gives a smaller regular polygon turned by an angle; all the sides of K + 1 such polygons are drawn, giving a swirl (for n = 4 it looks like 'rotating squares'), as pale-pink thin lines on dark purple-black with the line getting thinner from the outside in; all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam; the seed picks one of 6 sets (number of corners, fraction f, number of steps K): (4, 0.08, 60), (3, 0.07, 60), (5, 0.1, 45), (6, 0.06, 70), (8, 0.05, 80), (4, 0.15, 35). It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The wording 'pursuit problem' and the discretised construction are from my memory and I did not check the literature.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the radius 0.43, the line half width 0.0026 with fade 0.4, the 6 parameter sets, the pale-pink-on-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 0 to 5, but they cover only sets 5 and 2 (seeds 0, 3, 4, 5 are set 5 and seeds 1, 2 are set 2); seeds 6 to 11 were rendered to files but I did not look at each, so sets 0, 1, 3 and 4 have not been seen). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: the test computes all the sides independently from a **closed form** — the corners of polygon 0 are `R·i·ω^j` and every step multiplies the whole polygon by the complex number `1 − f + f·ω` (ω = e^(2πi/n)), so corner j of polygon k is `R·i·(1 − f + f·ω)^k·ω^j` (the sampler moves the corners step by step) — and checks that for each seed exactly one of the 6 preset sets has all the points along all sides (3 per side at 20%, 50% and 80%, 432 to 1,944 points) reading bright (> 0.3, the least value > 0.8) — the other 5 sets have hundreds of points reading dark — and that of 4,000 lattice points those more than 0.02 from every side all read dark (< 0.2). This shows that the sides the sampler draws by moving the corners step by step agree with the closed form; it does **not** prove anything else about the pursuit problem. The set for each seed (seeds 9, 11, 1, 6, 7, 0 give sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0517, the same to nine digits as for ellipsebilliard and lsystemplants; I guess it is the same upper limit of the slope of the height profile and did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid; set 4 (8 corners, 80 steps) is very dense and its lit share at 512² is 32.6%, far above the other sets.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 52, seed ^ salt)` picks one set (`variants`, 6 sets of (n, f, K)); the corners of the regular n-gon are `(0.43·cos(π/2 + 2πj/n), −0.43·sin(π/2 + 2πj/n))` (about the centre of the tile, one corner at the top); for k = 0 to K: each of the n sides of this polygon is put in as a segment (half width `0.0026·(1 − 0.4·k/K)`, filed into the 24×24 buckets it touches, at every sampling point along the path with four offsets of the half width plus half a step) and then every corner moves to `corner + f·(next corner − corner)` to give the next polygon. At sampling time the segments in the bucket are united as `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (t = `clamp(1 − d²/w²)`, exactly zero at the rim, so the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.72 − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(union / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·union·(0.88 + 0.12·0.72) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 off the line and metallic is 0; the retained cache has a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) plus JS arrays of 144 to 648 segments (6 numbers each) and the buckets; **I did not measure their byte size**. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): the 6 sets have 244, 183, 230, 426, 648 and 144 sides (counting K + 1 polygons); in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matched exactly one set, the 6 sets (0 to 5) being chosen 5, 6, 8, 7, 7 and 7 times, and for the first 8 seeds (0 to 7) the least colour along the sides computed from the closed form is about 0.845–0.846 with no point below 0.3; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 5.67%–11.86%, color is 0.02537–0.02566 to 0.87386–0.87417 with a mean of 0.08734–0.13927, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8462–0.8471 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 6.00%–32.59%, color is 0.02509–0.02522 to 0.87450–0.87462 with a mean of 0.09001–0.31103, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8488–0.8515 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 (sets 5 and 2) 13.7% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (22.7% for seeds 0 and 6); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (86.2, 53.9, 79.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0517 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`lsystemplants` adds L-system plants, bringing the current catalog from 1074 to 1075 kinds (1076 gallery choices including plain). Plants grown by Lindenmayer systems (L-systems) and drawn as thin lines by a turtle: a word is rewritten in parallel by rules a number of times, F moves one unit forward and leaves a segment, + and − turn left and right and [ and ] save and restore position and heading; the plant is scaled to fill 0.84 of the tile, centred and upright (growing upward), as pale-green thin lines on dark green-black; the seed picks one of 6 sets (axiom, rules, angle, number of rewrites), each one plant (1,488, 4,096, 3,125, 1,330, 4,096 and 3,125 segments); all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike the existing `pythagorastree` (a finite Pythagoras tree of glazed square tiles), `vicsekfractal`, `dragoncurve` and so on, these are branching plants grown by grammar rewriting. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The name 'L-system' and the 6 rule sets (looking like a fractal plant, a bush, a tree, a weed, a seaweed and a ternary tree) are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the rule strings may differ from the common versions.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 6 rule sets and angles (25°, 22.5°, 25.7°, 20°, 22.5°, 20°), the numbers of rewrites (5, 4, 5, 6, 4, 5), the fill 0.84, the line half width 0.0022, the pale-green-on-dark colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 0, 1, 2 and 3, which show 3 of the 6 sets (3, 5 and 0); seeds 4 to 7 (sets 3, 2, 1 and 3) were rendered to files but I did not look at each, so sets 1, 2 and 4 have not been seen). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: the test recomputes the segments of each set independently **in another way** (recursion on every letter down to the number of rewrites instead of rewriting the whole word again and again, and a turtle that keeps a unit direction vector and turns it with a rotation matrix instead of adding up an angle) and checks that for each seed exactly one of the 6 preset sets has all the points along all of its segments (3 per segment at 25%, 50% and 75%, 3,990 to 12,288 points) reading bright (> 0.3, the least value > 0.8) — the other 5 sets have thousands of points reading dark — and that of 4,000 lattice points those more than 0.02 from every segment all read dark (< 0.2). This shows that the sampler's segments agree with an independently computed turtle drawing; it does **not** show that the 6 rule sets agree with the literature. The set for each seed (seeds 2, 6, 5, 0, 20, 1 give sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0517, the same to nine digits as for ellipsebilliard; I guess it is the same upper limit of the slope of the height profile and did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 50, seed ^ salt)` picks one set (`variants`, 6 sets of (axiom, rule string, angle, number of rewrites), a rule string looking like `X=F+[[X]-X]-F[-FX]+X;F=FF`); every letter of the axiom is replaced in parallel by its rule (letters without a rule stay), the number of times given, which gives a word of at most about 11,116 characters; the turtle starts at the origin heading up: F moves one unit forward and leaves a segment, + and − turn left and right by the angle, [ and ] save and restore position and heading, all other letters do nothing; the figure is centred by its bounding box, scaled by `0.84 / the larger side of the box` and put upside down in the second coordinate (so the plant grows upward); every segment is filed into the 24×24 buckets it touches (half width 0.0022, at every sampling point along the path with four offsets of the half width plus half a step). At sampling time the segments in the bucket are united as `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (t = `clamp(1 − d²/w²)`, exactly zero at the rim, so the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.72 − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(union / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·union·(0.88 + 0.12·0.72) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 off the line and metallic is 0; the retained cache has a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) plus JS arrays of 1,330 to 4,096 segments (6 numbers each) and the buckets; **I did not measure their byte size**. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (the string rewriting, the turtle and the segment buckets) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): the 6 sets have 1,488, 4,096, 3,125, 1,330, 4,096 and 3,125 segments; in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matched exactly one set, the 6 sets (0 to 5) being chosen 8, 9, 6, 10, 2 and 5 times, and for the first 8 seeds (0 to 7) the least colour along the lines computed in the independent way is about 0.845–0.846 with no point below 0.3; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 2.59%–6.83%, color is 0.02534–0.02548 to 0.87339–0.87410 with a mean of 0.06201–0.09660, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8456–0.8492 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 2.79%–6.73%, color is 0.02509–0.02520 to 0.87429–0.87472 with a mean of 0.06334–0.09590, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8489–0.8520 relief; between seeds 2 and 6 (sets 0 and 1) 13.9% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (5.1% for seeds 2 and 0); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (16.4, 33.0, 22.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0517 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed some of the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`ellipsebilliard` adds the elliptical billiard path, bringing the current catalog from 1073 to 1074 kinds (1075 gallery choices including plain). A ball moves in a straight line inside an elliptical table (semi-major axis 0.43, semi-minor axis from one of 6 sets) and is thrown back by the law of reflection when it hits the wall; the 110 to 160 chords (the segments between hits) are drawn as thin mint lines on dark blue-black, with a thicker ring for the elliptical wall; the chords leave a region without lines whose boundary is the envelope of the chords (from memory I believe this is the caustic of the elliptical billiard, a conic confocal with the ellipse, an ellipse or a hyperbola, which I did not verify from the literature; in the previews some variants are hyperbola-like and some ellipse-like); the seed picks one of 6 sets (semi-minor axis, start parameter, end parameter of the first chord, number of chords); all of the figure is inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike the existing `stringart` (times-table chords between 96 points on a circle), this is one billiard trajectory whose chords are fixed by the law of reflection. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the semi-major axis 0.43, the wall half width 0.005, the chord half width 0.0022, the 6 sets (semi-minor axis 0.26 to 0.38, the ellipse parameters of the start and of the end of the first chord, 110 to 160 chords), the mint-on-navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at the previews of seeds 0, 1 (the same set, so the two are identical), 2, 3, 9 and 8, which show 5 of the 6 sets; the set of seed 5 was rendered to a file but I did not look at it). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: the test recomputes the path independently **in another way** (the next hit from the larger root of a quadratic, the reflection about the tangent of the wall instead of the normal) and checks that for each seed exactly one of the 6 preset sets has all points along all of its chords (13 per chord) reading bright (> 0.3, the least value > 0.8) — the other 5 sets have hundreds of points reading dark — that 720 points of the wall of that set all read bright, and that of 4,000 lattice points those more than 0.02 from every chord and from the wall (1,883 to 3,080 per seed) all read dark (< 0.2). This shows that the sampler's chords agree with an independently computed billiard path (including the law of reflection); it does **not** prove the statement about caustics. The set for each seed (seeds 5, 0, 9, 8, 2, 3 give sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered); seeds 0 and 1 pick the same set and differ only by grain. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0517, higher than for the neighbouring kinds; I guess because the wall is thicker and did not check). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 48, seed ^ salt)` picks one set (`variants`, 6 sets of (b, s₀, s₁, n)); first the elliptical wall (`x = 0.43·cos s`, `y = b·sin s` about the centre of the tile) is cut into 360 segments of half width 0.005; the ball starts at the wall point at the parameter s₀ and goes towards the wall point at the parameter s₁; the next hit is found as `t = −2(x·dx / a² + y·dy / b²) / (dx² / a² + dy² / b²)` (the ball is on the wall, so the other root is 0), at the hit it is reflected about the normal `n = (x / a², y / b²)` (`d ← d − 2(d·n)n / |n|²`, then taken to unit length), n times, every chord having half width 0.0022; every segment is filed into the 24×24 buckets it touches. At sampling time the segments in the bucket are united as `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (t = `clamp(1 − d²/w²)`, exactly zero at the rim, so the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.72 − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(union / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·union·(0.88 + 0.12·0.72) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 off the line and metallic is 0; the retained cache has a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) plus JS arrays of 470 to 520 segments (360 of wall and 110 to 160 chords, 6 numbers each) and the buckets; **I did not measure their byte size**. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 39 every seed matched exactly one set, the 6 sets (0 to 5) being chosen 8, 12, 6, 5, 5 and 4 times, with, for the first 8 seeds (0 to 7), the least colour along the chords computed in the independent way about 0.845–0.846 and no point below 0.3 (for the other seeds only the condition 'at most 4 points below 0.3' was checked); seeds 0, 1 and 7 give set 1, seed 0xffffffff gives set 5 and seed 13 gives set 0; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 13.30%–18.72%, color is 0.02534–0.02571 to 0.87366–0.87412 with a mean of 0.14977–0.19528, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8471–0.8497 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 13.31%–18.76%, color is 0.02509–0.02524 to 0.87465–0.87470 with a mean of 0.14993–0.19552, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8509–0.8520 relief; between seeds 0 and 3 (different sets) 22.2% of the cells of the 256² grid differ in whether color>0.5 (20.3% for seeds 0 and 2), and between seeds 0 and 1 (the same set) only 0.018% differ at 512²; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (32.2, 61.1, 62.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0517 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`lorenzattractor` adds the Lorenz attractor path, bringing the current catalog from 1072 to 1073 kinds (1074 gallery choices including plain). The Lorenz system (σ = 10, ρ = 28, β = 8/3, the classical parameters) is integrated from one of 6 start points for 8 time units, projected on the x–z, y–z or x–y plane (given by the start set) and drawn as one thin amber line on dark purple-black; one path per tile, put in the tile with a fixed centre and scale per plane (not dependent on the path), so the figure does not cross the seam; the ink gets thinner with time (half width from 0.0035 down to 0.0018); the seed picks one of the 6 sets. Unlike the just-added `harmonograph` (an artificial figure of damped sine waves) this is a real trajectory of a chaotic differential equation. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The name 'Lorenz' and the parameter values are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the path is integrated numerically with a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method, and a chaotic system is sensitive to error, which is why only 8 time units are integrated.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the step 0.005, the duration 8 (1,600 segments), the ink half width 0.0035 with fade 0.5, the scale `0.82 / 56` and the centres of the planes, the 6 start points, the amber-on-purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at previews: seeds 0 and 2 at the earlier duration of 22 and seeds 2 and 6 after changing to 8; seed 6 is the standard butterfly and I find it attractive). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: the test re-integrates the Lorenz equations independently for the 6 start points with a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method at **a quarter of the step**, projects them and puts them in the tile, and checks that for each seed exactly one of the 6 sets has all 6,401 points of its path reading bright (> 0.3, the least value > 0.8) — the other 5 sets have thousands of points reading dark — and that of 4,000 lattice points, those more than 0.02 from the path (every second point, 3,201 points) all read dark (< 0.2). This also shows that the sampler's integration agrees with the finer integration over the whole 8 time units to about 3×10⁻⁴ (in tile units; a probe with step 0.005 against 0.00125 measured the largest gaps of the 6 sets as 5.1×10⁻⁷, 6.3×10⁻⁷, 5.4×10⁻⁵, 8.2×10⁻⁵, 2.6×10⁻⁴ and 1.3×10⁻⁴). The start set for each seed (seeds 17, 0, 1, 2, 12, 6 give sets 0 to 5) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). **I first chose the duration wrongly**: I had set it to 22 and normalised the path by its bounding box, and then only set 1 came close to fitting (about 6% of its points read dark after a time of about 18) and the others had thousands of points reading dark, because the differences at the end of a path moved the scale of the whole figure; after changing to a fixed centre and scale per plane and cutting the duration to 16, sets 2, 3 and 5 still had 330, 1,128 and 1,580 points (of 12,801) reading dark, and a probe with step 0.005 against 0.00125 showed that for sets 2 to 5 the gap to the finer integration passes 0.001 of the tile after a time of about 8.7 to 14.3 (never for sets 0 and 1), which is chaos amplifying error, so I cut the duration to 8. **The thinning of the ink with time is not tested separately**, and no longer duration or other parameters (ρ and so on) were checked. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0492). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 47, seed ^ salt)` picks one start set (`variants`, 6 sets of (x₀, y₀, z₀, plane)); `x' = σ(y − x)`, `y' = x(ρ − z) − y`, `z' = xy − βz` are integrated with a fourth-order Runge-Kutta method for 1,600 steps (step 0.005), one point per step, projected as (x, z), (y, z) or (x, y) and placed at `0.5 + (a − centre a)·0.82/56` and `0.5 − (b − centre b)·0.82/56` (centres (0, 25), (0, 25), (0, 0)), so z points up; every step is a segment, the half width of segment i is `0.0035·(1 − 0.5·(i − 0.5)/1600)` and it is filed into the 24×24 buckets it touches. At sampling time the segments in the bucket are united as `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (t = `clamp(1 − d²/w²)`, exactly zero at the rim, so the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.72 − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(union / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·union·(0.88 + 0.12·0.72) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 off the line and metallic is 0; the retained cache has a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) plus JS arrays of 1,601 path points, 1,600 segments and the buckets; **I did not measure their byte size**. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (1,600 Runge-Kutta steps and the segment buckets) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 59 every seed matched exactly one start set, and the 6 sets (0 to 5) were chosen 7, 14, 8, 12, 11 and 8 times; for the 6 test seeds the least colour on the path is about 0.845 and none of the 6,401 points reads below 0.3; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 1.00%–4.07%, color is 0.02541–0.02573 to 0.87309–0.87373 with a mean of 0.04841–0.07415, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8467–0.8480 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 1.00%–4.11%, color is 0.02509–0.02530 to 0.87424–0.87471 with a mean of 0.04838–0.07451, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8488–0.8511 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 5.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (25.5, 19.5, 28.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0492 and the minimum z component is 252. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`harmonograph` adds the harmonograph figure, bringing the current catalog from 1071 to 1072 kinds (1073 gallery choices including plain). The figure of a two-pendulum harmonograph, one large figure per tile: x and y are each the sum of two damped sine waves (`x = 0.5 + 0.2·(sin(f₀t + p₀)·e^(−d₀t) + sin(f₁t + p₁)·e^(−d₁t))`, and the same for y with f₂ and f₃), with t running from 0 to 60, as a thin pale-blue line on dark blue-black; the swing decays, so the loops wind in to nested spirals, and the ink gets thinner with time (half width from 0.0045 down to 0.0018); the seed picks one of 6 presets (frequencies, phases, damping); the figure is never further than 0.4 from the centre (the sum of the two amplitudes 0.2), so all of it lies inside the tile and does not cross the seam. Unlike the existing `lissajoustable` (a 6×6 table of small undamped Lissajous curves), `spirographtable` (hypotrochoids) and `rhodoneatable` (rose curves), this is one large damped figure that fades. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The name 'harmonograph' and this description of damped pendulums are from my memory and I did not check the literature; real harmonographs often use 2 to 4 pendulums, and here each axis has two waves, a simplification.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the amplitude 0.2, the duration 60, the 3,200 segments, the ink half width 0.0045 with fade 0.6, the 6 parameter sets (frequency ratios such as 2:3:3:2.004, slightly detuned so that the curve does not close), the pale-blue-on-navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I picked them using previews: I looked at the previews of seeds 0 and 1 and found them attractive; I rendered six more seeds to files but did not look at each). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: for each seed exactly one of the 6 preset parameter sets has all 4,001 points of its curve (computed independently in the test from the formula above) reading bright (> 0.3, the least value > 0.8) — the other 5 sets have about half of their points reading dark — the least colour on the curve is about 0.845; and of 6,000 lattice points, those more than 0.02 from the curve (the 4,001 points) all read dark (< 0.2). The parameter set for each seed (seeds 0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 13 give sets 3, 5, 0, 2, 1, 4) was found with a probe and written into the test, so it is **not an independent oracle** (all 6 sets are covered). **The thinning of the ink with time is not tested separately** (it is only reflected indirectly in the value ranges), and no more parameter sets were checked. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0492). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 46, seed ^ salt)` picks one parameter set (`variants`, 6 sets of 12 numbers: f₀ to f₃, p₀ to p₃, d₀ to d₃); t from 0 to 60 is cut into 3,200 segments (each about 0.01875 of time), the half width of segment i is `0.0045·(1 − 0.6·(t_i − half a segment)/60)` and each segment is filed into the 24×24 buckets its bounding region touches (along the path at every sampling point with four offsets of the half width plus half a step). At sampling time the segments in the bucket are united as `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (t = `clamp(1 − d²/w²)`, exactly zero at the rim, so the field is C1 and there is no crease where segments overlap): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.72 − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, mask = `smooth(clamp(union / 0.35))`), height is `0.8·union·(0.88 + 0.12·0.72) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 off the line and metallic is 0; the retained cache has a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) plus JS arrays of 3,200 segments (6 numbers each) and the buckets; **I did not measure their byte size**. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (3,200 segments and their buckets) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): in a probe of seeds 0 to 59 every seed matched exactly one parameter set, and the 6 sets were chosen 12, 11, 8, 9, 10 and 10 times; for the 6 test seeds (0, 1, 3, 4, 5, 13) the least colour on the curve is about 0.845 and none of the 4,001 points reads below 0.3; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 8.43%–8.93%, color is 0.02533–0.02550 to 0.87374–0.87399 with a mean of 0.10999–0.11415, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8462–0.8496 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 6.14%–8.93%, color is 0.02513–0.02520 to 0.87433–0.87484 with a mean of 0.09085–0.11428, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8498–0.8525 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 11.4% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (24.5, 32.3, 45.0), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0492 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview (seeds 0 and 1, 2×2 tiles). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`delaunay` adds the Delaunay triangulation low-poly pattern, bringing the current catalog from 1070 to 1071 kinds (1072 gallery choices including plain). It is the Delaunay triangulation of a Poisson-disk point set on the torus (minimum distance 0.085): each triangle is one flat copper fill with a random tone between 0.25 and 0.6, the triangles are separated by thin dark-navy seams and each point is marked by a small dot; Delaunay means that the circumscribed circle of every triangle holds no other point (every point taken as its nearest image on the torus), so there are exactly 3 times as many edges as points and exactly 2 times as many triangles as points (a triangulation of the torus); the seed changes the point set. Unlike the existing `gabrielgraph` (the Gabriel graph, edges and points only) and `euclideanmst` (the minimum spanning tree), this is the whole triangulation with filled triangles. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The definition of 'Delaunay' is from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests verify it independently from the empty-circle definition.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the Poisson-disk minimum distance 0.085, the node radius 0.028, the seam half width 0.006, the triangle tone range 0.25 to 0.6 (`0.14 + 0.7·tone`), the copper-on-navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, seed 7: it looks like a low-poly copper collage, which I find attractive). The tests **read only the sampler output back**: the node centres are found as connected groups of at least 12 pixels with a colour above 0.66 (which leaves out the lone pixels that grain makes at the rim of a node; 87 to 88 nodes of 105 to 178 pixels each), and for every pair of nodes at most 0.25 apart a margin is computed **from the definition** (some circle through both nodes has no other node or torus image of a node inside; the circle centres lie on the bisector, each other node limits them to a half line, and the width of the remaining interval is the margin of the pair), and the seam is read along the segment (13 points at 35% to 65%, each the least colour of 5 points across the segment up to ±0.004 away; a seam when all 13 are below 0.2): pairs with a margin ≥ 0.006 must have a seam, pairs with ≤ −0.006 must not, and the seams read are exactly 3 times as many as the nodes; in addition, triples of nodes that are pairwise joined by seams and whose circumscribed circle holds no other node (by more than 0.004) are taken as faces, there are exactly 2 times as many faces as nodes, and in each face the interior grid points at least 0.012 from every side and 0.035 from every corner (outside the seams and the node discs) read the same colour (within 0.05, between 0.3 and 0.6). This shows that the sampler's seams agree with the empty-circle definition; it does **not** prove that the triangulation algorithm is right for arbitrary point sets, and pairs whose margin is close to 0 (nearly cocircular) are deliberately not judged. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0492). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): Poisson-disk dart throwing (candidates from the hash, kept when at least 0.085 from every point kept so far, at most 6,000 attempts, about 87 to 89 points); then for every point i the neighbours with a larger index within `maxEdge` = 0.3 as torus images (about 25) are taken, the circumscribed circle (centre and radius) of every pair of neighbours (j, k) is computed, circles of radius above 0.3 are skipped and for the others every point and image within 0.6 of i is checked to lie outside the circle (relative tolerance 1e-9); the survivors are the triangles (each is found once, from its vertex of least index); the triangles and their 3 sides are de-duplicated by an edge key and filed into 12×12 buckets (a triangle into every bucket its bounding box covers, in every one of the 3×3 translations that reach into the tile). At sampling time the bucket's points, segments and triangles are used: every point and every seam is a compactly supported kernel (united as `1 - Π(1 - t²)` with t = `clamp(1 − d²/r²)`, exactly zero at the rim) and the fill of the triangle is multiplied by the seam mask (exactly zero at the centre of the seam, so the jump of the tone between neighbouring triangles is hidden by the seam and the field stays C1, the tone rising with the fourth power of the distance): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor − gapTone)·cover + 0.7·(fill·seam·(1 − node) + node) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·cover·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the seams and metallic is 0; the retained cache has a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B (grain) plus JS arrays of points, segments and triangles (about 87 to 89 points, about 261 to 267 seams, about 174 to 178 triangles plus translated copies); **I did not measure their byte size**. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (about 300 pairs of neighbours per point, each with an empty-circle check against up to about 100 points) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): node counts (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) 87/87/88/89; the closest two nodes are 0.0825–0.0855 apart (probe, nine seeds); the edges with a margin ≥ 0.006 / ≤ −0.006 are 253/437, 259/433, 259/463 and 260/455 pairs for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7, all consistent with the seams read; the number of seams read equals 3 × the number of nodes (probe, nine seeds: 0, 1, 0xffffffff, 7, 2, 3, 100, 101, 102); the faces are 174/174/176 (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) = 2 × the nodes, every face has interior points to check and no face has a mismatching fill; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 26.17%–28.89%, color is 0.02631–0.02716 to 0.84991–0.85000 with a mean of 0.42040–0.42754, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8683–0.8716 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 26.13%–28.93%, color is 0.02539–0.02611 to 0.85036–0.85213 with a mean of 0.42039–0.42838, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8709–0.8746 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 39.4% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (115.0, 79.7, 70.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0492 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`perfectarray` adds the m-sequence perfect array, bringing the current catalog from 1069 to 1070 kinds (1071 gallery choices including plain). A maximal length sequence (1023 bits) from a 10-bit linear feedback shift register (LFSR) is folded by the Chinese remainder theorem into a binary array of 31 columns by 33 rows (bit i goes to column i mod 31 and row i mod 33, because 31 and 33 are coprime): bright cells are 1 and dark cells 0, with 512 bright cells; the periodic (torus) autocorrelation of such an array is exactly −1 at all 1,022 non-zero shifts, unlike a random binary array; the seed picks the feedback mask and the starting state (which amounts to shifting the whole array); the surface is a clean mosaic of binary-noise squares. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The names 'm-sequence' and 'perfect array' and the folding method are from my memory and I did not check the literature; the tests verify the autocorrelation only from its definition.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 31×33 cell counts, the two tones (bright `0.14 + 0.7`, dark `0.14`), the cream-on-navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices; because 31 and 33 differ the cells are slightly rectangular (aspect 33/31) (I looked at only one preview, seed 7: a clean mosaic of binary-noise squares with a faint diagonal structure). **The tests do not reproduce the LFSR at all**: they only read the 31×33 cell-centre colours back from the sampler (threshold 0.5, with no read-back within ±0.12 of the threshold) and verify that exactly 512 cells are bright and that the torus autocorrelation is exactly −1 at all 1,022 non-zero shifts (checked one by one for six seeds: 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 0xffffffff); a copy with one bright and one dark cell swapped confirms that the check is not vacuous (its autocorrelations are no longer all −1). In addition I probed seeds 100 to 299 (200 seeds): all read back cleanly with autocorrelation all −1, and 198 of them are distinct (200 seeds give only 198 different arrays). This shows that the sampler draws arrays with that property; it does **not** prove any general theorem about m-sequences, and no other size was checked (only 31×33). Between seeds 0 and 1, 50.05% of the cells differ (the test allows 0.4–0.6). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0196). The tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler): `hash(0, 43, seed ^ salt)` picks one of the 8 feedback masks `525, 531, 567, 581, 619, 627, 633, 639` (the first 8 of the 31 odd masks between 1 and 1023 for which, in a script I ran, the register goes through all 1,023 non-zero states) and `hash(1, 43, seed ^ salt)` picks the starting state `1 + floor(h · 1023)` (1 to 1023); then 1,023 iterations write `bits[(i mod 33)·31 + (i mod 31)] = state & 1`, with the feedback bit the parity of `state & mask` (by bit folding) and `state = ((state << 1) | feedback) & 1023`; at sampling time each cell is a compactly supported rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1, swept with 31, 33 and 128 cells): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + 0.7·bit − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Uint8Array(1023)` of 1,023 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 132,095 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): for six seeds (0/1/2/3/7/0xffffffff) the number of bright cells is 512 and the set of autocorrelation values is {−1}; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 35.84%–35.94%, color is 0.02526–0.02572 to 0.85419–0.85453 with a mean of 0.36525–0.36553, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8476–0.8483 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 35.84%–35.88%, color is 0.02516–0.02528 to 0.85468–0.85488 with a mean of 0.36540–0.36562, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8498–0.8502 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 35.9% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (96.5, 98.5, 88.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0196 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`kaprekar` adds the Kaprekar constant table, bringing the current catalog from 1068 to 1069 kinds (1070 gallery choices including plain). Kaprekar's routine on 4-digit numbers: arrange the digits of a 4-digit number (leading zeros kept) into the biggest and the smallest number, subtract, and repeat; the cell in row r and column c shows how many subtractions the number 100·r + c (0 to 9999, in 100 rows of 100 columns) needs to reach 6174, as one of 9 tones from dark to bright teal for 0 to 7 subtractions; the 10 repdigits (0000, 1111, …, 9999) never get there (the subtraction gives 0) and take the darkest tone; the seed moves the whole table around the torus; the surface shows a fine diagonal striping like weaving. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The names 'Kaprekar' and the constant 6174 are from my memory; the tests confirm with their own computation that every number that is not a repdigit reaches 6174 within 7 subtractions.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 100×100 table, the 9 tones (`0.7·(steps + 1) / 9`), the teal colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, seed 7: the cells are about 5 pixels wide and it looks like a fine teal weave-like texture of low contrast, which I do not think is especially attractive). The sampler sorts the digits as strings; the tests recompute the number of subtractions for all 10,000 numbers **in a different way** — taking the digits by division and sorting them as numbers — and confirm that the numbers needing 0 to 7 subtractions are 1, 383, 576, 2,400, 1,272, 1,518, 1,656 and 2,184 (9,990 in all, i.e. every number that is not a repdigit reaches 6174 within 7 subtractions) and that the 10 repdigits never get there; they also compare the cell-centre colours with each of the 10,000 possible shifts (grain amplitude 0.015, tolerance 0.03) and confirm that exactly one shift fits for every seed — under that shift the whole 10,000-cell table agrees with the test's own computation (the largest distance of a read-back from a whole step is 0.192 of a step, far below 0.5). This shows that the sampler draws this Kaprekar table; it does **not** prove the theorem 'every 4-digit number reaches 6174 within 7 steps' itself (here it is only computed by the test's own code over 0 to 9999), and other numbers of digits were not checked (only 4 digits). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0469). The lit-area shares are close at 256² and 512² sampling (see below), with cells about 2.6 and 5.1 pixels wide and an AO minimum of 0.6 (the cells are so small that the seams fill most of them); the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler), for every `number = 0…9999`: starting from `current = number` and `steps = 0`, while `current ≠ 6174` and `steps < 20` the number is padded to a 4-character string (leading zeros), its digits sorted and `next = the digits in descending order as a number − the digits in ascending order as a number`; `next = 0` (a repdigit) sets −1 and stops, otherwise `current = next` and `steps` goes up by one; the tone is `0.7·(steps + 1) / 9`, stored in a `Float64Array(10000)`; at sampling time each cell is a compactly supported rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1) and the cell index is shifted by amounts from `hash(0, 42, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 42, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 100): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(10000)` of 80,000 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 211,072 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM).
