Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (10,000 numbers, each with up to 7 string sorts and subtractions) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): the counts over all 10,000 numbers are (−1: 10; 0 to 7: 1, 383, 576, 2,400, 1,272, 1,518, 1,656, 2,184); each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has exactly one fitting shift, (20, 88), (2, 57), (6, 84) and (79, 66), with a worst fit error of 0.01477–0.01494; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 46.35%–46.54%, color is 0.02559–0.02576 to 0.77626–0.77657 with a mean of 0.43049–0.43078, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8388–0.8405 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 46.32%–46.40%, color is 0.02522–0.02532 to 0.77681–0.77701 with a mean of 0.43059–0.43064, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8412–0.8425 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 31.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ and 83.7% of the cell-centre colours differ by more than 0.05; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (65.3, 115.5, 98.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0469 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hypercube` adds the hypercube projection, bringing the current catalog from 1067 to 1068 kinds (1069 gallery choices including plain). The plane projection of a hypercube of 4 to 7 dimensions (picked by the seed, 16 to 128 vertices): the vertices are the 2ⁿ bit strings and two vertices are joined when they differ in exactly one bit; bit k of a vertex moves it by ±½ along the unit vector at the angle k·π/n, so the picture is the symmetric projection of the Petrie polygon, scaled to just fit the tile; a vertex is brighter the more bits it has set and an edge takes the number of bits of its lower end; thin pink lines and small dots on a deep purple-blue ground, like a symmetric star network. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (It differs from point-set graphs such as `gabrielgraph`: the figure here is the hypercube given by bit operations.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the way the dimension 4 to 7 is picked (quarters of `hash(0, 41, seed ^ salt)`), the dot radius 0.011, the line half width 0.0035, the scale that puts the biggest coordinate 0.44 from the middle of the tile, the pink colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14, tones from 0.45 to 1 of the span) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at previews of seed 7 (4 dimensions) and seed 0 (6 dimensions)). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**, compared with a projection geometry written separately in the test: with seeds 1, 4, 0 and 3 giving 4, 5, 6 and 7 dimensions (that mapping I measured first with a probe), for every pair of vertices with different projections the 13 sample points from 20% to 80% of the way along the chord between them, 5% apart, all being above 0.3 counts as 'the chord is on the drawing'; (1) pairs differing in one bit (the edges of the hypercube, n·2ⁿ⁻¹ = 32, 80, 192 and 448 of them) must all be on the drawing; (2) for the other pairs (many long chords lie on other edges and are not empty) the test's own largest distance of the chord's points from the nearest edge or vertex decides: under 0.002 is clearly on the drawing and the read-back must be all lit, over 0.004 is clearly not and the read-back must not be all lit, and in between is not judged (only for 7 dimensions, 1,428 pairs); pairs of vertices with the same projection are not judged (0 for 4 dimensions, 1 for 5, 18 for 6 and 1 for 7); for all four dimensions no pair disagrees under these judgements. This shows that the sampler's picture agrees with this projection geometry; it does **not** show that the choice of the angles k·π/n is the only or the standard way to draw it (that is my own choice and I did not look it up), nor that every seed falls on one of the four dimensions (the 17 seeds of the probe, 0–15 and 0xffffffff, were each one of them; no others were checked), and the 1,428 chords of the 7-dimensional picture between the margins are not judged. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0444). The lit-area share varies a lot with the dimension between seeds (see below) because higher dimensions have many more lines; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) `hash(0, 41, seed ^ salt)` picks the dimension `n` (4 to 7); for every vertex `v` (`0 ≤ v < 2ⁿ`) `x = Σ ((bit k of v) − ½)·cos(kπ/n)` and `y = Σ ((bit k of v) − ½)·sin(kπ/n)` are computed, then the largest absolute coordinate `extent` is taken and the position is `0.5 + (x / extent)·0.44`; every vertex is put into 16×16 buckets; for every vertex and every bit `k` that is 0 an edge goes to `v | 2ᵏ` and is filed into the buckets a sample point could be in (stepping along the path by 0.25/16 with the half width plus half a step as the reach), with the tone `0.45 + 0.55·(number of bits of the lower end + ½) / n`; at sampling time a vertex uses `t = max(0, 1 − distance² / radius²)` over the sample's bucket and its eight neighbours (the dot's tone is `0.45 + 0.55·number of bits / n`) and an edge the same formula over the segments in the sample's bucket, all combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the field is C1), the tones where they overlap being averaged with the weights `t²`; `total = 1 − complement`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, `tone` is `0.7 ×` the average tone), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the tables of vertices and edges (at most 128 vertices and 448 edges for 7 dimensions, bytes not counted item by item). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): seeds 1, 4, 0 and 3 are 4, 5, 6 and 7 dimensions (the probe also found seeds 7 and 11 at 4 dimensions, 9 and 0xffffffff at 5, seeds 2, 5, 6, 8, 12, 13 and 15 at 6 and seeds 10 and 14 at 7); all 32/80/192/448 edges read back as lit; judged chords (clearly on the drawing / clearly not / not judged): 0/88/0 for 4 dimensions, 155/260/0 for 5, 420/1,386/0 for 6 and 1,673/4,578/1,428 for 7, with 0 disagreements; the C1 probe (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff, along grid lines and over 16,000 sample points) found 0 violations; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 4.55%–17.14%, color is 0.02541–0.02574 to 0.84507–0.85068 with a mean of 0.07261–0.15547, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8345–0.8392 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 5.82%–17.13%, color is 0.02509–0.02530 to 0.84477–0.85190 with a mean of 0.07935–0.15533, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8403–0.8449 relief; between seed 0 (6 dimensions) and seed 1 (4 dimensions), 19.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 (4 dimensions) 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (29.4, 18.5, 43.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0444 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the previews (seeds 7 and 0, 2×2 tiles): the 4-dimensional one a symmetric octagonal network, the 6-dimensional one a dense dodecagonal mesh. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`fareygraph` adds the Farey graph, bringing the current catalog from 1066 to 1067 kinds (1068 gallery choices including plain). The Farey graph of an order from 7 to 12 (picked by the seed): its vertices are the reduced fractions between 0 and 1 (0/1 and 1/1 included) whose denominator is at most the order, and two fractions a / b < c / d are joined when c b − a d = 1; every edge is drawn as the semicircular arc on the segment between the two points and mirrored in the baseline, and the tile repeats with period 1 in both directions; thin cyan arcs on a deep blue ground, the big arcs dimmer and the small ones brighter, all converging in bright clusters near 0 and 1. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (It differs from the existing `fordcircles`, which draws Ford discs rather than the arcs of the Farey graph, and from `sterndiatomic`.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the way the order 7 to 12 is picked (sixths of `hash(0, 38, seed ^ salt)`), the line half width 0.004, the tone of the biggest arcs being 0.45 of the span, the cyan colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, seed 7, order 10). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: with seeds 0, 6, 15, 1, 5 and 3 giving the orders 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 (that mapping I measured first with a probe), all pairs of reduced fractions a / b < c / d with a denominator up to the order are taken and eleven points are read along the upper semicircle on the segment between them, at 15° to 165° in steps of 15°; an arc counts as drawn when all eleven are above 0.3; the tests check that 'drawn' agrees exactly with 'c b − a d = 1' (the Farey neighbour criterion, written from the determinant and not looked up), that the numbers of arcs drawn are 35, 43, 55, 63, 83 and 91 (counted from the read-back) and that, when read back at one order higher, some Farey neighbours are not drawn — i.e. no arc of the next order is drawn. This shows that the arcs the sampler draws are exactly the edges of the Farey graph of that order; it does **not** show that every point along an arc lies on a circle (only 11 points were taken), nor that every seed falls on one of the six orders (the 18 seeds of the probe, 0–16 and 0xffffffff, were each one of them; no other seeds were checked). **A mistake of my own**: the first version of the field had a crease near the top and bottom and the left and right edges of the tile (the C1 test failed, with a second difference divided by h of 1,152) — the biggest arc (0/1 to 1/1) touches the top and bottom edges of the tile exactly and I took only the nearest baseline and the nearest horizontal copy, so at the edge two copies each contribute but only one was taken and the slope flips on the edge; after uniting the arcs of the neighbouring tile copies (±1 in x and in y), the C1 probe found no violation for the three seeds used. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0422). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points on the thin lines differs; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) `hash(0, 38, seed ^ salt)` picks the order `n` (7 to 12), all reduced fractions `a / b` with denominator at most `n` (`gcd(a, b) = 1`, `0 ≤ a ≤ b`) are listed and for every pair `a / b < c / d` with `c·b − a·d = 1` an arc is made: centre at the middle of the two points, radius half the distance and tone `0.45 + 0.55·(1 − 2·radius)`; at sampling time every arc and its copies one period away in x and y are looked at when the point is within the radius plus the half width, using `t = max(0, 1 − (ρ − R)² / half width²)` where `ρ` is the distance of the sample from the centre on the baseline (the baseline is at `v = 0.5` and the distance to it is taken as an absolute value, so there is a mirror image on each side), each combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the union and the whole field are C1), the tones of arcs that meet being averaged with the weights `t²`; `total = 1 − complement`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, `tone` is `0.7 ×` the average tone), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the table of arcs (at most 91 for order 12, bytes not counted item by item). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time** (every sample point looks through all the arcs, skipping most of them by a cheap comparison with the half-width range). Measured (tool-run): seeds 0, 6, 15, 1, 5 and 3 are orders 7, 8, 9, 10, 11 and 12 (the probe also found seeds 2, 4, 10, 11 and 12 at order 7, seeds 7, 8 and 14 at order 10, seed 9 at order 11, seed 13 at order 12 and seeds 16 and 0xffffffff at order 8), with 19/23/29/33/43/47 fractions, 35/43/55/63/83/91 arcs and 136/210/351/465/820/990 pairs that are not arcs; for all six orders there is no pair whose read-back disagrees with the Farey criterion and the read-back at one order higher misses Farey-neighbour arcs; the lowest read-back colour at a sample point of a drawn arc is 0.440–0.449; the C1 probe (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff, along grid lines and over 17,000 sample points) found 0 violations after the fix; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 7.22%–8.77%, color is 0.02530–0.02565 to 0.84328–0.84671 with a mean of 0.09984–0.11182, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8400–0.8440 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 7.17%–8.67%, color is 0.02511–0.02526 to 0.84363–0.84834 with a mean of 0.09983–0.11170, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8439–0.8472 relief; between seeds 0 and 1 only 1.5% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ (the arcs of orders 7 and 10 are mostly the same); in the seed-7 (order 10) 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (21.0, 37.4, 56.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0422 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): cyan arcs converging in bright clusters near 0 and 1, the biggest circles tangent. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`knightstour` adds the knight's tour, bringing the current catalog from 1065 to 1066 kinds (1067 gallery choices including plain). A knight's tour of a 16×16 board (the knight moves like a knight and visits every square exactly once) by Warnsdorff's rule: from a starting square decided by the hash the knight always goes to the unvisited square from which it has the fewest further moves, ties being broken by the hash; the rule can get stuck, so up to 60 attempts are made (each with its own start and tie-breaking) and the first one that visits all 256 squares is kept, or the longest if none does; every square is a dot and every move a segment from the middle of one square to the middle of the next, its tone going from 0.45 of the span at the start of the tour to the whole span at its end; an amber web on a deep purple-black ground, with the edges of the board forming dark seams in the tile. The seed decides the starting square and the tie-breaking. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 16×16 board, the limit of 60 attempts, the dot radius of 0.22 squares, the line radius of 0.09 squares, the amber colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, seed 7). Warnsdorff's rule is written from my memory and **I did not look it up**. The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: on the 16×16 squares the colour at a square's centre above 0.3 means the path passes through it; two squares a knight's move apart (four directions) are joined when all 13 sample points from 20% to 80% along the segment between their centres, 5% apart, are above 0.3; for seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 0xffffffff, 109 and 110 the tests check that all 256 square centres are lit (no ambiguous read-back, nothing lit along the tile edge), that exactly two squares are joined to one square and the other 254 to two, and that walking along the joins from one end visits exactly 256 squares and arrives at the other end — a path through every square in which, because joining is defined by the knight's move, every step is a legal knight's move. This shows that the sampler draws a knight's path through every square for these eight seeds; the probe also checked seeds 100 to 199 and all 100 passed, but that is **not** a proof for every seed. I made a mistake of my own that is worth recording: the first version of the read-back used only 5 sample points (20%, 35%, 50%, 65%, 80%) and 24 of the 100 probe seeds came out as 'not a complete tour' — I first thought the sampler was wrong, but the read-back was at fault: for a pair that is not joined the 5 points on its segment happened to fall exactly on crossings of other knight's moves and it was taken to be joined; with 13 points none of the 100 seeds has a problem. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0280). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points on the lines differs; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) up to 60 attempts are made: attempt `attempt` starts on the square given by `hash(attempt, 0, seed ^ salt)`, and then at every step, among the unvisited targets of the 8 knight's moves, the one with the fewest unvisited knight's-move targets of its own is chosen, ties being decided one by one with `hash(attempt × 256 + step, 1 + number of ties, seed ^ salt) < 1 / number of ties` (reservoir sampling); an attempt ends when the knight cannot move, the first attempt that visits all 256 squares is kept and otherwise the longest; the result is stored as `following[cell]` (the number of the next square, −1 at the end) and `order[cell]` (the step number); at sampling time a dot uses `t = max(0, 1 − distance² / radius²)` over the sample's cell and its eight neighbours and a segment the same formula over the 'this square to the next' segment of every cell in the 7×7 around the sample (a knight's move is up to about 2.24 squares long, so ±3 squares must be looked at), the distance being that to the segment, each combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the union and the whole field are C1); where segments cross their tones are averaged with the weights `t²`, the tone is `0.7·(line tone·(1 − dot union) + dot union)`; `total = 1 − (complement of lines)(complement of dots)`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is `following` and `order` as `Int16Array(256)` of 512 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 132,096 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time, and I did not record how many attempts each seed used.** Measured (tool-run): seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 7, 0xffffffff, 109 and 110 all have 256 lit square centres, 255 joins, two ends with the others at degree 2, a walk of 256 squares to the other end, no ambiguous read-back and nothing lit along the tile edge; seeds 100–199 (100 seeds) pass the same checks; of the 255 moves of seeds 0 and 1, 93 are the same; a separate script that does not use the sampler's code (different random numbers and tie-breaking, not the sampler's hash) shows that a single Warnsdorff attempt gets stuck in 173 of 20,000 tries (0.865%) and ends in a closed tour, with the ends a knight's move apart, in 583 — this only explains why the sampler retries and is not a statistic of the sampler itself; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 24.39%–24.45%, color is 0.02546–0.02573 to 0.85101–0.85236 with a mean of 0.23899–0.23970, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8425–0.8440 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 28.21%–28.38%, color is 0.02513–0.02519 to 0.85238–0.85374 with a mean of 0.24216–0.24325, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8469–0.8493 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 25.9% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (70.8, 47.2, 42.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0280 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): an amber web of knight's moves. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`daynight` adds the Day and Night cellular automaton, bringing the current catalog from 1064 to 1065 kinds (1066 gallery choices including plain). The Day and Night cellular automaton on a 32×32 torus (a dead cell is born with 3, 6, 7 or 8 live neighbours among the 8 around it, a live cell stays with 3, 4, 6, 7 or 8), started from a random soup (each cell is alive with a probability of 50%, from the hash) and run for 24 generations; the tile shows four consecutive generations in 2×2 panels of 32×32 cells — the top left is the generation after the warm-up, the top right the next one, the bottom left the one after that and the bottom right the last; live cells are raised pale yellow rounded-square tiles and dead cells dark blue-grey, a blotchy camouflage-like pattern. The seed decides the initial soup. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The name 'Day and Night' for the rule is from my memory and I did not look it up; the tests check the rule spelled out above. It differs from the existing `gameoflife`, `elementaryautomata` and others.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 32×32 torus, the initial density of 50%, the 24 warm-up generations, the pale yellow and dark blue-grey colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, seed 7). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: the colour at the centre of each of the 64×64 cells above 0.5 reads as alive (no read-back within 0.15 of the threshold), sorted into the four panels; each of the three later panels must be exactly the next generation, by the rule above, of the panel before it (written separately in the test from the rule, the 8 neighbours wrapping round the torus), and the ordinary Life rule (born with 3, stays with 2 or 3) is used as a control: it must **not** give the next panel, so the check is not vacuous; the tests also check that 40%–60% of the cells of each panel are alive and that 20%–35% of the cells change between neighbouring panels. This shows that the four panels the sampler draws are four consecutive generations of this rule; it does **not** show that the name of the rule is right (I did not look it up), nor that the initial soup is uniformly random or that the 24 warm-up generations are right (the test sees none of the warm-up, only the four generations after it), nor that every seed was checked (only seeds 0, 1, 2, 7 and 0xffffffff). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0378). The lit-area share, the colours and the mean differ considerably between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the share of live cells differs between seeds and the cell width (4 and 8 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Uint8Array(1024)` holds the 32×32 torus: `hash(cell, 0, seed ^ salt) < 0.5` is alive; in each generation the number `n` of live cells among the 8 neighbours (wrapping round the torus) is counted for every cell, a live cell stays when `n ≥ 3` and `n ≠ 5` and a dead cell is born when `n = 3` or `n ≥ 6`; 24 generations are run and then 3 more, giving four consecutive generations that are put into the top left, top right, bottom left and bottom right panels of the 64×64-cell tile in turn; at sampling time each cell is a compactly supported rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, `tone` is 0.7 for a live cell and 0 for a dead one), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to about 0.7344 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is `grid` of 4,096 B, the four generations as `Uint8Array(1024)` of 4,096 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 139,264 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (27 generations × 1,024 cells × 8 neighbours) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/2/7/0xffffffff): of the 15 transitions between consecutive panels, the number of cells that disagree with the rule is 0 every time, with no ambiguous read-back; compared with the ordinary Life rule the same transitions disagree in 303–474 cells; the panels have 437–576 live cells (of 1,024); between neighbouring panels 242–311 cells change; between seeds 0 and 1, 51.8% of the 4,096 cells differ between alive and dead; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 32.83%–41.27%, color is 0.05897–0.05963 to 0.85431–0.85450 with a mean of 0.37886–0.44451, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8482–0.8494 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 30.09%–37.83%, color is 0.02514–0.02524 to 0.85452–0.85485 with a mean of 0.32823–0.38406, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8499–0.8508 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 35.6% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (100.0, 100.8, 76.7), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0378 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): blotchy camouflage of pale yellow and dark blue-grey, the four panels looking alike. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hamiltoncycle` adds the Hamiltonian cycle, bringing the current catalog from 1063 to 1064 kinds (1065 gallery choices including plain). A random Hamiltonian cycle of a 32×32 grid (one closed path that goes through every cell exactly once and returns to its start): a random spanning tree of a 16×16 coarse grid is taken by randomised Kruskal (the edges in the order of a hash) and thickened — every coarse cell is a 2×2 block of fine cells, a tree edge joins the two pairs of fine cells that face each other across it, and inside a block the join between the two fine cells along one side is used unless the tree has an edge through that side; every fine cell then has exactly two cycle edges and, because the tree is connected and has no cycle, the result is one single loop; a thick lime-green line winds over a deep purple-black ground like a labyrinth. The seed decides the spanning tree. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (The closest existing kinds are `moorecurve`, a fixed 8×8 Moore curve with one closed groove through every cell, and `perfectmaze`, an 8×8 maze of tree-shaped passages; this material is a random 32×32 Hamiltonian cycle generated from the seed, and its tests read it back to check that it really is one single loop.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 16×16 coarse grid, the path radius of 0.3 cells, the lime colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14, path tone 0.85 of the span) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, seed 7). The 'thickened tree gives a Hamiltonian cycle' construction is a standard method I wrote from memory and **did not look up**; only its result is checked below. The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: on the 32×32 cells the colour at a cell centre above 0.3 means the path passes through it, and the colour at the middle of the segment between two neighbouring cell centres above 0.3 means the two cells are joined (no read-back falls between 0.2 and 0.45 where it would be ambiguous); for seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 7 and 0xffffffff the tests check that all 1,024 cell centres are lit, that every cell is joined to exactly two neighbours, that walking along the joins from cell 0 visits exactly 1,024 cells and returns to cell 0 (a Hamiltonian cycle), and that nothing is lit along the edge of the tile (the loop never crosses the tile edge, so the paths of neighbouring tiles are a one-cell dark seam apart). This shows that the sampler draws one single Hamiltonian cycle for these six seeds; the probe also checked seeds 100 to 159 for the same conditions and all 60 passed, but that is **not** a proof for every seed. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0177). The colours and the lit-area share differ slightly between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points on the path differs; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) all 480 neighbouring edges of the 16×16 coarse grid are listed, sorted by `hash(k, 0, seed ^ salt)` and checked one by one with union-find (path halving): an edge whose two ends are not yet connected becomes a tree edge (`acrossTree` for the one to the right, `belowTree` for the one below); for every coarse cell `(x, y)` let `north`, `south`, `west` and `east` say whether the tree has an edge in that direction, `top = 2y·32 + 2x` the number of its upper left fine cell and `bottom = top + 32`, then `right[top] = north ? 0 : 1`, `right[bottom] = south ? 0 : 1`, `down[top] = west ? 0 : 1`, `down[top + 1] = east ? 0 : 1`; when `east` also `right[top + 1] = right[bottom + 1] = 1` and when `south` also `down[bottom] = down[bottom + 1] = 1` (`right[c]` and `down[c]` say that fine cell `c` is joined to the cell on its right or below it); at sampling time the path is a capsule for every cycle edge of the cell of the sample and its eight neighbours (`t = max(0, 1 − distance² to the segment / radius²)` in units of cells with a radius of 0.3), combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the union and the whole field are C1); `total = 1 − complement`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, `tone` is `0.7 × 0.85`), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is `right` and `down` of 1,024 B each, `acrossTree` and `belowTree` of 256 B each and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 133,632 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; the candidate and union-find arrays used by Kruskal are not counted). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): seeds 0, 1, 2, 3, 7 and 0xffffffff all have 1,024 lit cell centres, 1,024 joined pairs, degree 2 for every cell, a walk of 1,024 cells that returns to the start, no ambiguous read-back and nothing lit along the tile edge; seeds 100–159 (60 seeds) pass the same checks; of the 1,024 edges of seeds 0 and 1, 528 are the same (51.56%); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 49.30%–49.34%, color is 0.02536–0.02555 to 0.74908–0.74944 with a mean of 0.38348–0.38371, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8300–0.8313 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 49.48%–49.51%, color is 0.02510–0.02533 to 0.74961–0.74982 with a mean of 0.36626–0.36647, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8389–0.8398 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 25.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (78.5, 97.3, 60.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0177 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): a lime-green labyrinth-like line. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`paleyhadamard` adds the Paley Hadamard matrix, bringing the current catalog from 1062 to 1063 kinds (1064 gallery choices including plain). A Hadamard matrix from Paley's first construction: for a prime q with q mod 4 = 3 the matrix of order q + 1 with row 0 all +1, column 0 below it all −1, +1 on the rest of the diagonal and, for rows and columns i, j from 1 to q, the quadratic character of (i − j) mod q (+1 for a nonzero square, −1 otherwise); the seed picks one of the primes 43, 47, 59, 67, 71 and 79, so the order is 44, 48, 60, 68, 72 or 80; +1 is a bright gold and −1 a dark blue-grey rounded-square tile, the tiles raised with darker AO gaps. Because it depends only on i − j, the bulk shows diagonal bands (a Toeplitz structure) and row 0 and column 0 form a cross. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (It differs from the existing `hadamardmatrix`, the Sylvester construction of order 64, and from `paleytable`, a Legendre-symbol table of order 61 that has no row 0 or column 0 and is not a Hadamard matrix.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the way the six primes are picked (sixths of `hash(0, 36, seed ^ salt)`), the tone of −1 being 0.3 of that of +1, the gold and blue-grey colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, seed 7, order 68). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: with seeds 3, 1, 0, 7, 6 and 16 giving the orders 44, 48, 60, 68, 72 and 80 (that mapping I measured first with a probe), the colour at the centre of every cell above 0.6 reads as +1 and otherwise −1, with no read-back within 0.1 of the threshold; on the read-back matrix the tests check that every two different rows have inner product 0 and every row has inner product equal to the order with itself (the definition of a Hadamard matrix, computed pair by pair from the definition), that row 0 is all +1, that column 0 below it is all −1 and that the diagonal is all +1; and that flipping any one entry, or reading at a wrong order (4 more), breaks the orthogonality, so the check is not vacuous. This shows that the sampler draws Hadamard matrices of these six orders; it does **not** show the theorem behind Paley's construction (I did not verify that theorem, only that the six matrices drawn satisfy the definition), nor that every seed falls on one of the six orders (the 13 seeds of the probe, 0 to 11 and 0xffffffff, were all one of the six orders and a scan also found seed 16 to be order 80; no other seeds were checked). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0421). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points inside the cells differs; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) `hash(0, 36, seed ^ salt)` picks a prime `q` and the order `size = q + 1`; for `1 ≤ t < q` the squares `t² mod q` are marked; the value in row `row` and column `col` is +1 for `row = 0`, −1 for `col = 0` (with `row > 0`) and otherwise, with `delta = row − col`, +1 when `delta = 0` or `(delta + q) mod q` is a square and −1 otherwise, stored in a `Uint8Array(size²)`; the tone is `0.7` for +1 and `0.7 × 0.3` for −1; at sampling time each cell is a compactly supported rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is at most (order 80) a `Uint8Array(6,400)` plus a 79-byte table of squares and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, about 137.6 kB, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): all 13 seeds (0–11 and 0xffffffff) read back an orthogonal Hadamard matrix at one of the six orders with no ambiguous read-back; the lowest read-back colour for +1 is 0.825–0.826 and the highest for −1 is 0.364–0.365; seeds 3, 1, 0, 7, 6 and 16 are orders 44, 48, 60, 68, 72 and 80 (seeds 4 and 5 are also 44, 2 is 48, 8, 9 and 0xffffffff are 60, 10 is 72 and 11 is 68); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 36.35%–36.67%, color is 0.02521–0.02586 to 0.85421–0.85459 with a mean of 0.44404–0.44443, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8467–0.8479 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 36.28%–36.68%, color is 0.02509–0.02529 to 0.85460–0.85487 with a mean of 0.44381–0.44431, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8494–0.8500 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 41.6% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 (order 68) 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (117.6, 103.2, 65.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0421 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): diagonal bands of gold and dark with a cross along row 0 and column 0. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`cayleytable` adds the Cayley table, bringing the current catalog from 1061 to 1062 kinds (1063 gallery choices including plain). The multiplication table (Cayley table) of a group of order 16: the seed picks one of six groups — the cyclic group Z16, Z8×Z2, Z4×Z4, Z4×Z2×Z2, Z2×Z2×Z2×Z2 and the dihedral group of the octagon (a rotation a and a reflection bit b, element number `8b + a`, with `(a, b)(c, d) = (a + (−1)^b c, b + d)`); the elements of a direct product are numbered in mixed radix with the first factor varying fastest, so element 0 is the identity; the tile in row `row` and column `col` holds the number of the product of element `row` and element `col`, shown as one of 16 rose tones from dark to bright, the tiles raised with darker AO gaps. Every row and every column holds each number exactly once (a Latin square). It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (It differs from the existing `xortable`, which is the table of Z2⁶, and from number-theory tables such as `modulartable` and `paleytable`.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 16×16 size, the way the six groups are picked (sixths of `hash(0, 35, seed ^ salt)`), the rose tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only two previews, seeds 0 and 5, which are both Z2×Z2×Z2×Z2 in the probe and so look the same; I did **not** view the other four groups). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: the colour at the centre of every cell is `toneFloor` plus a whole multiple of `toneSpan / 15` plus grain of less than a third of a step, so rounding gives the number (the largest distance of a read-back from a whole step is 0.317–0.321 of a step); with seeds 0, 1, 4, 8, 12 and 13 covering the six groups, the tests check on the read-back 16×16 table that every row and every column has 16 different numbers (a Latin square), that row 0 and column 0 are the identity, that the product is associative for all 4,096 triples, and read off three quantities that tell the groups of order 16 apart — whether the table is symmetric, the number of elements other than the identity whose square is the identity and the largest order of an element — whose expected values (worked out by hand, not checked against the literature) are (symmetric, 15, 2) for Z2⁴, (symmetric, 7, 4) for Z4×Z2×Z2, (symmetric, 3, 8) for Z8×Z2, (symmetric, 3, 4) for Z4×Z4, (symmetric, 1, 16) for Z16 and (not symmetric, 9, 8) for the dihedral group, all six matching. This shows that the sampler draws multiplication tables of these six groups (identified by these invariants, the six being pairwise non-isomorphic); it does **not** show that the table is cell for cell the one in a textbook (these invariants say nothing about, for example, how the elements are numbered), nor that every seed falls on these six groups (the 200 seeds of the probe gave only these six combinations of invariants, 41/34/37/32/33/23 times for Z2⁴, Z4×Z2×Z2, Z8×Z2, Z4×Z4, Z16 and the dihedral group respectively, of which the dihedral group's 23 is the fewest and I did not check whether the distribution is uniform). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0069). The lit-area share differs slightly between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points inside the cells differs; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) `hash(0, 35, seed ^ salt)` picks a group and builds the multiplication table as a `Uint8Array(256)`: a direct product uses mixed radix, taking `(x mod m + y mod m) mod m` for every factor and multiplying by the radix weight; the dihedral group uses `(b xor d)·8 + ((a + (b = 0 ? c : 8 − c)) mod 8)`; the value in row `row` and column `col` is the number of element `row` times element `col` and the tone is `0.7·value / 15`; at sampling time each cell is a compactly supported rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Uint8Array(256)` of 256 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 131,328 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): all 13 seeds (0–11 and 0xffffffff) are Latin squares with the identity in row 0 and column 0 and 0 associativity failures; seeds 0, 1, 4, 8, 12 and 13 are Z2⁴, Z4×Z2×Z2, Z8×Z2, Z4×Z4, Z16 and the dihedral group respectively; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 35.74%, color is 0.02561–0.02575 to 0.85352–0.85447 with a mean of 0.36491–0.36498, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8444–0.8466 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 35.35%–35.37%, color is 0.02517–0.02537 to 0.85447–0.85485 with a mean of 0.36478–0.36493, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8483–0.8507 relief; between seed 0 (Z2⁴) and seed 1 (Z4×Z2×Z2) only 0.33% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ, but 25% of the cell-centre colours differ by more than 0.05; in the seed-7 (Z8×Z2) 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (105.8, 48.9, 70.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0069 and the minimum z component is 255. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sortingnetwork` adds the sorting network, bringing the current catalog from 1060 to 1061 kinds (1062 gallery choices including plain). A schematic of a sorting network for 16 wires: on 16 horizontal wires every comparator is drawn as a vertical link between two wires with a bright dot at each end; a comparator puts the smaller of the two values on the wire with the lower number; the seed picks one of three classical networks — Batcher's odd-even merge sort (63 comparators in 24 columns), the odd-even transposition sort (120 in 16) and the bitonic sort in its standard form (80 in 26); the comparators of one layer are dealt into columns by interval colouring and the layers follow one another from left to right; a green circuit pattern on a deep blue-green ground with the wires dimmer, the links brighter and the dots brightest. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 16 wires, the wire half width 0.0035, the link half width 0.0035, the dot radius 0.014, the tones (0.45 of the span for the wires, 0.2 more for the links and 0.35 more for the dots, span 0.7, floor 0.14), the blue-green to green colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at three previews, seeds 7, 1 and 0). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: on a 512×512 grid the pixels with a colour above 0.7 are grouped by a 4-connected flood fill on the torus and the centre of every dot is the circular mean (about 8–14 pixels each); the dots are split into columns by u (within 0.004), sorted by v within a column and paired two by two, and the tests check that every dot sits on a wire (the row within 0.05 of a wire spacing), that the midpoint of a pair's link is above 0.52 and that the gap midpoint to the next pair is not; the read-back comparators are then applied from left to right to all 65,536 inputs of 0s and 1s and every one must come out sorted — by the 0-1 principle that proves the network sorts every input (the 0-1 principle is a standard result about sorting networks that I use here and did not verify separately) — and leaving out the first, the middle or the last comparator must stop it sorting, so the check is not vacuous. The tests also check that every wire is a line of colour 0.43–0.48 outside the columns and that the rows between the wires are below 0.06. This shows that the sampler draws networks that really sort; it does **not** show that nothing else is on the picture (only the positions and tones of the dots, links and wires were checked), nor that the three networks are optimal or minimal, nor that every seed was checked (only seeds 0, 1 and 0xffffffff, with the probe also looking at seeds 2–7, which fall on the same three networks). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0192). The lit-area share, the highest colour and the mean differ widely between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the dots are tiny and where the sample points fall inside them and the resolution matter a lot; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) `hash(0, 34, seed ^ salt)` picks a network and builds its list of comparators `(top, bottom)`: the odd-even merge sort uses the standard recursion `merge(low, size, reach)` (with `step = 2·reach`, two recursive calls and then `(i, i + reach)` from `i = low + reach` in steps of `step`; when `step ≥ size` it adds `(low, low + reach)`); the bitonic sort in standard form first does for `size = 2, 4, …, 16` the 'flip' `(start + i, start + size − 1 − i)` and then, for `span = size / 4` halving each time, adds `(i, i + span)` for `i mod 2span < span`; the odd-even transposition sort makes 16 rounds, each with `(i, i + 1)` from `i = round mod 2` in steps of 2; every comparator is put in the layer after the last layer of its two wires, the comparators of a layer are sorted by their top wire and dealt into columns by greedy interval colouring, and the columns of the layers follow one another from left to right; at sampling time the wires are `t = max(0, 1 − distance² / half width²)` to the nearest wire, the links and dots use the same formula for every comparator of the sample's column and of the column on each side (a link uses the distance to a vertical segment, a dot the distance to a point, and the dot radius is wider so the neighbouring columns have to be looked at), each combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the unions and the whole field are C1); `total = 1 − (complement of wire)(complement of links)(complement of dots)`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`tone` is `0.7·(0.45 + 0.2·link union + 0.35·dot union)`), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the comparator and column tables (at most 120 comparators, bytes not counted item by item). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction (comparator list and column assignment) or the sampling time.** Measured (tool-run): seed 0 reads back 63 comparators in 24 columns with 126 dots; seed 1 reads back 120 in 16 with 240 dots; seed 0xffffffff reads back 80 in 26 with 160 dots (the probe also looked at seeds 2–7: seeds 3 and 6 are the odd-even merge sort, seeds 2, 4, 5 and 7 the odd-even transposition sort); no seed has a column with an odd number of dots, a dot off a wire, a link that is not lit or a gap bridged by a link; every read-back network sorts all 65,536 inputs; in the probe leaving out any one comparator of the three networks (63 + 120 + 80 removals) stops it sorting; for seed 0 the wires outside the columns have colour 0.4448–0.4699 and the rows between them 0.0251–0.0546 (16 wires and 16 rows checked); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 8.72%–11.72%, color is 0.02523–0.02564 to 0.7601–0.8416 with a mean of 0.13286–0.14309, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8195–0.8411 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 8.00%–10.08%, color is 0.02512–0.02530 to 0.8278–0.8497 with a mean of 0.11642–0.12685, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8435–0.8470 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 15.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 (odd-even transposition sort) 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (19.9, 43.5, 44.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0192 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the previews (seeds 7 and 1 are brick-wall-like regular grids, seed 0 a complicated circuit diagram). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`relativeneighborhood` adds the relative neighbourhood graph, bringing the current catalog from 1059 to 1060 kinds (1061 gallery choices including plain). The relative neighbourhood graph of a Poisson-disk point set on the torus: dart throwing on the unit torus first picks points at least 0.085 apart (about 90, selected as for `poissondisk`, `gabrielgraph` and `euclideanmst` with a different salt), then two points are joined when no third point is closer to both of them than they are to each other (the 'lune' between them is empty; the shortest way round the torus, distance at most 0.25); the points are drawn as small brighter discs and the edges as thinner lines, a pink network on a deep purple ground, sparser than the Gabriel graph and with a few more cycles than the minimum spanning tree. The seed decides the point set. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (It differs from `gabrielgraph` and `euclideanmst` in how the edges are chosen; 'minimum spanning tree ⊆ relative neighbourhood graph ⊆ Gabriel graph' is a standard result of geometric graph theory and I did not verify it here.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the minimum distance 0.085, the node radius 0.024, the edge half width 0.0075, the longest edge 0.25, the pink colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14, edge tone 0.55 of the node tone) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: as for `gabrielgraph` the pixels with a colour above 0.66 on a 512×512 grid are grouped and their circular means are the node centres (about 90 nodes of 150–180 pixels each, at least 0.083 apart); for every pair of nodes at most 0.25 apart a classification written separately in the test from the definition (the shortest way round the torus, no other centre closer to both of them than they are to each other) is used: for a pair that is clearly an edge (every other centre at least 0.003 further than the pair's distance from the farther of the two) the five points at 25%, 40%, 50%, 60% and 75% of the segment must all be above 0.3, and for a pair that is clearly not one (some centre at least 0.003 closer to both, and no third centre within 0.02 of the segment) those five points must not all be lit; the other pairs (within 0.003, or chain-like) are not judged. This shows that the sampler's edges agree with the definition of the relative neighbourhood graph for the pairs that are judged; it does **not** show that the excluded pairs or the pairs within 0.003 agree too, nor that the graph is connected or planar. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0157). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points and the resolution differ; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) 6,000 candidate points are taken one after another from `hash(k, 0/1, seed ^ salt)` and kept when their shortest torus distance to every point kept so far is at least 0.085 (about 87–92 points); for every pair of points (shortest torus vector, length at most 0.25) the pair becomes an edge when there is no third point k with `max(distance to i, distance to j) < the pair's distance`; every edge is filed into the 12×12 buckets that a sample point could be in (stepping along the path by 0.25/12, with the half width plus half a step as the reach), so a sample looks only into its own bucket; at sampling time a node uses `t = max(0, 1 − distance² / radius²)` over the points in the 3×3 buckets and an edge the same formula over the segments in the bucket (the distance being that to the segment), each combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the union and the whole field are C1); `total = 1 − (complement of the node union) × (complement of the edge union)`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`tone` is `0.7·(0.55 + 0.45·node union)`), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the point and edge tables (about 90 points and over a hundred edges, bytes not counted item by item). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): 89/89/87/92 read-back nodes, the closest pair 0.0848/0.0846/0.0851/0.0849 apart, 157–172 pixels per node on the 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff); clear edge pairs are 127/133/130/134, all with the five points lit (0 misjudged); clear non-edge pairs (chain-like pairs excluded) are 452/447/415/476, none with all five points lit (0 misjudged); the excluded chain-like pairs are 149/140/136/155; the pairs within 0.003 that are not judged are 18/15/16/25; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 17.63%–18.16%, color is 0.02543–0.02580 to 0.84884–0.85075 with a mean of 0.15242–0.15594, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8427–0.8456 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 17.63%–18.58%, color is 0.02519–0.02526 to 0.85096–0.85246 with a mean of 0.15240–0.15852, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8456–0.8485 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 29.3% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (52.2, 32.2, 58.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0157 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): a pink network with many quadrilaterals and a few dangling leaves. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`euclideanmst` adds the Euclidean minimum spanning tree, bringing the current catalog from 1058 to 1059 kinds (1060 gallery choices including plain). The Euclidean minimum spanning tree of a Poisson-disk point set on the torus: dart throwing on the unit torus first picks points at least 0.085 apart (about 90, selected as for `poissondisk` and `gabrielgraph` with a different salt), then Kruskal's algorithm picks, among the pairs at most 0.25 apart (shortest torus vector), the edges that join all the points with the shortest total length (about one edge fewer than points); the points are drawn as small brighter discs and the edges as thinner lines, an amber tree-like network on a dark brown ground that looks like constellation lines, with smooth unions where edges meet nodes. The seed decides the point set. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (It differs from `gabrielgraph` in how the edges are chosen: the minimum spanning tree is a subgraph of the Gabriel graph with far fewer edges. That subgraph relation is a standard result of geometric graph theory and I did not verify it here.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the minimum distance 0.085, the node radius 0.024, the edge half width 0.0075, the longest edge 0.25, the amber colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14, edge tone 0.55 of the node tone) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: as for `gabrielgraph` the pixels with a colour above 0.66 on a 512×512 grid are grouped and their circular means are the node centres; the sampler uses Kruskal's algorithm, but the test uses a **different criterion**, the cycle property: a pair is in the tree when every path between the two points that does not use their direct connection (through the shortest torus distances) has a longest step longer than the pair's own distance, and is not in it when some path has only shorter steps; pairs within 0.003 of their own distance are not judged. For a pair clearly in the tree the five points at 25%, 40%, 50%, 60% and 75% of the segment must all be above 0.3, and for a pair clearly not in it, with no third centre within 0.02 of the segment, those five points must not all be lit (chain-like pairs are excluded for the same reason as in `gabrielgraph`). This shows that the sampler's edges agree with the minimum spanning tree for the pairs that are judged; it does **not** show that all pairs (including those within 0.003) agree, nor that the tree is connected — although the tree that Prim's algorithm builds on the read-back centres has exactly one edge fewer than the number of points (see below). An important lesson from the measurements: the first version compared directly against a Prim tree built on the read-back centres and misjudged one pair for three of the seeds (an edge that should be in the tree swapped with one that should not), because the nearest-neighbour distances of a Poisson-disk set cluster in 0.085–0.115 and many edges differ in length by less than the error of the read-back centres, so a criterion with a margin, the cycle property, replaced it. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0157). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points and the resolution differ; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) 6,000 candidate points are taken one after another from `hash(k, 0/1, seed ^ salt)` and kept when their shortest torus distance to every point kept so far is at least 0.085 (about 86–93 points); all pairs with a shortest torus vector of length at most 0.25 are listed, sorted from the shortest and checked one by one with union-find (path halving): when the two ends are not yet in the same tree the edge is kept (Kruskal's algorithm, giving the minimum spanning tree, or a forest if 0.25 cuts the graph apart); every edge is filed into the 12×12 buckets that a sample point could be in (stepping along the path by 0.25/12, with the half width plus half a step as the reach), so a sample looks only into its own bucket; at sampling time a node uses `t = max(0, 1 − distance² / radius²)` over the points in the 3×3 buckets and an edge the same formula over the segments in the bucket (the distance being that to the segment), each combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the union and the whole field are C1); `total = 1 − (complement of the node union) × (complement of the edge union)`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`tone` is `0.7·(0.55 + 0.45·node union)`), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the point and edge tables (about 90 points and one edge fewer than points, bytes not counted item by item). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): 93/87/86/92 read-back nodes of 156–174 pixels each (512² grid); judged with the cycle property and a margin of 0.003: pairs clearly in the tree are 75/78/73/76, all with the five points lit (0 misjudged); pairs clearly not in the tree (chain-like pairs excluded) are 539/493/452/526, none with all five points lit (0 misjudged); the excluded chain-like pairs are 162/122/140/152; the unjudged pairs are 33/16/26/31; the tree that Prim's algorithm builds on the read-back centres has 92/86/85/91 edges (the number of points minus one) with a longest edge of 0.1138/0.1148/0.1095/0.1102; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 13.17%–14.08%, color is 0.02553–0.02572 to 0.84778–0.85061 with a mean of 0.12817–0.13472, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8412–0.8444 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 13.10%–14.04%, color is 0.02511–0.02522 to 0.85174–0.85329 with a mean of 0.12812–0.13471, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8451–0.8497 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 23.7% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (54.9, 37.2, 23.0), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0157 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): an amber tree-like network, like constellation lines. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`gabrielgraph` adds the Gabriel graph, bringing the current catalog from 1057 to 1058 kinds (1059 gallery choices including plain). The Gabriel graph of a Poisson-disk point set on the torus: dart throwing on the unit torus first picks points at least 0.085 apart (about 90, the same kind of selection as `poissondisk` with a different salt), then two points are joined when no third point lies inside the disc that has the segment between them as its diameter (the shortest way round the torus, distance at most 0.25); the points are drawn as small brighter discs and the edges as thinner lines, a cyan network on a deep blue ground with smooth unions where edges meet nodes. The seed decides the point set. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real. (It differs from the existing `poissondisk` in that it also draws the edges of the Gabriel graph.)

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the minimum distance 0.085, the node radius 0.024, the edge half width 0.0075, the longest edge 0.25, the cyan colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14, edge tone 0.55 of the node tone) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler**: on a 512×512 grid the pixels with a colour above 0.66 are grouped by a 4-connected flood fill on the torus and the centre of every node is the circular mean (about 90 nodes of 150–175 pixels each, at least 0.083 apart); for every pair of nodes at most 0.25 apart a classification written separately in the test from the definition (the shortest way round the torus, no other centre inside the disc that has the segment as its diameter) is used: for a pair that is clearly a Gabriel edge (every other centre at least 0.006 outside the disc) the five points at 25%, 40%, 50%, 60% and 75% of the segment must all be above 0.3, and for a pair that is clearly not one (some centre at least 0.006 inside the disc and no third centre within 0.02 of the segment) those five points must not all be lit. Pairs within 0.006 of the circle are not judged, and pairs with a third centre within 0.02 of the segment are not judged either — such pairs are common (a first version with a single midpoint sample misjudged them: the midpoint of a non-edge pair often lies on other edges of a third node, so the condition became five points all lit and such chain-like pairs are excluded). This shows that the sampler's edges agree with the definition of the Gabriel graph for the pairs that are judged; it does **not** show that the ambiguous pairs agree too, nor that the graph is planar or connected on the torus. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0152). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the position of the sample points and the resolution differ; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) 6,000 candidate points are taken one after another from `hash(k, 0/1, seed ^ salt)` and kept when their shortest torus distance to every point kept so far is at least 0.085 (about 88–92 points); for every pair of points (shortest torus vector, length at most 0.25) the pair becomes an edge when the disc centred on the midpoint with half the length as its radius holds no third point; every edge is filed into the 12×12 buckets that a sample point could be in (stepping along the path by 0.25/12, with the half width plus half a step as the reach), so a sample looks only into its own bucket; at sampling time a node uses `t = max(0, 1 − distance² / radius²)` over the points in the 3×3 buckets and an edge the same formula over the segments in the bucket (the distance being that to the segment), each combined as the union `1 − Π(1 − t²)` (every t² is C1 and exactly zero at the rim, so the union and the whole field are C1); `total = 1 − (complement of the node union) × (complement of the edge union)`, `mask = smooth(clamp(total / 0.35))`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`tone` is `0.7·(0.55 + 0.45·node union)`), height is `0.8·total·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the point and edge tables (about 90 points and some hundreds of edges, bytes not counted item by item). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the construction or sampling time.** Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7): 91/89/92/88 points, the closest pair 0.0849/0.0851/0.0850/0.0846 apart; the 512² grid pixels above 0.66 group into 155–171 pixels per node for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff; clear Gabriel-edge pairs are 227/229/223/215, all with the five points lit (0 misjudged); clear non-edge pairs (chain-like pairs excluded) are 364/321/386/328, none with all five points lit (0 misjudged); the excluded chain-like pairs are 152/153/157/139; ambiguous pairs (within 0.006 of the circle) are not judged; the probe counted these together with pairs whose length is within 0.25 ± 0.01 as 157/138/172/143, and the latter are in fact still judged when at most 0.25 long, so this total is slightly higher than the number of pairs actually left unjudged; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 27.26%–29.03%, color is 0.02534–0.02580 to 0.85028–0.85206 with a mean of 0.20498–0.21366, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8428–0.8445 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 26.86%–28.98%, color is 0.02510–0.02521 to 0.85166–0.85355 with a mean of 0.20193–0.21368, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8462–0.8486 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 40.3% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.7, 60.2, 75.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0152 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): a cyan network of triangles with slightly brighter nodes. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`schelling` adds Schelling segregation, bringing the current catalog from 1056 to 1057 kinds (1058 gallery choices including plain). Schelling's segregation model on a 48×48 torus: every cell is empty (about 10%) or holds a resident of one of two kinds (about 45% each); a resident is 'happy' when at least 40% of the occupied cells among its 8 neighbours (wrapping round the torus) hold its own kind (having no neighbour counts as happy); the start is a random mixture from the hash, after which sweeps in cell order move every unhappy resident to the first empty cell in the list of empty cells (counted from a hashed place) where it would be happy, until nobody moves or 60 sweeps are done; the result is a camouflage-like pattern in which the two kinds form patches with dark empty cells scattered between them (empty cells dark plum, one kind brown, the other amber). The seed decides the initial mixture. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of any real city.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 48×48 size, the 10% empty cells, the 40% happiness threshold, the limit of 60 sweeps, the plum-and-amber colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests check **only through values read back from the sampler** that this is a settled Schelling state: they read empty / kind 1 / kind 2 from the colour at the centre of every cell (thresholds 0.31 and 0.665, with no read-back within 0.05 of a threshold), then use a happiness test written separately in the test from the definition (8 neighbours, wrapping round the torus, at least 40% of the own kind) to confirm that every resident is happy, that no unhappy resident could be made happy by any empty cell, that each kind is 40%–60% of the residents, that 8%–12% of the cells are empty and that 78%–86% of the occupied neighbours are of the own kind (about 50% for a random mixture; I did not test that figure). This shows that the sampler draws a settled state that satisfies the definition; it does **not** show that it was produced by one particular order of moves (the start and the moves come from the hash and the test does not replay them), nor that every seed settles with everyone happy (only the seeds of the tests and the probe, six in all, were checked; see below). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0296). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the cell width (about 5.3 and 10.7 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Uint8Array(2304)` holds the cells (0 = empty, 1 and 2 = the two kinds of resident): `hash(i, 0, seed ^ salt)` below 0.1 is empty, below 0.55 is kind 1 and otherwise kind 2; then up to 60 sweeps are made, each of which goes through the cells in order and for every unhappy resident builds the list of empty cells and, counting from the place given by `hash(sweep × 2304 + i, 1, seed ^ salt)`, finds the first empty cell where the resident would be happy (the cell it leaves counts as empty) and moves it there; a sweep in which nobody moves ends the process; at sampling time each cell is a compactly supported rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, `tone` is `0.7·{0, 1, 2}/2`), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Uint8Array(2304)` of 2,304 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 133,376 B in all, lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; the lists of empty cells made during the moves are not counted). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **The construction and sampling time have only single uncontrolled measurements**: the sampler construction times in the probe for the six seeds were about 50.0 (including first-call warm-up), 8.9, 8.7, 9.4, 8.8 and 8.3 ms, not a reliable performance figure. Measured (tool-run, seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7/12345/99): empty cells 232/216/232/249/248/220 (of 2,304); unhappy residents and unhappy residents that any empty cell could make happy are 0 in every case; the share of occupied neighbours of the own kind is 0.8147/0.8202/0.8172/0.8180/0.8179/0.8303; no read-back is ambiguous for any seed; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 34.45%–35.16%, color is 0.02548–0.02591 to 0.85407–0.85463 with a mean of 0.45537–0.45802, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8474–0.8500 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area is 33.94%–35.57%, color is 0.02524–0.02548 to 0.85463–0.85485 with a mean of 0.45041–0.45840, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8499–0.8507 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 37.5% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ and 60.2% of the cell-centre colours differ by more than 0.05; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (126.9, 84.3, 53.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0296 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7, 2×2 tiles): patches of amber and brown like camouflage with small dark plum empty cells between them. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`josephus` adds Josephus, bringing the current catalog from 1055 to 1056 kinds (1057 gallery choices including plain). A 64×64 table of the Josephus problem: n people stand in a circle, counting starts at the first and every k-th person is eliminated until one is left; the cell in row n−1 and column k−1 (n and k from 1 to 64) shows which eighth of the circle the survivor stands in (`⌊8·J(n)/n⌋`, 0 to 7) as one of 7 steps from deep navy to gold, and the seed moves the table around the torus. The table shows regular diagonal and banded structure (k = 1, the last person; k = 2, a sawtooth) mixed with seemingly irregular regions. It is a schematic pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 size, the eighths (8 levels), the deep navy and gold colours (span 0.7, floor 0.14) and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler uses the recurrence `J(1) = 0`, `J(m) = (J(m − 1) + k) mod m`; the tests recompute the whole table **in an independent way** — actually playing the elimination out on a list — and I checked with a probe that the recurrence and the playing-out agree on all 4,096 cells; the tests check that with k = 1 the survivor is always n, that with k = 2 it is `2(n − 2^⌊log₂n⌋) + 1` (this closed form is the standard Josephus result, used here to cross-check the playing-out code; I did not verify the theorem itself separately), that 41 people with every third eliminated leave the 31st standing, that the eight levels occur 707/425/494/463/566/473/527/441 times (4,096 in all), and compare the cell-centre colours with each of the 4,096 possible shifts (grain amplitude 0.015, tolerance 0.03) to confirm that exactly one shift fits for every seed. This shows that the sampler draws the eighth-levels of this Josephus table; it does **not** show any particular statistical property of the irregular regions. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0378). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below) because the cell width (4 and 8 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ; the tests use the ranges of the 256² grid.
