`walshmatrix` adds a Walsh matrix, bringing the current catalog from 1024 to 1025 kinds (1026 gallery choices including plain). The 32×32 Walsh–Hadamard matrix in sequency order, drawn as rounded square tiles: along row `r` the sign changes exactly `r` times (row 0 is all +1 and row 31 changes sign at every cell); +1 cells glow (fading by 0.3 from the first to the last row) and −1 cells stay at the floor tone. The matrix has order `2^5 = 32`; the Hadamard row of row `r` is `h = bitReverse(grayCode(r))`, and the value in column `c` is `(−1)^popcount(h & c)`. Any two different rows are orthogonal (dot product 0), so the picture is a binary square with a lot of structure, with the frequency increasing downwards. Amber gold tiles lie on a deep blue ground, and the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic mathematical table, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 32×32 size, the row fade of 0.3, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the amber gold and deep blue colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler builds the sequency order with a Gray code and a bit reversal; the tests build the whole table in **another, independent way** — the Sylvester doubling method (`H = [[H, H], [H, −H]]`) with the rows sorted by their number of sign changes — and check that the sorted rows have exactly 0 to 31 sign changes, read ±1 back from the sampler's cell-centre colours (a lit cell is +1) and check that the matrix read back is a Hadamard matrix (any two different rows have dot product 0 and every row has dot product 32 with itself, whatever the shift), and then compare the colour at every cell centre against all 1,024 possible shifts and check that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). This shows that the sampler's matrix agrees with the independently built Walsh matrix (including the sequency order) and that the signs read back really are orthogonal. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0177). The lit-area share differs between 256² and 512² sampling (see below), because the cell width (8 and 16 pixels) and the position of the sample points inside the cells differ, not because of different seeds.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(1024)` tone table is built: for row `row` take `gray = row xor (row >> 1)` and reverse its 5 bits to get `hadamard`, and for column `col` take `parity = popcount(hadamard & col) mod 2`; if `parity = 0` (+1) `tones = 0.7·(1 − 0.3·row / 31)`, otherwise 0; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 5, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 5, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 32): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(1024)` of 8,192 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 139,264 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction or the sampling time. Measured (tool-run): the independently built Walsh matrix has the sign-change counts 0, 1, 2, …, 31 for its rows; for the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) the matrix read back is a Hadamard matrix (0 non-orthogonal row pairs), and each has a **unique** fitting shift, (12, 22), (4, 1), (22, 13) and (2, 6), with maximum fit errors of 0.01499/0.01499/0.01500/0.01498; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 32.09%–32.17%, color is 0.02581–0.02604 to 0.85314–0.85387 with a mean of 0.32965–0.32984, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8431–0.8452 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is always 37.06%, color is 0.02523–0.02538 to 0.85422–0.85461 with a mean of 0.33488–0.33499 and height is at most 0.8463–0.8492 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 76.2% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05 (35.9% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (90.7, 74.9, 44.0), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0177 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview: amber gold tiles on deep blue with one fully lit horizontal row (row 0) and vertical stripes and checker structures getting denser towards the bottom. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hermitemodes` adds Hermite-Gauss modes, bringing the current catalog from 1023 to 1024 kinds (1025 gallery choices including plain). An 8×8 chart of the Hermite–Gauss modes, which are the transverse modes TEM(m, n) of a laser beam (and the states of the 2D harmonic oscillator): the column is the index m along x and the row is the index n along y (each 0 to 7); every cell shows the intensity `I = (f_m(x)·f_n(y) / (peak_m·peak_n))²`, where `f_k(x) = H_k(x)·exp(−x² / 2)` and `H_k` is the physicists' Hermite polynomial, each 1D function normalised by its largest absolute value over the range so that the brightest point of each cell is close to 1. In every cell x and y run from −4.2 to 4.2, so low modes are a small spot in the middle and high modes are grids of bright lobes separated by dark nodal lines (m and n count the nodal lines in each direction). Orange-red lobes lie on a dark purple-black ground as rounded square tiles, and the seed moves the whole chart around the torus (in whole cells). It is a schematic mathematical chart, not a physical simulation of a laser beam (the beam waist of a real beam changes with the mode order, whereas here all modes share one range).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8×8 cells, the coordinate range ±4.2, the size of the rounded-square kernel, the tones (floor 0.1, span 0.74), the orange-red and dark purple-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview; it is rather dark and the lobes of the high modes are dense, and I did not tune it further). That Hermite–Gauss modes are laser transverse modes and eigenstates of the harmonic oscillator, and that the classical turning point of `m = 7` is about `√15 ≈ 3.87` (so the range ±4.2 is enough), are standard physical and mathematical facts which I did not verify here. The sampler computes the Hermite polynomial with the recurrence `H_(k+1) = 2x·H_k − 2k·H_(k−1)` and finds the 1D peak on a fine grid of 4,097 points; the tests recompute it in **another, independent form** — the explicit sum `H_k(x) = k!·Σ_j (−1)^j (2x)^(k − 2j) / (j! (k − 2j)!)`, with the peaks found on a grid of 8,193 points (a different size from the sampler's) — at 8,000 golden-ratio points and compare it with the sampler's colour (inside the kernel (quartic norm at most 0.65) the intensity tone, outside the kernel (norm above 1.02) the gap tone, and the soft edge zone in between is not compared), trying all 64 possible shifts and checking that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03); they also check the 1D peaks (1 for `k = 0`, between 580 and 590 for `k = 7`) and `H_1(0) = 0`. This shows that the intensity formula, the normalisation, the coordinate mapping and the arrangement of every cell agree with the independently written formula, **but not the shape of the soft edge zone of the kernel**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.00274, nearly flat).

At start-up (per sampler) the largest `|f_k|` is found for each `k = 0 … 7` at 4,097 equally spaced points between −4.2 and 4.2 (`peaks`), 8 sets and about 32,776 function evaluations (I did not measure the time of this part); at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), the position `(fx, fy)` (−0.5 to 0.5) inside the cell maps to `x = fx·2·4.2` and `y = fy·2·4.2`, and the cell index shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 4, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 4, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 8) gives `(m, n)`, with `amplitude = f_m(x)·f_n(y) / (peaks[m]·peaks[n])` and `tone = amplitude²`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + toneSpan·tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.1, `toneSpan` 0.74), height is `0.8·dome·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the 8 peaks, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure the sampling time** (each sample runs two recurrences of up to order 7 and two exponentials). Measured (tool-run): the 1D peaks for `k = 0 … 7` are 1.0000, 1.2131, 2.2920, 5.4226, 14.9596, 46.3971, 158.1936 and 584.0201; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (0, 2), (2, 4), (3, 4) and (5, 1), with maximum fit errors of 0.01500/0.01489/0.01482/0.01477 (of 8,000 points per seed, 6,718 are used for the comparison, 5,081 of them inside the kernel); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 4.81%–4.83%, color is 0.02551–0.02588 to 0.84838–0.85010 with a mean of 0.15925–0.15940, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8541–0.8609 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 4.55%–4.57%, color is 0.02519–0.02543 to 0.8526–0.8544 with a mean of 0.15929–0.15944 and height is at most 0.8671–0.8774 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 9.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (47.4, 19.4, 29.7), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.00274 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the preview: a regular 8×8 grid on a dark purple-black ground, the plainest small spot (m = n = 0) in the one cell where the seed's shift put it, and ever denser grids of orange-red lobes the larger m and n are. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`supershapes` adds superformula stars, bringing the current catalog from 1022 to 1023 kinds (1024 gallery choices including plain). A chart of 8×8 Gielis-style superformula shapes, one per cell: the column sets the number of folds `m` (2, 4, 6, 8, 10, 12, 14, 16, even values only) and the row sets the sharpness exponent `n` (0.35, 0.5, 0.7, 1, 1.4, 2, 3, 5, from very spiky at the top to nearly round at the bottom). The radius of a shape at the angle `t`, relative to its longest radius, is `(2·(cos⁴(m·t / 4) + sin⁴(m·t / 4)))^(−1 / n)`: 1 at the odd multiples of `t = π / m` (m tips in all), and falling to `2^(−1 / n)` in the valleys between tips (about 0.138 for n = 0.35 and 0.871 for n = 5); the fourth powers and even m keep the radius function smooth across the branch cut of the angle. The tone of a shape grows with column plus row (dark sea green to bright mint), and mint stars and flowers lie on a dark blue-black ground with softened edges and a domed height inside. The seed moves the whole chart around the torus (in whole cells). It is a schematic mathematical chart, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8×8 cells, the series of folds and sharpness values, the disc radius of 0.46, the edge softness of 0.05, the tones (floor 0.14, span 0.7), the mint and dark blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The shape formula is my own simplification (both exponents 4, a = b = 1), not the full Gielis superformula, and I did not compare its parameters with the original paper. One thing worth noting: because the range of `cos⁴ + sin⁴` is [0.5, 1], the smallest ratio of the shape radius is fixed at `2^(−1 / n)`, so the smaller n is, the more needle-like the star, and the tips for n = 0.35 are very thin. The tests recompute the formula in **another, independent form** (`cos⁴x + sin⁴x = 1 − sin²(2x) / 2`, giving the radius `(2 − sin²(2x))^(−1 / n)`) at 8,000 golden-ratio points and compare it with the sampler's colour (inside a shape, more than 0.06 cell from the rim, the shape tone; outside the rim by more than 0.005 disc radius, the gap tone; the soft rim zone in between is not compared), trying all 64 possible shifts and checking that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.01497, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03); they also check that the radius is 1 at a tip and `2^(−1 / n)` in a valley. This shows that the position, size, fold count, sharpness and tone of the shapes agree with the independently written formula, **but not the shape of the soft rim zone** (that zone is covered only by the C1 and bounded-value checks, which pass). My first run of the tests failed on one assertion: I had written the test comment and expectations as 'angle 0 is a tip', but angle 0 is actually a valley and the tips are at `π / m` (the sampler's comment was already right); I fixed the test's comment and expectations and re-ran. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0378).

There is no precomputation at start-up (only the 128² fine grain noise is created); at sampling time `x = fract(u)·8` and `y = fract(v)·8`, the position inside the cell divided by the disc radius gives `(px, py)` and `radius r = hypot(px, py)`, and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 3, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 3, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 8); `t = m·atan2(py, px) / 4`, `edge = (2·(cos⁴t + sin⁴t))^(−1 / n)`, `mask = smoothstep(clamp((edge − r)·discRadius / 0.05))`, `dome = smoothstep(clamp(1 − (r / edge)²))`, `tone = (column + row) / 14`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + toneSpan·tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14, `toneSpan` 0.7), height is `0.8·dome·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the shapes and metallic is 0; the retained cache is only a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction or the sampling time (each sample costs one `atan2`, one `cos`, one `sin` and one power). Measured (tool-run): each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (7, 1), (5, 5), (7, 7) and (3, 4), with maximum fit errors of 0.01473/0.01497/0.01479/0.01489 (of 8,000 points per seed, 7,057–7,098 are used for the comparison, 2,129–2,167 of them inside shapes); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 17.07%–17.13%, color is 0.02528–0.02590 to 0.85335–0.85415 with a mean of 0.20254–0.20261, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8583–0.8717 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 17.13%–17.19%, color is 0.02520–0.02528 to 0.85391–0.85458 with a mean of 0.20219–0.20228 and height is at most 0.8600–0.8736 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 28.0% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (34.7, 58.1, 64.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0378 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: a regular 8×8 grid of stars and flowers, very spiky in the upper rows and nearly round in the lower rows, with the fold count increasing to the right. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`zernikemodes` adds Zernike modes, bringing the current catalog from 1021 to 1022 kinds (1023 gallery choices including plain). An 8×8 grid of discs, each disc showing one Zernike polynomial, arranged in the OSA / ANSI single-index order (`j = (n(n + 2) + m) / 2`: cell 0 is `n = 0, m = 0`, cells 1 and 2 are `n = 1, m = −1, 1`, cells 3 to 5 are `n = 2, m = −2, 0, 2`, and so on, 64 modes in all, the last being `n = 10, m = 6`). Each mode is a radial polynomial times the cosine (`m ≥ 0`) or sine (`m < 0`) of the azimuth angle, and the radial polynomial is 1 at the rim of the disc so `|Z| ≤ 1`; the tone of a disc is `(1 + Z) / 2` from dark to bright, so each disc contains concentric rings, petals and saddles of light and shade, like a chart of optical aberrations (the n = 0 disc is bright all over). Pale cream discs lie on a dark blue-black ground with softened edges. The seed moves the whole table around the torus (in whole discs). It is a schematic mathematical chart, not a simulation of anything real and not the true wavefront of any optical system.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8×8 cells, the disc radius of 0.46 cell, the edge softness of 0.08, the tones (floor 0.1, span 0.72), the pale cream and dark blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The OSA / ANSI single index and the sign convention of sine and cosine are what I used from memory, **and I did not check them against the standard document this time**; that the Zernike radial polynomial equals 1 at the rim and `|Z| ≤ 1` is a standard theoretical fact that I did not prove here, I only saw in the probe's samples that all output colours lie in [0, 1]. The sampler computes the radial polynomial with the factorial series; the tests recompute it in **another, independent form** — the binomial sum of the Jacobi polynomial (`R = (−1)^k r^|m| P_k^(|m|,0)(1 − 2r²)`, `k = (n − |m|) / 2`) — at radius 0.6 inside every disc at four angles (256 points) and compare it with the sampler's colour, trying all 64 possible shifts and checking that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0134, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03); they also check the indices of the first six modes and the last mode, and the rim value of 1. This shows that the sampler's polynomials, signs and arrangement agree with the independently written formula, **but not that the formula itself matches the standard Zernike definition** (the formula in the tests was also written by me). Because the relief reuses 0.0008 and the height varies little across a disc, the maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps is only 0.00126 (nearly flat); that is expected and I did not tune it. My first run of the tests failed on one assertion because the mode list held `m = -0` where the expected value had `m = +0` (`toEqual` distinguishes them); I fixed the test (`m + 0`) and re-ran, and also replaced a clumsy `Math.cos(0)` expectation with 1.

At start-up (per sampler) the 64 pairs `(n, m)` are listed in order (n from 0, m from −n to n in steps of 2), and for every mode the powers `n − 2k` and coefficients `(−1)^k (n − k)! / (k! ((n + |m|) / 2 − k)! ((n − |m|) / 2 − k)!)` (k from 0 to `(n − |m|) / 2`) of the radial polynomial are precomputed and kept, with one `Int32Array(64)` each for n and m and small per-mode arrays; at sampling time `x = fract(u)·8` and `y = fract(v)·8`, the position inside the cell divided by the disc radius gives `(px, py)` and `radius r = hypot(px, py)`, and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 2, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 2, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 8); `Z = R(min(r, 1))·cos(m·atan2(py, px))` (m ≥ 0) or `·sin(−m·atan2)` (m < 0), `tone = 0.5 + 0.5·Z`, `mask = smoothstep(clamp((1 − r) / 0.08))`, `dome = smoothstep(clamp(1 − r²))`: color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + toneSpan·tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.1, `toneSpan` 0.72), height is `0.8·dome·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 outside the discs and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B plus the small per-mode arrays (I did not count the bytes of these). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction or the sampling time (each sample evaluates the polynomial of one cell, at most 6 terms, plus one `atan2` and one `cos` or `sin`). Measured (tool-run): each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (5, 2), (2, 5), (4, 1) and (4, 2), with maximum fit errors of 0.01265/0.01343/0.01269/0.01304; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 16.84%–16.90%, color is 0.02549–0.02579 to 0.83229–0.83345 with a mean of 0.30005–0.30010, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8587–0.8693 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 16.83%–16.86%, color is 0.02517–0.02525 to 0.8337–0.8339 with a mean of 0.30003–0.30012 and height is at most 0.8653–0.8723 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 24.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (82.0, 79.2, 79.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.00126 and the minimum z component is 255. I viewed the preview: a regular 8×8 grid of discs, each with a different pattern of concentric rings, petals and saddles, the n = 0 disc the brightest. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`rule110` adds rule 110, bringing the current catalog from 1020 to 1021 kinds (1022 gallery choices including plain). It draws the one-dimensional elementary cellular automaton rule 110 as a 96×96 space-time diagram: row 0 is a random row (every cell lights with probability 0.5), and every cell of every following row is decided by the states of the three cells above it (left, centre and right, wrapping around) read as a three-bit number (left = 4, centre = 2, right = 1), taking the matching bit of the rule number 110 to make it lit or dark; each row is a generation, evolving downwards. The result is the typical pattern of dark triangles of different sizes and diagonal gliders (these structures of rule 110 are known, a standard theoretical fact that I did not verify here). Lit cells are orange and dark cells deep purple, as rounded square tiles. The seed decides the random state of row 0 and moves the whole picture sideways; there is no vertical shift (the time axis is fixed). It is a schematic automaton space-time diagram, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; rule 110, the 96×96 size, the density of 0.5 in row 0, the orange and deep purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview; the picture is busy and high-frequency with about four tenths of the area lit, and I did not tune it further). Rule 110 is deterministic, so the tests **can verify the dynamics independently**: the tests read the state of every cell back from its centre colour (a colour above 0.5 is lit, and it must sit within the grain of one of the two tones, an error below 0.03), apply the rule written independently (left = 4, centre = 2, right = 1 as bits) and check that **every cell of rows 1 to 95** follows rule 110 (the number of cells that do not must be 0), and check that about half of row 0 is lit and that 50% to 60% of all cells are lit. Because the rule is translation-invariant, the horizontal shift does not affect this check, so the shift does not have to be found. To make sure the check is not vacuous I changed the rule number to 30 in a temporary probe and got 3,214, 3,218, 3,193 and 3,301 non-conforming cells for the four seeds (0 for rule 110 itself). This verifies that the space-time diagram produced by the sampler obeys the update of rule 110, but the randomness of row 0 (the hash) is not independently verified. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0468).

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(9216)` tone table is built: in row 0 `tones[col] = hash(col, 0, seed ^ salt) < 0.5 ? 0.7 : 0`, and every cell of row `row` forms `4·left + 2·centre + right` from the left, centre and right cells of the row above (wrapping modulo 96) and takes `(110 >> that value) & 1` to decide a tone of 0.7 or 0; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the column index is shifted by an amount decided by `hash(0, 1, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 96): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(9216)` of 73,728 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 204,800 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler in bun at about 1.5 ms (one build each for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7/2, all about 1.5–1.6 ms), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run): for the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) the number of cells that do not follow rule 110 is 0 in every case; 5,121/5,127/5,090/5,256 cells of the table are lit (55.6%/55.6%/55.2%/57.0%); row 0 has 45/47/52/49 lit cells (of 96); the last row has 51/55/55/58 lit cells; the colours match the two tones within a maximum error of 0.0150; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) covers 38.10%–38.25%, color is 0.02549–0.02613 to 0.85415–0.85447 with a mean of 0.38544–0.38724, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8472–0.8475 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area covers 39.75%–41.04%, color is 0.02523–0.02550 to 0.85463–0.85485 with a mean of 0.3917–0.4008 and height is at most 0.8497–0.8503 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 46.5% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05 (33.3% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (108.2, 68.9, 46.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0468 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview: fine orange squares on deep purple with dark triangles of different sizes. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`chromaticant` adds a chromatic ant, bringing the current catalog from 1019 to 1020 kinds (1021 gallery choices including plain). A multi-colour Langton's ant runs on a 96×96 torus: the board starts as all colour 0, the ant stands in the middle facing up, and the rule string is `RRLLLRLLLRRR` (12 colours); at each step the ant looks at the colour c of the cell under it, turns right if `rule[c]` is R and left if it is L, advances the cell's colour to `(c + 1) mod 12` and steps one cell forward (wrapping around); 100,000 steps are made in all. Finally every cell is shown as a rounded square tile with the tone `0.7·colour / 11`: cream to dark teal. The result is a chaotic block in the middle surrounded by large flat regions bounded by straight diagonal and horizontal or vertical lines that wrap around because of the torus (I only describe what I see in the preview and did not analyse the dynamics of this rule). The 12 colours occupy 4,869, 521, 293, 180, 337, 246, 1,288, 292, 234, 275, 319 and 362 of the 9,216 cells (colour 0 the most, then colour 6). The simulation of the ant does not depend on the seed (it is deterministic); the seed only moves the whole board around the torus. It is a schematic simulation result, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 96×96 size, the rule string, the 100,000 steps, the teal and cream colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: with a separate small prototype I ran five rules once each (RLLR for 20,000 steps, LLRR for 20,000, RLR for 12,000, LRRRRRLLR for 60,000 and RRLLLRLLLRRR for 100,000) and viewed the previews of three of them (LRRRRRLLR, RLLR and RRLLLRLLLRRR): RLLR grew only a small symmetric figure in the middle that did not fill the tile; LRRRRRLLR had diamond-shaped lines and a chaotic block; RRLLLRLLLRRR had the largest chaotic block and many wrapped straight lines, so I chose it (for LLRR and RLR I only printed the count of non-zero cells and did not look at a picture). The ant's rule is deterministic, so the tests **can rewrite it independently**: the tests simulate the ant again written differently (direction vectors instead of a heading counter), check that the numbers of cells of the 12 colours are exactly the ones above, rebuild the tone table and, for each seed, compare the colour at every cell centre against all 9,216 possible shifts and check that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). I did not analyse the behaviour of the rule itself (for example whether an ant highway appears), only that the sampler agrees with an independent simulation. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0468). The first version of a test comment described the 4,347 cells with a non-zero colour as 'cells that have been visited', which is wrong (a cell visited 12 times returns to colour 0), and I corrected it after running the tests.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Uint8Array(9216)` colour board is built by running 100,000 steps from `(48, 48)` facing up (see above), after which every cell's tone `0.7·colour / 11` is stored in a `Float64Array(9216)`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 0, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 96): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Uint8Array(9216)` of 9,216 B, a `Float64Array(9216)` of 73,728 B and a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 214,016 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler (100,000 steps) in bun at about 29.3 ms (first, including JIT), 9.5 ms, 9.1 ms, 6.9 ms and 1.9 ms (one build each for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7/2), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run): the cell counts of the 12 colours are as above; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (87, 75), (74, 2), (55, 37) and (76, 34), with a maximum fit error of 0.01496–0.01500; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 17.75%–17.89%, color is 0.02549–0.02601 to 0.85372–0.85416 with a mean of 0.23586–0.23604, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8440–0.8460 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 21.15%–21.20%, color is 0.02526–0.02547 to 0.8545–0.8549 with a mean of 0.23939–0.23951 and height is at most 0.8483–0.8503 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 31.7% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (64.4, 73.3, 63.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0468 and the minimum z component is 252.
