No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`gaussianprimes` adds Gaussian primes, bringing the current catalog from 1018 to 1019 kinds (1020 gallery choices including plain). A 64×64 table is laid out as rounded square tiles, every cell standing for a Gaussian integer `a + bi` (a and b each from −32 to 31, with the origin near the middle of the table), and the cells of Gaussian primes glow: an `a + bi` on an axis (`b = 0` or `a = 0`) is a Gaussian prime when `|a|` (or `|b|`) is a prime leaving remainder 3 on division by 4, and any other `a + bi` is a Gaussian prime when its norm `a² + b²` is an ordinary prime; the other cells stay at the base tone. The glow weakens with the distance to the origin (tone `0.7·(1 − 0.55·√(norm / largest norm))`), so the middle is brighter and the outskirts darker. The 64×64 cells hold 844 Gaussian primes, 24 of them on the axes (±3, ±7, ±11, ±19, ±23, ±31, on the four half-axes); the table is mirror-symmetric about both axes and both diagonals (the row and column at −32 have no symmetric partner because the range is −32 to 31), giving dot lattices of nested diamonds and stars. Rose pink dots lie on a dark purple ground, and the seed moves the whole table around the torus. It is a schematic number-theory table, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 64×64 cells, the norm fade of 0.55, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the rose pink and dark purple colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The sampler decides primality by trial division; the tests decide Gaussian primality in **another, independent way** — a brute-force search for a Gaussian-integer factor `c + di` of smaller norm (whether both the real and the imaginary part of `(a + bi)(c − di)` are divisible by `c² + d²`) — which is independent of the sampler's standard-theorem formula (on an axis check remainder 3, elsewhere check whether the norm is prime); I did not prove that theorem (the characterisation of Gaussian primes) separately, the tests only show that the two ways agree on all 4096 cells. After rebuilding the whole tone table the tests compare the colour at every cell centre for each seed against all 4096 possible shifts and check that **exactly one** shift fits (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03), and check 844 primes, 24 of them on the axes, and a few special cases (1 + i is prime; 2, 5, 0 and the units are not; 3 is). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0377). The statistics at 256² and 512² differ (see below) because a cell is only 4 (or 8) pixels wide and the sample points fall at different places within the cells, not because of different seeds; the tests use the 256² values.

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(4096)` tone table is built: for every cell take `a = |col − 32|` and `b = |row − 32|`, on an axis check `max(a, b) % 4 === 3` and primality, otherwise check whether `a² + b²` is prime (trial division), and if so `tones[row · 64 + col] = 0.7 · (1 − 0.55·√((a² + b²) / 2048))`, otherwise 0; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 0, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 64): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(4096)` of 32,768 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 163,840 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). **I did not measure** the construction time (trial division over 4,096 cells) or the sampling time. Measured (tool-run): 844 Gaussian primes, 24 of them on the axes; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, (22, 34), (40, 21), (51, 61) and (51, 37), with a maximum fit error of 0.01499–0.01500; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is 14.94%–14.98%, color is 0.05897–0.05967 to 0.8357–0.8397 with a mean of 0.21017–0.21026, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.7344 and height is at most 0.8395–0.8433 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 11.58%–11.63%, color is 0.02517–0.02532 to 0.8353–0.8390 with a mean of 0.18475–0.18484, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8443–0.8462 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 23.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (58.5, 30.3, 49.1), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: a lattice of rose pink dots on dark purple, brighter in the middle, with a symmetric structure of diamonds and stars. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`fordcircles` adds Ford circles, bringing the current catalog from 1017 to 1018 kinds (1019 gallery choices including plain). Ford circles: for every reduced fraction `n / d` (0 ≤ n < d, denominators d ≤ 12, 46 in all) a disc of radius `1 / (2 d²)` stands on the bottom edge of the tile with its centre at `u = n / d` (the disc of `0 / 1` has a diameter equal to the whole tile height), and a copy mirrored about the middle line of the tile stands on the top edge (91 discs in all, since the big disc of `0 / 1` and its mirror are the same one); the discs of consecutive Farey fractions touch exactly, and between the big discs strings of ever smaller discs line up like stair-stepped fractal beads. The tone of the discs brightens as the denominator shrinks (`0.55·((13 − d) / 12)^1.5`), amber gold discs lie on a dark navy gap ground with softened edges, and the inside of a disc has a domed height. The seed moves the whole picture sideways (by multiples of 1/256). It is a schematic number-theory pattern, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the denominator limit of 12, the 256 sideways shift steps, the edge softness of 0.2, the tones (span 0.55, floor 0.2, exponent 1.5), the amber gold and dark navy colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: the first version had only one row of discs standing on the bottom edge, and on viewing the preview the strings of small discs appeared along only one edge of the tile (the top edge in the preview) while the gaps between the big discs on the other side were empty, which made the picture asymmetric, so I added the row mirrored about the middle line for the top edge (the second preview, which I viewed, confirmed it: the two rows of small discs meet at the mirror line in symmetric strings of beads). I checked the disc geometry (tangency and non-overlap) with a probe, **not in the tests**: with independently written code I measured, for the 46 pairs of discs of consecutive Farey fractions, a largest difference of 1.1e-16 between the centre distance and the sum of the radii; comparing all pairs of the 91 discs (mirrored and wrapped) the smallest value of distance minus the radius sum is −9.7e-17 (the discs touch and their interiors do not overlap, within floating-point error). The tests compare the sampler with an independently written Ford-circle geometry (reduced fractions picked with the greatest common divisor, centre n / d, radius 1 / (2 d²), tones from the same formula as the preset): at 6,000 golden-ratio points, wherever the point is far enough from every disc edge (squared-radius ratio below 0.75 means inside, above 1.3 means gap, and the soft edge zone in between is not compared) the colour must be within 0.03 of the disc tone (or the gap tone), and all 256 possible sideways shifts are tried and the test checks that **exactly one** fits; this shows that the positions, sizes and tones of the discs follow the formula, **but not the shape of the soft edge zone** (that zone is covered only by the C1 and bounded-value checks). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0315). When I first ran the script that generates the tests it stopped part-way because the Hamming test sits at the end of the file and the search for a following describe failed; nothing had been written, and I fixed the script and re-ran.

At start-up (per sampler) the Euclidean algorithm picks the 46 reduced fractions and three arrays of length 46 (centre, radius, tone) are built; at sampling time `x = fract(u + shift)` and `y = min(fract(v), 1 − fract(v))`, and for every disc the wrapped horizontal distance `dx` and `dy = y − radius` give `s = (dx² + dy²) / radius²`; only discs with `s < 1` contribute (the interiors of the discs do not overlap, so at most one is non-zero): `mask = smoothstep(clamp((1 − s) / 0.2))`, `dome = smoothstep(1 − s)`, color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.05, `toneFloor` 0.2), height is `0.8·dome·(0.85 + 0.15·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the shift is `floor(hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt) · 256) / 256`; the retained cache is three arrays of 46 numbers plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B. Every sample loops over the 46 discs (I did not measure the time), and I did not measure the construction time either. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run): 46 reduced fractions; each of the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7) has a **unique** fitting shift, 133, 45, 240 and 173 (each over 256), with a maximum fit error of 0.01477–0.01488 (about the grain's maximum amplitude of 0.015; about 3,875–3,887 of the 6,000 points are used for the comparison per seed); the total disc area (including the mirrored discs, without softening) is 0.9560 of the tile; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5, which covers the discs of denominator ≤ 4) is 82.45%–82.49%, color is 0.03553–0.03645 to 0.76426–0.76446 with a mean of 0.63341–0.63359, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8205–0.8228 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is 82.45%–82.56%, color is 0.03518–0.03558 to 0.76469–0.76490 with a mean of 0.63332–0.63349 and height is at most 0.8234–0.8244 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 26.1% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (160.5, 136.7, 86.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0315 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview: amber gold discs on dark navy, with strings of small discs between the big ones and the two mirrored rows forming symmetric strings of beads. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`hammingtable` adds a Hamming distance table, bringing the current catalog from 1016 to 1017 kinds (1018 gallery choices including plain). A 32×32 table is laid out as rounded square tiles: the tone of the tile in row `row` and column `col` is decided by how many bits differ between the binary representations (5 bits) of its two indices — the Hamming distance `popcount(row xor col)` — with distance 0 (the diagonal) the darkest and distance 5 (the two indices are each other's complement) the brightest, with the tone `0.7·(distance / 5)^1.6`. The 32×32 cells hold the distances 0 to 5 in 32, 160, 320, 320, 160 and 32 cells (32 times the binomial coefficients). Because the table uses the binary exclusive or, it repeats the same layout of blocks at every power of two (groups of 2, 4, 8 and 16), like a fractal grid that unfolds a hypercube, with the brightest tiles along one diagonal line. Amber yellow tiles lie on a dark plum gap ground, and the seed moves the whole table around the torus (by a number of cells chosen by the seed). It is a schematic number and bit-operation table, not a simulation of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 32×32 cells, the 5 bits, the tone exponent of 1.6, the tones (span 0.7, floor 0.14), the amber yellow and dark plum colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: I first tried 64×64 cells, 6 bits and a tone exponent of 1 and, on viewing the preview, found the tiles too small and the tones concentrated on the middle distances, so the picture was busy and the contrast low; I changed to 32×32 cells, 5 bits and an exponent of 1.6 (I viewed the preview of both versions, once each). Because of the symmetry of the exclusive or, shifting the whole table by 16 cells (half the table) in both directions at once gives exactly the same table, so for every seed there are **two** torus shifts that fit (the true shift and the one with 16 added in both directions); the test checks explicitly that there are exactly these two and that they are related by adding 16 (the half-table shift is a symmetry of the exclusive or, not two independent solutions). The tests rebuild the whole tone table from an independently written bit count (turning `row xor col` into a binary string and counting the ones) and compare it with the sampler's colour at the centre of every cell (maximum error 0.0150, from the grain; the threshold is 0.03). The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0177).

At start-up (per sampler) a `Float64Array(1024)` tone table is built, `tones[row · 32 + col] = 0.7 · (popcount(row xor col) / 5)^1.6`; at sampling time every cell has one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1), and the cell index is shifted by amounts decided by `hash(0, 0, seed ^ salt)` and `hash(1, 0, seed ^ salt)` (modulo 32): color is `gapTone + (toneFloor + tone − gapTone)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)` (`gapTone` 0.04, `toneFloor` 0.14), height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone) + 0.08·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO drops to 0.6 in the gaps and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(1024)` of 8,192 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 139,264 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Construction is only 1,024 bit counts and one noise table, **I did not measure the construction time**, and sampling is a constant number of operations, which I did not measure either. Measured (tool-run): every seed has two fitting torus shifts, for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 (30, 2) and (14, 18), (10, 13) and (26, 29), (21, 12) and (5, 28), (26, 9) and (10, 25), with a maximum fit error of 0.01498–0.01499 (equal to the grain's maximum amplitude of 0.015); on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) is always 10.94%, color is 0.02568–0.02574 to 0.8530–0.8535 with a mean of 0.2910–0.2911, roughness is always 0.4, AO is at least 0.6 and height is at most 0.8401–0.8467 relief; on a 512² grid (four seeds) the lit area is always 13.48%, color is 0.02509–0.02529 to 0.8540–0.8545 with a mean of 0.2955 and height is at most 0.8440–0.8475 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 24.7% of the 512² samples with color>0.5 differ, and 77.9% of the cells differ in centre colour by more than 0.05; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (89.4, 66.1, 56.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0177 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview: amber yellow tiles on dark plum, with a brightest band of tiles running diagonally and nested block structure. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`aggregationfrost` adds aggregation frost, bringing the current catalog from 1015 to 1016 kinds (1017 gallery choices including plain). It runs diffusion-limited aggregation (DLA) on a 96×96 torus: the cell at the centre is the first member, every further particle starts on a random free cell and steps at random to one of its four neighbours (wrapping around), sticking as soon as it shares an edge with a member of the cluster; 900 particles in all (the centre plus 899 random walkers) form a fractal, branching cluster like frost or a tree. Every particle has an 'age' given by the order in which it stuck, and the tone fades from the centre (the oldest) towards the branch tips; it shows thin ice-blue branches on a dark blue-black ground, one cluster per tile that does not join neighbouring tiles (the farthest branches are only about 37–44 cells from the centre while the torus half-width is 48). The seed decides every particle's start and every step's direction, so every seed gives a completely different branching pattern. It is a schematic simulation result, not a simulation of real frost or Lichtenberg figures. The catalog also has the similarly named `dendriticfrost` and `frost`, which are different materials unrelated to this simulated aggregation.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 900 particles, the 96×96 size, the cap of 60,000 steps per walk, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (line 0.72, age floor 0.3), the ice-blue and dark blue-black colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). I first used a separate small prototype (64×64 with 520 particles, only to confirm the method and its speed) to check that DLA is feasible and then changed to 96×96 and 900 particles. I did not check whether any walk reached the cap of 60,000 steps (in which case it is abandoned and the particle starts again), and I did not check whether the fractal dimension of the cluster matches the literature value for DLA, so I do not claim it is 'standard DLA', only the result of this implementation of the algorithm. The tests cannot reproduce the random walks independently (the hash random numbers are internal to the sampler), so I **did not rewrite the aggregation algorithm independently**: the tests read the occupied cells back from the node colours, use an independent breadth-first search to check that the cluster is connected and has exactly 900 cells, and that the colour falls with the graph distance from the centre (a correlation below −0.6), **which shows that the cluster really is a connected tree-like structure and that the age tone has the right direction, but does not prove that the random walks are uniform**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0377). My first attempt at generating the test failed part-way because one expected string did not match (the lower height bound of the percolation test is 0.98, not 0.99); nothing had been written, and I fixed it and re-ran.

At start-up (per sampler) the centre cell `(48, 48)` is set as the first member of the cluster (tone 1), and for every particle `particle = 1 … 899` the code repeats: the starting cell is chosen with `hash(particle, attempt, seed ^ salt)` (if it is already occupied, the next attempt is tried), the walk lasts at most 60,000 steps, in each step the particle sticks if it shares an edge with the cluster (one of its four neighbours is occupied: the cell is marked occupied with tone `1 − particle / 900`), and otherwise it moves in one of four directions (wrapping) chosen by `hash(particle × 65537 + attempt, step, seed ^ (salt + 3))`; at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the occupancy map and `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))` re-sharpens it, while a second `latticeField` blends the age tone map: color is `0.05 + 0.72·line·(0.3 + 0.7·age) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·line·(0.7 + 0.3·age) + 0.2·grain`, roughness drops by 0.2 on the line (base 0.4), AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is two `Float64Array(9216)` (occupancy and age) plus a `Float64Array(128²)`, 278,528 B, with a build-time `Uint8Array(9216)` occupancy table, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler in bun at about 150 ms (first), 135 ms, 126 ms and 130 ms (one run per seed), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: 900 cells are occupied and for all four seeds all 900 can be reached from the centre over four-neighbour edges (the cluster is connected); the largest graph distance in the cluster is 59/62/51/59; the farthest cell from the centre (shortest torus distance) is 41.1/40.5/36.9/44.0 cells away; the colours of the occupied nodes are 0.2564–0.7794, the brightest empty node is 0.0651 and the centre node is 0.7561–0.7733; the correlation between graph distance and colour is −0.7945/−0.7536/−0.8800/−0.8088; on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 3.95%–4.06%, color is 0.0356–0.0358 to 0.7725–0.7758 with a mean of 0.0922–0.0925, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9697–0.9848 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 3.97%–4.05%, color is 0.0352–0.0353 to 0.7734–0.7779 with a mean of 0.0922–0.0925 and height is at most 0.9795–0.9870 relief; the occupied cells of seeds 0 and 1 differ in 14.8% of positions; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (23.0, 31.2, 45.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0377 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): frost-flower-like ice-blue branches on a dark blue-black ground, one per tile, brighter near the centre and darker at the tips. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`cyclicwaves` adds cyclic waves, bringing the current catalog from 1014 to 1015 kinds (1016 gallery choices including plain). It runs an eight-state cyclic cellular automaton on a 96×96 torus: every cell has a state from 0 to 7, started at random; in every synchronous step a cell in state k advances to `k + 1` (7 is followed by 0) if at least one of its four neighbours up, down, left or right (von Neumann neighbourhood, wrapping) is already in state `k + 1`, and otherwise stays; 150 steps are run. The result is rings of waves that follow one another (every state right after the previous one), forming spirals and labyrinth-like waves wherever the random start happened to be locally ordered; states 0 to 7 map to eight tones from dark indigo to amber yellow, and the wave fronts show short steep ramps from bright to dark. The eight states each take about an equal share (11.96%–13.19% per state across the four seeds), and about 97% of neighbouring cells differ by at most one state (only 37.5% at the random start). The seed decides the starting states, so every seed gives completely different waves. It is a schematic automaton snapshot, not a simulation of chemical waves or of anything real.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8 states, the von Neumann neighbourhood, the threshold of 1, the 150 steps, the 96×96 size, the tone (span 0.72), the indigo and amber yellow colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustment record: I first tried a few rules with a separate small prototype (Moore neighbourhood with threshold 2 or 3 and so on): after 100 steps the Moore neighbourhood with threshold 2 or 3 gave a share of neighbours differing by at most one state of only 0.18–0.68 (0.684 for 8 states with threshold 2, 0.371 with threshold 3; 0.242 for 12 states with threshold 3; 0.182 for 16 states with threshold 3; 0.344 for 10 states with threshold 2), the Moore neighbourhood with threshold 1 (6, 8, 10 and 12 states, 150 to 250 steps) gave 0.74–0.88, and the von Neumann neighbourhood with threshold 1 gave 0.95–0.98 (0.952 for 5 states and 0.976 for 8 states), so I chose the von Neumann neighbourhood with 8 states; every setting was run once with the same seed, so this is a rough comparison; the prototype's random numbers differ from the sampler's hash and were used only to choose the rule. I looked at only one preview. The tests cannot reproduce the dynamics independently (the hash random numbers are internal to the sampler), so I **did not rewrite the update rule of the cellular automaton independently**: the tests read the state of every cell back from the sampler's node colours (the nearest of the eight tones), check that the colours sit on the eight tones, and check statistics (about 97% of neighbour pairs differ by at most one state, every cell has a neighbour whose state is one more or one less than its own, and each of the eight states has a share between 11.5% and 14%), **which shows that the result is not random noise, that all states occur and that the colouring logic is right, but does not prove the update rule itself is right**. In the first draft of a test comment I wrote the share of neighbour pairs within one state at the random start as 'about a quarter', which is wrong (with 8 states it is 3/8 = 37.5%) and I corrected it before the commit. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0120).

At start-up (per sampler) the initial state of every cell is `floor(hash(x, y, seed ^ salt) · 8)`, followed by 150 synchronous steps: a cell moves to `(own + 1) mod 8` if any of its four (wrapped) neighbours is in that successor state and otherwise stays, swapping two `Uint8Array(9216)` buffers; afterwards every cell's tone is `state / 7`; at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the tone map: color is `0.05 + 0.72·tone + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·tone + 0.2·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is a `Float64Array(9216)` of 73,728 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 204,800 B in all, with two build-time `Uint8Array(9216)` buffers, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler (150 steps) in bun at about 78 ms (first), 39 ms, 44 ms and 40 ms (one run per seed), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: among the 96×96 nodes (sampled at the nodes) each state has 1,102–1,216 cells (11.96%–13.19%); the share of neighbour pairs differing by at most one state is 0.9779/0.9746/0.9782/0.9715; every cell has at least one neighbour whose state is one more or one less than its own (all 9,216 cells for all four seeds); the colours at all 9,216 nodes match the eight tones within a maximum error of 0.0150 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03); on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 35.93%–37.11%, color is 0.0378–0.0398 to 0.7800–0.7816 with a mean of 0.4049–0.4120, roughness is always 0.4, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9792–0.9899 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 36.22%–37.50%, color is 0.0366–0.0389 to 0.7818–0.7831 with a mean of 0.4049–0.4120 and height is at most 0.9862–0.9884 relief; between seeds 0 and 1, 49.3% of the cells with state ≥ 4 are at different positions and 46.5% of the nodes with color>0.5 differ; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (109.8, 93.9, 67.8), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0120 and the minimum z component is 254. I viewed the preview (seed 7): spiral and labyrinth-like waves in indigo and amber yellow, the wave fronts showing short gradients. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`isingdomains` adds Ising domains, bringing the current catalog from 1013 to 1014 kinds (1015 gallery choices including plain). It is a snapshot of Metropolis dynamics of the two-dimensional Ising model on a 64×64 torus: every cell is an up or down spin, started at random and run for 150 sweeps in checkerboard order at a temperature of 2.35 (coupling and Boltzmann constants set to 1; the critical temperature of the two-dimensional Ising model is about 2.269, a standard value that I did not verify here); a flip that changes the energy by dE is accepted when `dE ≤ 0` or when a hash-derived uniform number is below `exp(−dE/temperature)`; the result is domains of aligned spins: up is bright and down is dark, lightly tinted by the fraction of the four neighbours that share a cell's spin so that the domain walls are darker, in a lime-green camouflage-like pattern. The share of up spins of the four seeds lies between 24.3% and 55.3%, and the share of neighbour pairs with equal spins is about 79%–83% (50% at the random start). The seed decides the starting configuration and the random numbers of every step, so every seed gives a completely different pattern. It is a schematic snapshot of a model, not a simulation or measurement of a magnetic material, and it is not guaranteed to have reached equilibrium.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the temperature of 2.35, the 150 sweeps, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (spin 0.6, agreement 0.12), the lime green and dark green colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, whose pattern is mostly dark because it leans towards the majority spin). The tests cannot reproduce the dynamics independently (the hash random-number stream is internal to the sampler), so I **did not rewrite the Metropolis update independently**: the tests read the spins back from the sampler's node colours, check that the colours agree with (spin, number of equal neighbours), and check statistics (the share of equal neighbour pairs is about 0.78–0.84 and not the 0.5 of a random start; 100–150 same-spin regions; a largest region above 1,800 cells; an up share between 0.2 and 0.6), **which shows that the result is not random noise and that the colouring logic is right, but does not prove it is correct Metropolis sampling, and equilibrium was not verified**. One test failed along the way: I copied the roughness check from the percolation test (expecting it to drop to about 0.2 on lines) but this material has a constant roughness of 0.4, so the failing part was the copied expectation; I had met the same problem with the sandpile identity and still missed it this time; after changing it to check that the roughness equals the preset value the test passed. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0244).

At start-up (per sampler) the initial spins (±1) are decided by `hash(x, y, seed ^ salt) < 0.5`, followed by 150 sweeps, each split into two half-sweeps (the two parities of the checkerboard; cells of one parity are not adjacent and can be updated independently): for every cell the code sums the wrapped neighbour spins `around`, computes the energy change `dE = 2·spin·around` and flips when `dE ≤ 0` or `hash(cell, sweep × 2 + parity, seed ^ salt + 2) < exp(−dE / 2.35)`; afterwards it records for every cell whether it is up (`marks`) and the fraction of its four neighbours that share its spin (`agree`); at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the up map and `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))` re-sharpens it, while a second `latticeField` blends the agreement map: color is `0.05 + 0.6·line + 0.12·agree + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.7·line + 0.1·agree + 0.2·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is two `Float64Array(4096)` (the up map and the agreement) plus a `Float64Array(128²)`, 196,608 B, plus a 4,096 B `Int8Array` of spins. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I measured the construction of the sampler (150 sweeps) in bun at about 102 ms (first), 64 ms, 65 ms and 65 ms (one run per seed), which are single measurements, not a benchmark; sampling itself does a constant number of operations and I did not measure it. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: the share of up spins is 55.3%/24.3%/52.4%/32.5%; the share of neighbour pairs with equal spins is 0.8164/0.8296/0.8115/0.7908; there are 109/144/133/127 4-connected same-spin regions, the largest has 2,153/3,058/1,863/2,683 cells and the second largest 1,590/573/1,834/619; the colours at all 4,096 nodes match the independent model of the test (spin and number of equal neighbours) within a maximum error of 0.0150 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03); on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.4) covers 55.39%/23.71%/52.35%/32.05%, color is 0.0415–0.0441 to 0.7830–0.7843 with a mean of 0.2931–0.4803 (it varies with the seed), roughness is always 0.4, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9895–0.9962 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 55.37%/23.85%/52.35%/32.17%, color is 0.0370–0.0388 to 0.7839–0.7846 with a mean of 0.2929–0.4803 and height is at most 0.9956–0.9983 relief; the up spins of seeds 0 and 1 differ in 54.0% of positions; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (77.6, 100.8, 36.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0244 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): lime-green domains on dark green with pixelated rounded edges and many isolated small dots. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`percolationclusters` adds percolation clusters, bringing the current catalog from 1012 to 1013 kinds (1014 gallery choices including plain). It runs critical site percolation on a 64×64 torus: every cell is occupied or not according to a hash, with an occupation probability of 0.5927 (the standard value I know for the critical probability of site percolation on the square lattice, which I did not verify here); occupied cells that are neighbours up, down, left or right (wrapping around) form a cluster, found with union-find; every occupied cell is toned by `ln(cluster size) / ln(largest cluster size)` (the largest cluster is brightest, a lone cell is darkest but still brighter than an empty cell), and empty cells are the dark ground, giving a camouflage-like pattern in sulfur yellow. Because of random fluctuation the actual occupied fraction is slightly below the target (2,358–2,414 cells for the four seeds, 57.6%–58.9%). The seed decides which cells are occupied, so every seed gives a completely different pattern. It is a schematic random pattern, not a simulation or measurement of real percolation.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the occupation probability of 0.5927, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (line 0.72, tone floor 0.3), the sulfur yellow and dark olive colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). Two of my test expectations were wrong at first: the lit-area range in my first test was written from probe numbers for `color > 0.3` while the test uses `color > 0.5`, so the first run failed (0.4475 < 0.55); after using the range measured with `color > 0.5` (44.75%–48.62% on a 256² grid) it passed; later the mean range failed once because I had computed only three seeds and missed seed 7 (0.3844), and I relaxed it to 0.38. Both were mistakes in my test expectations, not sampler problems. The cluster labelling of this material is checked by the test by reading the occupied cells back from the sampler's node colours, relabelling the clusters with an independent flood-fill algorithm and computing the expected colours, so it verifies the cluster logic (including the torus wrap) **but not the hash-determined occupancy itself**. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0260).

At start-up, for every cell of the `64 × 64` grid the code decides occupancy with `hash(x, y, seed ^ salt) < 0.5927`, merges every occupied cell with its occupied right and lower neighbours (wrapping) using union-find (with path compression), counts the size of every cluster, `largest` is the size of the largest cluster (at least 2), and an occupied cell gets mark 1 and tone `ln(cluster size) / ln(largest)`; at sampling time `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the occupancy map and `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))` re-sharpens it, while a second `latticeField` blends the tone map: color is `0.05 + 0.72·line·(0.3 + 0.7·tone) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·line·(0.7 + 0.3·tone) + 0.2·grain`, roughness drops by 0.2 on the line (base 0.4), AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the retained cache is two `Float64Array(4096)` (occupancy and tone) plus a `Float64Array(128²)`, 196,608 B, with build-time scratch arrays (occupied 4,096 B, parents 16,384 B, cluster sizes 16,384 B), all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample does a constant number of operations; I did not measure the time. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: the independent flood-fill algorithm finds 2,358/2,414/2,391/2,408 occupied cells, 105–138 clusters, a largest cluster of 1,212–1,846 cells, a second largest of 72–639, 66–78 lone-cell clusters, and a largest cluster that covers all 64 rows (four seeds) and all 64 columns (three seeds; seed 1 covers 50); the colours at all 4,096 nodes match the independent model within a maximum error of 0.0150 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03); on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 44.75%–48.62%, color is 0.0357–0.0360 to 0.7837–0.7842 with a mean of 0.3844–0.3984, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9929–0.9962 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 40.83%–44.44%, color is 0.0352–0.0354 to 0.7844–0.7846 with a mean of 0.3840–0.3979 and height is at most 0.9974–0.9988 relief; the occupied cells of seeds 0 and 1 differ in 49.5% of positions; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (112.7, 107.6, 48.5), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0260 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): a camouflage-like sulfur-yellow pattern on dark olive, with the large cluster in bright yellow and small clusters darker. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`voronoifacets` adds Voronoi facets, bringing the current catalog from 1011 to 1012 kinds (1013 gallery choices including plain). The same Voronoi plates as `voronoicells` (one jittered site per cell of an 8×8 grid, soft-weight partition, 64 plates and dark thin seams), but a plate does not have a single tone: it has a linear gradient in a random direction (facet-like): every site has its own tone and gradient direction and size (up to ±0.35 of tone change per cell width), so the tone inside a plate shifts from darker on one side to brighter on the other, like the facets of an emerald or gem; in emerald green, with seams that are still dark, rough (the roughness rises by 0.4) and AO-darkened. The seed decides the sites, tones and gradients. It is a schematic faceted-gem look, not a real mineral, and nothing real was compared. It shares the sampler branch with `voronoicells` and `voronoipillows` and adds gradient fields; the known defect is the same as for voronoicells: blurry smudges at sharp junctions.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the gradient strength of 0.35, the tones (plate 0.7, tone floor 0.3), the base roughness of 0.3, the seam roughness increment of 0.4, the relief of 0.0012, the emerald tones and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). To share the branch I added the field `facet: 0` to the `voronoicells` and `voronoipillows` presets; the gradient term adds 0 when facet is 0 (the values do not change) and the `smoothstep(clamp())` of the tone is applied only when facet is non-zero, so their behaviour is unchanged and both of their tests (8 test cases each) still pass; I did not compare the outputs before and after the change bit for bit and rely only on those tests. The known defects are the same as for voronoicells (blurry smudges, no independently rewritten site model, and tests that only check observable behaviour). Error record: the first version of my test asserted that the colour spread of every plate is above 0.2, and all four seeds failed (the smallest plate spread was only 0.083); I had measured only the largest spread over all plates (0.31–0.36) and not the distribution; after measuring the distribution (smallest 0.029–0.036, median 0.135–0.175, mean 0.141–0.168) I changed the assertion to a mean spread between 0.13 and 0.18, a largest spread above 0.28 and every plate below 0.4, and it passed; the mistake was in my test expectation, not in the sampler.

It reuses the voronoicells sampler (which now serves `voronoicells`, `voronoipillows` and `voronoifacets`): at start-up every cell additionally gets a gradient `gradientX = 0.35·2·(hash − 0.5)` and `gradientY` from the internal hash (with two different seed salts); at sampling time, over the 25 sites of the 5×5 neighbouring cells, besides the weights `w_i = exp(−(d_i − d_min)/0.02)` the code keeps the displacement `(fromX, fromY)` from the sample to each site, and the tone is `Σ w_i·(tone_i + gradientX_i·fromX_i + gradientY_i·fromY_i) / Σ w_i`, limited to [0, 1] by `smoothstep(clamp(tone))`; the boundary measure (Gini impurity), color, height and so on are as in voronoicells: color is `0.05 + 0.7·(0.3 + 0.7·tone)·(1 − edge) + 0.02·edge + 0.02·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·(1 − edge)·(0.8 + 0.2·tone) + 0.06·grain`, `roughness = 0.3 + 0.4·edge`, `occlusion = 1 − 0.45·edge` and metallic is 0; the cache totals five `Float64Array(64)`, four `Float64Array(25)`, one `Int32Array(25)` and a `Float64Array(128²)`, 134,432 B plus 100 B, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample needs about 25 distance and exponential evaluations; I did not measure this material's time. Measured (tool-run): at 512² for the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7), splitting the pixels with occlusion above 0.97 into 4-connected regions (wrapped) gives exactly 64 regions for every seed; the region sizes are 1,325–1,739 pixels at the smallest and 4,681–5,242 at the largest; the colour spread inside a plate (maximum minus minimum) has a mean of 0.141–0.168, a median of 0.135–0.175, a minimum of 0.029–0.036 and a maximum of 0.307–0.356 (for the flat plates of voronoicells the maximum is only 0.0654, from the grain); the mean colours of the regions run from 0.2595–0.2609 (darkest) to 0.7445–0.7469 (brightest); these interior pixels cover 74.54%–75.93%; at 256² (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) color is 0.0619–0.0626 to 0.7589–0.7592 with a mean of 0.4211–0.4377 (it varies with the seed), roughness is 0.3 to about 0.6997, the lowest AO is 0.5503–0.5504 and height is at most 0.8569–0.8583 relief; at 512² (four seeds) color is 0.0610–0.0617 to 0.7595–0.7597 with a mean of 0.4211–0.4377 and height is at most 0.8588–0.8592 relief; the interior masks (512²) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 36.3% of pixels; a second-difference C1 scan (seed 0, including the cell grid lines and 16,384 golden-ratio points) finds no point above 0.03; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (67.9, 125.1, 105.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0468 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the preview (seed 7): emerald-green polygonal plates, each with a light-to-dark gradient from one side to the other, separated by dark thin seams, with blurry smudges only at a few sharp junctions. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`multiplicativeorder` adds a multiplicative order table, bringing the current catalog from 1010 to 1011 kinds (1012 gallery choices including plain). It is a 48×48 grid of squares in which cell (col, row) stands for the residue `a = col + 1` (1 to 48) modulo `n = row + 2` (2 to 49): if a and n share a factor, a has no multiplicative order and the cell is painted in the darkest tone (887 cells); otherwise it is toned by the multiplicative order `ord_n(a)` (the least positive k with `a^k ≡ 1 (mod n)`) divided by `φ(n)` (the number of residues coprime to n), raised to the power 1.5: a ratio of 1 means a is a primitive root modulo n (406 cells; these exist only for n equal to 2, 4, a prime power or twice a prime power, which is a standard fact of number theory that I did not verify in the tests), 189 cells have order 1 (a ≡ 1), and the largest order is 46 (a primitive root modulo the prime 47). It shows ice-blue on deep navy, the bright cells looking like irregularly scattered dots and short lines. The cells are rounded raised squares showing gaps through height and AO, and the seed shifts the whole table around the torus. It shares the cell shape with number-theory tables such as `totienttable` and `divisorcount` (and reuses the Mandelbrot tiles' 'inside' tone treatment for the cells without an order). It only shows the order ratios of the first 48×48 residues; it does not prove or illustrate any theorem of number theory.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the toneExponent of 1.5, the toneFloor of 0.14, the toneSpan of 0.7, the insideTone of 0.02, the ice-blue and deep navy tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). I did not check whether the residues a mod n for a ≥ n create visible periodic repeats in the table (for example the rows for small moduli such as n = 2 and 3 are periodic); that is a property of this way of assigning values. The cell shape and tone combination reuse the totienttable parameters. The tests passed on the first run with no need to adjust ranges; the number of cells without an order (887), of primitive-root cells (406), of cells of order 1 (189) and the largest order 46 are values computed in the test with independent repeated multiplication and coprime counting, and were not compared with theoretical values.

At start-up the code checks `gcd(a, n)` for every cell (`n = row + 2`, `a = col + 1`): if it is not 1 the cell is recorded as `−1` (no multiplicative order); otherwise the order is found by repeated multiplication (starting from `power = a % n`, multiplying by `a % n` modulo n until it returns to 1, the count being the order), `φ(n)` is counted by coprime residues, and the tone is `(order / φ(n))^1.5`; at sampling time every cell uses one compact-support rounded-square kernel (a quartic superellipse through smoothstep, exactly zero before the cell boundary, so the cell lookup never jumps and the field is C1): for `tone ≥ 0` color is `0.04 + (0.14 + 0.7·tone − 0.04)·mask + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, and for `tone < 0` `0.02` replaces `0.14 + 0.7·tone`; height is `0.8·dome·(0.88 + 0.12·tone)` (0.5 replaces the bracket for cells without an order) `+ 0.08·grain`, `occlusion = 1 − 0.4·(1 − mask)`, roughness is fixed at 0.4 and metallic is 0; the cache totals a `Float64Array(2304)` of 18,432 B plus a `Float64Array(128²)` of 131,072 B, 149,504 B in all, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample does a constant number of operations; I did not measure the time. Measured (tool-run): of the 2304 cells 887 have no multiplicative order, 406 are primitive roots, 189 have order 1 and the largest order is 46; on a 256² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) the lit area (color>0.5) covers 12.50%–12.64%, color is 0.0055–0.0058 to 0.8541–0.8544 with a mean of 0.2146–0.2153, the lowest AO is 0.6 and height is at most 0.8753–0.8768 relief; on a 512² grid (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7) the lit area covers 12.47%–12.74%, color is 0.0052–0.0054 to 0.8545–0.8547 with a mean of 0.2142–0.2163 and height is at most 0.8772–0.8784 relief; for each seed exactly one torus shift (seed 0: (28, 20), 1: (38, 22), 0xffffffff: (20, 37), 7: (37, 9)) makes the colours at the 2304 cell centres match the tones that the test rewrites independently, within a maximum error of 0.0150 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03); between seeds 0 and 1, 59.9% of the cell centres differ in colour by more than 0.05, and the light masks (512²) differ on 20.4% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (45.4, 59.2, 78.2), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0300 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): ice-blue rounded squares scattered into an irregular pattern of dots and short lines on deep navy, with a few rows repeating regularly. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sandpileidentity` adds a sandpile identity, bringing the current catalog from 1009 to 1010 kinds (1011 gallery choices including plain). It draws the identity element of the abelian sandpile group of a 64×64 grid: every cell holds a pile of sand, a cell with 4 grains topples and gives one grain to each of its four neighbours, and grains that fall off the border are lost into a sink; the identity is obtained by Dhar's method: stabilise twice the maximal stable configuration of 3 grains per cell (6 grains per cell), subtract the result from 6 to get the remainder, and stabilise once more. The result is a pattern of heights (0 to 3 grains): 396 cells are 0, 152 are 1, 1,476 are 2 and 2,072 are 3, symmetric left-right, top-bottom and across the diagonal (transpose), forming an ornate mandala-like design; the four height levels map to shades of gold (0 darkest, 3 brightest), and the edges and the large flat square areas are characteristic of the identity. The seed only shifts the whole 64×64 pattern around the torus; because the identity itself is not periodic (its border is a sink), a framed seam formed by the pattern's border is visible when tiled. It is only a visualisation of this mathematical object, not a real sandpile.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the size of 64×64, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tone (span 0.72), the gold and dark brown colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). I did not check the original literature for Dhar's identity formula; it is written from my understanding (stabilise twice the maximal configuration, subtract, stabilise again), and the tests check it through the necessary property of an identity, that `e + e` stabilises back to `e`, and through an independently written sweeping toppling algorithm (different from the stack-based one in the sampler), rather than relying on the formula alone; **this only shows that the result is an element of the group with `e + e = e`, and I did not separately verify that it is the identity for all recurrent configurations**. The tiling seam is a consequence of the design and I did not try to hide it. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0297). One test failed along the way: I copied the roughness check from the T-square test (expecting the roughness to drop to about 0.2 on lines), but this material has a constant roughness of 0.4, so the failing part was the copied expectation, not the sampler; after I changed it to check that the roughness equals the preset value the test passed.

At start-up (computed once per process and cached by size, shared by all seeds and samplers) the all-6 configuration on the `64 × 64` grid is stabilised (a stack processes every cell with height ≥ 4: `toppled = floor(height/4)`, the cell loses `4·toppled` and each of its existing neighbours gains `toppled`, grains beyond the border vanish), the result is subtracted from 6 and stabilised once more, giving the identity as a `Uint8Array(4096)` (in my timing script the first stabilisation took 2,323,784 topplings and the second 881,488, and the whole computation took about 69 ms in bun, a single measurement, not a benchmark); every sampler builds one `Float64Array(4096)` per height threshold 1, 2 and 3 (1 where the height is at least the threshold, shifted by the seed's torus shift), and at sampling time each is blended by `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) and re-sharpened with `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(field − 0.5))`, the three summed and divided by 3 giving the tone: color is `0.05 + 0.72·tone + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·tone + 0.2·grain`, roughness is fixed at 0.4, AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the cache per sampler is 3×4,096 + 128² = 28,672 Float64 values / 229,376 B, plus the shared 4,096 B identity, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample does a constant number of operations; I did not measure the sampling time. Measured (tool-run): the identity that the test computes with an independent sweeping algorithm has 396/152/1,476/2,072 cells of height 0/1/2/3, is symmetric left-right, top-bottom and under transpose, and `e + e` stabilises back to `e`; at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 86.28%–86.31% (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff), color is 0.0364–0.0374 to 0.7840–0.7844 with a mean of 0.6030–0.6031, roughness is always 0.4, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9950–0.9973 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 85.87%–85.88%, color is 0.0356–0.0358 to 0.7846–0.7847 with a mean of 0.6034–0.6036 and height is at most 0.9984–0.9991 relief; each seed's 64×64 nodes (sampled at the nodes) match the independent model at exactly one torus shift (seed 0: (52, 10), 1: (14, 48), 0xffffffff: (9, 46), 7: (6, 37)) over all 4,096 nodes within a maximum error of 0.0150 (equal to the grain's maximum amplitude 0.03×0.5; the test's threshold is 0.03), with 3,548 lit nodes (heights 2 or 3, = 1,476 + 2,072) each time; seeds 0 and 1 differ in 23.3% of the lit nodes; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (165.0, 143.7, 93.7), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0297 and the minimum z component is 253. I viewed the preview (seed 7): dark dotted ornaments and mandala-like designs on a golden ground, with large flat square areas. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`voronoipillows` adds Voronoi pillows, bringing the current catalog from 1008 to 1009 kinds (1010 gallery choices including plain). The same Voronoi plates as `voronoicells` (one jittered site per cell of an 8×8 grid, soft-weight partition, 64 plates and dark thin seams), but the height of every plate is a raised dome (pillow-shaped): the height falls smoothly with the distance to the weighted mean site, highest at the middle of the plate and sinking to the bottom near the seams; the colour is terracotta (each plate with its own random lightness) and the seams are still dark, rough and AO-darkened. The seed decides the sites and tones. It is a schematic clay-tile or pillow look, not real clay, and nothing real was compared. It shares the sampler branch with `voronoicells` and only the preset differs, plus new dome fields. The known defect is the same as for voronoicells: blurry smudges at sharp junctions.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the dome radius of 0.55 cells, the dome height of 0.5, the plate base height of 0.4, the roughness of 0.45, the relief of 0.0016, the terracotta tones and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview, and it shows only the base colour and not the domes, so the domes are verified through the probe and the height statistics of the tests, and **I never saw the lit 3D appearance**). To share the branch I added the fields `domeRadius: 0.55` and `domeHeight: 0` to the `voronoicells` preset (a dome height of 0 leaves its behaviour and values unchanged, and its 8 test cases still pass). The known defects are the same as for voronoicells (blurry smudges, no independently rewritten site model, and tests that only check observable behaviour). The tests passed on the first run with no need to adjust ranges.

It reuses the voronoicells sampler (which now serves `voronoicells` and `voronoipillows`): after the weights `w_i = exp(−(d_i − d_min)/0.02)` over the 25 sites of the 5×5 neighbouring cells, besides the weighted mean tone and the Gini impurity (the boundary measure) it computes the weighted mean distance `Σw_i·d_i / Σw_i` (smooth, because it is a smooth function of the normalised weights) and the dome term is `domeHeight·(1 − edge)·smoothstep(clamp(1 − mean distance/0.55))`; height is `0.4·(1 − edge)·(0.8 + 0.2·tone) + 0.5·(1 − edge)·dome + 0.08·grain` (at most about 0.98, never above 1); the rest is as in voronoicells: color is `0.06 + 0.62·(0.35 + 0.65·tone)·(1 − edge) + 0.02·edge + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, `roughness = 0.45 + 0.3·edge`, `occlusion = 1 − 0.45·edge`, metallic is 0, and the cache is that of voronoicells (133,008 B plus 100 B). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.0016 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample needs about 25 distance and exponential evaluations; I did not measure this material's time. Measured (tool-run): at 512² for the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7), splitting the pixels with occlusion above 0.97 into 4-connected regions (wrapped) gives exactly 64 regions for every seed; the region sizes are 1,326–1,850 pixels at the smallest and 4,559–4,956 at the largest; the colour spread inside any region is at most 0.0687; the mean colours of the regions run from 0.2770–0.2825 (darkest) to 0.6731–0.6768 (brightest); these interior pixels cover 74.27%–75.37%; the height difference inside each plate (maximum minus minimum, in relief units) is 0.5297–0.5966 (about half the relief; a flat plate would vary only by the grain) and the peak height of each plate is 0.8482–0.9677 relief; at 256² (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) color is 0.0674–0.0689 to 0.6880–0.6915 with a mean of 0.4115–0.4312, roughness is 0.45 to 0.7497–0.7498, the lowest AO is 0.5503–0.5504 and height is at most 0.9585–0.9625 relief; at 512² (four seeds) color is 0.0667–0.0676 to 0.6894–0.6941 with a mean of 0.4115–0.4312 and height is at most 0.9646–0.9677 relief; the interior masks (512²) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 35.8% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (116.4, 78.6, 59.4), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0820 and the minimum z component is 250. I viewed the preview (seed 7, base colour only): terracotta polygonal plates with dark thin seams and blurry smudges only at a few sharp junctions. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`voronoicells` adds Voronoi cells, bringing the current catalog from 1007 to 1008 kinds (1009 gallery choices including plain). It is the engine's first material of the Voronoi (nearest-site) family: on a periodic 8×8 grid every cell holds one jittered site (at most ±0.4 cell widths from the cell centre), 64 sites in all, each with a random tone; the whole texture is split by the nearest site into 64 polygonal plates, each plate with one tone (blue-grey, from dark to light), with thin dark seams between plates (rougher, darkened by AO and lower in height). The borders use soft weights (see the technical details) rather than a hard nearest-site lookup, so the field is smooth (C1) and the seam width is a fixed small amount. The seed only decides the sites and tones (every seed gives a different arrangement of plates). It is a schematic slab or mosaic look, not real stone, and the lightness of the plates is random and not compared with any real rock. A known defect: where the edges meet at very sharp angles the seam turns into a small blurry triangular smudge (a few are visible in the preview).

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the 8×8 cells, the jitter of 0.8, the softness of 0.02, the edgeGain of 10, the tones (plate 0.62, tone floor 0.35, seam 0.02), the blue-grey colours, the relief of 0.0012 and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices. Adjustments and error record: (1) the first version used a softness of 0.04 and an edgeGain of 6, and the preview showed several blurry smudges; changing to a softness of 0.02 and an edgeGain of 10 made the smudges smaller but did not remove them (I looked at three previews, the last two of which are byte-identical after I tidied the code). (2) The first version used a 3×3 window of neighbouring cells and the C1 test failed (second-difference ratio 332.8): scanning point by point with a probe (seed 0) found 213 (point, axis, channel) combinations above 0.03; the cause is that the window changes side when the point crosses a cell boundary, and the site that drops out is sometimes within only about a tenth of a cell width of the nearest distance, so its weight cannot be ignored and creates a slope jump; with a 5×5 window the same scan finds none above the threshold and the statistics are identical to the earlier ones (to 1e-15). The tests passed after changing to 5×5. (3) I did not rewrite the site model independently for this material: the sites come from an internal hash, and the tests check only observable behaviour (64 plates, one tone per plate, the properties of the seams, C1 and periodicity), **without comparing site coordinates**.

At start-up, on the periodic 8×8 grid, the site x and y offsets (`0.8·(hash − 0.5)` cell widths) and the tone (`hash`) of every cell are computed from the internal hash (three different seed salts); at sampling time the code computes, for the 5×5 cells around the sample's cell (25 sites in all, positions in unwrapped coordinates and cell indices taken modulo), the distances `d_i` and the nearest distance `d_min`, with weights `w_i = exp(−(d_i − d_min) / 0.02)` (shifting by the nearest distance only avoids numerical underflow and does not change the result after normalisation); the tone is the weighted mean, the boundary measure is the Gini impurity `1 − Σ(w_i / Σw)²` (0 inside a plate, 1/2 where two plates meet) and `edge = 1 − exp(−10·impurity)`: color is `0.06 + 0.62·(0.35 + 0.65·tone)·(1 − edge) + 0.02·edge + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·(1 − edge)·(0.8 + 0.2·tone) + 0.08·grain`, `roughness = 0.4 + 0.3·edge`, `occlusion = 1 − 0.45·edge` and metallic is 0; the cache totals three `Float64Array(64)`, two `Float64Array(25)`, one `Int32Array(25)` and a `Float64Array(128²)`, 133,008 B plus 100 B, all lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample needs about 25 distance and exponential evaluations; I measured a 512² maps generation only three times (seeds 0, 1 and 2, once each) at about 143–182 ms, which are single measurements, not a benchmark, and I did not compare them with other materials. Measured (tool-run): at 512² for the four seeds (0/1/0xffffffff/7), splitting the pixels with occlusion above 0.97 (far from the seams) into 4-connected regions (wrapped) gives exactly 64 regions for every seed; the region sizes are 974–1,851 pixels at the smallest and 4,536–5,019 at the largest; the colour spread inside any region is at most 0.0654; the mean colours of the regions run from 0.2764–0.2892 (darkest) to 0.6676–0.6765 (brightest); these interior pixels cover 74.47%–75.25%; at 256² (seeds 0/1/0xffffffff) color is 0.0668–0.0694 to 0.6842–0.6902 with a mean of 0.3962–0.4315 (it varies with the seed), roughness is 0.4 to about 0.6998, the lowest AO is 0.5503–0.5505 and height is at most 0.8734–0.8754 relief; at 512² (four seeds) color is 0.0664–0.0671 to 0.6850–0.6938 with a mean of 0.3959–0.4315 and height is at most 0.8755–0.8790 relief; the interior masks (512²) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 35.9% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (87.3, 99.6, 111.6), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0468 and the minimum z component is 252. I viewed the final preview (seed 7): blue-grey polygonal plates with dark thin seams and varying plate tones, with blurry smudges only at a few sharp junctions. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`cantordust` adds a Cantor dust, bringing the current catalog from 1006 to 1007 kinds (1008 gallery choices including plain). It draws the order-4 two-dimensional Cantor set (Cantor dust) on an 81×81 lattice: split the square into 3×3, keep only the four corners and remove the plus-shaped five blocks (the four edges and the centre), repeated four times; that is, a cell (x, y) survives when at every pair of base-3 digits from the coarsest to the finest neither the digit of x nor the digit of y is 1. There are 4⁴ = 256 surviving cells, drawn as small golden dots, and the other cells are shaded in different dark tones by the level at which they were removed: the coarsest level (the plus of five 27×27 blocks, 3,645 cells) is brightest and the finer levels (1,620, 720 and 320 cells) get darker in turn, so the whole looks like constellations of dots with at least two cells between neighbouring dots. The seed only shifts the whole lattice around the torus. It shares the sampler branch with `vicsekfractal` and only the survival rule differs (the Vicsek fractal keeps the plus, the Cantor dust keeps the four corners). It is only a schematic fractal pattern, not an exact mathematical diagram.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the order 4, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (line 0.72, depth 0.14), the golden and dark indigo colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). Very little of the image is bright (about 3%) and most of it is the dark brownish depth tone; I did not try enlarging the dots. To share the branch I added a field `rule: 0` to the `vicsekfractal` preset (0 = plus, 2 = Cantor dust), which does not change its behaviour or values, and its tests still pass; I did not implement rule 1 (the X shape), so no preset uses it. The relief reuses 0.0008 without further tuning (maximum normal tilt² of the 512² maps 0.0426). The tests passed on the first run with no need to adjust ranges; the numbers of cells per level and of surviving cells in the test come from a model rewritten independently by subdivision and agree with my closed-form calculation (5·27², 4·5·9², 16·5·9, 64·5).

It reuses the sampler branch of vicsekfractal (which now serves `vicsekfractal` and `cantordust`): at start-up, on an `81 × 81` lattice, the code checks every cell level by level (`unit = 3^(3 − level)`, asking whether the base-3 digits of x and y at that level are 1); rule 0 (Vicsek) records that level as the level of removal when neither digit is 1, and rule 2 (Cantor dust) when either digit is 1; surviving cells get `marks = 1`, removed cells get `marks = 0` and `depth = (4 − level) / 4`, and the cells are written into two `Float64Array`s shifted by the seed's torus shift; at sampling time it is identical to vicsekfractal: `latticeField` (C1 smoothstep) blends the survival map and `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(8·(pattern − 0.5))` re-sharpens it, a second `latticeField` blends the depth map, color is `0.05 + 0.72·line + 0.14·depth·(1 − line) + 0.03·(128² fine grain − 0.5)`, height is `0.8·line + 0.2·grain`, roughness drops by 0.2 on the line (base 0.4), AO is always 1 and metallic is 0; the cache totals 81² × 2 + 128² = 29,506 Float64 values / 236,048 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample does a constant number of operations; I did not measure the time. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: 256 surviving cells and 3,645/1,620/720/320 removed cells per level; on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 2.96%–2.98%, color is 0.0688–0.0705 to 0.7819–0.7838 with a mean of 0.1861–0.1864, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9818–0.9934 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 2.97%–2.98%, color is 0.0678–0.0682 to 0.7834–0.7844 with a mean of 0.1862–0.1864 and height is at most 0.9917–0.9974 relief; each seed's 81×81 nodes (sampled at the nodes) match the independently rewritten model, depth tones included, at exactly one torus shift (seed 0: (74, 64), 1: (62, 2), 0xffffffff: (47, 31), 7: (64, 29)) over all 6,561 nodes within a maximum error of 0.0149 (the error comes from the grain; the test's threshold is 0.03), with 256 lit nodes each time; seeds 0 and 1 differ in 7.6% of the lit nodes; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (54.0, 43.8, 41.9), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0426 and the minimum z component is 252. `tsquarefractal` adds a T-square fractal, bringing the current catalog from 1005 to 1006 kinds (1007 gallery choices including plain). It draws the order-5 T-square fractal on a 64×64 lattice: first a square of side 32 at the centre, then squares of half the side centred on the four corners of every square, five levels in all (sides 32, 16, 8, 4 and 2; 1, 4, 16, 64 and 256 squares, 341 in all); the squares overlap, and every covered cell remembers the deepest level that covers it (the smallest squares are drawn on top). 3,124 cells are covered (76.3% of the 4,096), with 324, 432, 576, 768 and 1,024 cells at deepest levels 0 to 4, and the 972 uncovered cells form a dark brown skeleton of crosses and T shapes; the covered area is cream, and the deeper the level the brighter. The seed only shifts the whole lattice around the torus. It is only a schematic fractal pattern, not an exact mathematical diagram, and it is the covered area (not the outlines of the squares) that is bright.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source or photograph cited and no photograph compared; the order 5, the tanh sharpness of 8, the tones (line 0.5, level 0.22), the cream and dark brown colours and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices (I looked at only one preview). The tests passed on the first run with no need to adjust ranges; the per-level cell counts (324/432/576/768/1,024 and 972 uncovered) in the test come from a model rewritten independently by recursion.

Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Each sample does a constant number of operations; I did not measure the time. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7: 3,124 covered cells, 324/432/576/768/1,024 cells by deepest level and 972 uncovered; on a 256² grid the lit area (color>0.5) covers 75.78% (the same for all four seeds), color is 0.0362–0.0366 to 0.7833–0.7843 with a mean of 0.5505–0.5506, roughness is 0.2001–0.3999, AO is always 1 and height is at most 0.9905–0.9960 relief; on a 512² grid the lit area covers 75.64%–75.65%, color is 0.0355–0.0356 to 0.7842–0.7846 with a mean of 0.5505–0.5506 and height is at most 0.9963–0.9984 relief; each seed's 64×64 nodes (sampled at the nodes) match the independently rewritten model, level tones included, at exactly one torus shift (seed 0: (26, 49), 1: (24, 40), 0xffffffff: (56, 59), 7: (39, 48)) over all 4,096 nodes within a maximum error of 0.0150 (this equals the grain's maximum amplitude 0.03×0.5; the test's threshold is 0.03), with 3,124 lit nodes each time; seeds 0 and 1 differ in 35.1% of the lit nodes; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (152.1, 132.9, 96.3), the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0260 and the minimum z component is 253. `vicsekfractal` adds a Vicsek fractal, bringing the current catalog from 1004 to 1005 kinds (1006 gallery choices including plain). It draws the order-4 Vicsek fractal (the plus-shaped fractal) on an 81×81 lattice: split the square into 3×3, keep the five blocks of the plus and remove the four corners, repeated four times; that is, a cell (x, y) survives when at every pair of base-3 digits (digit of x, digit of y) from the coarsest to the finest at least one of the two equals 1. There are 5⁴ = 625 surviving cells, drawn as thin gold lines (the finest level is a plus arm one cell wide), and the other cells are shaded in different dark teal tones by the level at which they were removed: the coarsest level (the four 27×27 corners, 2,916 cells) is brightest and the finer levels (1,620, 900 and 500 cells) get darker in turn. The seed only shifts the whole lattice around the torus. It is a block fractal like `sierpinskicarpet`, but the plus shape instead of a removed centre, with the surviving cells as slightly raised thin lines (higher than their surroundings) rather than recessed squares as in `sierpinskicarpet`. It is only a schematic fractal pattern, not an exact mathematical diagram.

`squarekoch` adds a square Koch island, bringing the current catalog from 1003 to 1004 kinds (1005 gallery choices including plain). A thin salmon-pink line on a dark oxblood ground traces the order-3 type 1 quadratic Koch island: starting from `F+F+F+F` (a square) and replacing every `F` by `F+F−F−F+F` three times gives a closed loop of 500 unit steps and 376 distinct lattice points (the end returns to the start); unlike the Minkowski sausage (`minkowskisausage`, which uses `F+F−F−FF+F+F−F`), the edges of this island touch each other at corners (none of the 500 edges is walked twice, but some of the 376 vertices are visited more than once); its bounding box is 27×27 cells on a 32×32-cell torus, leaving about 4 cells of empty space between it and the island of the neighbouring tile so that they do not join; the line is a third of a cell wide with a faint glow outside it. The seed only shifts the whole curve around the torus. It is a schematic fractal trace, not a real island or map. It shares the trace sampler branch with `dragoncurve`, `peanocurve`, `levycurve` and `minkowskisausage`, and only the vertex list and replacement rule differ.

I computed beforehand that the order-3 bounding box is 27×27 cells, which on a 32×32-cell torus with an offset of 2 leaves about 4 cells of empty space between it and the island of the neighbouring tile, so they do not join; I did not try order 4 (2,500 steps and a bounding box of about 135 cells, which exceeds the torus sizes this trace branch uses).
