Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff/7 on a 512² grid: light areas (color>0.5) cover 47.3%–52.8%, color is 0.0600 to 0.9400 with a mean of 0.484–0.517 and roughness is 0.30–0.65; the light masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 51.5% of pixels; a discrete Fourier component on a 128×128 grid has an amplitude of 0.1051–0.1060 at the five wave vectors (the five within 1% of each other) while the non-wave vectors (3, 5), (6, 1), (9, 9), (1, 10), (7, 3) and (12, 12) are all at most 0.0007; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (103.4, 119.6, 149.1) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0716. I viewed the preview: dark blue pentagon rings and dots on a pale blue ground that read at once as a five-fold interference pattern, but the tile is periodic and not a quasicrystal. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sudoku` adds Sudoku, bringing the current catalog from 960 to 961 kinds (962 gallery choices including plain). A newspaper puzzle grid: thin dark blue-grey rules for a 9×9 grid, each 3×3 box framed by a thicker two-pixel rule, and about two fifths of the cells (about 32–36 per seed) holding one seeded 3×5-pixel digit (1 to 9) while the rest are empty. **The digits are placed at random and the grid is not a legal or solvable Sudoku**, nor any real puzzle. The digits are 3×5-pixel glyphs, slightly rounded and bold from the smooth blending.

In the first version the box rules were three pixels thick and the dark rules covered too much area in the preview; I changed them to two pixels and adopted that; the digit strokes still look bold and slightly blurry in the preview, which is a limit of 3×5-pixel glyphs, and I did not enlarge the grid for it.

`hestain` adds H&E-stained tissue, bringing the current catalog from 952 to 953 kinds (954 gallery choices including plain). A schematic of a microscope slide of hematoxylin-and-eosin stained tissue: a pale pink-violet cytoplasm with mottle and fibre streaks along v, scattered with dark purple oval nuclei whose positions and shapes come from the spot regime of periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion (a high threshold leaves only the cores), each with a very faint pale halo. It is not real histology: there are no cell membranes, no chromatin structure inside nuclei, no cell-type differences, vessels or tissue layers, the nuclei are more evenly spread than in real tissue, and because of the single dark-to-light gradient the cytoplasm is lavender rather than eosin pink.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source, histology atlas or measurement cited and no photograph compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters equal `cheetahfur`'s (feed 0.04, kill 0.065, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the nucleus threshold of 0.6 (higher than cheetahfur's 0.5, so the nuclei are smaller), the sharpness, the halo, the purple and pink tones and the 0.05 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real tissue. In the first preview the cytoplasm was a dark lavender (0.72); I raised the base to 0.8 and lowered the halo to 0.04 (also so that the sum of tones stays inside [0, 1]), and it is still lavender rather than pink, which is a limit of a single gradient.

Defaults are a 0.05 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 190–296 ms and 512² maps about 281 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark).

`turingmaze` adds a Turing maze, bringing the current catalog from 950 to 951 kinds (952 gallery choices including plain). A dark ink labyrinth on white paper: curved, branching, partly closed thick stripes produced by periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion in its labyrinth regime, whose width and density vary slightly with slow noise, over a fine paper grain. On the tested seeds the ink forms one connected network. This is a reaction-diffusion stripe pattern and **not a fingerprint** (fingerprint ridges are much finer and have whorls and bifurcations), nor real printing or ink; the preview has a single ink-to-paper gradient.

This material is an authored schematic with no specific source cited and no photograph compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters (feed 0.03, kill 0.057, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the threshold and sharpness, the warp amount, the ink and paper tones and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real object. I first named it fingerprint, but after viewing the preview the stripe spacing was roughly five to ten times too coarse and there were no whorls, so it was renamed `turingmaze`.

It reuses the shared helpers `latticeField` and `grayScott` added for `cheetahfur`. A dedicated sampler looks the same periodic pattern up after a light noise warp (±0.025 UV) and takes a smooth stripe mask `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(9·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.5 ± 0.12 moving with a slow 7×7 noise); ink density is stripe × (0.82 + 0.18·7×7 noise) and color is `0.94 − 0.86·ink + 0.05·(160² fine grain − 0.5)`; the cache totals 96² + 5² + 7² + 7² + 160² = 34,939 Float64 values / 279,512 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses about 294,912 B of scratch arrays, of which only v is kept). Height is about 0.7 × stripes plus 0.3 × grain; roughness drops by up to 0.15 on ink. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). The labyrinth parameters were stable on the 12 seeds I scanned (raw peak v of 0.32–0.35 and a consistent edge density), which does not guarantee stability for every seed. Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 192–252 ms and 512² maps about 293 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark).

`cheetahfur` adds cheetah fur, bringing the current catalog from 949 to 950 kinds (951 gallery choices including plain). Black oval spots on short tawny fur, where the spot positions, sizes and shapes come from a periodic Gray-Scott reaction-diffusion simulation, so they are irregular but similarly spaced like natural spots rather than random dots or a fixed grid; the fur carries fine fibres along v and the spots are slightly rougher. It is not a real cheetah's coat gradient, the pale halo around spots, white belly fur or fur direction, and the preview has only one tawny-to-black gradient.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of cheetah markings. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the reaction-diffusion parameters (feed 0.04, kill 0.065, 6000 steps, a 96×96 grid), the spot threshold and sharpness, the warp amount, the fur and spot tones and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real cheetah. It is the first material in this engine that runs a simulation while its sampler is built; every other material is still a pure noise function.

A dedicated sampler plus two shared helpers: `latticeField(values, nx, ny)` is a periodic lattice sampler (the same smoothstep blend as the existing `cachedNoise`, C1; `cachedNoise` now calls it), and `grayScott(size, seedCells, feed, kill, steps, seed)` runs Gray-Scott on a periodic size×size grid (Du 0.2097, Dv 0.105, dt 1; only additions, subtractions and multiplications are used, with no transcendental functions, so the bits do not depend on the engine). The initial perturbation is one 3×3 block per jittered `seedCells×seedCells` cell so that no seed can start as a long band, and the inhibitor concentration is normalised to [0, 1]. Sampling looks the pattern up after a light `warpField` distortion (±0.015 UV) and takes a smooth spot mask `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(7·(pattern − level))` (level = 0.5 ± 0.1 moving with a 5×5 slow noise, so spot sizes differ slightly); fur color is `0.86·(1 − spot) + 0.05·spot` plus a 200×28 fibre noise stretched along v and a 128² fine grain; the cache totals 96² + 6² + 5² + 200×28 + 128² = 31,261 Float64 values / 250,088 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM; building also uses four 96² scratch arrays u, v, nextU and nextV, about 294,912 B, of which only v is kept). Simulation cost: on this machine under bun a sampler build took about 169–176 ms and 512² maps about 271 ms (single measurements, not a benchmark). Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement).

`jade` adds jade, bringing the current catalog from 948 to 949 kinds (950 gallery choices including plain). A polished green nephrite surface: a mid-green cloudy tone (a broad plus a fine cloud), crossed by pale green veins (following iso-contours of a noise field, so they form closed or winding curves) and finer hairline veins; the surface is smooth (low roughness) and slightly rougher on the veins. It is not a real jade's translucency, subsurface scattering, cotton-like inclusions, orange rind or real vein distribution, and the preview reads more like marbling drawn along iso-contours.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of polished nephrite jade. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts of the noise fields, the cloud weights, the iso-contour positions and widths of the veins, the dark and light green tones, roughness and the 0.15 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real jade.

A dedicated sampler takes the cloud as `0.7·cloud(5×5) + 0.3·fine(18×18)` periodic noise; the veins are thin bands around an iso-contour of a noise field, `exp(−((n − c)/w)²)` (C-infinity; a ridge `|n − c|` would not be C1), with `n` a 7×7 noise field, `c = 0.5` and `w = 0.045`, plus hairline veins from a 13×13 noise field with `c = 0.45` and `w = 0.03`, joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; a 128² fine grain is added; the cache totals 25 + 324 + 49 + 169 + 16,384 = 16,951 Float64 values / 135,608 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height is about 0.5 relief × cloud plus 0.2 × veins plus 0.3 × grain; roughness rises by 0.06 on veins; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.15 m nominal tile and 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: pale veins (color>0.6) cover 2.3–4.9% (varying a lot with the seed), color is 0.201–0.768 with a mean of 0.376–0.399, roughness is 0.20–0.26 and height is at most 0.859–0.902 relief; the vein masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 8.5% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (77, 115, 87) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0057. I viewed the preview: pale green iso-contour veins over a mid-green cloudy ground that read as a marbled green stone, but the vein paths (closed loops and sharp turns) are more regular and unnatural than a real jade's, and there is no translucency at all. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`spectrogram` adds spectrogram, bringing the current catalog from 947 to 948 kinds (949 gallery choices including plain). A spectrogram-style surface on a deep blue ground: 12 horizontal yellow harmonic lines bent into waves by vibrato, 5 vertical broadband burst bands and scattered speckle, with a time-frequency energy field deciding where it shows (patches fade). It is not a real audio spectrum, real harmonic ratios, time/frequency scales, a colour-scale legend or text; every harmonic has the same vibrato depth (real higher harmonics wobble more), and colour is a single linear dark-blue-to-bright-yellow gradient rather than the multi-colour scales common on real spectrograms.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a spectrogram. No specific source document, photograph, audio data or measurement is cited and no real spectrogram was compared; the harmonic count (12), vibrato depth and cycles, drift amount, energy-field resolution and threshold, burst count and weight, the deep blue and bright yellow tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices.

A dedicated sampler draws the harmonic lines as an integer number (12) of `exp(−sin²(π·12·(v − shift))/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile) with shift = `(0.2·sin(2π·6·u) + 0.18·(drift(u) − 0.5))/12` (vibrato plus a slow drift from an 8×2 periodic noise field); the bursts are an integer number (5) of vertical `exp(−sin²(π·5·u)/w²)`; the speckle is a 96×96 periodic noise field; all three are multiplied by a smooth gate from a 20×14 energy field, `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(5·(noise − 0.35))`, and joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)` so intensity stays in [0, 1]; the cache totals 16 + 280 + 9,216 + 16,384 = 25,896 Float64 values / 207,168 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Colour is pigment mapped from intensity (0.04 + 0.9 × intensity), height is about 0.6 relief × intensity plus 0.4 relief of paper grain; roughness is always 0.4; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bright lines (color>0.5) cover 6.31–6.76%, color is 0.0400–0.939 with a mean of 0.155–0.161 and height is at most 0.971–0.982 relief; the harmonic line position follows the vibrato (about +0.2 of a spacing at a positive vibrato peak and about −0.2 at a negative one, verified by the tests for each seed, with a tolerance including the drift's upper bound of 0.09); the bright-area masks (color>0.2) of seeds 0 and 1 differ on more than 5% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (50, 41, 67), r>128 covers 7.0% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.092. I viewed the preview: neat yellow wavy lines and vertical bright bands on a deep blue ground that read as a stylised spectrogram, but too regular (all harmonics bend in phase and are equally spaced). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`barchart` adds bar chart paper, bringing the current catalog from 946 to 947 kinds (948 gallery choices including plain). A pale blue-grey chart paper: two charts per tile (stacked), each with 12 dark navy bars (heights random, 15–95% of the plot area, with a slightly lighter gradient at the top), four horizontal pale-grey grid lines and a darker baseline. It is not a real chart's axis ticks, numeric labels, legend, title or multi-series data.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a bar chart. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the chart and bar counts (2 charts × 12 bars), bar width, height range, grid line count and width, plot-area bounds, navy and paper tones, roughness and the 0.25 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real chart.

A dedicated sampler draws each bar as a smooth box — a width term `smooth(clamp((0.34 − |dx|)/0.03))` plus one top term and one baseline term, each `smooth(clamp(…/0.03))` — kept entirely inside its own column (half-width 0.34 < 0.5); the grid lines are `exp(−sin²(π·steps)/w²)` inside the plot area (C-infinity, limited by a plot-area mask) and the baseline is `exp(−d²/w²)`; bar heights come from a per-column hash; everything is a convex mix; the cache totals 24 + 16,384 = 16,408 Float64 values / 131,264 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, bar and baseline height is about 0.6 relief plus 0.4 relief of paper grain and roughness drops 0.08 on bars; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bars (color<0.3) cover 25.1–29.4% and paper (color>0.85) 65.0–69.4%, color is 0.025–0.970 with a mean of 0.695–0.730, roughness is 0.54–0.62 and height is at most 0.994–0.999 relief; scanning down each column centre finds 24 bars whose heights are 13–91% of the plot area and differ by more than 0.5; the mean bar-height difference between seeds 0 and 1 is about 0.22; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (182, 189, 206), r<110 covers 26.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.061. I viewed the preview: neat dark navy bars and pale grey grid lines that read as chart paper, but with no ticks or text. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`ecgpaper` adds ECG paper, bringing the current catalog from 945 to 946 kinds (947 gallery choices including plain). A pale pink medical chart paper: a 40×40-per-tile fine grid (a heavier major line every 5 cells, so 8×8 large squares), three horizontal recording strips each repeating six heartbeat waveforms (P, Q, R, S and T waves, with ±18% amplitude variation from beat to beat) drawn in a thin dark maroon line on the strip baseline. It is not a real ECG's lead labels, calibration pulse, time scale, pathological waveforms or printed text; the waveform is a simplified schematic curve (its T wave has a flat top).

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of ECG chart paper. No specific source document, photograph, medical standard or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the grid (40×40 per tile, major every 5), the strip and beat counts (3 strips × 6 beats), the wave positions and heights, line width, pink paper and maroon ink tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real ECG paper or to be usable for medical purposes.

A dedicated sampler draws the minor and major grids as one integer-count family per direction of `exp(−sin²(π·n·s)/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping with the tile), joined by the union `1 − Π(1 − x)`; each strip's heartbeat is five compact bumps for the P, Q, R, S and T waves — `a·smooth(1 − ((x − c)/s)²)` is exactly zero for `|x − c| ≥ s` and C1, so each beat is exactly zero at its own ends and the per-beat amplitudes leave no step between beats (I first used Gaussians, whose tails are not exactly zero and left a jump of about 10⁻¹² at beat boundaries, which the C1 test magnified to about 0.038 and failed on); the trace is `exp(−d²/w²)` of width 0.0035 with `d = dy / √(1 + slope²)` the first-order distance to the curve so steep strokes keep a similar thickness, limited by two C1 windows to the vertical range the curve can reach and to its own strip; the grid and paper grain are combined and the ink is mixed in by a convex mix; the cache totals 18 + 16,384 = 16,402 Float64 values / 131,216 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, trace height is about 0.6 relief plus 0.4 relief of paper grain and roughness drops 0.1 on ink; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: ink (color<0.3) covers 3.23–3.27% (3.13% at seed 7), paper (color>0.85) covers 73.8–73.9%, color is 0.05–0.955 with a mean of 0.859–0.860, roughness is 0.60–0.70 and height is at most 0.983–0.992 relief; the baseline of every strip and the top of every R wave are ink (the test verifies each beat, 3 strips × 6 beats); the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on only 0.75% of pixels (only the per-beat amplitudes and the paper grain change with the seed); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (228, 206, 206), r<110 covers 2.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.061. I viewed the preview: three repeating heartbeat traces on pink grid paper that read as ECG paper overall, though the R waves are short and the T wave is flat-topped, unlike a real waveform. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`redalder` adds red alder, bringing the current catalog from 944 to 945 kinds (946 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Alnus rubra face: an even light yellowish-tan to slightly reddish ground, a fine uniform texture, two very faint darker bands, longitudinal fibre grain and very few (about 0.15%) fine dark short marks (standing in for the occasional aggregate rays). It is not a heartwood/sapwood distinction, the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots, wavy grain or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Red Alder](https://www.wood-database.com/red-alder/) (Color/Appearance: light tan to reddish brown, darkening and reddening with age, no visible heartwood/sapwood distinction, occasional small streaks from aggregate rays; Grain/Texture: generally straight with a moderately fine, uniform texture; Endgrain: diffuse-porous with small to medium, numerous pores) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/alnus-rubra.jpg) (an even light tan face, very faint lengthwise color change and scattered tiny dark short marks). These are color and grain-form references only: the wide streaks of aggregate rays, knots and wavy grain are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or real dimensions are not derived from the photograph; the numerous small pores are too small to show here, and a few dark marks stand in for the occasionally visible rays.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany`, `shagbarkhickory`, `eastindianrosewood`, `bubinga`, `jarrah` and `merbau`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 36×12 vessel-site table (13,824 B), two undulating (bandWarp 0.8), very low-contrast (bandContrast 0.1) dark bands, a 220×9 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,104 Float64 values / 160,832 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the dark marks are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Because the shared sampler keeps the body color at about 0.25–0.46 of the palette, I chose a lighter warm-brown palette (dark (178, 124, 80) / light (246, 204, 150)) so the body color approaches the photograph's light tan. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: dark marks (AO<0.9) cover 0.12–0.15%, undented body covers 99.8%, body color is 0.254–0.459, the across/along color-difference ratio is 9.98–10.64, roughness 0.50–0.602, height 0.45–0.503 relief and minimum AO 0.75; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (204, 155, 107), AO<230 covers 0.147% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0008. I viewed the preview: an even light tan face with very faint bands and scattered fine dark marks, similar to the photograph in overall tone and evenness; the photograph is finer and more orange-yellow (my by-eye estimate is about (215, 170, 120), not a measurement). No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`sherpafleece` adds sherpa fleece, bringing the current catalog from 943 to 944 kinds (945 gallery choices including plain). A cream curly-pile fabric surface: many randomly rotated, edge-roughened cream lumps pile up into fluffy curled tufts, with occasional occluded light-brown creases between them (about 1%) and a tone and domed highlight per lump. It is not a real fleece's fibres, curl volume, woven backing or pile direction, and the preview reads more like bumpy cream crumbs or popcorn, only a loose approximation.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of sherpa fleece. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts, probabilities, sizes and aspect ratios of the two lump layers, the edge noise, the tones, roughness and the 0.15 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real fabric.

It reuses the existing two-layer rotated-ellipse piece sampler of `granola` by fallthrough (the constructor only selects the preset; no new sampler): large lumps (12×12 grid, probability 1, semi-axes 0.7–1.1 cell × a 0.55–1.45 aspect) and small lumps (24×24 grid, probability 0.7, semi-axes 0.45–0.85 cell) are each jittered ±0.5 in their cell with a random rotation, and each pixel composites the pieces of its 5×5 cells in a fixed order (the lumps of this preset can extend about 1.8 cells, which a 3×3 window would cut — the reason I later widened the shared sampler to 5×5) — `value = value·(1 − m) + piece·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.6))`, `q` multiplied by an edge perturbation from a 64×64 periodic noise field — large lumps first, small lumps over them, so every term is C1; the uncovered part has colour 0.3 and AO 0.4; the cache totals 1,008 + 4,032 + 4,096 + 16,384 = 25,520 Float64 values / 204,160 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.85 relief plus 0.15 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.15 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). I tuned this preset twice: the first version (22×22 grid, smaller lumps) looked like coarse sand or crumbs, and the second, with larger lumps, read more like fluffy tufts and was adopted; the first version's tones also let colour reach 1.01 (outside [0, 1]), and lowering the large/small lump tones to 0.52/0.58 and the dome to 0.2 brought the maximum back to 0.93. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: bright tufts (color>0.7) cover 38.8–41.3%, the crease ground (AO<0.45) covers 0.92–1.72%, color is 0.234–0.931 with a mean of 0.659–0.670, the crease ground averages 0.296, roughness is always 0.92, minimum AO is 0.4 and height is at most 0.996–0.998 relief; the bright-tuft masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 48.2% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (203, 191, 174), AO<200 covers 5.2% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.788. I viewed the preview: fluffy cream lumps piled up, but not like a real fleece's fibres. No new API or dependency; Worker, cache and texture ownership follow the existing paths; this paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`tilledsoil` adds tilled soil, bringing the current catalog from 942 to 943 kinds (944 gallery choices including plain). A dark brown soil surface: randomly rotated, edge-roughened clods (mid brown, overlapping, covering about three fifths) with darker, occluded fine soil in the gaps, and a few (about 7–9%) smaller pale pebbles or grit. It is not a real soil's roots, worm holes, moist sheen, plant litter or grain-size distribution, and the preview can also read as a camouflage pattern.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of tilled soil. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts, probabilities, sizes and aspect ratios of the clod and pebble layers, the edge noise, the layer tones, roughness and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real soil.

It reuses the existing two-layer rotated-ellipse piece sampler of `granola` by fallthrough (the constructor only selects the preset; no new sampler): clods (8×8 grid, probability 1, semi-axes 0.34–0.62 cell × a 0.7–1.3 aspect) and pale pebbles (16×16 grid, probability 0.3, semi-axes 0.1–0.22 cell) are each jittered ±0.45 in their cell with a random rotation, and each pixel composites the pieces of its 5×5 cells in a fixed order (the largest piece, at maximum stretch and edge perturbation, can reach more than one cell past its own, so a 3×3 window would cut it) — `value = value·(1 − m) + piece·m` with the mask `m = smooth(clamp((1 − q)/0.4))`, `q` multiplied by an edge perturbation from a 48×48 periodic noise field — clods first, pebbles over them, so every term is C1; the part not covered by any piece has colour 0.14 and AO 0.45; the cache totals 448 + 1,792 + 2,304 + 16,384 = 20,928 Float64 values / 167,424 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, dome height is about 0.8 relief plus 0.2 relief of grain; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). While writing this preset I first set the pebble tone to 0.78 and the probe showed colour up to 1.03 (outside [0, 1]); lowering it to 0.66 ± 0.08 fixed that. Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: the gap ground between clods (AO<0.46) covers 35.9–41.8% (42.0% at seed 7), pale pebbles (color>0.5) cover 6.8–9.4%, color is 0.094–0.899 with a mean of 0.270–0.288, the gap ground averages 0.140, roughness is always 0.92, minimum AO is 0.45 and height is at most 0.994–0.997 relief; the cover masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 43.7% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (62, 47, 35), AO<200 covers 50.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.894. I viewed the preview: lighter brown clods and small pebbles over a dark brown gap ground that read as loose soil, but quite like a camouflage pattern and far flatter than real soil. `heatsinkfins` adds heat sink fins, bringing the current catalog from 941 to 942 kinds (943 gallery choices including plain). This material is an authored schematic of the general look of an extruded aluminium heat sink. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the fin count (20 per tile), the fin-top to gap ratio and sharpness, the metal tones, extrusion-line and mottle strength, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real heat sink specification.

A dedicated sampler takes the fin weight `0.5 + 0.5·tanh(3.5·sin(2π·20·u))` (tanh of a sine is a smooth square wave, C-infinity; the integer fin count wraps with the tile), which blends colour between the gap tone 0.14 and the fin tone 0.7; the fin tops also carry a 4×160 extrusion-line noise elongated along v (applied only on the tops), a 4×4 anodising mottle and a 128² fine grain; in the gaps roughness rises by 0.2 and AO drops to 0.5; the cache totals 640 + 16 + 16,384 = 17,040 Float64 values / 136,320 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). `metallic` is 1 over the whole sampled range, and the kind is added to the `ProceduralMaterial` metal-factor list and to the tests' non-metal exception list. Color is the metal's reflectance colour, fin-top height is about 0.8 relief, extrusion lines 0.1 and grain 0.1; there is no mortar. Defaults are a 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.01 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured (tool-run) at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: fin tops (color>0.5) cover 47.1–47.3% and gaps (color<0.25) 43.4–43.7%, the region with AO<0.9 is always 56.25% (seed-independent), color is 0.099–0.777 with a mean of 0.416–0.421, roughness is 0.38–0.58, minimum AO is 0.50, metallic is always 1 and height is at most 0.988–0.992 relief; on a fin top the per-pixel colour difference along u (across fins) is about 4.9–5.3 times that along v (the extrusion lines); in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (76, 79, 86), the metallic channel averages 255 and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.716. I viewed the four-panel preview: neat straight fins with deep gaps that read as an extruded-aluminium heat sink, but very simplified (no fin height, chamfers or base plate). `jerky` adds beef jerky, bringing the current catalog from 940 to 941 kinds (942 gallery choices including plain). A dried-meat strip surface: a dark red-brown ground with dense fibres elongated along u, a broad low-frequency tone variation in the same direction, position-dependent sheen (roughness) and scattered near-black cracked-pepper flecks. It is not a real jerky's shrunken outline, fat specks, salt crystals or oiliness, and the preview can also be mistaken for brushed dark wood grain.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of beef jerky. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited and no photograph was compared; the cell counts of the fibre and tone noise, the pepper density and size, the red-brown tones, roughness and the 0.12 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real jerky.

A dedicated sampler combines a 14×240 fibre noise (elongated along u), a 4×8 broad low-frequency tone noise, a 6×36 sheen noise (roughness ± 0.1) and a 128² fine grain; cracked-pepper flecks are `smooth(1 − q)` discs on a 36×36 grid (about 14% chance, radius 0.22 cell, jitter 0.26, so radius plus jitter stays under half a cell and each stays inside its own cell) that darken the meat colour **multiplicatively** (`color = meat × (1 − 0.85·pepper)`); the cache totals 2,592 + 3,360 + 216 + 32 + 16,384 = 22,584 Float64 values (180,672 B) plus a 1,296 B Uint8 pepper-presence table = 181,968 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height combines 0.45 relief of fibres, 0.15 of pepper and 0.4 of grain; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Thin black hatch lines on cream paper are added by a low-frequency tone field: dark areas get a first diagonal family, darker areas add the opposite diagonal to form a crosshatch, and the darkest areas add horizontal lines; line width also grows with tone while highlights stay bare paper. A dedicated sampler lets a 6×6 low-frequency noise field decide the tone; three integer-count line families (`u+v` diagonal, `u−v` opposite diagonal, horizontal `v`) each fade in with a smooth ramp at their own threshold, a single line is `exp(−sin²(π·n·s)/w²)` (C-infinity, wrapping at integer counts), and the width grows from 0.06 to 0.3 with tone; the families join as the union `1 − Π(1 − x)` (not `max`, which creases where two families are equal and is not C1 — my C1 test failed on exactly that while implementing, see ACCEPTANCE), so the whole is C1; the cache totals 6² (36) plus a 128² paper grain (16,384) = 16,420 Float64 values / 131,360 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, ink height is about 0.7 relief plus 0.3 relief of paper grain; roughness drops 0.08 on ink; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. Defaults are a 0.25 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metric displacement). Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid (tool-run): dark ink (color<0.5) covers 5.33–14.64% (it follows the tone field), bare paper (color>0.85) covers 70.3–87.3%, color is 0.040–0.960 with a mean of 0.796–0.883, roughness 0.72 to 0.80 and height at most 0.997 relief; the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 8.01% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (201, 192, 172), r<110 covers 9.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.168. This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a coir (coconut fibre) doormat. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; patch directions, fibre thickness, tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real product or material specification.

A dedicated sampler uses four value-noise lattices stretched along different directions — horizontal (12×170 cells), vertical (170×12) and two diagonals sampled with the integer shears `(u+v, v)` and `(u−v, v)` (170×12 each, which still wrap with the tile because the shears are integer) — plus a 128² fine fuzz noise and a 5×5 low-frequency patch noise; the patch noise × 4 selects the direction, the four direction weights are `cos²(π/2·distance)` (a cyclic distance, non-zero only below 1), which have zero slope at the hand-over and always sum to one, so the blend is C1. The cache totals 24,569 Float64 values / 196,552 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: color runs from 0.007–0.053 up to 0.654–0.678 with a mean of 0.348–0.358 and a standard deviation of about 0.101, roughness is 0.935–0.965, height 0.024–0.953 relief, minimum AO 0.553–0.558 and the across/along color-difference ratio 1.03–1.23 (no global fibre direction); the mean sampled color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is 0.113; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (91, 65, 40), r<90 covers 45.2%, AO<200 covers 15.7% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.618. I viewed the four-panel render: coarse directional patchy fibres and a strongly textured normal map. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`europeanyew` adds European yew, bringing the current catalog from 917 to 918 kinds (919 gallery choices including plain). It approximates the heartwood of an unfinished flatsawn Taxus baccata face: an orange-brown ground, fine uniform texture, 16 dense undulating arched darker brown growth rings (about a seventh of the area) and fine longitudinal fibre grain. It is not the narrow pale yellow-tan sapwood band, a darker purplish color variation, knots, burls or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database European Yew](https://www.wood-database.com/european-yew/) (Color/Appearance: sapwood usually a thin band of pale yellow or tan, heartwood orangish brown, sometimes with a darker brown or purplish hue; Grain/Texture: straight grain with a fine uniform texture and good natural luster) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/taxus-baccata-300x600.jpg) (an orange-brown face with fine dense growth rings and arches and one dark knot). These are color and grain-form references only: the photograph's knot, sapwood band and purplish hue are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the `douglasfir` ring-index sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `longleafpine`, `westernredcedar`, `sitkaspruce`, `europeanlarch` and `europeanolive`); only the constructor selects the preset (rings 16, arch 1.9, warp 0.6, latewood 0.55–0.9, lateTone 0.32, earlyTone 0.82); a 36-value warp table plus a 200×6 fibre field and 128² fine grain total 17,620 Float64 values / 140,960 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0, latewood is slightly higher and ring color is pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.0025 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: color<0.6 covers 14.9–15.2%, color>0.75 covers 70.2–70.5%, the color range is 0.469–0.881, roughness 0.421–0.490, height 0.498–0.642 relief, the across/along color-difference ratio 3.64–3.66 and the minimum AO 0.96; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean r/g/b is about (216, 143, 68), g≥140 covers 72.4% (g<140 covers 27.6%) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0149. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`raindropripples` adds raindrop ripples, bringing the current catalog from 916 to 917 kinds (918 gallery choices including plain). On a smooth dark grey-blue water surface, 8×8 position-jittered raindrops each spread concentric ripple rings (random amplitude and phase), and neighbouring ripples superpose into interference patterns; bright and dark ring crests each cover about 6–9% of the area, the reflected color hovers around a mid grey-blue, roughness rises slightly on the waves and the normals show clear ring undulation. It is not time-evolving spreading, refraction below the surface, splashes, foam or shore reflection.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of concentric ripples from raindrops on water. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; cell count, ring wavelength, envelope radius, amplitude range, tones, roughness and the 0.4 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real water body or fluid-dynamics model (no dispersion, decay law or wave-speed relation).

A dedicated sampler stores four Float64 values per cell (jittered offset x, y, amplitude and ring phase), 256 Float64 values for the 8×8 cells, plus a 96² fine grain (9,216 Float64 values), 9,472 Float64 values / 75,776 B of lattice arithmetic in total (not total RAM). Ripples are summed: each drop contributes `amplitude·smooth(1 − q/R²)·cos(2π√q/λ − phase)` (envelope R = 0.78 cell with zero value and slope at the outer rim; `cos(k√q)` is even in the radius, so it is smooth at the centre too) over the 3×3 neighbour cells, and `tanh(1.1·Σ)` maps the unbounded sum to reflected bright/dark, so overlaps stay C1. Color is pigment (water reflection), height only feeds the normal; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.4 m nominal tile and 0.0022 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. I corrected one error: the first version divided the ring frequency by the cell count again, rendering overly wide rings; after fixing it I viewed the four-panel render and confirmed fine concentric rings (wavelength 0.2 cell × 64 pixels per cell ≈ 12.8 pixels, a computed value). Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color>0.75 covers 6.1–8.6%, color<0.25 covers 6.1–8.6% (the two differ by under 0.3 percentage points), color is 0.111–0.887 with a mean of 0.4999–0.5004, roughness is 0.080–0.122, height 0.044–0.954 relief and AO 1; along three horizontal lines the color crosses mid grey 32–66 times; the mean sampled color difference between seeds 0 and 1 is 0.189; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (115, 132, 143), r<80 covers 12.8%, r>150 covers 12.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.107. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`gamedice` adds game dice, bringing the current catalog from 915 to 916 kinds (917 gallery choices including plain). A tray of 6×6 ivory rounded-square dice, each with round black pips pressed into the face (the standard one-to-six layouts, rolled per die by seed), separated by a darker, rougher tray with AO; the faces are smooth and the pips recessed and rougher. It is not the three visible faces of 3D dice, tilted or stacked dice, geometry beyond the rounded rim, pip paint thickness or wear.

This material is an authored schematic based on the standard pip layouts (1–6) of a six-sided die. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; die size, corner rounding, pip radius and depth, tones, roughness and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real dice specification (such as dimensions or opposite faces summing to seven), nor do they simulate how real pips are recessed.

A dedicated sampler rolls 1–6 for each of the 36 dice from `hash` by seed, with the pips taken from the standard layouts over seven candidate sites (four corners, two side centres and the centre); a die body is the product of two smooth edge ramps (flat top, zero slope at the rim) and a pip is `smooth(1 − q/r²)` pressed into the face, with tray and die colors blended by the die-body weight, so everything is C1. The cache is a 36-entry Uint8 pip table plus a 64² fine grain (4,096 Float64 values), 32,804 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: the set of dark sites among the seven on every die is exactly one of the six standard layouts; across the 108 dice of the three seeds the pip counts are 21 ones, 17 twos, 19 threes, 18 fours, 21 fives and 12 sixes; face color is 0.921–0.939, pips 0.04, tray 0.16; face height is 1.0 relief, pips 0.78, tray 0; roughness is 0.30 on faces, 0.55 on pips and 0.40 on the tray; tray AO is 0.5 and face AO 1; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 143.7, r<60 covers 33.0%, r>180 covers 46.3%, AO<200 covers 39.2% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.532. I viewed the four-panel render and confirmed the two-, three-, five- and six-pip layouts match standard die faces. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`europeanolive` adds European olive wood, bringing the current catalog from 914 to 915 kinds (916 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished flatsawn Olea europaea face: a pale yellow-tan ground, fine uniform texture, six thin undulating arched darker yellow-brown growth streaks (under a tenth of the area) and fine longitudinal fibre grain. It is not the deep brown to near-black streaks and veins, curly/wild grain, burl, a sapwood/heartwood boundary or a finish.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database Olive](https://www.wood-database.com/olive/) (Color/Appearance: heartwood from yellow to light reddish brown with darker brown to black streaks and veins, yellowish sapwood sharply demarcated from heartwood; Grain/Texture: straight, interlocked or wild, fine uniform texture with moderate natural luster) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/olea-europaea-300x600.jpg) (a pale yellow-tan face with thin dark growth lines and arches). These are color and grain-form references only: the deep brown to near-black streaks and veins, wild grain and burl described on the page are **not** reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the `douglasfir` ring-index sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `longleafpine`, `westernredcedar`, `sitkaspruce` and `europeanlarch`); only the constructor selects the preset (rings 6, arch 3.4, warp 0.9, a narrow latewood line at 0.8–0.96, lateTone 0.14, earlyTone 0.78); a 49-value warp table plus a 220×5 fibre field and 128² fine grain total 17,533 Float64 values / 140,264 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0, latewood is slightly higher and ring color is pigment. The default 0.18 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. I first set lateTone to 0.3, but the render's ring lines were too faint, so I lowered it to 0.14. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 256² grid: color<0.72 covers 9.1–9.9%, color>0.8 covers 33.1–34.1%, the color range is 0.605–0.847, roughness 0.381–0.450, height 0.498–0.602 relief, the across/along color-difference ratio 2.44–2.49 and the minimum AO 0.97; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean r/g/b is about (223, 194, 141), g≥185 covers 95.9% (g<185 covers 4.1%) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0052. `poolcaustics` adds pool caustics, bringing the current catalog from 913 to 914 kinds (915 gallery choices including plain). A bright, branching network of fine light lies over a blue pool floor, with darker deep-blue patches between the meshes; about a third of the area is bright, roughness is slightly lower in the light network and the floor has faint grain relief. It is not time-evolving caustics, real refracted-ray tracing, tile joints, water-surface reflection or a depth gradient.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of pool-floor caustic light. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the light network is built from three bent line families of my own design and only visually approximates a light net, it is not a physical caustics model. Family directions, widths, gain, tones, roughness and the 0.5 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real pool or optical specification.

A dedicated sampler uses three integer-wavenumber line families `(6,0)`, `(3,5)` and `(−3,5)`, each phase further bent by three integer-wavenumber sinusoids (with seed phases); each family contributes `exp(−sin²(π·phase)/w²)` (C∞), and the sum saturates through `S/(1+S)` into color and roughness; where bending squeezes lines together their glows add into brighter, thinner branches. The cache is a 96² pool-floor grain (9,216 Float64 values) plus 3 phases and 3 offsets, 9,222 Float64 values / 73,776 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment, height only feeds the normal; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.5 m nominal tile and 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. Iteration: the first version (warpAmplitude 0.9, lineWidth 0.2, gain 0.9) rendered tangled thin loops that did not look like caustics; the second widened the lines (0.55) and lowered bending and gain, giving a soft light net with low contrast; the final version uses lineWidth 0.42, gain 0.9 and baseTone 0.16 for more contrast, and I viewed it to confirm a bright branching network with dark meshes. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color>0.55 covers 33.3–36.9%, color<0.3 covers 22.3–24.3%, color is 0.144–0.793 with a mean of 0.449–0.461, roughness is 0.554–0.698 and AO is 1; the bright masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 43.9% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/g/b is about (99, 138, 165) and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.066. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`metalflakepaint` adds metal-flake paint, bringing the current catalog from 912 to 913 kinds (914 gallery choices including plain). Round metal flakes of random position, tilt and brightness (a 64×64 grid with about half the cells holding a flake) are scattered over a deep blue clear-coated base, covering about 21–22% of the area; the flakes are pale lavender-silver and form a partial metal mask in the metallic channel (at most about 0.68, not full metal), their small tilts make the normals sparkle and the clear base is non-metal. It is not pearlescent / color-shift (multi-hue) paint, polygonal flake shapes, independent reflection directions per flake or clear-coat thickness.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of metal-flake car paint. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; flake size, density, tones, metallic coverage, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real paint or color code.

A dedicated sampler stores five Float64 values per cell (jittered offset x, y, tilt x, y and tone; a missing flake has tone 0), 20,480 Float64 values for the 64² cells, plus a 128² clear-coat grain of 16,384 Float64 values, for 36,864 Float64 values / 294,912 B of lattice arithmetic in total (not total RAM). Flakes are summed rather than owned: each is a `smooth(1 − q/r²)` dome (radius 0.55 cell, zero value and slope at the rim) over the 3×3 neighbour cells (a flake reaches at most 0.9 cell from its cell centre, which the neighbourhood covers); height is the sum of each dome times `1 + 2·tilt·(tiltX·dx + tiltY·dy)`, so overlaps stay C1. The coverage `S/(1+S)` (S being the weighted sum times flakeGain 1.2) saturates smoothly into color, metallic, roughness and AO without hard clipping. This is why the kind is added to the metallic list in `procedural-material.ts` (metallic factor 1, controlled by the per-sample metallic channel) and to the generic 'non-metal' exception list in the tests. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. My first render used 48 cells, radius 0.78 and presence 0.85, and after viewing it the face was almost entirely silver with no blue base visible, so I changed to 64 cells, radius 0.55, presence 0.5 and flakeGain 1.2. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: metallic>0.3 covers 21.5–22.3%, metallic peaks at 0.671–0.683, bottoms at 0 and averages 0.117–0.121, color is 0.165–0.748, height runs from 0.25 to 1.31–1.38 relief, roughness is 0.052–0.12, minimum AO is 0.932 and the color–metallic correlation is about 0.999; the flake masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 33.3% of pixels; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r/b is about (73, 113), the mean metallic channel is 30.3/255 with 21.9% above 76 and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.351. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`tapemeasure` adds a tape measure, bringing the current catalog from 911 to 912 kinds (913 gallery choices including plain). One tile is a 100 mm segment of yellow tape: 100 millimetre ticks (0.2 of the tile height long), a longer tick every 5 mm (0.3) and the longest, thicker tick every 10 mm (0.42), all near-black and hanging from 0.08 below the band edge; the cross-section is a cosine bow with raised rims and a concave centre, so the glossy coat has a lengthwise normal gradient. It has no numerals, imperial scale, end hook, case or wear.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a metric tape measure. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; tick lengths and widths, the yellow, the bow depth, roughness and the 0.1 m nominal tile (exactly one 100 mm segment) are authored choices and do not claim to match any real tape standard or accuracy class.

A dedicated sampler finds the nearest tick with `k = round(u·100)` and picks the length by the k 1/5/10 mm hierarchy; ink = `smooth(1 − d²/w²)` times 0.004 top and bottom ramps, zero beyond the tick width, so the nearest-tick ownership change at half a millimetre never jumps; the bow height is `0.1 + 0.55·(0.5+0.5cos 2πv)`, with zero slope at both rims, so it is C1 across tiles, and the rims carry AO (at most 0.25). The cache is only a 64² paper/coat grain (4,096 Float64 values / 32,768 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Color is pigment, ink height is 0.04 relief; metallic is 0 (a painted tape) and there is no mortar. The default 0.1 m nominal tile and 0.03 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices; I first used 0.01, then saw the normals were too flat and raised it to 0.03. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: at v = tickTop + 0.1 all 100 ticks are dark (color 0.016–0.043) and color between ticks is at least 0.886; at lengths 0.25 / 0.35 there are 20 / 10 dark ticks and 0 beyond the longest; overall color is 0.016–0.915, height 0.100–0.653 relief, AO 0.75–1 and roughness 0.375–0.544; in the seed-7 512² maps the mean r/g/b is about (217, 185, 35), yellow pixels (r>180, g>150, b<70) cover 94.3%, r<100 covers 4.3% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.111. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`ledmatrix` adds an LED dot-matrix panel, bringing the current catalog from 910 to 911 kinds (912 gallery choices including plain). A 48×48 grid of round LEDs split into 8×6 character cells (5×7 LEDs plus one blank column and row each); each cell lights 2–4 random short horizontal, vertical or diagonal strokes by seed (pseudo-glyphs, not a font); lit LEDs are bright red-orange, unlit ones dark red, the LED lenses are smooth and slightly domed and the black plate is rougher with AO. It is not a real font or readable text, scrolling animation, emission, color mixing or RGB sub-pixels.

This material is an authored schematic of the general structure of an LED dot-matrix display panel. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; the LED count, character-cell size, stroke generation rule, tones, roughness, AO and the 0.16 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real product.

A dedicated sampler draws strokes per character cell from `hash` by seed at construction into a 2,304-entry Uint8 lit table, plus 2,304 Float64 brightness jitters (2,304 B + 18,432 B = 20,736 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). At sample time each LED owns its square cell; the lens is `smooth(1 − q/r²)` with r = 0.46 < 0.5, zero (value and slope) at the cell boundary, so lit/unlit tone changes never jump at a seam, and the black plate shows between lenses. Color is pigment (there is no emission), lit LEDs add a 0.1 lens highlight tone; height only feeds the normal and AO; metallic is 0 and there is no mortar. The default 0.16 m nominal tile and 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. I first set litTone to 0.88; probing showed lit LED color reaching 1.0199 (outside [0,1]), so I lowered it to 0.84, after which lit LED color is 0.900–0.980. Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: lit fraction 12.9–14.1%, lit LED color 0.900–0.980, unlit LED 0.150–0.170, lens height 1.0 relief / plate 0, lens roughness 0.17 / plate 0.62, plate AO 0.55 / lens 1, plate color 0.02; the lit masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 21.5% of LEDs; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 48.0, r>160 covers 3.07%, AO<200 covers 67.6% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.413. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`barcodelabel` adds a barcode label, bringing the current catalog from 909 to 910 kinds (911 gallery choices including plain). One tile is a full label width: 10-module quiet zones on both sides, a Code 128 Start B pattern (11 modules), nine data symbols (each six alternating bar/space widths of 1–4 modules summing to 11) and a 13-module stop pattern, 143 modules in total; the bars occupy only the v 0.1–0.9 label band with blank paper above and below. Near-black toner (slightly raised and smoother) is printed on bright rough paper with a fine paper-fibre grain. It is not a decodable Code 128: the data symbols are seed-chosen random widths with no check symbol and without the parity rule (bar widths summing to even, space widths to odd), and there is no human-readable text, other label elements or curvature.

The structure follows the actually read [Wikipedia “Code 128”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Code_128): each symbol is three black bars and three white spaces of 1–4 modules each summing to 11 modules and starting with a bar and ending with a space; the stop pattern is 13 modules including a final 2-module bar; the quiet zone is at least 10 modules on each side. The Start B bit pattern `11010010000` and the stop pattern `1100011101011` that I use come from my recollection of the standard's symbol table; the text extracted from that page did not include the tables, so those two bit strings are **not verified by the page**. The appearance (black bars on white paper, 0.14 m tile, toner height, roughness, paper color) is authored, with no specific label photograph or measurement cited.

A dedicated sampler, at construction, draws nine symbols from `hash` by seed (five widths of 1–4 each, the sixth derived from the sum of 11 and required to fall in 1–4, retried up to 4,096 times and falling back to the Start B widths on failure) into a 143-module bit array; at sample time x = fract(u)·143 finds the module and each bar edge blends over ±`edgeRamp/2` = 0.11 module with `smooth` (zero slope at both ends, hence C1), and the label band edges use a 0.012 `smooth` ramp. The cache is a 96² paper-fibre grain (9,216 Float64 values / 73,728 B) plus a 143-entry module-bit array. Color is pigment; toner has height 0.35 relief and paper grain at most 0.1; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.14 m nominal tile and 0.0006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color<0.5 covers 30.1–34.8%, the lowest color is 0.0276, the highest 0.982, mean toner height is about 0.39 relief versus about 0.055 for paper and roughness spans 0.445–0.575; in the seed-7 512² maps mean r is 173.3, r<128 covers 31.1% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0036. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`topographicmap` adds topographic contour paper, bringing the current catalog from 908 to 909 kinds (910 gallery choices including plain). On warm off-white paper, constant-width brown contour lines are printed over a terrain made of seven integer-wavenumber sinusoids (16 contour levels, every fifth an index contour that is heavier and darker), with a very faint elevation tint and fine paper-fibre grain; the ink sits slightly above the paper. It is not real terrain data, elevation labels, rivers, roads, a grid or legend text.

This material is an authored schematic of the general look of a contour map. No specific source document, photograph or measurement is cited; level count, index interval, line width, ink and paper colors and the 0.3 m nominal tile are authored choices and do not claim to match any real map specification or scale.

A dedicated sampler sums seven integer-wavenumber sinusoids (seed-chosen phases, ±20% amplitude jitter) into a periodic analytic (C∞) terrain; the contour distance `sin²(πd)/π² ÷ (levels·|∇|)²` converts level distance to squared UV distance (|∇| has a 0.4 floor so summits and saddles stay smooth), so line width does not widen on flat ground; line = `smooth(1 − distance²/width²)` and the index weight is `((1+cos(2πd/5))/2)^6`, so width and ink are C∞. The cache is a 128² paper-fibre grain plus 7 phases and 7 amplitudes, 16,398 Float64 values / 131,184 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Color is pigment; ink has height 0.6 relief and paper grain at most 0.15; metallic is 0, there is no mortar and AO is 1. The default 0.3 m nominal tile and 0.0015 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) are authored choices. At seeds 0/1/0xffffffff on a 512² grid: color<0.7 (including edge falloff) covers 9.3–10.5%, color<0.45 covers 6.7–7.6%, the lowest color is 0.14 (index ink), the highest 0.925–0.930, the mean 0.839–0.846 and mean ink height is about 0.575 relief versus about 0.077 for paper; the ink masks of seeds 0 and 1 differ on 17.6% of pixels; the seed-7 512² mean base color is about (222, 206, 180), b<170 covers 10.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.111. I viewed the first render and confirmed the line width looks consistent on both flat and steep ground before settling. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`eastindianrosewood` adds East Indian rosewood, bringing the current catalog from 907 to 908 kinds (909 gallery choices including plain). It approximates an unfinished longitudinal Dalbergia latifolia face: a deep purplish-brown ground, five darker near-black undulating streaks, fine longitudinal fibre grain and scattered short open-vessel pits (about 1.2%). It is not a golden-brown pale face, white sapwood, a polished surface, interlocked/wavy figure or oily luster.

Appearance follows the actually read [Wood Database East Indian Rosewood](https://www.wood-database.com/east-indian-rosewood/) (Color/Appearance: heartwood from golden brown to deep purplish brown with darker blackish streaks, darkening with age to a deep brown) and the actually downloaded and viewed [wood-face photograph](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/dalbergia-latifolia-1-300x600.jpg) (a deep brown, purple-tinged longitudinal face with darker streaks and fine pores). These are color and grain-form references only: the golden-brown variation, pale sapwood and real vessel distribution are not reproduced, no source image is shipped, and true color, roughness or physical size is not inferred from the photograph.

It reuses the existing Padauk/Bloodwood-family long elliptical vessel sampler by fallthrough (the same path as `blackwalnut`, `teak`, `honduranmahogany` and `shagbarkhickory`); only the constructor selects the preset: a 40×14 vessel-site table (17,920 B), five strongly undulating (bandWarp 0.8), high-contrast (bandContrast 0.45) dark bands, a 220×9 longitudinal fibre field, 128² fine grain and the fixed 3×4 warp table, totalling 20,616 Float64 values / 164,928 B of lattice arithmetic (not total RAM). Metallic is 0; the vessel pits are real height depressions while color streaks are pigment. No specific source document, product photograph or measurement is cited, so it does not claim to match any real ball, dimple diameter/depth/count or rule; colors, roughness, AO, relief layers and the 0.028 m nominal tile (7 columns of 4 mm) are authored choices. The 7×8 grid makes the hex row pitch (7/8 ≈ 0.875) close to the ideal 0.866 while keeping the row count even so the stagger parity wraps with the tile.

A dedicated sampler computes the isotropic squared distance `q` to the nearest dimple centre in the row above, the row itself and the row below (odd rows offset by half a column); dimple = `smooth(1 − q/r²)`, with zero slope at the centre and rim, so bowls and lands stay C1. An even row count makes the stagger parity wrap in v. Only a 128² grain is cached (16,384 Float64 values / 131,072 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Metallic is 0 and there is no mortar; relief is 0.012 UV-relative (not metres of displacement; raised to this value because 0.0012 left the normals almost flat). Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: bowl-centre height 0.220–0.226 relief, AO 0.55 and roughness 0.441–0.479; the land halfway to the same-row neighbour has height 0.620–0.626, AO 1 and roughness 0.321–0.360; AO<0.9 covers 52.9% of a 256² grid. The seed-7 512² mean base-color red is about 231.8, AO<230 covers 52.8% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.030. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`laptopkeycaps` adds chiclet laptop keycaps, bringing the current catalog from 893 to 894 kinds (895 gallery choices including plain). An 8×8-cell grid carries one rounded-square dark matte keycap per cell (a quartic superellipse outline, half-width 0.43 cell, about 68% of the area) with a slightly dished top that rises toward the key edge, separated by narrow dark low gaps (AO 0.25, roughness ≥ 0.9); each key has a slightly different tone, fine matte grain and an edge highlight. There are no legends, backlight, switch mechanism or chassis.

This material is an authored schematic of a generic chiclet (island) keyboard. No specific source document, product photograph or measurement is cited, so it does not claim to match any real keyboard, key pitch, keycap profile or material; colors, roughness, AO, relief layers and the 0.152 m nominal tile (8 cells at 19 mm) are authored choices.

A dedicated sampler uses `s = ((dx/hw)²)² + ((dy/hw)²)²`, a quartic superellipse polynomial; `smooth(clamp((1−s)/bevel))` gives a C1 rounded square that reaches zero before the cell boundary, so the `fract()` cell wrap and the per-key tone lookup never change continuity. Top height is topHeight − dishDepth·(1 − r²). Constructor caches are 64 per-key tones (512 B) and a 160² matte stipple (25,664 Float64 values / 205,312 B of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM). Metallic is 0 and there is no mortar; relief is 0.004 UV-relative (not metres of displacement). Measured at seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: key-centre height 0.620–0.632 relief, 0.649–0.660 at 0.75 half-widths from the centre (the dish rises outward), gap height 0.06 and gap AO 0.25; AO>0.9 covers 68.4% of a 256² grid; per-key tone standard deviation is 0.022–0.024. In the seed-7 512² maps, gaps with r<20 cover 32.9%, key faces with r≥30 cover 66.9% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.465 (steep key edges). No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. This paragraph does not claim browser gallery verification.

`qrcodelabel` adds a printed QR-style label, bringing the current catalog from 892 to 893 kinds (894 gallery choices including plain). One paper label fills a tile: 29×29 modules plus a four-module white quiet zone (37×37 in total); 7×7 finder patterns (dark rim, light ring, 3×3 dark core) with white separators at the top-left, top-right and bottom-left, alternating timing patterns along row and column 6, a 5×5 alignment pattern near the bottom right, and seed-dependent pseudo-random data modules. Dark ink sits on light paper with fine fibre grain. **This is not a decodable QR code**: there is no encoded message, format information, masking or error correction, only a QR-style appearance.

The structural concept follows the actually read [Wikipedia “QR code”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/QR_code): three finder patterns of superimposed concentric squares at the upper-left, upper-right and lower-left corners, and a smaller square near the fourth corner. The 29×29 modules, four-module quiet zone, 7×7/5×5 sizes, timing placement, ink and paper colors, roughness and the 0.05 m tile are authored choices; nothing is cross-checked against ISO/IEC 18004, and it does not claim to be any QR version or to scan.

A dedicated sampler fills a 37×37 `Uint8Array` module table (1,369 B) from the seed and a hash in the constructor. Sampling blends the four neighbouring modules bilinearly with smoothstep weights near module boundaries; the weights have zero slope at module centres, so edges are narrow but C1, and module indices wrap by the tile size so the label repeats periodically. A 128² paper grain and a 48² fibre field are the other caches (18,688 Float64 values / 149,504 B). Metallic is 0 and there is no mortar; the default is a 0.05 m nominal tile and 0.0006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement). Measured at module centres for seeds 0/1/0xffffffff: ink color is always 0.04 and paper color is 0.876–0.925; the data region (excluding finder/timing/alignment) is 46.9%/49.1%/50.4% dark, and 49.1% of data positions differ between seeds 0 and 1. In the seed-7 512² maps r<60 covers 28.3%, r>200 covers 66.8% and the maximum normal tilt² is about 0.0004. No new API or dependency; Worker/cache/texture ownership uses existing paths. The concept follows the actually read [Wikipedia “Perforated hardboard”](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pegboard): tempered hardboard (coated with a thin linseed-oil layer and baked) pre-drilled with evenly spaced holes; Peg-Board is Masonite's expired brand name often used generically. A dedicated sampler uses the distance `r` to each cell centre for smoothstep holes and rounded rims; both go to zero inside the cell, so the `fract()` cell wrap does not affect continuity or C1. Outside holes the value is `(base + sheen + grain + fleck − rim)`; inside holes it is near black with low height, AO about 0.15 and roughness ≥ 0.92. `turingpattern` adds Turing-style labyrinth/spot coat-pattern schematics, bringing the current catalog from 887 to 888 kinds (889 gallery choices including plain). Three integer wave vectors (13, 12.5 and 13.0 cycles per tile) are summed as cosines into a near-hexagonal spot lattice, a periodic noise warp bends the coordinates, and a slowly varying threshold moves between small round spots (high threshold) and labyrinth networks (low threshold). Soft-edged patches are dark brown on a pale camel ground, with slightly darker, slightly raised centers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an analytic three-wave approximation, not a reaction–diffusion simulation, and it does not try to reproduce the markings of any particular animal; every parameter and color is authored, and no external artwork is cited or shipped. Each sampled point costs three cosines and four periodic-noise reads, with no loops or allocations.

`ammonitestone` adds ammonite-fossil limestone schematics, bringing the current catalog from 891 to 892 kinds (893 gallery choices including plain). Each of the 2×2 cells holds one disc-shaped ammonite with its own jittered position, scale and starting phase. The shell is a logarithmic spiral: the fractional part of whorl = ln(ρ/r₀)/ln(g) − θ/2π is the whorl cross-section coordinate, with integer values forming the recessed, AO-dark sutures and the middle a rounded tube with a central keel; 18 ribs per whorl twist falcoidally and fade in from the inner whorls to avoid aliasing. The matrix is gray-brown limestone (slow mottling plus fine grain); the shell is cream and smoother (roughness 0.55 against 0.88). The growth ratio g is 2.3, the outer shell radius is 0.4 of a cell, giving about 3.1 whorls. Metallic and mortar are 0.

Within a stripe, blade strands come from two layers of value noise stretched along v (192×48 and 384×96) sampled through the integer shear x = u + lean·v (lean = 1, +1 on even stripes, −1 on odd), so the blades lean opposite ways in adjacent stripes while both axes stay periodic. Slow clump tone, strand-valley AO and slight roughness variation are added. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: individual blade geometry, dead grass, bare soil and weeds are not modeled; the lean is fixed at 45° (a limit of the integer shear), not a measurement of real grass; no external artwork is cited or shipped. Defaults are a 2.0 m nominal tile, 0.0028 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger to resolve the strands; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`atomicboomerang` adds atomic-age boomerang laminate schematics, bringing the current catalog from 896 to 897 kinds (898 gallery choices including plain). Each of the 5×5 cells carries one print: about 62% are V-shaped boomerangs (arms y = k|x| with k = 0.4 and width tapering to the tips as 1−t³), and about 70% of the remaining cells hold a four-point astroid star (|x|^0.55 + |y|^0.55 ≤ r^0.55). Every print has a random position, scale (80–100%) and angle, and is either pale cream or deep teal. The ground is pale gray-teal with fine dark speckle (a 160×160 noise threshold); prints are slightly raised and glossier. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored retro-pattern schematic, not a copy of any laminate brand's or model's design; no external artwork is cited or shipped. The print's center offset plus its half length stay below half a cell, so every print lies entirely inside its own cell and a point only needs its own cell. Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.0008 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger to resolve the star and boomerang tips; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`celticplait` adds carved Celtic two-ribbon plait schematics, bringing the current catalog from 897 to 898 kinds (899 gallery choices including plain). Four horizontal carved bands each consist of two interlacing ribbons (y = ±A·sin(2π·4u), A = 0.052, ribbon half-width 0.029), giving 8 crossings per tile; at every crossing the ribbon that is rising passes over the falling one, so each ribbon alternates over and under along its length. Ribbons have a round cross-section height, a thin center groove and a contact shadow (AO only) on whatever lies beneath; two thin rails separate the bands, and the recessed stone ground carries fine grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored, simplified two-strand plait: the three-or-more-strand structures, corners and zoomorphic forms of Celtic knotwork are not modeled; no external artwork is cited or shipped. The perpendicular distance to each ribbon is approximated by the vertical offset divided by √(1+slope²), an approximation rather than an exact offset curve. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.0042 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 or larger to resolve the center groove; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`garnetschist` adds garnet mica-schist schematics, bringing the current catalog from 898 to 899 kinds (900 gallery choices including plain). The base is wavy foliation stretched along u: periodic noise wobbles v, two value-noise layers (3×28 and 6×112 cells) add coarse and fine layering, and sparse mica flecks come from a 224² noise threshold. About 60% of the 5×5 cells hold one garnet porphyroblast with a hexagonal outline (distance is the largest of three face-normal projections, apothem 0.1–0.19 of a cell), six pyramid faces with their own tones, a brighter crown at the center, raised, smoother and lower in AO, flanked by a pale quartz pressure shadow stretched along the foliation (major axis 2 radii, minor axis 0.7 radii). The dark ramp endpoint is dark red-brown, so garnets read dark red-brown and the schist pinkish brown. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the garnet is a 2D hexagon with six facets, not a true dodecahedral or trapezohedral crystal habit; the foliation does not actually bend around the porphyroblasts, and the directional glint of mica is not modeled. One scalar ramp only approximates red and is not spectral or mineralogical measurement. No external artwork is cited or shipped. Each garnet's circumscribed circle and pressure shadow plus position jitter stay below half a cell, so a point only queries its own cell. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0035 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `topographiccontours` adds topographic contour-map schematics, bringing the current catalog from 899 to 900 kinds (901 gallery choices including plain). Three periodic value-noise layers (3², 6² and 12² cells, weights 0.5/0.3/0.2) form a smooth elevation field f, divided into 16 contour intervals per tile on pale beige paper with hypsometric tinting (each interval changes the base tone by 0.42/16). Contours use |f − nearest level| ÷ |∇f| (the gradient from forward differences) as spatial distance, so line width does not vary with slope; every 5th line is a thicker, darker index contour. Subtle paper-fiber noise is added. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: it is not real terrain data and has no elevation labels, rivers, coordinate grid or legend; the gradient has a floor so flat areas do not blow up the line width, and very close contours (steep slopes) merge because of their line width. Defaults are a 1.0 m nominal tile, 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies.
