This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`digitalcamo` adds digital pixel-camouflage schematics, bringing the current catalog from 900 to 901 kinds (902 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 64×64 square pixels, each with one of four tones (dark olive, olive brown, khaki, sand). The tone comes from two layers of periodic value noise (4² and 12²) plus a per-block hash jitter, and about half of the pixels borrow the value of their 2×2 parent block (32²), clustering the pixels into larger squares. The quartiles of all pixel values are the thresholds, so each tone covers exactly a quarter of the pixels. A 128×128-thread-per-tile plain-weave canvas lies over the print (tone ±0.03, with height and AO variation). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a copy of any military or commercial camouflage pattern, and it makes no claim about visible or near-infrared concealment; no external artwork is cited or shipped. Defaults are a 1.0 m nominal tile, 0.0007 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Building a sampler sorts 4096 pixel values (millisecond scale); prefer 512 or larger so each pixel spans at least 8 px and the weave shows, 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`radarscope` adds radar-scope display schematics, bringing the current catalog from 901 to 902 kinds (903 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one circular scope (radius 0.46 UV) on a dark green-black ground: 5 evenly spaced range rings (the outer one heavier), 24 bearing spokes every 15° (every 6th a heavier crosshair), one bright sweep arm at a seed-chosen angle, a 1.3 rad phosphor afterglow behind it that fades quadratically, and 6 blips at random polar positions (brighter the closer they are behind the arm, keeping at least 40% brightness). 192 horizontal scanlines modulate brightness, with slight noise. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored UI-style schematic: it is not the screen of any radar model and has no text, scale numbers or real range/bearing meaning; the sweep arm is fixed in the tile and does not move over time. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `hazardstripes` adds worn hazard-warning-stripe schematics, bringing the current catalog from 902 to 903 kinds (904 gallery choices including plain). Yellow-and-black stripes run at 45° (the integer shear a = u + v, 8 stripes per tile, i.e. 4 yellow and 4 black) over steel; the paint chips away according to three wear terms: 96² noise chips, scratches stretched along the stripes (192×10-cell noise in the integer-shear coordinates a = u + v and b = u − v) and an edge weight favoring stripe borders (+0.35 within 0.3 of a stripe width of a border). Where the paint is gone, bare steel shows through as the neutral gray (153,153,139) of the existing mortar mix, while the metallic M mask and the mortar weight are the same wear value (M1 = bare steel, M0 = paint). Paint keeps pure yellow / pure black base tones; roughness is 0.45 yellow, 0.62 black and 0.36 steel; paint stands 0.14 above the steel and chipped edges have slightly darker AO.

This is an authored schematic: it is not the color or stripe proportion mandated by any standard (for example OSHA or ISO 3864) and has no rust, welds, rivets or dents; bare steel is only approximated by the existing neutral gray, not an alloy or optical measurement. No external artwork is cited or shipped. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.0032 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 1; explicit `createMaterial({ metallic: 0 })` changes only the scalar factor, not the stored M mask. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `kiwislices` adds kiwi-fruit slice schematics, bringing the current catalog from 903 to 904 kinds (905 gallery choices including plain). Each of the 2×2 cells holds one round slice (radius 0.42 of a cell, with jittered position, 92–100% scale and starting angle): green flesh with 64 pale radial fibers (darker away from the core), a pale yellow-green core disc (radius 0.115 of a cell), two rings of dark oval seeds outside the core (20 on the inner ring at 0.175 of a cell, 28 on the outer ring at 0.24, offset by half a pitch), and a dark-brown skin ring with fine fuzz noise (width 0.045 of a cell); dark gaps separate the fruit. This is an authored simplified schematic, not a mandala pattern of any religion, tradition or culture; no external artwork is cited or shipped. `needlepoint` adds needlepoint-tapestry schematics, bringing the current catalog from 905 to 906 kinds (907 gallery choices including plain). Color comes from a 12×12-stitch motif repeated 4×4 per tile: concentric diamond rings (ring width 2 stitches, a three-tone cycle) with a bright cross accent through the motif center, and every stitch has ±0.03 tone jitter. The motif is mirror-symmetric in both x and y. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`dicefaces` adds dice-face schematics, bringing the current catalog from 906 to 907 kinds (908 gallery choices including plain). A 4×4 field of rounded-square ivory faces (half edge 0.43 of a cell, corner radius 0.11, with a domed bevel at the face edge and dark gaps between faces), each hash-chosen to carry 1–6 recessed pips. The pips sit on a 3×3 lattice (spacing 0.255 of a cell, radius 0.078) in the standard point-symmetric layouts: 1 = center; 2 = diagonal; 3 = diagonal plus center; 4 = corners; 5 = corners plus center; 6 = two rows of three; each face is also randomly turned by 90° and mirrored so the 2, 3 and 6 layouts vary in direction. Pips are hemispherical recesses (depth 0.35, darker AO); faces are glossy (roughness 0.3) and gaps rough (0.9). Metallic and mortar are 0.

`cinderblockwall` adds a concrete-masonry-unit wall, bringing the current catalog from 907 to 908 kinds (909 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 8 courses × 4 blocks in a half-block running bond (odd courses shifted right), blocks at a 2:1 aspect; recessed mortar joints 0.0095 tile wide use the existing `mortar` channel with the neutral grout color. Block faces carry a ±0.08 per-block tone shift, a low-frequency cloudy mottle, 160×160 aggregate grain relief, chamfered edges and about 940 small air voids per tile (one per 56×56 cell with probability 0.3, radius 0.0025–0.0059 tile) that are recessed and darker in color and AO. Metallic is 0.

This is an authored optical schematic, not a physical moire simulation: there is no observer view, camera sampling or screen sub-pixels; the fringes are the mathematical product of the two gratings. Because the wave vectors are integers, both gratings and their difference and sum are continuous across the tile boundary. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0014 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. `azulejotiles` adds Portuguese-style painted ceramic tiles, bringing the current catalog from 909 to 910 kinds (911 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a 4×4 grid of identical glazed square tiles separated by recessed grout lines 0.012 tile wide (using the existing `mortar` channel with the neutral grout color); each tile carries a cobalt-on-white glaze design with full square symmetry: a four-lobed central rosette (radius 0.15 of a tile, lobe amplitude 0.055), a thin ring at radius 0.3, and quarter-disc corner motifs that join into full circles where four tiles meet (with a white thin ring inside). The blue has brush-stroke tone variation, the glaze carries faint craquelure lines on a 28×28 cell scale per tile, tile edges are bevelled, the glaze is smooth (roughness 0.2) and the grout rough. Metallic is 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a measurement of a particular historical design or origin (such as Delft or Talavera); there is no hand-painted variation between tiles — every tile is identical, and because the design has full square symmetry, turning a tile would make no visible difference in this material. `tumblingblocks` adds a tumbling-blocks (isometric cube) patchwork, bringing the current catalog from 910 to 911 kinds (912 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a hexagonal lattice of 7 columns × 8 rows; every pointy-top hexagon (circumradius 1) is split by three rays from its center to the upper-right, upper-left and bottom vertices into a top face (light, tone 0.92), a right face (mid, 0.62) and a left face (dark, 0.3), giving the isometric-cube illusion. Each face also gets ±0.06 per-block tone jitter, fine woven-fabric grain, and thin seams between faces (dark, slightly recessed, darker AO). The lattice is aligned with a hexagon center at u = v = 0; because the UV tile is square and the lattice is 7√3 wide by 12 tall (about 1.01), the hexagons are stretched about 1% non-uniformly. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored patchwork schematic, not a measurement of a particular quilt design: there is no stitching, batting or fabric wrinkling, and the cubes' 3D appearance is baked tone (the light and dark faces do not respond to light direction). Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.0018 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `kilimflatweave` adds a kilim flatweave rug, bringing the current catalog from 911 to 912 kinds (913 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 48×48 weave cells arranged top to bottom in four 12-row bands: stepped diamonds (12-cell period, mirror-symmetric in both axes, stepped concentric colors), a stepped zigzag (6-cell period, each row half in each of two colors), horizontal stripes (a 12-row palindrome: dark, dark, red, red, ochre, white, white, ochre, red, red, dark, dark) and crosses (44 of the 144 cells in each 12×12 motif carry the cross color). Colors are four tone steps (indigo, madder red, saffron, undyed-wool white) with ±0.025 per-cell dye jitter, horizontal weft-faced ribs (3 per cell) and a low-amplitude fibre mottle; where the color changes between neighboring cells the cell's left edge carries a 0.14-cell-wide slit (dark, recessed, darker AO), imitating the vertical slits of a flatweave at color boundaries. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored simplified schematic, not a measurement of a particular tribe or region's kilim, and no traditional provenance is claimed; warp/weft interlacing detail, fringes and wear are not modeled. `ean13barcodes` adds EAN-13 barcode labels, bringing the current catalog from 912 to 913 kinds (914 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 4 labels stacked vertically, each filling the tile width (9 modules of quiet zone on each side plus 95 modules of bars, 113 modules in all), encoded per the EAN-13 specification: start guard 101, six left digits (L or G codes chosen by the first digit's parity pattern), center guard 01010, six right digits (R codes), end guard 101, and a correct thirteenth check digit. The twelve data digits derive from the seed and row (so rows differ); they are not registered product numbers and no human-readable digits are drawn. Guard bars run slightly lower than digit bars, bar edges are softened, the ink has low-amplitude density variation and the paper faint fibers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the symbols are generated from the published EAN-13 encoding tables so that structural "scanning" is valid, but print quality (such as ISO 15416 grades), bar-width gain compensation, human-readable text and the leading digit are not modeled; the tests verify structure and check digits only and no physical scanner or decoder library was used. Marks are round-ended capsules one unit thick; each line has a faint center guide, the ink has low-amplitude density variation and the paper faint fibers. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`sandripples` adds wind-formed sand ripples, bringing the current catalog from 914 to 915 kinds (916 gallery choices including plain). The windward side is lighter, the lee side darker with extra AO; there is also 384×384 grain relief and bright mica/mineral specks in about 5% of cells. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`lissajousgrid` adds a Lissajous-figure table, bringing the current catalog from 930 to 931 kinds (932 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds a 4×4 oscilloscope-style table of Lissajous curves: cell (column, row) draws the parametric curve x = A·sin(a·t + π/2), y = A·sin(b·t) with frequencies a = column + 1 and b = row + 1 (A = 0.4 cell, t from 0 to 2π, approximated by a 160-segment polyline), so the 16 ratios run from the 1:1 circle to 4:4; when a and b share a factor the curve retraces itself, and cases such as a = 2b degenerate into a parabola arc. Lines are bright green (half width 0.014 cell) with a soft glow on a deep-green panel, a faint cell frame and center cross graticule, and faint grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`ramennoodles` adds ramen noodles, bringing the current catalog from 934 to 935 kinds (936 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 22 wavy noodle strands running along u, layered from top to bottom with later strands lying over earlier ones: the center line of strand i is y = (i + 0.5)/22 + 0.085·sin(2π(k·u + phase)), with k cycling through 3, 4, 5 and the phase taken from the golden ratio (the fractional part of i × 0.618…), so the strand shapes are the same for every seed and only tone and grain change with the seed; strands have a half width of 0.026 and a round tube profile (bright along the center line, darker toward the edges with lower height and ambient occlusion), ±0.06 per-strand tone variation, and about 7% of the area shows dark broth between strands. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there are no curled noodles, breaks, oil slicks, toppings or broth reflections; because every strand is a wave with a fixed stacking order, the pile looks fairly regular. Distance to a strand uses a first-order approximation (vertical offset over √(1 + slope²)), so strand width is slightly off where the slope is steep at the crests. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.01 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `connectfourboard` adds a Connect Four board, bringing the current catalog from 935 to 936 kinds (937 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one 7-column × 6-row board with one extra row of base tray below: a blue panel with round holes, each hole dark (empty) or holding the first player's disc (mid tone) or the second player's disc (near-white), with an inner ring and a slightly raised rim. The position comes from simulating a legal game from the seed: the two players alternate dropping discs into random columns (the first player starts), discs stack from the bottom by gravity, and a drop that would complete four in a row is rerolled into another column; there are 18–30 moves. So every column's discs are unbroken from the bottom, the first player has either as many discs as the second or exactly one more, and nobody has completed four in a row. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there is no real red and yellow (colors are brightness interpolated linearly between the dark and light ends, so the first player is a mid blue-gray and the second near-white); the position is a random legal one, not a played strategy, and nothing guarantees that both sides would "sensibly" have played it. `pegsolitaire` adds peg solitaire, bringing the current catalog from 937 to 938 kinds (939 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds one 7×7 English cross board: the four 2×2 corners are solid wood with no holes, the other 33 cells are holes holding either nothing (dark) or a light round-headed wooden peg (with a highlight and a small dome). The position comes from the seed by starting at the solved end state (one peg in the center) and playing 8 random moves backwards (each reverse jump turns "peg, empty, empty" in a line into "empty, peg, peg"), so the picture — 9 pegs, or fewer if the attempt budget runs out — can always be solved to a single peg by playing the jumps forward. The board has wood grain stretched along u. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`xylophonebars` adds xylophone bars, bringing the current catalog from 938 to 939 kinds (940 gallery choices including plain). Each tile holds 12 wooden bars side by side (the twelve semitones of an octave), all centered on the middle line of the tile; the first is the longest (0.9 tile) and each following bar is 2^(−1/24) ≈ 0.9715 of the previous one — a tuned bar's frequency goes as 1/length², so one equal-tempered semitone (frequency ratio 2^(1/12)) shortens it by 2^(−1/24), and twelve semitones (an octave) by 2^(−1/2). Each bar has a suspension hole 22.4% in from each end (the node positions of the first free–free bending mode), and the holes of neighboring bars are joined by a thin line (the cord); the wood grain runs along the bar and the bar tone lightens slightly from long to short on a dark felt background. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the length ratios and node positions are drawn — bar thickness, width and cross-section (real xylophone bars are often undercut to tune the overtones) are not modeled, nor are resonator tubes; the cord is a straight line between holes and snaps back at the tile seam (from the last bar to the next tile's first bar), a deliberate discontinuity. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0035 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `sliderulescale` adds slide-rule scales, bringing the current catalog from 939 to 940 kinds (941 gallery choices including plain). Each tile stacks 8 ivory logarithmic C scales, one decade spanning the whole tile width: the graduation x is drawn at u = log10(x), so 10 coincides with the 1 of the next tile and the tile repeats seamlessly. Graduations follow the usual rule — every 0.02 in [1, 2), every 0.05 in [2, 4), every 0.1 in [4, 10) — for 150 ticks at three lengths: integers (9, longest), tenths in [1, 4) and halves in [4, 10) (33 medium) and the remaining 108 shortest; each integer tick has a 3×5 dot-matrix digit 1 to 9 to its right. `spirographrosettes` adds spirograph rosettes, bringing the current catalog from 940 to 941 kinds (942 gallery choices including plain). Each tile draws one hypotrochoid per quadrant (the curve traced by a pen at some distance from the center of a small gear rolling inside a large ring) with ring/gear radius ratios 5/3, 8/3, 7/2 and 9/4, giving 5, 8, 7 and 9 lobes (for coprime R and r the lobe count equals R); the curve closes after t has run through 2π·r/gcd(R, r). The pen distance varies with the seed and quadrant between 0.37 and 0.73 gear radii and each figure is rotated by the seed; the pen always reaches exactly the outer circle (radius 0.215 tile), so all lobe tips lie on one circle. The four quadrants use slightly different ink brightness and the paper has a fine grain. Metallic and mortar are 0.

Implementation: when the sampler is created the curves are stamped (about 108 thousand points) into a 640×640 Float32 ink-coverage mask (about 1.6 MB, one per sampler) and every sample is just a bilinear lookup; the mask resolution is fixed at 640, so above 640 px the lines are magnified by the bilinear filter and get slightly softer rather than sharper.

This is an authored schematic: only four fixed ring/gear ratios are drawn (not arbitrary R, r), the curve is a polyline of uniformly spaced t samples (9000 points per loop, not an exact distance field); colors are brightness interpolation (near-black ink on cream paper) and do not represent pen hues. Defaults are a 0.3 m nominal tile, 0.0012 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 512 to 1024; 32 is a coarse preview. `juliacells` adds Julia-set cells, bringing the current catalog from 941 to 942 kinds (943 gallery choices including plain). Each tile draws one filled Julia set z → z² + c per quadrant with a real c (about −0.4, −0.75, −1.0 and −1.25, each jittered by up to ±0.04 by the seed; for real c in [−2, 1/4] the set is connected and the picture is mirror symmetric in both axes). Each cell's view radius is 2, equal to the escape radius, so points on a cell border escape immediately and there is no seam between cells or at the tile repeat. The interior (points still bounded after 96 iterations) is near black; outside, the smooth escape count μ = n + 1 − log₂(ln|z| / ln 2) drives a glow 1 − exp(−μ/9) from dark to bright, and height and roughness follow the same glow. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only four real-parameter Julia sets — no Mandelbrot set and no complex c (a complex c is not mirror symmetric and would leave a seam at the tile border); the iteration cap is 96, so slowly escaping points near the boundary are drawn as interior; colors are brightness interpolation (near-black navy to warm cream) and do not represent any particular palette. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0035 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. The pattern table was typed from memory and decoded back independently in the tests using the structural rule described on Wikipedia's Code 39 page (two wide bars encode a number 1–10 with the weights 1, 2, 4, 7, 0; the one wide space out of four picks one of the groups U–Z plus symbols / digits / A–J / K–T), confirming that the patterns of all 38 data characters and of the `*` delimiter follow that rule; they were not checked against a real barcode scanner or the full text of ISO/IEC 16388, and the codes were never actually scanned.

Because the wave vectors are integers the whole pattern is exactly periodic over the tile and repeats seamlessly. Metallic and mortar are 0.

Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.0016 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `bluenoisemask` adds a blue-noise mask, bringing the current catalog from 962 to 963 kinds (964 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 64×64 blue-noise dither mask built with the void-and-cluster algorithm (Ulichney): on a torus (edges wrapping) a Gaussian energy (σ = 1.5) finds the "tightest cluster" and the "largest void"; about 10% random initial points are relaxed to a stable pattern, then all 4096 texels are ranked 0 to 4095 with every rank used exactly once; brightness = rank ÷ 4095, so the brightness histogram is exactly flat and low-frequency energy is strongly suppressed. The mask is computed on a torus and repeats seamlessly; height rises with brightness and roughness rises slightly. Metallic and mortar are 0.

One-off local measurement (seed 0, discrete Fourier power of the 64×64 mask divided by the power expected for white noise): about 0.000 for frequencies of radius 1 to 5, about 0.003 for radius 8 to 12 and about 1.61 for radius 24 to 31 (near Nyquist); a random permutation of the same variance (white noise) gives about 1.21, 1.14 and 0.96. Creating a sampler takes about 66 ms (one-off, not a benchmark).

This is an authored product with limits: the mask size is fixed at 64×64 texels (larger would make the algorithm too slow) and it is sampled nearest-neighbour, so on a 512 px image each texel is an 8×8 px block (for texel-exact blue noise set the size to 64 or sample it with repeat in a shader); the seed only chooses the initial random points — different seeds give different masks of similar spectral quality; colors are brightness with no hue meaning. Defaults are a 0.2 m nominal tile, 0.002 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. No three-backend or cross-browser verification is claimed.

This is an authored schematic: only four rules, a fixed width of 31 cells and 31 rows; the ring boundary makes the pattern wrap around the left and right edges (it does not continue into the neighboring panels); the first row contains random points, so it is not the classic single-seed triangle (set seedDensity to 0 for a single seed); "an odd ring does not die out" was observed on the seeds tested here and has no mathematical proof; colors are brightness (near-black ink, light-grey grid, cream paper). The 6 peg colors are six brightnesses (0.34 to 0.9, 0.12 apart), the holes are dark brown and the board is wood brown with a grain stretched vertically; a line separates the code row from the guesses. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the guesses are random, not reasoned from earlier feedback (so later guesses need not agree with earlier feedback, and no row is guaranteed to be a complete hit); there is no cover hiding the code; colors are only brightness and the six peg colors are hard to tell apart at small sizes; the feedback pegs' conventional "black/white" for exact/partial is shown here as bright/dark. Each tile is split into 2×2 circles: each circle has 96 evenly spaced points numbered 0 to 95, and point i is joined by a straight line to point (k·i mod 96), where k is the circle's multiplier (2, 3, 4 and 5 in the four circles, shuffled between quadrants by the seed, with each circle turned by a small angle of less than one point spacing). The envelope of these lines is a cardioid for k = 2 and a nephroid for k = 3, with more lobes for larger k. Lines add up and are compressed into brightness (1−e^{−1.6·sum}), so one line is about 0.8 bright and overlaps saturate, with a thin dark ring on the circumference on a deep blue-black background. Metallic and mortar are 0.

The sampler measures the distance to up to about 95 chords of the pixel's own circle for every pixel, about 223 ms for one 512×512 build, which is slower than most materials and not optimised. `chinesecheckersboard` adds a Chinese checkers board, bringing the current catalog from 1008 to 1009 kinds (1010 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a wooden Chinese checkers star board: a round board plate on a light tabletop, carrying a six-pointed star of 121 round holes — a central hexagon of radius 4 (61 holes) and a 10-hole triangle on each of the six points. The holes are dark recesses holding marbles of six brightness levels (dark to light: about 0.30, 0.42, 0.55, 0.69, 0.83, 0.96); each point starts with ten marbles of one level, and then the seed moves 14 marbles, each to a random empty hole, so every level still has exactly 10 marbles and there are 60 in total. Holes map to a honeycomb lattice through cube coordinates (q, r, s=−q−r): the star is the union of two opposite triangles, "all three coordinates ≥ −4" and "all three ≤ 4". Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the six marble kinds differ by brightness only, with no hue (the real game has six colours), and neighbouring levels (about 0.12 to 0.14 apart) are hard to tell apart at small sizes or under different lighting; the moves are random swaps and do not represent legal jump moves (the jumping rules are not checked); each player's goal corner is not marked; the wood grain is only low-amplitude noise. Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`colormapregions` adds a map-colouring pattern, bringing the current catalog from 1009 to 1010 kinds (1011 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a seamlessly tiling "map": 6×6 randomly jittered points seed a periodic Voronoi partition (36 regions, with thin darker border lines), and every region gets one brightness such that **no two neighbouring regions (including neighbours that meet across the tile edge, onto the next tile) share a brightness**. The colouring uses backtracking: four brightnesses are tried first and, failing that (node limit 30000), five (0.30, 0.44, 0.58, 0.72, 0.86); over 100 seeds I measured 66 using only four, 34 needing five, and none failing to colour. Neighbours are found by the sampler scanning a periodic 512×512 grid for owner changes (diagonals included). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: because the map lives on a torus (left meets right, top meets bottom) it is not covered by the planar four-colour theorem — four colours are not always enough, about a third of the seeds need five (measured above), and the name does not mean only four are used; neighbours are detected by scanning, so a border shorter than about 0.002 of the tile could in principle be missed (rescanning seeds 2 and 3 on a 1024 grid found none missing, but I did not prove this for all seeds); colour is brightness only. Building the sampler costs about 32 ms extra (mean over 100 seeds, measured in Bun, not a performance certification). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`draughtsposition` adds a draughts (checkers) board, bringing the current catalog from 1010 to 1011 kinds (1012 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is an 8×8 draughts board: a checkered board of light and dark brown squares on a light tabletop, with pieces only on the dark squares (those where row + column is odd). Each side has 6 to 12 pieces (random per seed), one side pale discs and the other charcoal discs; about a fifth of the pieces are kings, with a concentric ring of the opposite tone in the middle of the disc. Positions are chosen by the seed: the 32 dark squares are shuffled and the two sides take consecutive runs, so pieces never overlap or land on a light square. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not a legal game state: the positions are random and need not match any move history (a man may stand on the far rank without being crowned, and the two sides may be mixed together); it does not say whose turn it is; colour is brightness only (pale pieces contrast little with the light squares, and charcoal pieces have limited contrast with the dark squares); the wood grain is only low-amplitude noise. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`multiplicationtable` adds a times table, bringing the current catalog from 1011 to 1012 kinds (1013 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 9×9 multiplication table: the first row and column are the factors 1 to 9 on a dark background with reversed dot-matrix digits (the top-left corner is blank), and the other 81 cells hold the matching products (1 to 81, single digits centred, two digits side by side in 3×5 glyphs); the square numbers on the diagonal (1, 4, 9, …, 81) have a slightly darker background. The table sits on pale paper with thin grid lines. The content is fixed and does not change with the seed; the seed only affects the faint paper noise. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the factors stop at 9 (not the common 12×12 table); because the content is fixed, different seeds differ only by noise; the dot-matrix digits are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `moonphases` adds a moon-phase calendar, bringing the current catalog from 1012 to 1013 kinds (1014 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a calendar of 30 moons, 5 columns by 6 rows on a deep-blue night sky, standing for 30 consecutive days of the synodic month (29.53 days): new moon, first quarter, full moon, last quarter and back to a thin crescent. Each moon is a grey disc with the same 24 random craters (it is the same Moon), the lit part pale and the shadow dark grey; waxing moons (the first half of the cycle) are lit from the right and waning moons from the left, with an elliptical terminator, and the lit share of the disc is (1−cos 2πφ)/2 where φ is the phase within the cycle. The calendar starts at a seed-driven fraction of a day, so different seeds differ slightly in phase. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic, not an ephemeris: phase uses only the simple cosine formula (a fixed synodic month of 29.53 days), with no libration, earthshine or real lunar terrain; the view is northern-hemisphere (waxing lit on the right), and a southern-hemisphere observer sees the mirror image; 30 days cover a bit more than one 29.53-day cycle, so the first and last moons have close but not identical phases; colour is brightness only. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`treemaprects` adds a treemap, bringing the current catalog from 1013 to 1014 kinds (1015 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a treemap: a square area cut into 12 rectangles whose **areas are proportional to their values**, each value (an integer from 4 to 30, chosen by the seed) written in 3×5 dot-matrix digits in the rectangle's top-left corner; the larger the value, the lighter the fill (a linear map onto the dark-to-light ramp). The layout: the values are sorted in descending order and split into two groups of nearly equal total (each next value goes to the group with the smaller total so far), the current rectangle is cut across its longer side in the proportion of the two totals, and each half is handled recursively until one value is left; dark thick lines separate the rectangles. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: it is not the usual "squarified" treemap algorithm, only balanced binary recursion, so the rectangles' aspect ratios are not guaranteed to be near square (I did not measure the worst aspect ratio); the values are random and carry no real data; the labels are a fixed-size dot matrix and a very narrow rectangle could let a label spill over its edge (the tests only confirm that the labels of nine seeds read back correctly and do not check that a label fits entirely inside its rectangle, nor is it proven that it cannot overflow); colour is brightness only. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`analogclocks` adds analogue clocks, bringing the current catalog from 1014 to 1015 kinds (1016 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 4×4 wall of clocks: 16 round faces on a grey wall (pale face, dark rim, twelve tick marks), each showing a seed-chosen time (1 to 12 o'clock, whole minutes 0 to 59). The hands are set the way a real clock turns them: the minute hand 6° per minute; the hour hand 30° per hour plus 0.5° per minute, so the hour hand creeps with the minutes instead of sitting at the hour position. The hour hand is shorter and thicker (0.5 of the face radius), the minute hand longer and thinner (0.8), with a small hub at the centre. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there is no second hand, no numerals and no AM/PM distinction; there are only 12 ticks and no minute ticks; the hands are plain straight bars with no ornamental shapes; each face is random independently so the times on one wall are not related; colour is brightness only. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.005 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `piechartwedges` adds a pie chart, bringing the current catalog from 1015 to 1016 kinds (1017 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a pie chart: a circle cut into 8 wedges whose **central angle equals the wedge's percentage × 3.6°**, each percentage (at least 4%, all eight adding up to exactly 100%) written in 3×5 dot-matrix digits in the middle of the wedge. The seed decides the percentages: each wedge first gets a base of 4%, the remaining 68% is shared out by random weights, and the largest-remainder rule makes the total exactly 100. The first wedge starts at a seed-driven angle and the others follow clockwise; every wedge has its own brightness (by size rank, a linear map from dark to light, ties broken by position); wedges and the rim are separated by thin dark lines, and the digits are dark or light depending on the fill. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the percentages are random and carry no data meaning; the smallest wedge is 4% (about 14.4°) and the labels are a fixed-size dot matrix, so a small wedge's label may sit close to its edges; brightness is only the size rank, with no hue; there is no legend, title or axis. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`regressionscatter` adds a regression scatter plot, bringing the current catalog from 1016 to 1017 kinds (1018 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a scatter plot: on pale paper a square plot area (thin frame, a light 4×4 grid) holds up to 28 dark dots scattered round a line whose slope and intercept come from the seed (each point's noise is the sum of three uniform randoms, an approximation of a normal distribution), no two dots closer than 0.075 (in plot units); the **least-squares** regression line is then fitted to those dots (slope = Σ(x−x̄)(y−ȳ) / Σ(x−x̄)², intercept = ȳ − slope·x̄) and drawn across the whole plot as a thinner mid-grey line. Because the fit is computed from the dots actually drawn, the line always passes through their centroid. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: because the minimum-spacing rejection sampling has an attempt cap the point count can fall below 28 (I did not tally the actual counts per seed; the tests only require at least 15); there are no tick numerals, title or legend; no correlation coefficient or residuals are computed; the noise is approximately but not strictly normal; colour is brightness only (dark dots, a mid-grey line, light grid lines). Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`barchartbars` adds a bar chart, bringing the current catalog from 1017 to 1018 kinds (1019 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a bar chart: on pale paper a dark baseline with 10 bars side by side, each a **whole number of units** high (a unit is 0.075 of the tile height, values 1 to 9 chosen by the seed), with the value written above the top of each bar in centred 3×5 dot-matrix digits; there is a very faint horizontal rule at every whole height; each bar's fill follows its value linearly along the dark-to-light ramp (larger values lighter). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: there are no axis tick numerals, title or legend; all bars share one height unit; the values are random and carry no data meaning; bars reach at most 9 units (about 0.675 of the tile height); colour is brightness only. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `truthtablelogic` adds a truth table, bringing the current catalog from 1018 to 1019 kinds (1020 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is the truth table of a four-input Boolean function: a dark header row reads A, B, C, D (inputs) and X (output) in 3×5 dot-matrix letters (the X header is slightly lighter), and below it 16 rows count ABCD in binary (0000 to 1111, A the most significant bit) with the output X in the last column; cells where X is 1 have a darker background so they stand out. The seed picks the output from eight functions: (A∧B)∨(C⊕D), (A⊕B)∧(C∨D), A?B:C (a multiplexer, independent of D), ¬(A∨B)∨(C∧D), (A∨C)∧(B∨D), majority(A,B,C)⊕D, (A∧¬B)∨(C∧¬D), and 4-bit parity (A⊕B⊕C⊕D). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only those eight fixed functions occur (not arbitrary truth tables); darkening the cells where the output is 1 is decoration; no simplified Boolean expression or logic-gate symbol is drawn; the dot-matrix digits and letters are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`fouriersquarewaves` adds Fourier square waves, bringing the current catalog from 1019 to 1020 kinds (1021 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is six horizontal panels stacked: panel n draws the partial sum of the first n odd harmonics of the square wave's Fourier series, (4/π)·Σ sin(kt)/k (k = 1, 3, …, 2n−1). Panel 1 is a plain sine (amplitude 4/π); each added harmonic flattens the plateaus further but puts more ripple on them and steepens the transitions, while the overshoot of about 9% of the jump on either side of an edge (the Gibbs phenomenon) does not go away and tends to about 1.179 times the square wave's level. Each panel has a faint axis and two reference rules at the ideal square wave's levels, the waveform is a dark curve (its width is corrected for slope so steep stretches do not thin out), and each tile spans 2 periods horizontally. The content is fixed; the seed only affects faint paper noise. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only 1 to 6 harmonics are drawn, none higher; the curve is computed from the analytic formula per pixel, not plotted from points; the vertical scale is fixed with no axis labels; the "about 9% overshoot" is the theoretical Gibbs value, and the tests only verify that the measured maximum lies between 1.1 and 1.2 rather than equalling it exactly. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`pascaltrianglenumbers` adds Pascal triangle numbers, bringing the current catalog from 1020 to 1021 kinds (1022 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is the first 10 rows of Pascal's triangle (rows 0 to 9, the largest entry being 126) in 3×5 dot-matrix digits laid out as a centred triangle; each entry is the sum of the upper-left and upper-right entries of the row above, and odd entries sit on a darker disc while even entries are bare paper, so the odd discs trace out the Sierpinski triangle pattern. The content is fixed and the seed only affects faint paper noise. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the first 10 rows are drawn; the odd/even discs and the digits are deterministic; no binomial expansion or row sums are labelled; the dot-matrix digits are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `convexhullpoints` adds a convex hull, bringing the current catalog from 1021 to 1022 kinds (1023 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a scatter of points (up to 16, at least 0.12 UV apart and at least 0.07 UV from the tile edge so the tile repeats seamlessly) with their convex hull: hull vertices are marked with larger dark dots, inner points with smaller dots, and the hull polygon is filled light grey with a thin outline. The hull of the seed's point set is computed with Andrew's monotone chain. To keep the hull unambiguous the sampler picks a point set in which no vertex is nearly collinear with its two neighbours and no inner point hugs an edge (up to 48 candidate sets are tried; if none qualifies the last is used). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: at most 16 points (the minimum spacing means some seeds place fewer); only the hull is shown, not the algorithm's steps; "unambiguous" is a threshold I chose (a vertex at least 0.012 UV from the line through its neighbours, an inner point at least 0.02 UV from any edge), not a mathematical requirement; if all 48 candidates fail the last is used anyway (this caused no test failure across the 600 seeds I tried, but I did not count how often all 48 are used up). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`delaunaytriangles` adds a Delaunay triangulation, bringing the current catalog from 1022 to 1023 kinds (1024 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a scatter of points (up to 18, at least 0.1 UV apart and at least 0.06 UV from the tile edge so the tile repeats seamlessly) joined into their Delaunay triangulation: each triangle is filled with a slightly varied light grey, the edges are thin lines and the vertices small dark dots. The triangulation is found by brute force: a triple of points is a Delaunay triangle when no other point lies strictly inside its circumcircle (a few hundred triples times the remaining points, computed once when the sampler is created). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the resulting triangulation is drawn, without circumcircles or the algorithm's steps; at most 18 points (the minimum spacing means some seeds place fewer); the positions are seed-driven pseudo-random and near-ties (four nearly cocircular points) are not specially handled, so whether such a triple counts as Delaunay depends on floating-point error and overlapping triangles can in principle appear, which I did not guard against; each pixel scans about 30 triangles and 47 edges, so it costs more per pixel than most materials (about 0.4 s for a single 512×512 render under Bun). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`collatzsequences` adds Collatz sequences, bringing the current catalog from 1023 to 1024 kinds (1025 gallery choices including plain). Each tile has 10 rows, each the Collatz (hailstone) sequence of a start value: halve an even number, otherwise triple it and add one, until 1 is reached. Every number takes one cell (up to 13 cells), written in 3×5 dot-matrix digits; cells holding odd numbers have a darker background so the "triple and add one" rises are visible, and the rest of the row after the sequence ends is left blank. The seed shuffles the 21 start values from 2 to 60 whose sequences have at most 13 terms and takes 10 of them (all different), for example 3, 13, 21, 53 or 40. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only start values with sequences of at most 13 terms appear (no long trajectories such as 27's), so it says nothing about the Collatz conjecture itself; numbers have at most three digits (53's sequence contains 160); the dot-matrix digits are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `hammingcodewords` adds Hamming code words, bringing the current catalog from 1024 to 1025 kinds (1026 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a Hamming(7,4) code word table: the header reads positions 1 to 7 and S (the syndrome), and below it 16 rows hold the 7-bit code word for the data nibbles 0000 to 1111 (row number r) with positions 1 to 7 being p1 p2 d1 p3 d2 d3 d4 (the parity bits at positions 1, 2 and 4 on a slightly darker background). The seed decides for each row whether one bit is flipped (about one row in eight is left alone), and the flipped cell has the darkest background; the rightmost column S is the syndrome (the XOR of the positions holding a 1 in the received word), which equals the flipped position exactly, with 0 meaning no error. So flipping back the bit that S points to gives the original code word, whose data bits are the row number. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the Hamming(7,4) code, with the 16 rows fixed to data 0 to 15, and at most one flipped bit per row (a Hamming code cannot correct two-bit errors, so none are drawn); the flipped positions are seed-driven pseudo-random; the dot-matrix digits are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`cayleytables` adds Cayley tables, bringing the current catalog from 1025 to 1026 kinds (1027 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is the Cayley (multiplication) table of a group of order 8: a 9×9 grid whose top row and left column are dark headers listing the elements 0 to 7, and in the remaining 8×8 body the cell in row a, column b is the product of a and b; cells holding 0 (the identity) have a darker background, tracing the Latin-square pattern of the identity. The seed picks one of the five groups of order 8: the cyclic group Z8, Z4×Z2, Z2×Z2×Z2, the dihedral group D4 and the quaternion group Q8, and shuffles the labels of elements 1 to 7 (0 stays the identity). Every table therefore satisfies the group axioms: an identity, every row and column a permutation, and associativity; the table's shape shows whether the group is commutative and the order of each element. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only those five groups of order 8, with no other orders and no group names shown; the shuffled labels hide any regular pattern; the dot-matrix digits are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`romannumerals` adds Roman numerals, bringing the current catalog from 1026 to 1027 kinds (1028 gallery choices including plain). Each tile has 14 rows: on the left a decimal number (1 to 199, right-aligned in three cells), then an equals sign and its Roman numeral (in 3×5 dot-matrix letters I, V, X, L and C, in the standard subtractive form, e.g. 4 as IV, 9 as IX, 40 as XL, 90 as XC; flush left, at most nine letters, e.g. 188 as CLXXXVIII); odd rows have a slightly darker background. The seed picks the 14 numbers from 1 to 199, all different and in ascending order. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`signedencodings` adds signed integer encodings, bringing the current catalog from 1027 to 1028 kinds (1029 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a 4-bit lookup table: 16 rows list 0000 to 1111, and each row has the binary bits (the column of the most significant bit, the sign bit, has the darkest background), the unsigned value (0 to 15, header U) and the signed value (header: the encoding's code). The seed picks one of three signed encodings: two's complement (2C, where 1000 is −8 up to 1111 as −1), one's complement (1C, where 1000 is −7 and 1111 is "−0") and sign and magnitude (SM, where 1000 is "−0" and 1001 is −1 up to 1111 as −7); negative rows (including "−0") have a slightly darker background and a "−" sign written before the signed value. Metallic and mortar are 0.

`matrixproducts` adds matrix products, bringing the current catalog from 1028 to 1029 kinds (1030 gallery choices including plain). Each matrix has square brackets around it, the cells of the product C have a slightly darker background, and the times and equals signs sit on the middle row. `kochsnowflake` adds a Koch snowflake, bringing the current catalog from 1029 to 1030 kinds (1031 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is divided into four 2×2 panels showing the Koch snowflake after 0, 1, 2 and 3 iterations: 0 is an equilateral triangle, and each iteration replaces the middle third of every edge with an outward equilateral bump. The panels' order and each one's rotation are drawn by the seed, and each polygon (up to 192 segments) is filled by the even-odd rule and outlined with a thin dark line. The boundary length therefore grows by 4/3 per iteration and the area follows A₀·(8/5 − (3/5)(4/9)ⁿ) (A₀ at 0, tending to 1.6·A₀). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only 0 to 3 iterations are drawn, none higher, and it is not the true fractal limit; the side length of 0.36 UV (circumradius about 0.208 UV) is fixed and the panels do not overlap; each pixel scans up to 192 edges, about 0.3 s for one 512×512 render under Bun (from the preview script, measured once). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`newtonbasins` adds Newton basins, bringing the current catalog from 1030 to 1031 kinds (1032 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is the basin-of-attraction picture of Newton's method for z^n − 1 (the n-th roots of unity): a square window of the complex plane from −1.6 to 1.6 in both real and imaginary parts, where each point is painted with the brightness of the n-th root that the Newton iteration z ← z − (z^n − 1)/(n z^(n−1)) finally converges to (more roots mean more brightness levels), with slowly converging points slightly darker (by up to 10 steps). The seed picks n from 3, 4 and 5; the coordinates pass through a triangle-wave fold, so the pattern is continuous across the tile edge. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only the polynomials z^n − 1 with n from 3 to 5; brightness only tells which root and how fast, not hue (procedural materials only have a dark-to-light ramp); basin boundaries are fractal, so pixels near them are sensitive to floating-point error, each pixel iterates at most 40 times and a point that does not converge (near a boundary or a pole) is assigned by its final position; the triangle-wave fold mirrors the pattern left-right and top-bottom. Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`mandelbrotbands` adds Mandelbrot bands, bringing the current catalog from 1031 to 1032 kinds (1033 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a smooth escape-time contour picture of the Mandelbrot set: the seed picks one of four fixed windows — the whole set (centre −0.6, half-width 1.6, 80 iterations), the seahorse valley (−0.745 + 0.113i, half-width 0.06), a branch near the imaginary axis (−0.16 + 1.0405i, half-width 0.04) and the neighbourhood of the Feigenbaum point (−1.401155, half-width 0.02), the last three zoomed windows with 160 iterations each. The inside of the set (points that do not escape within the iteration limit) is dark; outside, each point's brightness comes from the smooth escape time ν = n + 1 − log₂(log|z| / log 256) (larger ν is brighter, with a cosine contour band of period 3 added), so rings of bands surround the set. The coordinates pass through a triangle-wave fold so the pattern is continuous across the tile edge. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only those four windows, with no interactive zoom; the inside is decided by the iteration limit, so pixels on the set's edge can differ slightly with the limit (in a temporary test over 120 extra seeds the best window's agreement was 1.0000 (the runner-up at most 0.265), at a 0.02 tolerance on an 80×80 grid, which does not mean every pixel agrees); brightness only encodes escape speed, not hue; the triangle-wave fold mirrors the pattern. Each pixel iterates at most 160 times, about 0.15 s for one 512×512 render under Bun (from the preview script, measured once). Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`cantorsetrows` adds Cantor set rows, bringing the current catalog from 1032 to 1033 kinds (1034 gallery choices including plain). Each tile stacks 8 horizontal bands from top to bottom, the k-th (k = 0 to 7) being the set after k steps of the Cantor construction: band 0 is the whole strip and each further step removes the middle part of every interval. The seed picks one of three fractions removed: a third (the classic Cantor set, where band k has 2^k intervals of length (1/3)^k), a fifth (two fifths kept each step, leaving more) and a half (a quarter kept each step, leaving less); band k has 2^k equal intervals with total length (1 − r)^k, r being the fraction removed. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only 8 steps (at step 7 the intervals are narrower than a pixel and only faint stripes show) and only those three removal fractions; each band's edge is softened by distance to the interval boundary; the paper shows between bands. Defaults are a 0.8 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`conicsections` adds conic sections, bringing the current catalog from 1033 to 1034 kinds (1035 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is divided into four 2×2 panels showing a circle, an ellipse, a parabola and a hyperbola with eccentricity e of 0, 0.6, 1 and 1.6, the arrangement of the panels being chosen by the seed. The curves are drawn from the definition "distance to the focus r = e × distance to the directrix" (the semi-latus rectum l is fixed at 0.09 UV; written r = |l − e·x'|, where x' is the offset from the focus along the axis); the focus is a small dot and the directrix (for e > 0) a dashed line; the parabola and hyperbola run to the panel edge and both branches of the hyperbola are drawn. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only those four curves, with the axis fixed horizontal (no rotation) and no axes or labels; the line width is softened by a first-order distance estimate of the implicit function, so it can vary slightly on steep stretches far from the vertex; each panel's focus position is set by hand to centre the curve (the hyperbola's focus sits left of centre and the ellipse's right). Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `rosecurves` adds rose curves, bringing the current catalog from 1034 to 1035 kinds (1036 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is nine 3×3 panels, each drawing a rhodonea rose r = R·cos(kθ) with k equal to 1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 3/2, 5/2, 5/3 and 7/3 (an integer k gives k or 2k petals, a fractional k gives overlapping multi-petal roses, and k = 1 is a circle); the seed decides how the nine curves are arranged in the panels. Lines are drawn using a first-order distance estimate to the polar implicit function, and the origin is marked. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only those nine values of k, a fixed amplitude and no rotation phase; no formula or labels are shown; a fractional-k curve needs several turns to close (the denominator times 2π), and the sampler evaluates the distance estimate over twice the denominator half-turns for each pixel, so the line width can vary slightly where petals cross. Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

This is an authored schematic: only those 7 ratios, always horizontal, with no axes or labels; the line width is softened by a first-order distance estimate of the implicit function (at the midpoint between the foci the gradient is zero, so I floor it at 1e-6 to avoid dividing by zero, see the log below); only three focal separations to choose from. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `twosourceripples` adds two-source ripples, bringing the current catalog from 1036 to 1037 kinds (1038 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is the interference pattern of two identical circular wave sources: the sources sit horizontally in the middle of the tile 0.22 or 0.32 UV apart, with a wavelength of 0.04, 0.052 or 0.07 UV (both picked by the seed), and each point's brightness comes from the sum of the two waves, cos(k·r₁) + cos(k·r₂) = 2 cos(k(r₁+r₂)/2) cos(k(r₁−r₂)/2) (r₁ and r₂ being the distances to the two sources), so on the hyperbolas where r₁ − r₂ is an odd multiple of half a wavelength the waves cancel and the brightness sits at its middle value (the nodal lines), while the crests and troughs are brightest or darkest where the waves are in step. The coordinates pass through a triangle-wave fold so the pattern is continuous across the tile edge. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only two point sources of equal amplitude and phase, with no attenuation or reflecting boundary (the triangle-wave fold is only for a continuous seam, not physical mirroring); brightness is just interference intensity, not hue. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.006 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview (a wavelength of 0.04 UV is only about 20 pixels at 512×512, and smaller sizes alias). This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`luhnnumbers` adds Luhn numbers, bringing the current catalog from 1037 to 1038 kinds (1039 gallery choices including plain). Each tile has 10 rows of 16-digit numbers (in groups of four with a gap between groups); the last digit of each row is the check digit (on a darker background) and each row ends with a mark: a check mark means the whole number passes the Luhn test (from the right, double every second digit, subtract 9 from any result above 9, and the total is a multiple of 10) and a cross means it does not. The first 15 digits of each row are drawn by the seed and the check digit is computed from them; about 60% of the rows are left valid and in the others one digit is changed to a different one (changing any single digit always breaks the Luhn sum), so the marks agree with the actual check result. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: the digits are random, not real card numbers (no issuer prefix or length rules are modelled), only an illustration of the Luhn algorithm; the share of valid rows in a tile comes from the seed's pseudo-randomness (about 60%, not a fixed count); odd rows (second, fourth, …) have a slightly darker background; the dot-matrix digits are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.4 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`bezierconstruction` adds a Bezier construction, bringing the current catalog from 1038 to 1039 kinds (1040 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is divided into four 2×2 panels, each drawing a cubic Bezier curve (four fixed control points P₀ to P₃, in four different shapes, arranged by the seed) together with de Casteljau's construction at one parameter t: a dashed line joins the control polygon, the end points P₀ and P₃ are filled squares and the two inner control points P₁ and P₂ are hollow rings, then the first- and second-level segments obtained by interpolating neighbouring points at t are drawn as thin lines, and the final interpolated point, which lies on the curve, is marked with a filled dot. The seed picks t from 1/4, 1/3, 1/2 and 2/3, shared by all four panels. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only four fixed cubic curves and four fixed values of t; the curve itself is a 64-segment polyline approximation (each pixel takes the distance to 64 segments); the dashes only suggest the control polygon and their gaps come from a screen-space grid, not equal dashes along the line; about 0.2 s for one 512×512 render under Bun (from the preview script, measured once). Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `vennregions` adds Venn regions, bringing the current catalog from 1039 to 1040 kinds (1041 gallery choices including plain). Each tile draws a Venn diagram of three sets A, B and C: three equal circles arranged as an equilateral triangle, partly overlapping, form seven regions (only A, only B, only C, A and B, A and C, B and C, and all three), each with its element count in the middle (0 to 40, drawn by the seed, written in 3×5 dot-matrix digits); the background gets darker where circles overlap (the more circles a point lies in, the darker), and the circles are outlined with a thin dark line; the top left lists three totals "A=…", "B=…" and "C=…", each the sum of all regions inside that circle, so the size of the union can be checked by inclusion–exclusion. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only three sets and seven regions, with the circles' positions and sizes fixed; the counts are random, not real data; totals have at most three digits (for example A=105); the dot-matrix digits are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. `ieee754floats` adds IEEE 754 single-precision floats, bringing the current catalog from 1040 to 1041 kinds (1042 gallery choices including plain). Each tile has six single-precision numbers from top to bottom: above each, a line with its decimal value (to 4 decimal places, in 3×5 dot-matrix digits with a decimal point and a minus sign), and below it its 32 bits: 1 sign bit (on the darkest background), 8 exponent bits (bias 127, on the next darkest) and 23 mantissa bits (on the lightest), with thin lines between the fields. The value is (−1)^sign × 2^(exponent−127) × (1 + mantissa/2²³); the seed draws each number's sign, exponent (124 to 133, so magnitudes roughly between 0.125 and 128) and mantissa, so the printed decimal and the bits correspond. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only normal single-precision numbers, with the exponent fixed to 124 to 133 and no zero, infinity, NaN or subnormals; the decimal value is printed to only 4 decimal places, the exact value rounded; the bits are drawn as 3×5 dot-matrix 0s and 1s and are hard to read at small sizes. Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `bellcurvebands` adds bell-curve bands, bringing the current catalog from 1041 to 1042 kinds (1043 gallery choices including plain). Each tile draws the bell curve of a normal distribution (the Gaussian e^(−z²/2) with z = (x − mean)/σ), with the area under the curve split into four bands by how many standard deviations from the mean: within 1σ the darkest, 1 to 2σ the next, 2 to 3σ lighter and beyond 3σ the lightest; an axis runs along the bottom with a tick at each σ from −3σ to +3σ. The width σ is picked by the seed from 0.07, 0.09 and 0.11 UV, and the height of the curve is fixed. Because the area is proportional to the integral of e^(−z²/2), the ratio of the band areas is the normal distribution's 68–95–99.7 rule (about 68.27%, 95.45% and 99.73%). Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: just one standard normal curve with σ chosen from only three values and no axis labels or numbers; the line width is corrected for slope; the bands use brightness only (procedural materials only have a dark-to-light ramp); the height is fixed, so curves with different σ enclose different areas (they are only similar in shape), which makes this an illustration of proportions rather than of absolute probability density. Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

`roundingmodes` adds rounding modes, bringing the current catalog from 1042 to 1043 kinds (1044 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is a rounding comparison table: a dark header row reads X and the codes of five ways of rounding — FL (floor), CE (ceiling), TR (truncation toward zero), RN (round to nearest, halves away from zero) and RE (round to nearest, halves to even, "banker's rounding") — and 12 rows below each hold a number x (to one decimal place) with its integer result under each of the five. The seed picks the 12 values from a fixed pool of 20 (from −3.5 to 6.5, including negatives, 0 and several exact halves) and lists them in ascending order; in rows where x is exactly a half the RN and RE columns have a darker background, since those are the only cases where the two can differ (for example 2.5: RN gives 3 and RE gives 2; 3.5: both give 4). A result of zero is always printed as "0", never with a minus sign. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only those five modes, and x with one decimal place; the pool of values is fixed, not arbitrary numbers; the dot-matrix text is hard to read at small sizes (the four characters of the x column exactly fill the cell width). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `binaryaddition` adds binary addition, bringing the current catalog from 1043 to 1044 kinds (1045 gallery choices including plain). Each tile stacks three column additions from top to bottom, each adding two random 8-bit binary numbers: a row of small digits on top holds the carries (into positions 1 to 8), followed by addend A, addend B with a "+" sign, a rule, and at the bottom the 9-bit sum (one bit longer than the addends to hold the final carry), with a darker background on the sum row. Each small carry digit sits right above the column that receives it; the units column receives no carry, so it has none. Every column obeys the full-adder rule: A bit + B bit + carry in = sum bit + 2 × carry out. A and B in the three problems come from the seed (hash randomness); carry chains are not deliberately selected. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only 8-bit unsigned addition, with no negative numbers, overflow flag or decimal equivalent; carries are only smaller, lighter digits without a colour of their own (procedural materials only have a dark-to-light ramp). Defaults are a 0.5 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. `abeliansandpile` adds an abelian sandpile, bringing the current catalog from 1044 to 1045 kinds (1046 gallery choices including plain). Each tile is the stable pile left after thousands of grains are dropped on the centre cell of an 81 × 81 grid: whenever a cell holds four or more grains it gives one grain to each of its four neighbours per four it holds, until every cell holds at most three; grains that leave the grid vanish. Each cell is painted in one of four brightnesses (darkest to lightest) for 0 to 3 grains. The seed picks the grain count from 4000, 5200 and 6400. The final pile of such a sandpile does not depend on the order of the topplings (the abelian property), so the result is deterministic and has the eightfold symmetry of the square. Metallic and mortar are 0.

This is an authored schematic: only a single source at the centre and only three grain counts, with no other initial configurations; there are no lines between cells, and the edges show slight stair-steps when the grid does not line up with pixels (81 cells do not map to a whole number of pixels). The pile covers only part of the tile; the rest is the 0-grain background. The sampler has to simulate the whole pile when it is first called and is a lookup afterwards; the preview script measured about 224 ms per run at 512² (Bun, not a formal benchmark). Defaults are a 0.6 m nominal tile, 0.004 UV-relative relief (not metres of displacement) and metallic factor 0. Existing periodic opaque maps, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache APIs and texture ownership are reused without new APIs or dependencies. Prefer 1024 or larger; 32 is a coarse preview. This description does not claim three-backend or cross-browser verification.

This is an authored schematic: only square-lattice site percolation; clusters do not connect across the tile boundary (the grid is cut at the edges, so clusters of neighbouring tiles do not join and breaks show at the tile seams); there are no lines between cells, the sizes have only three levels, and brightness only encodes cluster size, no other physical quantity. The three values of p are fixed, and the threshold or whether a cluster spans the tile is not marked. `bitwiselogic` adds bitwise logic, bringing the current catalog from 1047 to 1048 kinds (1049 gallery choices including plain).
