`flangenuts` adds an authored top-view approximation of steel hexagonal flange nuts: a trimmed six-flat hex body stands on a lower circular conical flange with an open central bore revealing rougher dark steel backing; it is neither flangeless Hex Nuts nor the closed dome of Cap Nuts. Proportions follow only the DIN 6923 M5–M20 table and drawing trend: flange diameter dc is about 1.38–1.48 across-flats s, minimum across-corners e is about 1.10–1.115 s, minimum bore da is about 0.60–0.67 s, and the drawing shows a 15–30 degree flange face; this material uses a flange/flat ratio near 1.40 and a bore/flat ratio near 0.68. Sixteen seeded owners cache six plane normals; 16×12 plane values plus 96² grain use 9,408 Float64 elements / 75,264 table bytes, not total RAM. The 0.413 flange radius stays inside the 0.5 owner; each point uses six smooth plane products, one hypot and a few SmoothStep calls, with no allocation, hash, trigonometry or neighboring-cell scan, and generic detail is skipped. The 0.08 m nominal tile follows Hex Nuts; the 0.03 UV-relative relief and palette are authored approximations. The whole tile including dark steel backing is metallic 1, the root-factory default is 1, and explicit factor 0 does not rewrite maps. It does not include underside serrations, full 3D nuts, internal threads, transparency, steel hardness, corrosion data or DIN/ISO certification.

Eight behaviors use the actual sampler on each seed’s 16 owners without copying private planes: 720-ray bisection first finds the mask’s flange edge and bore edge, then a height isocontour finds the hex-body outline. It requires six corner lobes, about 60-degree spacing, a 1.05–1.15 corner/flat ratio, flat-edge projection spread below 0.006, near-circular flange and bore (max/min below 1.03), a minimum flange radius 1.25–1.6 times the flat radius and at least 1.1 times the corner radius, a bore of 0.45–0.85 flat radius whose floor is within 0.02 of backing, a hex top 0.2–0.5 above the flange rim, a flange rim 0.15–0.4 above backing, a 0.03–0.15 cone rise, and bounded wall AO, backing roughness/color separation and random-orientation concentration. Twenty-one valid variants — cool/warm steel palettes, two roughness values, two reliefs, larger/smaller nuts, two flange ratios, two bore sizes, two cone heights, two hex and flange heights, two wall-AO strengths and a quintic flange shoulder — pass all eight cases. Twenty-eight real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: flange hugging the hex corners, flange smaller than the hex, owner-clipped flange, closed/oversized bore, no height step, flange as tall as hex, no/steep cone, no wall AO, no backing roughness/color separation, black palette, absent/extreme relief, tiny nut, height speckle, over-clipped octagon corners, pentagon/octagon body, square/oval flange, oval bore, nonmetal, C0 grain, linear bevel, fixed orientation and missing hex body. Oversized bore, same-height flange, steep cone and missing body are rejected because the hex isocontour lobe count degenerates, not through independent diagnostics. Three-seed observed-curvature C1 over hex bevels, corner trims, bore rims, wall rings, flange rims and signed UV passes; 512 maps include steep bevel normals, while 32 keeps macro color and coarse normals. Forced WebGPU/WebGL2 and shipped root factory, native Worker, cache and ownership paths were exercised; limits are in ACCEPTANCE and do not extend cross-browser, Canvas2D or fastener certification.

References actually read: [Fuller Fasteners DIN 6923 table](https://fullerfasteners.com/tech/din-6923-specifications-hex-flange-nuts/) (c, da, dc, dw, e, m, mw, s and r for M5–M20) and its viewed drawing, showing a circular flange around a hexagon and bore plus a 15–30 degree flange cone. No photograph, third-party search result or other standard page was used as dimensional evidence, and no drawing or table is copied or bundled.

`capnuts` adds an authored top-view approximation of steel hexagonal cap nuts: six straight flats on a lightly trimmed hex body, a closed circular dome and rougher dark steel backing; it is not the through-bored Hex Nuts material. Proportions follow only the DIN 1587 table trend: dome diameter dk is about 0.93–0.96 of across-flats s, minimum across-corners e is about 1.106–1.113 s, and a lower 30-degree chamfer ring approximates the corners. The whole tile including dark steel backing is metallic 1, the root-factory default is 1, and explicit factor 0 does not rewrite maps. It does not include full 3D nuts, internal threads, transparency, steel hardness, DIN/ISO certification or measured steel data.

Eight behaviors use the actual sampler on each seed’s 16 owners: the dark-backing mask centroid and 720 bisected true-contour rays require six corner lobes, about 60-degree spacing, a 1.05–1.15 corner/flat ratio and flat-edge projection spread below 0.006, without copying private planes. The dome must be closed, descend monotonically from the center in every direction, have a near-circular half-height isocontour at 0.6–0.85 of the flat radius, a rim at about 0.88–1.0 of the flat radius, stand 0.35–0.55 above the hex top, and the hex top must stand 0.35–0.55 above backing; corner chamfer drop, neck AO, backing roughness/color separation and random-orientation concentration are also bounded. Twenty-seven real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: no/tiny/oversized dome, over-clipped octagon corners, no/excessive chamfer, hex top collapsed to backing, over-tall dome, no neck AO, no roughness/color separation, black palette, absent/extreme relief, tiny or owner-clipped giant nuts, height speckle, pentagon/octagon, through bore, hex-shaped/oval dome, nonmetal, C0 grain, linear bevel, fixed orientation and pointed dome. Unclipped corners are accepted because the observed ratio cannot distinguish them from wide trim; this is not claimed as detectable. Forced WebGPU/WebGL2 and shipped root factory, native Worker, cache and ownership paths were exercised; limits are in ACCEPTANCE and do not extend cross-browser, Canvas2D or fastener certification.

Other search-result pages, the textual fasteners.eu page without its 3D render, and the Wikipedia nut article were not used as dimensional evidence; no drawing, table or photograph is copied or bundled.

`bedfordcord` adds an authored khaki warp-direction woven-rib surface approximation: twenty vertical cords are each made of twenty-four flat weft-direction dashes, adjacent cords are staggered by half a dash pitch, and continuous fine grooves separate the cords; the cord body lies below the dashes and the grooves lower still. It is neither corduroy cut-pile wales, rib-knit loops, faille/grosgrain transverse weft ribs nor a yarn-by-yarn draft float. A separate case is used instead of forcing this lattice into the existing warp/weft yarn kernel: each point performs only floor/fract, squares and SmoothStep composition, with no allocation, hash, trigonometry, square root or neighboring-cell scan, and generic detail is skipped. The 20×24 dash-tone table plus 96² grain use 9,696 Float64 elements / 77,568 table bytes, not total RAM; dash half-extents 0.45/0.46 remain inside the 0.5 owner. The seed changes dash tone and fine grain only; cord pitch, dash pitch and stagger are fixed. The 0.07 m nominal tile, 0.0018 UV-relative relief, 20 cords / 24 rows and khaki palette are authored approximations, not calibrated to fabric weight, yarn count or photograph scale; metallic maps and the root-factory default are 0, and explicit factor 1 does not rewrite maps. It does not include real warp/stuffer interlacement, cloth physics, transmission, fuzz, fiber meshes or cotton specification/provenance certification.

Eight behaviors measure a 480² actual sampler raster for the whole tile without copying private tables: column means find continuous dark grooves and the cord count; each cord center yields 24 dashes with uniform spacing, 0.8 of the row pitch in length and 0.833 of the cord pitch in width; every adjacent pair, including the last cord wrapping to the first, must be offset by half a dash pitch; groove/cord-body/dash height, color and roughness ordering and dash height/tone scatter must remain bounded. Twenty valid variants — warm khaki, olive, neutral-gray and green palettes, two reliefs, 16×20 and 24×28 cord/row layouts, 20/28 rows, two roughness sets, stagger 0.45/0.55, two dash proportions, stronger tone variation, softer crown, quintic shoulders and four-power rounded rectangles — pass all eight cases. Twenty-nine real faults are rejected with ERR_ASSERTION: zero/quarter stagger, odd-cord seam, coarse/needle cords, too few/many rows, absent/wide grooves, flat/over-tall dashes, body as deep as groove, wrong color/roughness, collapsed contrast, absent/excessive relief, short dashes, dashes spilling into grooves, tone/height speckle, transposed axis, drifting stagger, metal cloth, C0 grain, linear shoulders, random pile spikes and nonperiodic rows. Three-seed relief-normalized observed-curvature C1, cord/row/half-row join and signed UV checks pass. Actual 512 maps resolve low-amplitude four-direction normals; 32 retains macro color and tiny normals, not resolved cord detail. Forced WebGPU/WebGL2 and the shipped root factory, native Worker, cache and ownership paths were exercised; limits are in ACCEPTANCE and do not extend cross-browser, Canvas2D or cloth certification.

References actually read: [Yorkshire Fabric Bedford Cord article](https://www.yorkshirefabric.com/zh/blogs/ranges/new-range-bedford-cord) and [Fawn product record](https://www.yorkshirefabric.com/products/fawn-100-cotton-bedford-cord) (lengthwise woven-in ribs, no cut pile, often stuffer yarns, 12 oz / 360 g cotton), [HFW Bedford cord journal](https://www.hfwltd.com/journal/15) (warp-faced vertically aligned woven ribs, less pronounced than corduroy). Their swatch collage, 1200 px fawn close-up and trouser photograph were viewed; the close-up was temporarily downloaded only to measure its 2D autocorrelation (about 32 px cord pitch, 27 px dash pitch and roughly half-pitch stagger, with unknown physical scale), then deleted. Unread search-summary claims and an unrelated cotton index page are not evidence; no image is copied, bundled or used for calibration.

`staurolite` adds authored dark-brown 60-degree crossed-prism surface profiles: two straight-sided, blunt-ended prisms join into four arms and share one flat top rather than stacking double height at the crossing. Both the light coarse-grained host and lower-roughness crystals are opaque dielectric. Sixteen seeded owners cache both axis cosine/sine pairs, centers, inverse scales and tints; the relative angle is calculated in the constructor. Sixteen × eight pose values plus 128² grain use 16,512 Float64 elements / 132,096 table bytes, not total RAM. The per-axis support bound hypot(0.32,0.07)×0.98+0.07=0.391016 stays below 0.5; point sampling has no allocations, hashes, trig, square roots or neighboring-cell scans and skips generic detail. The 0.12 m nominal tile, 0.0035 UV-relative relief and 60-degree UV angle are authored surface approximations, not calibrated crystal dimensions; no full prism meshes, schist foliation, transmission/refraction, mineral identification or chemical/specimen certification.

Eight behaviors find centers from an actual 128² full-tile / 32²-per-owner dark mask, using 4-connected crystals and 8-connected background so diagonal openings are not false holes. Actual contour rays in 720 directions identify four long arms, 60/120-degree gaps, parallel straight sides and blunt ends; transverse measurements stop at the first exterior boundary instead of re-entering the other arm. Center and arm tops stay level without copying private hashes/poses or pinning a smoothing formula. Fourteen valid palette, finish, relief, length/width, 58/62-degree, equivalent supplementary 120-degree, quintic-shoulder and slightly unequal-twin variants pass all eight cases. Twenty-six real missing-arm, wrong-angle, stacked/open/enclosed-hole crossings, fixed orientation, wrong finish/color/metal, owner clipping, C0 and linear-shoulder faults are rejected. Three-seed relief-normalized observed-curvature C1, owner/grain joins and signed UV checks pass. Actual 512 maps resolve four-direction rim normals; 32 has low-amplitude macro normals, not resolved fine rims. Forced WebGPU/WebGL2 and the shipped root factory, native Worker, cache and ownership paths were exercised; browser and diagnostic-probe caveats are in ACCEPTANCE, without extending cross-browser, Canvas2D or physical-mineral certification.

References: [Handbook of Mineralogy: Staurolite](https://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/staurolite.pdf), [Lavinsky crossed-crystal specimen record](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Staurolite-65715.jpg) and [Lavinsky light-matrix specimen record](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Staurolite-121725.jpg). The handbook describes common 60-degree and less common 90-degree twins; the selected surface uses only authored 60-degree profiles. Available specimen images were viewed as morphology references, not copied/bundled or treated as dimension, lighting or mineral-authentication data.

`dowelpins` adds authored silver solid unthreaded headless pin side elevations: parallel straight shafts, one rounded end, an opposite small entry bevel and a shallow transverse cylindrical crown. There is no Clevis Pin head/tail bore, Linchpin loop or flat key face. It reuses the Clevis Pin seeded-pose, smooth-cover and crown kernel, selecting headless/holeless branches and precalculating end curvature in the constructor without evaluating skipped head/hole profiles or adding another pin kernel. Sixteen six-value poses plus 96² grain remain 9,312 Float64 values / 74,496B of tables, not total RAM; there is no new table. Maximum rotated support hypot(0.36,0.095)×0.95+0.016=0.369708 stays inside the 0.5 owner boundary. Sampling allocates nothing and uses no hashes, trigonometry, square roots or neighbor scans; backing skips grain and generic detail is skipped. Steel is metallic 1 and opaque gray backing 0, with default material factor 1/explicit 0. The 0.12m nominal tile, 0.0032 UV-relative relief and proportions are authored approximations, not calibrated DIN dimensions or hardness. Four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership remain intact, without full cylinder meshes, transparency, threaded extraction bores, press/interference-fit physics, load, rustproofing or DIN/ISO certification.

Eight behaviors locate each actual metal mask with PCA, refine its axis from measured parallel-side midlines, then binary-search the actual contour for distinct end forms, uniform shaft width, no head/enclosed bore and a shallow transverse crown without copying private seeded poses. Progressive rounded curvature is recognized without pinning a quadratic formula: eleven valid palette, finish, relief, shaft length/width, cap/bevel and smooth non-quadratic cap variants pass all eight cases. Twenty-five actual head, bore, single-direction, metal-backing/nonmetal-shaft, thread-like rib, flat/excessive crown, missing/wrong cap/bevel, thin/broad/short/owner-clipped, wrong pigment/finish/relief, linear-rim and tiny visible-grain C0 faults fail assertions; an added but unused head calculation is inert and not counted as a fault. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 covers observed-curvature refinement, a 128² grid, owner joins and 4,096 signed UV probes. Actual 32/512 five maps verify steel/gray nonmetal backing separation, finish, AO and opacity; 512 checks four signed rim normals while 32 requires only resolvable macro normals. All 817 prior kinds retain 3,268 four-seed seven-point signed-UV sampler streams exactly; 48 cases across eight related metal surfaces at 32/512 retain byte-identical five maps, preserving prior Clevis behavior.

Appearance references: the actually read [Elesa DIN6325 sheet](https://www.elesa.com/siteassets/PDF/PDF_EN/DIN%206325.pdf) describes steel, a ground plain fit diameter and centering step; it explicitly says its dimensions do not conform to ISO8734. The read [Fastener Mart Dowel Pins](https://www.fastenermart.com/din-6325-dowel-pins.html) describes headless solid parallel cylinders with rounded and entry-chamfered ends; its [profile diagram](https://www.fastenermart.com/mm5/graphics/00000001/DIN6325.gif) was actually viewed, not a photograph. Only an authored side-silhouette/surface approximation is made: no drawing/dimension table is reproduced or bundled, and source hardness/fit/standard claims do not certify the shader.

`europeanbeech` adds an authored pale pink-tan fine straight-grained radial face with numerous diffuse shallow longitudinal vessels and minute flush ray flecks, distinct from White Ash coarse earlywood bands, broad White Oak flecks and raised burls. It reuses the existing White Ash/White Oak cached-noise, compact-vessel and curved-ray kernel, equalizing early/late vessel widths and probability, reducing band contrast and using constructor-only pore jitter to reduce regular column structure. Rays change pigment/finish and suppress vessels without adding raised height. The 48×24×4 vessel values, 6×18×6 ray values and 4×3, 96×4, 128² noise total 22,036 Float64 values / 176,288B of tables, not total RAM. Support including jitter stays within vessel X≤0.445/Y≤0.485 and ray X≤0.42/Y≤0.25844 owner-cell units, below 0.5. Sampling allocates nothing and uses no hashes, trigonometry, square roots or neighbor scans; generic detail is skipped. The 0.24m nominal tile, 0.0012 UV-relative relief, pigment and density are authored approximations, not calibrated timber dimensions or vessel diameters. Opaque dielectric M0/explicit override, four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership remain intact; there are no vessel meshes, transmission, species identification, steaming/chemical, waterproofing, structural or provenance certifications.

Eight behaviors use actual 512² roughness/AO masks and four-connected PCA to measure short fleck axes, flush height and pigment contrast, shallow longitudinal openings and measured vessel distribution over frequencies 1–64, rejecting ring bands or fixed columns without copying private hashes/placement tables. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 covers observed-curvature refinement, a 128² grid, vessel/ray owners and 4,096 signed UV probes. Actual 32 and 512 five-map output checks warm pink-tan pigment, finish and opaque M0; only 512 requires resolved micro normals in four directions, without claiming resolved tiny pores at 32. Nine valid palette/finish/relief/density/fineness/fleck/jitter variants pass all eight cases. Twenty-five real missing/broad fleck, missing/ring/coarse/sparse/deep/unrecessed vessel, fixed-column, absent ray pigment/finish/grain, wrong pigment/finish/relief, metal, raised/grooved ray, linear vessel/ray shoulder, tiny C0 and unshaded-opening faults fail assertions. All 816 prior kinds retain 3,264 four-seed seven-point signed-UV sampler streams exactly; 48 cases across eight related woods at 32/512 retain byte-identical five maps.

Appearance references: the actually read [The Wood Database European Beech](https://www.wood-database.com/european-beech/) describes pale straw/pink-brown pigment, fine straight grain, diffuse/sometimes semi-ring pores and minute quarter-sawn flecks. Its raw/finished/full-board photographs were viewed without claiming all are radial cuts. The read [GL Veneer European Beech](https://glveneer.com/species/european_beech/) describes fine uniform grain and small silvery rays; its identified [quarter-cut](https://glveneer.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Beech-Euro-Steamed-Quarter-Cut.jpg) and [figured quarter-cut](https://glveneer.com/wp-content/uploads/2021/10/Beech-Euro-Steamed-Quarter-Cut-Figured-1.jpg) photographs were viewed. Woodworking Network and the Woodveneerz species sheet were also read. This authors a pale pink-tan uniformly diffuse radial approximation, not baked photograph lighting, a copied board/curl pattern or calibrated steaming; photographs are not bundled.

`habotai` adds an authored pearl-white fine dense 1/1 plain silk surface with same-dye warp/weft, shallow crossing relief and soft sheen, distinct from matte cotton Batiste, Surah twill, long-float Sateen and irregular Shantung slubs. It reuses the existing balanced-plain kernel and smooth yarn shoulders, adding only a preset/constructor selection; the 128² grain totals 16,384 Float64 values / 131,072B of tables, not total RAM, with no extra float table. Sampling allocates nothing and performs no hashes, trigonometry or square roots; generic detail is skipped. The 84/84 yarn and 336/336 filament-shading counts, 0.04m nominal tile and 0.0002 UV-relative relief are authored selections, not calibrated textile density or thickness. Pearl pigment and lower roughness give soft reflection without adding an anisotropic silk BRDF. Opaque dielectric M0/explicit overrides, four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership remain unchanged. Real Habotai may be sheer; this preset selects an opaque surface approximation, without transmission, fold/fiber meshes, cloth physics, momme/composition or conservation-performance certification.

Eight behaviors infer actual over/under arm heights, neighboring 1/1 transitions, same-dye/equal-height yarns, shallow crossover/binding drops, recessed gaps/AO and lower roughness. An 8,192-point output profile measures 84 dominant yarns on each axis while accepting a valid 80-thread variant instead of pinning preset literals; private hashes are not copied. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 covers observed-curvature refinement, a 128² grid, yarn-owner/filament joins and 4,096 signed UV probes. Actual 512 five-map output verifies pearl dye, gentle normals in four directions, finish and opaque M0. At 32px only supported color/finish/opacity are required, not unresolved microholes or normals. Nine valid variants pass all eight cases, including coarser 80/80 yarns and two weft-filament groups; twenty missing/excess/inverted lift, wrong finish/dye, coarse/unbalanced yarn, narrow weft/open mesh, quantized-away/excess normals, dark tone, unequal dye, always-warp/basket topology, linear shoulder, metal and tiny-C0 faults fail genuine assertions. All 815 older kinds retain exact seven-point signed-UV sampler output across 3,260 seeded streams; eight related fabrics retain byte-identical five-map output in 48 cases at 32/512.

Appearance references: the actually read [Tissura Habotai guide](https://tissura.com/articles/silk-habotai-fabrics) describes fine plain weave, smooth soft sheen and potentially sheer cloth; its [pink Habotai photograph](https://tissura.com/media/15286_2.jpg) was actually viewed. The read [IN SITU conservation supplier catalog](https://www.insituconservation.com/en/product/silk-fabrics/) lists ecru, medium white and heavy white Habotai; its shared multi-product image is not treated as a uniquely identified sample. CAMEO returned403 and was not used as read evidence. This preset authors a pearl-white flat opaque face, not photographed pink dye/folds, a measured weight or conservation suitability; photographs are not bundled.

`azurite` adds authored deep-blue broad tabular/prismatic faces with strongly oblique parallel ends, shallow longitudinal striae and locally parallel triples rotated between clusters above dark rough mineral backing. It differs from radiating short Cavansite needles, narrow strongly ridged Kyanite blades and near-square orange Wulfenite plates. It reuses the existing Celestine/Barite/Kyanite seeded-plate kernel, adding only a profile: twenty-five six-value poses plus 128² grain total 16,534 Float64 values / 132,272B of tables, not total RAM. Rotated support hypot(0.23,0.3446)×0.975+0.025=0.428948 stays inside the 0.5 owner boundary. Sampling allocates nothing, performs no hashes or neighbor scans, retains one existing stria cosine and skips generic detail. Low-roughness opaque dielectric M0 faces do not bake photographic white specular reflections into metallic maps or white pigment. The 0.1m nominal tile, 0.0034 UV-relative relief, colors and cluster density are authored approximations. Four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership remain unchanged. No complete crystal meshes, transparency/refraction, pleochroism, growth, mineral/chemical or copper-safety certification is added.

Seven behaviors locate faces through a 512² actual color mask and four-connected components, refine PCA with a local minimum-area fit, and regress both observed end contours over eleven transverse sections to measure obliquity, parallelism and straightness without copying private hashes/poses. They also check local parallel triples, inter-cluster directions, broad aspect, shallow striated core span, raised smoother faces and dominant rough host. Existing observed-curvature refinement plus a 128² grid, owner joins and 4,096 signed UV probes checks three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1. Actual 512 five-map output verifies deep blue, host, finish, four signed shoulder-normal directions and opaque M0. Eight valid variants pass all seven cases; twenty square/weakly/excessively oblique ends, narrow/wide/single/sparse plates, absent/deep striae, tilted cores, wrong dye/finish/relief, linear end, metal, tiny C0 and flush-face faults fail genuine assertions. All 814 older kinds preserve exact seven-point signed-UV sampler output in 3,256 seeded streams; eight related minerals retain byte-identical five-map output in 48 cases at 32/512.

Appearance references: the actually read [Handbook of Mineralogy Azurite sheet](http://www.handbookofmineralogy.org/pdfs/azurite.pdf) describes tabular and short-to-long prismatic habits, wedge-like terminations, blue colors and vitreous luster. The read Harvard [MGMH 93556](http://tmn.fas.harvard.edu/objects/TSNB707) and [MGMH 2020.7.1943](http://tmn.fas.harvard.edu/objects/TSNB645) records have actually viewed [closeup](https://tmn.fas.harvard.edu/_astro/Exhibit2_MGMH93556_Azurite_55mmFOV_Southwood.D1oJyTlG_Z2tDNMa.webp) and [specimen](https://tmn.fas.harvard.edu/_astro/Exhibit2_MGMH2020.7.1943_Azurite_81mm_Southwood.Bu2-5Tkb_Nszgp.webp) photographs. This preset selects dark-blue oblique tabular faces, not the whole specimen, malachite intergrowth, white photographic highlights or calibrated mineral optics; images are not bundled.

`whiteoak` adds an authored warm olive-brown quarter-sawn face with broad long flush transverse ray flecks across straight grain and shallower recessed longitudinal vessels. It differs from White Ash without broad flecks, compact dense Lacewood scales and raised burls. It reuses the White Ash ring-porous/cached-noise kernel, adding eighteen six-value curved-ray records only for White Oak: 18,680 Float64 values / 149,440B of tables, not total RAM. Ray support including jitter stays within X≤0.46 and Y≤0.47124 owner-cell units, below 0.5. Sampling allocates nothing and uses no hashes, trigonometry, square roots or neighbor scans; unused generic detail is skipped. Rays alter pigment and finish, suppressing vessels at full coverage without raising height; only micrograin and vessel recesses shape normals. The 0.24m nominal tile, 0.0016 UV-relative relief, colors and density are authored approximations, not calibrated specimens. Opaque dielectric M0/explicit overrides, four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership remain unchanged. No pore meshes, transmission, species identification, resin chemistry, waterproofing, structural or sourcing certification is added.

Seven behaviors measure broad horizontal flecks through a 512² actual roughness mask and four-connected PCA, including coverage, near-horizontal axes and variable lengths. Flush height is measured in pore-free ray cores, avoiding false failures from legitimate partially covered vessel edges. AO identifies recessed vessels and their longitudinal axes; private hashes/ray records are not copied. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 covers a 128² grid, observed vessel contours, reconstructed actual ray-cover contours, owner joins, noise and signed UV. Actual 512 five-map output verifies warm dye, finish, shallow normals in four directions and opaque M0. Eight valid variants pass all seven cases; twenty missing/uniform-length/short/upright/swollen/dense ray, absent/flat/deep/horizontal vessel, wrong dye/finish/relief, raised/linear/metal ray and tiny-C0 faults fail genuine assertions. Linear rays measure C1=37.8918, not below 0.04. All 813 older kinds retain exact seven-point signed-UV sampler output over 3,252 seeded streams; eight related woods retain byte-identical five-map output in 48 cases at 32/512.

Appearance references: the actually read [Wood Database White Oak entry](https://www.wood-database.com/white-oak/) describes ring porosity, prominent quarter-sawn ray flecks, long rays and frequent tyloses; its [finished](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/quercus-alba-qs2.jpg) and [raw quarter-sawn face](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/quercus-alba-qs.jpg) photographs were actually viewed. The read [red/white oak comparison](https://www.wood-database.com/wood-articles/distinguishing-red-oak-from-white-oak/) warns that color alone is unreliable. This authored surface selects broad transverse flecks and shallow vessels, not microscopic tylosis identification, copied lighting, bundled photos or physical wood performance.

`clevispins` adds an authored silver side elevation of an unthreaded cylindrical pin: a short head projects on both sides of its shaft, with one enclosed circular transverse bore near the opposite end. The shaft has a shallow rounded crown, without a Linchpin retaining ring, bent R-clip wire, one-sided Gib head or a solid key end. An independent kernel follows existing seeded-pose/smooth-cover conventions, uniting a short rectangular head and straight shaft with small tip chamfers before cutting the bore. Sixteen six-value poses plus 96² grain total 9,312 Float64 values / 74,496B of tables, not total RAM. Maximum rotated support sqrt(0.38²+0.18²)×0.95+0.016=0.415452 remains inside the 0.5 owner boundary. Sampling allocates nothing and uses no hashes, trigonometry, square roots or neighbor searches; empty backing/full bores skip grain and generic detail noise is disabled. Steel metallic is 1, opaque bore/backing 0; default material factor 1 allows explicit 0. The 0.12m nominal tile, 0.0032 UV-relative relief and proportions are authored, not DIN measurements. Four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and independent texture ownership remain unchanged, without complete cylindrical/through-hole meshes, transparency, inserted cotter/R-clip assembly, hinge physics, load ratings or standards certification.

Six behavior cases use a 128² actual metallic mask, its PCA axis and four-connected backing components to locate enclosed bores. Bore direction distinguishes the short bilateral head from the long straight shaft; measurements cover aspect, head width/length, two-shoulder symmetry, constant shank width, tail-bore position/roundness/diameter, opaque recessed backing and a shallow transverse shaft crown. No private hashes/poses are copied. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 covers a 192² grid, observed inner/outer contours at three thresholds over 120 directions, grain and signed UV. Actual 512 five-map output checks silver steel/nonmetal backing, finish and four signed normal directions; 32px retains metal/backing without claiming every bore is resolved. Eight valid variants pass all six cases; 23 absent/misplaced/open/missized/elliptical bores, absent/unilateral/long heads, wide shafts, absent/excess crowns, wrong finish/dye/relief/scale, owner overlap, linear shoulders, tiny C0 and nonmetal-pin faults genuinely fail assertions. All 3,248 32px RGBA streams from 812 old kinds and 48 five-map cases across eight related hardware presets remain byte-identical.

Appearance references: the actually read [mbo Oßwald DIN 1444 Form B catalog](https://www.mbo-osswald.de/en/configurators/bolts-din-1444-form-b), its viewed [pin image](https://www.mbo-osswald.de/media/0c/7f/e8/1598602952/bolzen-mit-loch-und-kopf-din.png?ts=1598602969) and [side drawing](https://www.mbo-osswald.de/media/14/d8/7b/1677505203/bolzen-mit-loch-und-kopf-din_massbild.jpg), plus the actually read [Boneham Clevis Pins sheet](https://www.bonehamusa.com/wp-content/uploads/2017/10/Clevis-Pins-Metric-ISO-DIN.pdf), which describes a head, shank and cross-drilled hole at the opposite end. ITA introductory text calls the pins partially threaded, conflicting with its own Thread: - table and plain-shaft drawing; that text was not used to add threads. This authors an unthreaded single-bore side elevation rather than copying photographed illumination/dimensions, bundling images or certifying DIN/ISO compliance.

`whipcord` adds authored charcoal single steep ribs and same-dye warp/weft yarns: a selected warp-faced 3/1 draft with continuous three-pick floats, lower single-point weft bindings, densely packed warps and sparser wefts produces an approximately 72° diagonal. This is distinct from existing fine short-float Gabardine, paired Cavalry Twill wales, plain weave, transverse Grosgrain ribs and cut-pile Corduroy. It reuses the existing profiled-weave/whole-float tables and smooth yarn shoulders rather than creating another cloth kernel; 4×4×6 profiles plus 128² grain total 16,480 Float64 values / 131,840B of tables, not total RAM. Sampling allocates nothing and performs no hashes, trigonometry or square roots; unused generic detail noise is skipped. The 0.06m nominal tile, 0.0016 UV-relative relief, yarn counts and dye are authored approximations; 3/1 is not a universal Whipcord specification. Existing opaque dielectric M0/override1, four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and individual texture ownership remain unchanged, without translucency, fiber/cloth meshes, anisotropic shading or garment physics.

Seven behaviors cluster actual heights to verify raised warp ribs above weft bindings, then infer three-over/one-under topology, a single diagonal binder, uninterrupted long-float joins, valleys between separate yarns and same-dye yarns from actual height. Independent 1024×97 output-profile spectra measure 84/28 dominant frequencies and 71.565°; integer harmonics are excluded from competing-rib comparisons, so a valid coarser 60/20 draft is not rejected for its second harmonic. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 covers exposed yarn shoulders, whole-float ends, fibers/grain and signed UV. Actual 512 five-map output checks charcoal coverage, matte finish, four signed normal directions and opaque M0; 32px retains color/AO contrast without claiming resolved fine-yarn normals. Ten valid variants pass all seven cases; 20 plain/2/2/basket drafts, absent/shallow lift, wrong relief/finish/dye, 32px aliasing, loose mesh, 45° diagonals, absent/reversed rib heights, per-pick beads, linear shoulders, tiny C0, metal and contrasting-weft faults genuinely fail assertions. All 3,244 32px RGBA streams from 811 old kinds and 48 five-map cases across eight related fabrics remain byte-identical.

Appearance references: the actually read [Scavini Whipcord/Cavalry Twill article](https://www.scavini.fr/en/2025/10/whipcord-cavalry-twill-les-classiques-intemporels-du-vestiaire-masculin/) describes pronounced oblique ribs at about 70°; its [Whipcord closeup](https://www.scavini.fr/wp-content/uploads/2025/10/WHI-600x600.jpg) was viewed. `vanadinite` adds authored orange-brown raised hexagonal crystal rims with one smaller aligned recessed hexagon and a darker flat opaque floor over pale rough mineral backing. Unlike solid flat Pyromorphite/Red Beryl terminations, four-sided Bismuth hoppers, pointed crystals or transparent tubes, this profile selects a single recessed termination. An independent kernel follows existing smooth-hexagonal-half-plane/seeded-pose conventions, separately blending the outer rim and inner depression rather than introducing max/absolute radial-distance seams. The 5×5×6 poses, 8² cloud and 128² grain total 16,598 Float64 values / 132,784B of tables, not total RAM; support (0.24+0.05)/sqrt(0.75)+0.06=0.394863 stays below the 0.5 owner boundary. Sampling has no allocation, hash, trigonometry, square root or neighbor search and skips generic detail noise. The 0.1m nominal tile, 0.0038 UV-relative relief, palette and density are authored approximations. Opaque dielectric M0/explicit overrides, four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and independent texture ownership remain unchanged; no complete crystal-prism/cluster mesh, transparency/refraction, growth/genesis simulation, chemistry/XRD, provenance or lead-safety certification.

Seven behaviors independently locate low-roughness crystal faces on a local grid, refine centers with opposing rays and bisect 120-direction inner/outer contours to check sixfold periodicity, straight-hexagon fit, a smaller aligned recess, flat rims/floors, recession and a floor above rough backing. Three-seed six-channel relief-normalized C1 covers observed outer/inner shoulders and core joins, grain/owner grids and signed UV without copying private hashes or poses. Actual 512 five-map output checks orange-brown crystals/pale host, four signed normal directions and opaque M0. Eight valid profiles pass all seven cases; 18 absent/pointed/missized/deep recess, tiny/overlapping crystal, wrong finish/palette/relief, circular face, absent AO, metal, raised center, linear shoulder and tiny C0 faults genuinely assert. All 810 older kinds’ 3240 32px RGBA streams and eight neighboring minerals’ 48 five-map cases remain byte-identical.

Appearance references: the actually read [Minerals.net Vanadinite](https://www.minerals.net/mineral/vanadinite) describes orange/red hexagonal crystals, partial hollows and hopper habits; the [Handbook of Mineralogy](https://handbookofmineralogy.org/wp-content/uploads/2022/07/vanadinite.pdf) describes commonly cavernous crystals and red-orange through brown colors. [John Betts specimen 9565](http://www.johnbetts-fineminerals.com/jhbnyc/mineralmuseum/picshow.php?id=9565) explicitly describes orange-brown prisms and a cavernous hoppered top termination; its [photograph](http://www.johnbetts-fineminerals.com/jhbnyc/mineralmuseum/9565.jpg) was viewed. Four maps/optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and independent texture ownership remain unchanged; no mesh holes, transparency, bent-tab/nut assembly, anti-loosening mechanics, load or standards certification.

Maximum rotated corner reach sqrt(0.22² + (0.22×1.08)²) + jitter 0.16 = 0.483812 < 0.5 prevents owner changes from cutting faces. Squared-distance smooth products avoid center absolute-value cusps; sampling has no allocation, hash, trig, sqrt or neighbor scan, with inverse squares, directions and tone cached by the constructor. The 0.06m nominal tile, 0.003 UV-relative relief and orange palette are authored references, not specimen dimensions, plate thickness in metres or calibrated optics. Opaque M0, optional height, tint, repeats, cache, native Worker and independently owned textures remain; transmission/refraction, actual crystal/cluster mesh, bipyramidal form, lead chemistry/toxicity and mineral, origin, value or safety certification are not added. The existing Barite/Kyanite observed fixture expands to eighteen cases while both old samplers, presets and tile values stay unchanged. Actual color/height connected components and minimum-area rotated bounding rectangles recover near-square outlines without the ambiguous PCA orientation of equal square eigenvalues. Measured fill, aspect, varied size/orientation, same-component eroded flat cores, lift/finish and actual 32/512 five-map packing do not copy private hashes, poses or square equations. Six-channel C1 normalizes height by relief and follows observed AO contours plus observed adaptive curvature; the former incidental boundary-count assertion is removed. Signed UV periods remain checked. Eight nearby legal presets each pass eighteen cases, while twenty-three actual assertion-based negative controls reject wrong color, finish/relief, absent/equal-size/elongated/round/aligned crystals, owner crossing, linear/hard shoulders, domes/missing lift, lost host roughness/AO or face AO, metal and a tiny height C0 step.

Morphology references: [Australian Museum — Wulfenite, D.50729](https://australian.museum/learn/minerals/mineral-factsheets/wulfenite-mexico/) and [Western Australian Museum — Wulfenite, M178.1985](https://museum.wa.gov.au/research/collections/earth-and-planetary-sciences/mineral-collection/wulfenite/). Their blocky/tabular shape, orange color and dark-host descriptions were read, and the AM 1200×779 and WA 700×400 specimen images were viewed. Only near-square plate faces are selected; photographs, illumination and measured color/size are not copied or shipped, nor are complete specimens, bipyramids or transparent optics reconstructed.

`lignumvitae` selects an authored polished dark olive-brown longitudinal lignum-vitae face: fine long grain and softly interleaved pigment remain coplanar, with only sparse short vessels recessed, darker and rougher—not golden Iroko, blood-red Bloodwood, purple Purpleheart or exaggerated zebra stripes. It reuses the complete Iroko/fine-grain core with constructor-only kind/preset selection and unused generic-detail exclusion; the per-point evaluator is verbatim unchanged. All 798 old four-map outputs and seven neighboring woods' 32/512 three-seed five-map outputs remain byte-identical, without new per-sample allocation, hash, trig, sqrt or runtime dependencies. The 32×20×4 pore poses, 3×4 warp, 256×10 fiber and 128² grain use 21,516 Float64 / 172,128B of tables, not total RAM. Maximum vessel half-width 0.06 is below its 0.25 owner margin and half-length 0.21 below 0.35; band support 0.46 < 0.5, five integer bands and periodic caches retain C1 and signed UV periods. The 0.12m nominal tile, 0.002 UV-relative relief, roughness 0.32 and olive-brown palette are authored references, not measured fiber sizes, thickness in metres or luster. Opaque M0, optional height, tint, repeats, cache, native Worker and independently owned textures remain; no wood/vessel mesh, transparent pores, oil/varnish layer, directional BRDF, species/endgrain or Guaiacum/substitute identification, oil/density/self-lubrication properties, origin or legal-sourcing certification is provided. Ten consumer cases are shared with Iroko while retaining its original bounds. Actual AO locates vessel contours and cores for measured aspect, depth, dark/rough pore floors, coplanar grain and direction, without private hashes or site coordinates. Six-channel C1 normalizes height by relief and reuses observed adaptive curvature refinement; actual five-map opacity/M0, named color/polish, shallow normals and signed periods are checked. Eight nearby legal presets each pass ten cases, while twenty-four actual assertion-based negative controls reject wrong color/finish, absent/dense or round/owner-crossing pores, raised grain/vessels, linear/hard shoulders, metal, lost AO/roughness, non-closing bands, tiny height C0 and unresolved/excessive normals.

Appearance reference: [The Wood Database — Lignum Vitae](https://www.wood-database.com/lignum-vitae/) describes olive to dark green/brown heartwood, fine interlocked grain and natural polishable luster. Its published [Guaiacum officinale longitudinal scan](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/guaiacum-officinale.jpg) and [Guaiacum sanctum flatsawn scan](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/guaiacum-sanctum.jpg) were viewed. Only an authored fine-grained olive-brown longitudinal appearance is selected; images, calibrated color/size, aging or endgrain-based solitary-pore species identification are not reproduced, nor are sourcing or wood physics certified.

`sateen` selects authored ivory five-harness filling-faced cotton sateen: one isolated warp binder per row and column in a 5×5 repeat, dispersed by a two-step satin counter, with the other four crossings forming continuous filling floats across four warp ends—not adjacent twill, plain weave, crossing-by-crossing beads or the existing purple warp-faced Satin. Only constructor preset selection changes; the former fineTwill flag is renamed fineCloth to include satin structure, and the complete per-point evaluator is unchanged. All 797 old 32px four-map outputs and seven adjacent fabrics' 32/512 three-seed five-map outputs remain byte-identical. The 55×55 yarns, 220×220 fiber frequencies, 5×5×6 float profiles and 128² grain use 16,534 Float64 / 132,272B of tables, not total RAM. Fifty-five is divisible by five, closing the draft at UV seams while avoiding an all-gap alias at 32px without resolution-specific branches. Radius 0.495 < 0.5, continuous floats and C1 yarn shoulders reuse the existing core without new per-sample allocation, hash, trig, sqrt or runtime dependencies. The 0.04m nominal tile, 0.0008 UV-relative relief, ivory palette and roughness 0.45 are authored references, not measured thread count, thickness, dye or luster. Opaque M0, optional height, tint, repeats, cache, native Worker and independently owned textures remain; no yarn/cloth mesh, transmission, drape physics, directional BRDF or cotton-content, fiber, textile-grade, finishing-process or durability certification is added. Behavioral tests infer front-yarn orientation from actual height curvature rather than copying private draft, hash or lift equations; both legal satin counters, shifted binder phases and nearby valid presets such as 50 yarns are accepted. Observed binders locate intermediate owners within four-end filling floats, checking uninterrupted lift, six-channel C1 with relief-normalized height, signed periods, actual 32/512 opaque five-map packing, ivory coverage, finish and resolved normals. The twelve-case fixture accepts eight legal variants and rejects twenty-one actual assertion-based negative controls covering wrong structures/faces, bead-like lifts, C0/linear shoulders, color, metal, finish, relief and non-closing draft.

Structure references: [CottonWorks — Basic Woven Fabric Designs](https://cottonworks.com/learning-hub/weaving/basic-woven-fabric-designs/), [Sateen](https://cottonworks.com/encyclopedia-item/sateen/) and [Counter (Satin)](https://cottonworks.com/encyclopedia-item/counter-satin/). The definitions and five-harness/two-or-three-counter explanation were read, and its FABRICAST 7258 Sateen photograph and filling-face draft illustration were viewed. This preset selects five-harness filling-faced cotton sateen; it does not claim every use of the name has that structure. No images, lighting, measured color or thread count are copied or shipped.

`parallelkeys` approximates a top view of double-rounded Form A parallel keys: solid silver-gray long bars with broad flat faces, parallel sides and two curved ends, smoothly beveled into dark, rougher dielectric backing. They are not cylinders, ellipses, square-ended bars, hollow rings or Woodruff segments. It follows the existing hardware seeded-pose and cached-grain pattern, using squared distance to a line segment for a bounded capsule footprint, with no per-sample allocation, hash, trigonometry or square root and no new runtime dependency. The 4×4 six-value poses plus 96² grain total 9,312 Float64 / 74,496B of tables, not total RAM; maximum rotated reach times scale plus jitter is 0.399525 < 0.5, preventing owner boundaries from cutting a key. The 0.12m nominal tile and 0.003 UV-relative relief are authored references, not CAD dimensions or displacement in metres. Metal tops remain separate from M0 backing; the factory defaults its metallic factor to 1 to preserve the map and still honors an explicit 0 override. Opaque four-map output, optional height, tint, repeats, cache, native Worker and independent texture ownership are retained. No key mesh, keyway assembly or mechanics is added, and DIN dimensions/tolerances, C45 composition, heat treatment, torque and safety are not certified. The related Woodruff sampler is completely unchanged. Shared consumer cases infer silhouettes, lift and flatness from actual metal-mask components and PCA; measured widths narrow at both tips while remaining parallel through the middle, allowing two transverse raster pixels of error rather than copying private poses, hashes or capsule equations. Six-channel C1 is checked at observed outer exits and flat-core bevel transitions with height normalized by relief.

Appearance reference: [Gardette, Parallel key with 2 rounded ends / DIN 6885 Form A](https://gardette.com/en/catalog/parallel-key-with-2-round-ends). The main text, full-part image and rounded-end close-up were consulted for the flat double-rounded shape only; no product photograph, illumination or machining marks are copied or shipped, and manufacturer specifications do not certify this procedural surface's dimensions or strength.

`smithsonite` selects an authored apple-green botryoidal appearance: irregular rounded crowns join into one bounded relief layer, with brighter, smoother crowns and darker, rougher green interstices. It is not a flat green-dot pattern or sky-blue Hemimorphite with pale interstices. It reuses the complete smooth joined-cap core; only constructor preset selection and unused generic-detail exclusion change, with no added per-point allocation, hash, trig, sqrt or runtime dependency. The 0.12m nominal tile and 0.006 UV-relative relief are authored references, not measured crystal dimensions or displacement in metres. It stays opaque M0 with the existing optional height, tint, repeats, cache, native Worker and independent texture-ownership contracts; transmission, refraction, dispersion, clearcoat and crystal meshes are not added, and mineral identity, chemistry, provenance and physical properties are not certified. One hundred cached sites use five Float64 values each; 128² grain plus 5×7 and 17×19 tone fields bring the tables to 17,242 Float64 values / 137,936 bytes, not total RAM or a promise of 100 separately visible crystals. Maximum radius 0.74 plus jitter 0.26 is 1.0 < 1.5, retaining the 3×3 neighbor-halo margin; the normalized layer ceiling is 0.643 rather than additive overlapping heights. Hemimorphite's point evaluator, old presets and tiles remain unchanged. The paired behavioral cases observe actual crowns, connected relief, interstice contrast and finish, six-channel curvature and signed periods without copying private seeds or footprint equations.

Appearance references: [Australian Museum, Smithsonite on Cerussite, D.50652](https://australian.museum/learn/minerals/mineral-factsheets/smithsonite-on-cerussite/) and [NMNH / Smithsonian, The Ultimate Honor](https://www.smithsonianmag.com/blogs/national-museum-of-natural-history/2024/06/18/the-ultimate-honor-why-a-colorful-mineral-honors-the-smithsonians-namesake/). The text and two green specimen images were consulted for rounded joined form only; no specimen photographs are copied or shipped, and color, lighting and translucency are not calibrated. The authored green interstices do not reconstruct exposed cerussite anatomy.

`macassarebony` approximates an authored polished longitudinal Macassar-ebony face: dark brown with unequal near-black streaks and fine sparse recessed vessels that are rougher and more occluded. Pigment stays coplanar—not carved grooves, board seams, pale-gold Zebrawood or closed-eye Bocote figure. It reuses the complete Bocote/Zebrawood kernel; constructor-only kind/preset selection chooses a 32×4 warp cache while both old kinds retain 3×5. The per-sample evaluator is verbatim unchanged. The 32×24×4 pores, 32×4 warp, 32×4 width, 64×4 fiber and 128² grain total 19,968 Float64 / 159,744B tables, not total RAM. Maximum band support is 0.39 < 0.5, each signed shoulder equation has a u-derivative lower bound of 1.76 > 0, and maximum vessel half-width/length 0.06/0.31 remain within their owners. Sampling adds no allocation/hash/trig/sqrt or runtime dependency. The 0.18m nominal tile, 0.0016 UV relief and brown palette are authored references, not measured growth rings, wood-fiber dimensions or displacement in meters. Opaque dielectric/M0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership retain their contracts; no board/vessel mesh, transparent holes, varnish layer or directional BRDF, and no species, endgrain/mineral-fill, mechanical/durability, origin/legal-sourcing or safety certification. Related Zebrawood tests now observe actual surfaces rather than copying private hash/noise code.

Appearance reference: [The Wood Database — Macassar Ebony](https://www.wood-database.com/macassar-ebony/) describes yellow to reddish-brown heartwood with darker brown/black stripes, usually straight but sometimes interlocked grain, fine uniform texture and natural luster. Its published [sanded scan](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/macassar-ebony1.jpg) and [sealed scan](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/macassar-ebony-sealed1.jpg) were actually viewed. This preset selects darker, near-straight longitudinal striping; it neither copies/bundles the images nor measures their color, scale or finish, and does not reproduce the article’s endgrain pore grouping or establish anatomical identification.

`serge` approximates authored matte navy balanced 2/2 Serge: equally dyed warp/weft stagger one yarn per row, with continuous two-over/two-under short floats on both axes, broad smooth yarn shoulders and weak grain—not printed diagonal stripes, crossing-by-crossing beads, plain weave or warp-faced 3/1. Constructor-only preset/fineCloth selection reuses the complete Surah/Lyocell kernel; the per-sample evaluator is verbatim unchanged. The 52×52 yarns, 208×208 fiber frequencies and four-step draft use 4×4×6 profiles plus 128² grain: 16,480 Float64 / 131,840B tables, not total RAM. Radius 0.495 stays inside each thread owner; C1 shoulders and signed periods remain, without new per-sample allocation/hash/trig/sqrt or runtime dependencies. Fifty-two yarns avoid the all-gap alias at the supported 32px minimum without a resolution special case. The 0.04m nominal tile, 0.004 UV relief and navy palette are authored references, not measured yarn density, fiber dimensions, thickness in meters or calibrated dye. Opaque dielectric/M0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership are unchanged; no fuzzy wool mesh, double-sided garment/drape/transmission physics or directional fabric BSDF, and no fiber, uniform-grade, warmth, durability, fire or acoustic certification.

Morphology references: [TRC Leiden — Serge](https://trc-leiden.nl/trc-needles/textile/materials/woven-and-interlocking-materials/serge) describes diagonal twill on both faces; [Paisley Museum / OneRen — 2/2 Twill Weave](https://www.oneren.org/culture/paisley-museum/heritage-on-your-doorstep/we-are-weavers/2-2-twill-weave/) explains two over/two under with each row starting one yarn along. The [Hainsworth True Heritage](https://shop.hainsworth.co.uk/products/true-heritage) 606 Navy Serge photograph was actually viewed at 1414×2000 for dark navy woven appearance, not copied or bundled. The selected 2/2 draft is not a claim that all Serge has this draft, that the photograph establishes its exact interlacement, or that color, roughness, dimensions or performance were measured.

`garterstitch` approximates an authored warm-cream garter surface: soft horizontal ridges carry staggered curved purl crowns and lower return arcs, uniform dye, weak grain and gentle seeded course wander—not a straight V/bar knitting chart, printed stripes, vertical ribbing, seed-stitch dots or metal. The standalone leaf uses existing cachedNoise/smooth with compact elliptical-ring and half-plane shoulders; three front neighbors and both half-cell return neighbors retain their support, with product unions and exposed underpasses rather than a max crease. The 24-column/20-ridge preset caches 96² grain plus a 24×20 course field: 9696 Float64 / 77,568B tables, not total RAM. Conservative full-ellipse row support is 0.465660 < 0.5, course half-width 0.49 < 0.5, and horizontal outer support 0.576906 is below the nearest discarded-neighbor distance 1. No per-sample allocation/hash/trig/sqrt is added. The nominal authored tile is 0.12m; actual height/normals create the relief, not printing. Opaque dielectric/metallic 0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and ownership retain existing contracts. No complete intermeshed-yarn/fuzz mesh, elasticity/drape/two-sided garment construction, fiber composition, measured physical gauge or calibrated BRDF is supplied. Existing Seed Stitch and Rib Knit remain unchanged.

Morphology reference: [Emily Wessel / Tin Can Knits — Garter Stitch, Stockinette Stitch, and Ribbing](https://blog.tincanknits.com/2013/06/14/basicstitches/) explains knitting every row when worked flat, alternating knit/purl rounds in the round, and distinguishes vertical ribbing. Its published Marshmallow-mitts and Malt-blanket-edge photos were actually viewed for horizontal ridges and curved purl loops, not copied images, lighting, garment design, color or physical gauge. The source’s softness, stretch and reversible appearance do not establish cloth physics for this 2D material.

`woodruffkeys` approximates scattered silver-grey solid Woodruff-key faces: a straight chord and one circular arc bound a shallow disc segment, with seeded orientation, position, size and small tone changes—not coins, triangles, oblong slots or bored washers. Existing periodic cachedNoise/hash/smooth combine circular and half-plane compact C1 shoulders, nearly flat raised metal with weak grain and a dark matte dielectric backing, not transparent gaps. The constructor caches 4×4×6 poses plus 96² grain: 9312 Float64 / 74,496B tables, not total RAM. The rotated whole-disc support plus jitter is 0.434 < 0.5, so owner changes cannot cut a part; no per-sample allocation, hash, trig or sqrt is added. The nominal authored tile is 0.08m; opaque RGBA, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and texture ownership retain existing contracts. The default material metallic factor is 1 while the actual metal map separates parts from the dielectric ground, and explicit overrides still win. No thickness mesh, shaft/keyway assembly, load/material-grade/DIN/safety certification or photo-calibrated dimensions, color or BRDF is supplied.

Morphology references: the solid-part photo and dimensioned drawing from [mbo Oßwald — Woodruff keys DIN 6888](https://www.mbo-osswald.de/en/shop/woodruff-keys-din-6888) were actually viewed for the straight-chord/circular-arc face, not copied product illumination, machining marks or assembly geometry. [Woodstock Industrial — DIN 6888](https://www.woodstockindustrial.com/specs/din-6888) describes a disc segment with a flat top and lists e.g. h2.6 / d7, so the segment need not be an exact semicircle. This is an authored silhouette and nominal tile, not access to the full standard, tolerance verification or certification of a supplier part.

`barite` approximates selected opaque pale-cream tabular baryte: locally parallel triples of broad four-sided plates with staggered ends, nearly flat faces smoother than a matte brown mineral host—not narrow blue three-ridged Kyanite, round caps, a tile grid or a color print. It shares the complete existing Kyanite blade sampler; only the original 0.05 face-tilt and 0.08 ridge-height coefficients move to its preset and are captured once by the constructor, while Barite selects 0 / 0.002. Old Kyanite values, multiplication order and output are preserved. No new synthesis engine or per-sample allocation/hash/trig/sqrt is added; the existing stria cosine remains. The 4²×6 poses plus 128² grain total 16,480 Float64 / 131,840B of tables, not total RAM. Plate half-width 0.09 stays below the nearest-blade owner half-pitch 0.095; maximum rotated bundle support plus jitter is about 0.419992, below the cell-owner half-width 0.5. Smooth product shoulders and signed periods remain. Nominal 0.08m tile and 0.003 UV relief are authored references, not measured crystal dimensions, thickness or meter-unit displacement. Opaque dielectric/M0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership remain unchanged. No transparency/refraction, real crystal mesh/complete specimen, cleavage optics or radial desert-rose cluster, nor composition, origin, value, density, use or safety certification is supplied. Related old Kyanite private-hash/pose assertions are replaced by blind connected-face/PCA transverse profiles detecting three real raised smoother ridges, not an implementation oracle.

Morphology references: [A.E. Seaman Mineral Museum — BARITE](https://museum.mtu.edu/pdfs/BARITE.pdf) describes opaque white sprays, white tabular/bladed/comb plates and other habits, not one universal specimen. [Carlesmillan — 6158M-barite2](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:6158M-barite2.jpg) and [Ivar Leidus — Cerro Warihuyn](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Barite_-_Cerro_Warihuyn,_Miraflores,_Huamalies,_Huanuco,_Peru.jpg) show transparent/almost-colorless tabular morphology; their published 960×909 and 500×750 previews were actually viewed. The former original returned 429 and is not claimed as viewed; the latter is focus-stacked. Transparent references do not give this opaque preset transmission. Illumination/fractures are not copied, color is not calibrated, and images are not bundled.

`surah` approximates an authored warm copper-colored, balanced 2/2 fine silk-twill surface: two over/two under stepping one yarn per row, with continuous two-pick floats on both axes—not plain weave, warp-faced 3/1, grouped 2×2 basket weave, crossing-by-crossing beads or copper metal. It reuses the complete existing Lyocell-family weave sampler: constructor-only fineCloth/preset selection uses existing whole-run float profiles and equally dyed warp/weft; the per-sample evaluator is verbatim unchanged. The 60×60 yarns, 240×240 fibers and four-step draft use 4×4×6 profiles plus 128² grain: 16,480 Float64 / 131,840B tables, not total RAM; no new per-sample allocation/hash/trig/sqrt or runtime dependency. Radius 0.495 stays inside each thread owner; C1 shoulders and signed UV periods remain. Nominal 0.015m tile, 0.0007 UV relief and warm copper palette are authored references, not measured sett, fiber dimensions, geometry thickness, meter-unit displacement or calibrated dye. Opaque dielectric/M0, optional height, tint/repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership remain unchanged. SILKNOW defines Surah only as soft twilled silk; Première Vision’s Silk Twill provides the two-over/two-under reference and its viewed photograph is blue, not copper. This does not make every Surah 2/2 or copper-colored. No silk-composition, origin, hand, durability or safety certification, true reverse-side/drape/transmission, directional silk luster or new sheen BSDF. Sixty yarns retain complete four-step repeats without the all-gap 32px sampling alias of 64 yarns; the adjusted nominal tile keeps authored yarn density unchanged, with no minimum-resolution special case.

References: [SILKNOW — Surah](https://skosmos.silknow.org/thesaurus/en/page/13) (soft twilled silk definition) and [Première Vision — Textile Glossary: Silkies / Silk Twill](https://www.premierevision.com/en/articles/76034207-ea4d-f011-8f7c-000d3a2e1c0a/textile-glossary-silkies) (2/2 silk-twill text and the actually viewed blue fine-twill photograph). Only weave structure is referenced; no images or product are bundled, and the reference photograph is not presented as a copper-colored Surah specimen.

`bocote` approximates a selected polished longitudinal Bocote face with a golden-brown body, high-contrast dark-brown to near-black grain and locally closed eye figure—not a claim that all Bocote has eyes, an endgrain anatomy diagram, pasted concentric targets or raised rings. It reuses the complete Zebrawood sampling kernel with only constructor preset selection; stronger authored phase warping folds longitudinal grain back into closed contours. Light and dark figure remain coplanar; only sparse short longitudinal vessels recess. A 16×8×4 pore table plus 3×5 warp, 24×4 width, 64×4 fiber and 128² grain total 17,263 Float64 values / 138,104 bytes of tables, not total RAM. There are no new point allocations, hashes, trigonometry, square roots or synthesis engine. Maximum band support 0.392 stays below the 0.5 phase-owner half-width; maximum vessel half-width 0.06 and half-length 0.31 fit inside the nearest owner margins 0.25 and 0.35. C1 shoulders and signed periods are retained. Vessels are an authored surface appearance, not circular copies of the few medium-to-large endgrain pores. The 0.24 m nominal tile and 0.0016 UV relief are not measured grain spacing, pore diameter, meter-valued displacement or wood thickness. Opaque dielectric maps (metallic 0), optional height, tint, repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership are unchanged. No real vessel geometry, directional luster, aging or species/figure-origin/oil/finish/durability/mechanical/toxicity/sustainability certification is supplied. Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('bocote', { seed: 7 })`.

Appearance reference: the actually read [Wood Database — Bocote](https://www.wood-database.com/bocote/) describes a yellowish-brown body, dramatic dark-brown to almost-black stripes and frequent eyes / figured interlocked grain, while noting that plain straight grain also exists. Its diffuse-porous endgrain has few medium-to-large pores; this does not put those circular/radial arrangements on the longitudinal face. The [sanded](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/bocote.jpg), [sealed](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/bocote-sealed.jpg) and [flatsawn bookmatched](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/bocote-flat.jpg) photographs were actually viewed. Only the golden-brown, dark-grained eye appearance is selected—not bookmatch joints, copied images or lighting, calibrated dimensions/colors or product performance.

`hemimorphite` approximates a selected sky-blue botryoidal mineral crust: irregularly sized and positioned rounded caps join across cells, leaving pale recesses and fine grain—not flat polka dots, a regular equal-bead grid, metallic copper or a complete stalactite mesh. It follows the existing cached C1 noise, compact circular support and weighted-globule conventions, but connects variable-radius caps through 3×3 periodic neighbors. Normalized weighted height stays inside one layer instead of adding overlap heights; the existing Chrysocolla and Botryoidal Copper leaves remain unchanged. An 8²×5 pose table, 128² grain and 5×7 plus 17×19 frost fields total 17,062 Float64 values / 136,496 bytes of tables, not total RAM. Seeds, radii and fixed weights are prepared at construction; sampling allocates nothing and performs no hashes, trigonometry or square roots, sharing one normalization reciprocal. Maximum support 0.72 is below the nearest omitted-neighbor distance 1.26. C1 shoulders, joined surfaces and signed UV periods are retained. Two C1 pigment frequencies avoid single-grid frosting; actual AO output is also checked against hard halos. The authored 0.12 m nominal tile and 0.008 UV relief are not calibrated specimen dimensions, meter-valued geometry displacement or mineral thickness. Opaque dielectric maps (metallic 0), optional height, tint, repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership are unchanged. No transmission, refraction, microcrystal sparkle, complete specimen geometry or mineral/locality/filling/composition/hardness/value/safety certification is provided. Use `await ProceduralMaterial.create('hemimorphite', { seed: 7 })`.

Appearance evidence: the actually read [GIA Fall 2002 Hemimorphite from Congo, pp. 263–264](https://www.gia.edu/dam/migrated-assets/gems-and-gemology/pdf/FA02.pdf) records mottled blue / banded blue-and-white material and botryoidal structure; one cabochon contained a filler. Those specimens' transmission and treatment are not transferred to this opaque crust. Rob Lavinsky's [173448 attribution](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hemimorphite-173448.jpg) and [199442 attribution](https://commons.wikimedia.org/wiki/File:Hemimorphite-199442.jpg) were read; the first 600×458 original and second published 250px thumbnail were actually viewed. The second original returned 429 and does not count as viewed. Only the blue joined rounded appearance is referenced—not photographs, lighting, calibrated color/size, complete specimens or commercial assurances; not every Hemimorphite habit is claimed to look this way.

`monkscloth` approximates a selected natural-cream coarse four-by-four Monk’s Cloth. Thirty-two warp and weft yarns alternate in 4×4 basket groups; three recessed internal grooves keep each group’s four yarns distinct, and individual floats remain continuous across four crossings—not 2×2 Hopsack, single-yarn plain weave, diagonal twill, painted checkerboard or merged wide strips. It reuses the existing whole-run float builder and point arithmetic; only constructor basket selection is extended from Hopsack to the appropriate preset. An 8²×6 profile table plus 128² grain retains 16,768 Float64 values / 134,144 bytes, not total RAM, without new point allocations, hashes, trigonometry, square roots or caches. Integer 32-yarn counts divide the eight-step draft, and radius 0.46 stays within owner half-width 0.5, preserving C1 shoulders and signed periods. Warp and weft use the same dye; base color does not bake fake checkerboard lighting, while genuine height/normal conveys four-yarn direction and float continuity. The authored 0.03 m nominal tile and 0.0018 UV relief are references, not measured yarn diameter, calibrated 7.5 count or metre-valued displacement. Matte opaque dielectric metallic-zero maps, recessed-interstice AO, optional height, tint/Worker/cache/repeats and ownership remain unchanged. No transparent holes, yarn geometry, embroidery/punch-needle interaction or cloth simulation is supplied. Not every Monk’s Cloth is claimed 4×4; Oxford double threads and white guidelines are not copied, and cotton content, brand, density, durability, care/shrinkage or safety are not certified.

Weave references: the actually read [Needlery/Nordic Needle Monk’s Cloth account](https://needlery.org/guides/stitching-materials-guides/fabrics/monks-cloth/) explicitly describes four warp and four weft threads forming float blocks. The [Zweigart 3528 manufacturer metadata](https://shop.zweigart.de/produkt/3528-monks-cloth/) and [Lakeside raw coarse-cloth listing and viewed swatch](https://www.lakesideneedlecraft.co.uk/zweigart-75-count-monks-cloth---raw-298687-p.asp) were inspected. Zweigart warns that some images may be AI-generated, so its image is not used as authentic-fiber evidence; the old Nordic Needle image failed TLS and does not count as viewed. The actually read/viewed [Oxford yardage](https://amyoxford.com/products/monks-cloth-yardage) instead specifies about 13 double threads/inch and two-inch white guidelines, demonstrating why the name alone does not make every variant 4×4. This preset selects the four-thread natural-cream appearance only, bundles no photographs and inherits no product-use or performance guarantee.

`hopsack` adds navy 2×2 basket-weave suiting: 32 warp and 32 weft yarns, paired on both axes, with continuous two-pick floats and a recessed groove separating the two yarns in each group. It is not painted checkerboard, diagonal 2/2 twill or single-yarn plain weave. Both yarn systems use the same dye. It reuses the existing whole-run cloth profile builder without changing the sampling kernel: a 128² grain lattice plus 96 profile values total 16,480 Float64 values / 131,840 B of table storage, not total RAM. The authored nominal tile is 0.016 m and UV relief is 0.0025, not measured thread diameter or thickness. Opaque dielectric maps (metallic 0), optional height, tint, repeats, Worker/cache and caller ownership remain unchanged. Recesses are opaque shading, not transparent holes; no cloth geometry, simulation, fiber-composition or breathability certification is added.

Appearance reference: [De Oost — Hopsack Cloth Suiting](https://www.deoost.com/blog/hopsack-cloth-suiting) explicitly describes two threads together in both warp and weft. The navy [swatch photograph](https://images.squarespace-cdn.com/content/v1/59df58c946c3c4aa7173a4cc/1512208797229-DM72A90S64R6Q9NJ8VBX/Blue%2BHopsack%2BCLASSIC%2BWORSTEDS%2BCOLLECTION%2BHOLLAND%2BAND%2BSHERRY%2BHS%2B1165.jpg) was actually viewed; palette, spacing and relief are authored approximations, not photograph-calibrated optical or product measurements. No photograph is packaged.

`basswood` approximates a selected finely sanded unfinished longitudinal Tilia americana face: uniform pale cream/light tan color, low-contrast long straight grain and shallow micrograin, not every Tilia species, endgrain anatomy, coarse dark vessels, transverse curl, knots, coating or species identification. The Wood Database account and both raw/finished photographs were actually read/viewed; only the raw appearance is selected. The source explicitly describes diffuse porosity and medium, very numerous endgrain vessels: a smooth face approximation is not a claim of pore-free anatomy. Direct fallthrough reuses the formal NickelSilver two-cache affine field with a constructor-only preset choice. A 96×4 long-grain field and 128² micrograin total 16,768 Float64 values / 134,144 bytes of lattice arithmetic, not total RAM or texture-cache size. Lower pigment/height coefficients, a different long-grain axis and a pale cream palette distinguish it from merely setting a metal factor to 0 while retaining the old transverse brush. Every old NickelSilver key/value and point operation order remains unchanged. Each point retains two cached lookups with no new allocation, hash, trigonometry, square root, kind branch or neighbor scan; no unused zero-curl Anigre fields, third cache or second synthesizer are added. Fine color/roughness and very shallow height approximate sanded wood shading, not coarse grooves, raised strips, actual fibers or displacement. The authored 0.10 m nominal tile and 0.0012 UV relief are not photograph-measured thickness. Metallic maps and actual default/createMaterial factor are 0, AO 1/mortar 0; four opaque default maps and optional height retain options, tint, Worker/cache, repeats and ownership. No runtime dependency, mesh, coating shader, mechanical/acoustic/hardness/health or anatomical certification is added. At actual512, very shallow signed normal slopes primarily quantize to adjacent127/128 bytes; this does not claim larger resolved relief. Normal direction is checked against raw height slope rather than increasing relief to force a visible normal.

Appearance reference: the actually read [Wood Database Basswood account](https://www.wood-database.com/basswood/) and actually viewed [raw pale longitudinal face](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/tilia-americana.jpg) and [warmer finished face](https://www.wood-database.com/wp-content/uploads/tilia-americana2.jpg); only the former is selected. The account states pale white to light brown, mostly uniform face color, subtle growth rings and straight fine even grain, while its endgrain description says diffuse-porous with medium, very numerous vessels. Synthesized search claims of no open pores or very small vessels are not adopted. The raw image includes some weak curved flatsawn figure; this preset selects understated long straight grain rather than reconstruct individual cathedral/ray/vessel anatomy. Photograph lighting does not calibrate authored palette, roughness, nominal tile or UV relief. No photograph bundle or species-identification, hardness, mechanical, acoustic, health or coating certification is added.

`sphericalwashers` approximates selected silver form-C-style stainless spherical washers as complete circular annuli intentionally flipped convex seating-face up. The normally upward flat bearing face, mating D/G conical seats, outward-rising straight cup-washer walls and three-wave spring washers are different surfaces. The actually viewed Halder stainless product photograph and section identify the spherical face on the underside in normal assembly; this preset explicitly reverses its display orientation instead of mislabeling the flat top as convex. Twenty-five fixed-center owners cache only per-ring tones and 128² grain, totaling 16,409 Float64 values / 131,272 bytes of field-table arithmetic, not total RAM or texture-cache size. Following the existing annular squared-radius C1 shoulders, lower opaque dielectric backing and cachedNoise conventions, the true spherical profile uses sqrt(R²-q), not a paraboloid, inverted cup cone or torus. This genuinely different geometry keeps a short independent case rather than adding profile dispatch or another closure to the old cup hot path. Only nonempty metal faces require one necessary square root and one grain lookup; no point allocation, hashing, trigonometry or neighbor scan is added. R 0.54 exceeds outer radius 0.36, leaving a spherical radicand of at least 0.162 throughout support and 0.14 clearance to the 0.5 owner half-width. Grain affects pigment/roughness only, not carved concentric grooves. The continuous inward-high/outward-low metal face is M1, round bores/backing M0, with coherent C1 partial coverage and AO 0.3/0.95; actual default/createMaterial factor 1 preserves authored B. The authored 0.10 m nominal tile and 0.025 UV relief are not DIN dimensions or measured thickness. Four opaque default maps and optional height retain options, tint, Worker/cache, repeats and ownership. No mesh holes, knurled sidewalls, transparency, mating-part reconstruction, tilt compensation, clamping/contact mechanics, grade/corrosion/hardness/load/DIN certification or photograph bundle is added.

Appearance references: the actually read [Halder stainless Spherical Washers/Conical Seats account](https://www.halder.com/gb/PM/Standard-Parts/Clamping-Elements/Spherical-Plain-Washers/Spherical-Washers-Conical-Seats-similar-to-DIN-6319-stainless-steel), actually viewed [silver three-part product photograph](https://www.halder.com/ix_pim_assets/image/Foto_ArtGrp_png/all/IM0007762_Foto_ArtGrp.webp), [isolated form-C photograph](https://www.halder.com/ix_pim_assets/image/Foto_png/all/small/IM0004067_Foto_small.webp) and [original section](https://www.halder.com/ix_pim_assets/image/Zeichnung_png/en/IM0002187_Zeichnung_en.webp). The first component has a flat bearing face and lower convex spherical seat; the other two are conical seats. Only the first component’s spherical face, displayed flipped upward, is selected. The actually read [Elesa/Ganter DIN6319 PDF](https://www.elesa-ganter.com/siteassets/PDF/EN/DIN%206319.pdf) distinguishes types/materials, but its dimensions, hardness and force values are not promoted to API guarantees. The first Halder steel account explicitly states manganese phosphating, so its dark photograph is excluded rather than passed off as bare conductor evidence; Kipp returned 406 and is not treated as acquired evidence. Silver uncoated-metal behavior is an authored PBR interpretation, not photograph-calibrated roughness, spectrum or microfinish.
